From spike basicly-zv48 dimension 1. Commits and gates carry only the human git identity; the runner name/model is known at dispatch and discarded (includeCoAuthoredBy is false). The D3 run-record (.basicly/usage/run-records.json) already holds agent+model per bead; this bead surfaces that provenance as attribution on the landed commit and the gate result.

## Acceptance Criteria

- run_record gains a latest_record(repo_root, bead_id) -> RunRecord | None accessor returning the most recent record for the bead (None when absent or empty).
- The landing merge commit carries agent attribution as git trailers sourced from the latest run-record: Harness-Runner: <agent>, plus Harness-Model: <model> when the run pinned one. - The verify gate records the runner: br gate report gets --actor <agent> and the model folded into the note, sourced from the latest run-record, for both the loop landing (loop._record_verify) and basicly verify --issue. No record -> no actor and the note is unchanged.
- Graceful when no run-record exists (verify run outside a dispatch): nothing breaks, no attribution added.
- Regression tests: the latest_record accessor; the merge message with and without a record; report_gate passing actor/model; the loop wiring reads the record.
- Architecture section 12.8 (and the dimension-1 attribution note) updated.
- pytest, ruff, and the projection checks stay green.

## Scope

Attribution from the existing run-record only: a merge-commit trailer and a gate actor. No per-agent bot identity (basicly-smzg), no commit signing or tamper-evidence, no new attribution source. Trailer chosen over a synthetic Co-Authored-By (no fake identity/email) per the and/or in the spike recommendation.

## Context

Three practices this repo depends on lived only in a session handover and an agent's memory, which
is the exact condition `basicly-ze8z` exists to remove: if you need memory to run basicly
correctly, the repo is wrong. Externalized at the lowest tier each one fits.

Tier 2 (skills), because each applies in a specific situation rather than always:

- `test-discipline` — mutate a fix in **both** directions. Deleting the fix was already taught;
  making the check fire on everything was not, and that is the direction that finds the missing
  test. It found one the same session it was written: a per-lane report labelling every lane
  REFUSED passed the whole file, because no admitted-lane control existed.
- `test-discipline` — restore a mutation from a copy, never `git checkout -- <file>`. A mutation is
  applied to a tree that usually holds the uncommitted change being verified.
- `harness-loop` — a remainder bead is a claim about unfinished work. Two in consecutive sessions
  (`jr0l.53`, `jr0l.55`) were already delivered by their parent and closed with no diff.

Tier 3 (always-on), one line only, because the rule already existed and merely failed to name the
form: `require-explicit-confirmation` listed "destructive resets" without naming
`git checkout -- <path>`, `git restore`, `git stash` or `git clean`. The omission is not
hypothetical - this session discarded an uncommitted module with `git checkout --` while restoring

payload.close_reason: Fixed in 76f330b: condition-based waits plus monotonic idle measurement
payload.description:
## Context

The three StallWatchdog tests shipped with basicly-kjc5.25 asserted a timing outcome after a fixed time.sleep, so whether they passed depended on how fast the host scheduled a background thread. They passed on ubuntu and windows and failed on macos-latest in run 30168113819, turning main red immediately after the kjc5.25 landing.

Could not be reproduced locally even under twelve CPU spinners, which is the point: a tuned sleep constant cannot be validated on the host that is not failing.

Fixed by waiting for the condition instead of for a duration (a _wait_until helper with a generous timeout), so the assertions no longer encode an assumption about host speed. Also corrected StallWatchdog._watch to measure idle time against a monotonic clock rather than accumulating the nominal poll interval - genuine correctness (a slow probe or an overrunning Event.wait made the flag arrive later than stall_after) though not the cause of the red.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the stall watchdog tests when they run on any supported runner then they assert the flag fired without depending on how fast the host schedules a thread, and main is green on all runners
payload.title: Stall watchdog tests asserted timing after a fixed sleep and went red on macos CI

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given an open bead whose worktree external_ref names a worktree that no longer exists when the loop derives its phase then the bead is either driveable again or reported as a repairable stale binding and a supervisor pass does not silently re-adopt and discard it forever
payload.description:
## Problem

A bead whose `worktree:` external_ref survives the worktree it names is wedged at phase `build`
and no code path can move it again.

`loop_state.derive_phase` reaches the `build` rung on `worktree is not None`, where *worktree* is
the binding parsed from the external_ref - existence of the ref, not existence of the worktree.
So a bead whose worktree was removed without clearing its ref keeps deriving `build` forever.
Meanwhile `supervise.derive_session` adopts it with `live=False`, `ready_lanes` drops every
non-live lane, and `advance_parked` skips on `not lane.live`. The bead is therefore
simultaneously at `build` (so the loop will not re-drive it from intake or classify) and
undispatchable (so nothing ever advances it). Nothing detects or clears the dead ref.

Observed on `basicly-jr0l.4`, which is residue from an earlier session and is re-adopted and
re-discarded on every single supervisor pass.

## Steps to Reproduce

```sh
uv run basicly loop status basicly-jr0l.4
ls -d ../basicly.worktrees/basicly-jr0l-4
git worktree list
```

Observed - `loop status` reports `phase: build` and
`worktree: basicly-jr0l-4 on harness/basicly-jr0l-4`, while the directory does not exist
("No such file or directory") and `git worktree list` does not list it. Every
`basicly loop supervise basicly-jr0l` pass prints
`adopted: basicly-jr0l.4 (open) -> basicly-jr0l-4 on harness/basicly-jr0l-4 [worktree missing]`
and then does nothing with it.

Expected - a binding whose worktree is gone either derives a phase the loop can act on, or is
reported as a repairable inconsistency with a command that clears it. A bead must not be able to
reach a state where it is both past classify and permanently undispatchable.

## Scope

- src/basicly/loop_state.py
- src/basicly/supervise.py
- tests/test_loop_state.py
- tests/test_supervise.py

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an open bead whose worktree external_ref names a worktree that no longer exists when the
  loop derives its phase then the bead is either driveable again or reported as a repairable
  stale binding, and a supervisor pass does not silently re-adopt and discard it forever
payload.title: A worktree binding that outlives its worktree wedges the bead at build phase forever

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a release cut whose beads already have an epic of origin when a supervised pass is composed for it then every chosen bead can be included without changing any beads parent and the pass fans out over exactly the chosen set and a test fails if membership requires a parent-child edge
payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Measured 2026-08-05 at `d31f6bd`, composing the `v0.7.0` release pass. `basicly-jr0l.65`
is a `v0.7.0` blocker whose parent is its epic of origin, `basicly-jr0l`:

```
uv run br dep add basicly-jr0l.65 basicly-yc0x -t parent-child
Error: Validation failed: depends_on_id: issue basicly-jr0l.65 already has parent
basicly-jr0l; clear or replace the existing parent before adding basicly-yc0x
```

Expected — a release cut can be assembled from beads that already belong to an epic.

## Why this blocks the factory's central workflow

`supervise <root>` fans out over the root's **`parent-child` dependents** and takes no
lane allowlist (`basicly loop supervise --help`: the only options are `--runner` and
`--autonomy`). Membership in a release epic must therefore be a `parent-child` edge —
that was the correction made on 2026-08-04 after `basicly-yc0x` was filed with `blocks`
edges and `preflight` reported `0 open child(ren)`.

But `br` permits exactly **one** parent. So a release epic can only fan out over beads
that are **parentless**, and a `v0.7.0` cut assembled from `tcmy`, `jr0l` and `m4zv`
children cannot be run as one supervised pass at all. Measured on this cut: of six
chosen beads, only two (`basicly-cdhq`, `basicly-3yi3`) could be adopted; the four with
an epic of origin (`jr0l.65`, `tcmy.34`, `tcmy.35`, `m4zv.14`) were refused.

The plan's §5 already notes the four beads adopted on 2026-08-04 "had no parent of their
own". That reads as an incidental detail; it is in fact the **only** case the mechanic
supports, and the note should say so.

## Why the three obvious workarounds are all wrong

- **Re-parent under the release epic.** Violates the plan's §14 — a bead's parent stays
  its epic of origin, and phase membership is a label rather than a re-parenting. It also
  destroys which review found the defect, which is the information `tcmy` carries.
- **Root the pass at the epic of origin instead.** Uncontrolled fan-out: rooting at
  `basicly-tcmy` offers 19 open children to routing, which then picks by scheduler score
  rather than by the release's content. That dispatches unplanned, unsized work with
  unmapped scope collisions — the exact defect `basicly-qorx` fixed, re-entered
  voluntarily.
- **Give the release epic `blocks` edges as well.** Refused as a cycle (recorded
  2026-08-04); and `br`'s cycle detection is insertion-order-dependent, so this
  sometimes appears to work.

## Fix shape

The engine side is the cheap half and does not touch the tracker's shape:

- **Give a pass an explicit lane set.** `supervise` accepts the beads to fan out over —
  a `--lane` repeatable flag, or a root plus a label selector (`--label release-v0.7.0`),
  so membership can be the label the plan's §14 already says it should be. This decouples
  "what a pass runs" from "who a bead's parent is", which are two different questions the
  `parent-child` edge is currently forced to answer at once.
- Then a release cut is a label, no bead is re-parented, and the §14 rule holds without
  costing the factory its own workflow.

Carry the one-parent constraint forward as a **requirement on the `v0.8.0` replacement**
(`basicly-vkh0`): the owned work graph should let a record belong to more than one
grouping, because "epic of origin" and "release cut" are independent axes and forcing
them through one edge is what created this. That is a requirement, not a licence to grow
the schema of the component being replaced (plan §10).

## Interim, for this cut

Two lanes supervised under `basicly-yc0x` (`cdhq`, `3yi3`), and the four parented beads
driven as single-track `loop run <id> --root basicly-yc0x`, which binds them to the
epic's grant without changing any parentage (`--root`: "Session root issue whose autonomy
grant may cover the checkpoints"). Correct, and it costs the concurrency on four of six
lanes.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`
- `tests/test_cli_loop.py`
- `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md`
payload.title: A release epic can only fan out over parentless beads so a cut drawn from existing epics cannot be one pass

payload.text:
Narrowed 2026-08-05, same day, after hitting the second half of this in practice. **Grant coverage is not broken - only fan-out is.** The bead's body implied a release cut cannot use the epic's grant either; that is wrong, and the mechanism was already built for exactly this case.

policy.session_issue_ids (policy.py:1293) walks **two** edge kinds: parent-child *dependents* and the root's own **blocks dependencies**. Its docstring states the intent directly - 'A release, or any root that gates work it did not parent, records that work as its own blocks dependencies - a bead's parent is its epic of origin and nothing is re-parented, so a descent-only walk found a session of exactly one bead and the grant covered nothing at all (basicly-jr0l.40)'. It even says 'no set of per-parent grants can substitute for following the edge that defines it'.

Measured here. loop run basicly-jr0l.65 --root basicly-yc0x refused with 'the active L3 grant on basicly-yc0x does not cover basicly-jr0l.65: it is not in that session's issue tree'. After 'br dep add basicly-yc0x <id> -t blocks' for the four parented beads, session_issue_ids returns 14 ids and all four are covered. No parentage changed.

**So the two requirements want opposite edges, and that is the whole defect:**

| Need | Edge that satisfies it | Works for a bead that already has a parent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| supervise fan-out | parent-child *dependent* | no - one parent only |
| grant coverage | root's blocks *dependency* | yes |

A release epic therefore needs parent-child for its parentless beads and blocks for its parented ones, and it can only *fan out* over the first group. That is why the 2026-08-04 correction (from blocks to parent-child) fixed fan-out and silently broke grant coverage for anything with a parent - the two changes look like the same edit and are not.

Adding both types between the same pair is refused as a cycle, so this is a genuine either/or per bead, not a both.

**This narrows the fix**: the engine does not need a new coverage mechanism, only a way to fan out over a set that is not the parent-child children - the --lane / --label selector already proposed. Keep the v0.8.0 requirement (a record should belong to more than one grouping); drop any implication that grants need changing.

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a config entry overriding the copilot agent without restating deny_style when any dispatch of it is formatted then the deny list is either emitted in copilots wire form or not injected at all rather than raising with a regression test covering the override path
payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-31 while exercising basicly-kjc5.59 through `basicly runner dry-run`. Not caused by
that change - reproduced on base `main` with a config that names no tier at all.

`[[runner.agents]]` replaces a builtin wholesale by design, so an entry overriding `copilot`
that does not restate `deny_style` gets `deny_style = None`. But `_inject_copilot_deny_tools`
still injects the permissions.yaml deny list onto that spec, and `format_command` then raises
because `deny_tools` is set with no style to spell it. The result is that **every** dispatch of
the overridden agent fails, including `basicly runner dry-run`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a scratch repo, write `basicly.toml` containing only:
   `[runner]` / `default = "copilot"` / `[[runner.agents]]` / `name = "copilot"` /
   `command = ["copilot", "-p", "{prompt}"]`
2. Run `basicly runner dry-run --runner copilot --prompt go`
3. Observed: `Error: runner 'copilot' sets deny_tools but has deny_style None; known: [...]`
   Expected: either the deny list is emitted in copilot's wire form, or it is not injected onto
   a spec that cannot express it.

The wholesale-replacement stance is deliberate and documented, so the fix is most likely to make
the injection carry the style it needs (or skip injecting when the spec cannot express it) rather
than to re-default the whole spec.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a config entry overriding the copilot agent without restating deny_style when any
  dispatch of it is formatted then the deny list is either emitted in copilot's wire form or not
  injected at all rather than raising, with a regression test covering the override path
payload.title: Keep the copilot deny style when a config entry overrides the builtin

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given an unrecognised key or section in basicly.toml or basicly.local.toml when the config loads then it fails naming the key and the sections that accept it and the forward-compatibility stance is recorded
payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

```
printf '\n[loop]\nconcurrency = 2\n' >> basicly.local.toml
uv run basicly loop preflight basicly-yc0x | rg forecast
# forecast: ~84816225 tokens if all 5 lanes start (cap x per-lane)   <- still 5
```

Observed 2026-08-04 - a `concurrency` key written under `[loop]` was **silently ignored**; the real
home is `[worktree] concurrency`. The only symptom was the committed default continuing to apply,
which is indistinguishable from the override having worked at the value it was already at. Expected -
an unknown section or key in a config file this project owns fails loudly.

## Context

Cost a wasted dispatch decision this session: the override was written to bound a pass to what the
grant funded, the forecast silently kept the committed cap of 5, and only re-reading the loader
found it. The failure mode is exactly the one `basicly-23ep` closed for a sibling declaration - there,
`[runner] context_windows` naming an unknown agent now raises, on the reasoning that *a declaration
whose only symptom is the silent default it was written to replace is the defect it was meant to
fix*. The same argument applies to the key itself, not just its value.

The blast radius is wider than a mistyped section. `basicly.local.toml` is gitignored and
machine-local, so a stale or misplaced key there diverges one machine's behaviour from committed
intent with no diff to review and no gate to catch it - the hazard the file's own header warns about
in prose and nothing enforces.

## Fix shape

- Fail on an unrecognised key or section in `basicly.toml` and `basicly.local.toml`, naming the key
  and the sections that do accept it. A strict-schema pass over the loaded tables, not a hand-listed
  denylist that goes stale the next time a key is added.
- Weigh forward compatibility explicitly and record the decision: a consumer on a newer config with
  an older engine would start failing. A warn-then-error staging, or erroring only on a key that is
  a near-miss for a known one, are both defensible - pick one and say why.
- `basicly check` is the natural home; a malformed local overlay should also surface in
  `loop preflight`, since that command exists to answer what a run needs.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `tests/test_config.py`

payload.acceptance_criteria: An interactive loop run refuses to dispatch a runner when the root's grant is halted and surfaces the halt reason instead of dispatching; the working-set band admission applies to that dispatch as it does to a supervised lane, with the never-checked notice recorded the same way; the checkpoint challenge reprints the operator's own runner selection so relaying a confirm code cannot convert a manual handoff into a live dispatch; regression tests cover a halted grant and a scopeless bead reaching the interactive dispatch path
payload.description:
## Problem

`_dispatch_runner` is a fourth dispatch site that D3's spend halt does not cover.
`policy.spend_status` is the one halt predicate, and its own docstring names the three
call sites that enforce it — delegated checkpoint approval, supervised lane admission,
and decider delegation. An interactive `basicly loop run` at the classify to build
transition dispatches a headless agent without consulting it, and without calling
`supervise.admit_working_set` either. So the path a human is most likely to take by
hand is the one path with no cost gate on it at all.

Observed 2026-08-01. `basicly-jr0l`'s grant was exhausted — 43599830 spent against a
21000000 token budget, with `basicly loop preflight basicly-jr0l` reporting
`remaining 0` and `halted: L1 grant token_budget spent ... the session is human-only
until re-granted`. A `loop run` on basicly-jr0l.60 that omitted the `--runner manual`
override resolved `[runner] default = "auto"` to headless claude and dispatched a real
metered agent regardless. The lane ran to completion and committed.

Two things make this worse than a cosmetic gap. The challenge text a checkpoint prints
reprints the command to re-run **without** any `--runner` the operator originally
passed, so relaying a confirm code verbatim silently converts a manual handoff into a
live dispatch. And an exhausted grant is exactly the state in which an operator
believes no dispatch can occur.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Exhaust a root's grant, so `basicly loop preflight <root>` prints `remaining 0` and
   a `halted:` line.
2. Take a leaf bead on that root to the classify to build transition, with
   `[runner] default = "auto"` and a headless agent CLI on PATH.
3. Run `basicly loop run <bead> --root <root> --confirm <code>` with no `--runner`.

Observed: the runner is dispatched and metered spend continues past the ceiling.
Expected: the halt refuses the dispatch, as it does for a supervised lane.

## Root Cause

`src/basicly/loop.py:510` `_dispatch_runner` calls `sizing_at_dispatch` only to
*record* a forecast, then calls `runner.run`. There is no `policy.spend_status` check
and no `supervise.admit_working_set` call, so neither the spend ceiling
(basicly-jr0l.22, basicly-vz78) nor the working-set band (basicly-jr0l.60) applies.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
- `tests/test_cli.py`

Widened from the four-line scope this bead was filed with, which named only `loop.py`,
`policy.py` and `tests/test_loop.py` and so did not cover its own third acceptance
criterion: the challenge reprint is built in `cli.py`. Declaring the ground before the
work rather than recording a scope violation at the landing.
payload.title: an interactive loop run dispatch consults neither the spend halt nor the band gate

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a recorded context occupancy greater than the declared window for its runner spec when the check runs then it fails naming both figures and the six existing records are the fixture and a control passes inside the window and the window is declared per agent in config with its source recorded rather than defaulted silently
payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

```
rg -n "_CONTEXT_WINDOWS" src/basicly/runner.py
rg -n "DEFAULT_CONTEXT_CEILING|DEFAULT_WORKING_SET_MAX" src/basicly/config.py
uv run python -c "
import json, pathlib
d = json.loads(pathlib.Path('.basicly/usage/run-records.json').read_text())
for k, v in d.items():
    for r in v:
        if r.get('context_tokens'):
            print(k, r['context_tokens'], r.get('forecast_tokens'))"
```

Observed - `basicly-tcmy.5` recorded a final context occupancy of **223221 tokens** while the
engine declares the claude window as **200000**. Expected - a lane cannot occupy more of a window
than the window has.

## The defect is a stale capability constant, not a sizing error

`context_occupancy` (`runner.py:1592-1601`) is documented as *"how full the model's window was at
the end of the run"* - the last assistant message's own usage on the `claude-stream-json` arm, not a
cumulative sum. So a recorded 223221 is a direct measurement of window occupancy, and it exceeds the
declared window. **The repo's own telemetry refutes `runner.py:119`.**

`_CONTEXT_WINDOWS = {"claude": 200_000, ...}` was written when 200000 was the right figure. The model
this repo now dispatches is Claude Opus 5, whose context window is **1000000** (checked against the
vendor's live model documentation on 2026-08-04, not recalled). The consequence chain:

- `ceiling_tokens` = `context_window * context_ceiling` = `200000 * 0.6` = **120000**
- the true guard, on a 1M window at the same 0.6 fraction, is **600000**
- so the finalize protocol fires at one fifth of its intended point

Seven lanes carry a measured occupancy; six crossed 120000 and **every one is far below 600000**:

| lane | context_tokens | over 120000 | over 600000 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| basicly-tcmy.5 | 223221 | yes | no |
| basicly-gczc | 210721 | yes | no |
| basicly-vkh0.10 | 193096 | yes | no |
| basicly-tcmy.6 | 190177 | yes | no |
| basicly-tcmy.22 | 171029 | yes | no |
| basicly-jr0l.64 | 170530 | yes | no |
| basicly-8ry8 | 80211 | no | no |

**Every one of those six finalizations was spurious.** The tracker holds **twelve**
`(context-ceiling overrun)` follow-up beads, eight still open, and the 2026-08-03 pass shipped four
beads while creating three of them - so `basicly-tcmy.5`, `.6` and `.22` are partial landings whose
remainders (`basicly-tcmy.39`, `.38`, `.37`) exist only because of this constant. At a one-to-one
ship-to-follow-up ratio the release ladder does not converge, which makes this the single highest
-leverage defect open against the factory.

This is the family basicly-z2wi, basicly-3w44, basicly-ipx2 and basicly-tcmy.34 belong to, seen from
a new angle: not a number in the wrong unit, but a number describing a capability the runtime no
longer has. It is also the exact shape of the owner rule that a vendor capability must be read from
the vendor's live documentation rather than recalled - the constant was correct when written and
nothing re-checked it.

## Fix shape

**Do not hardcode 1000000 from the documentation either** - that repeats the original mistake with a
newer number, and a consumer pinning a different model or a 200k session inherits a window we made
up for them. Three parts:

- **Declare the window, per agent, in config.** `runner.py:116` already documents the field as
  config-overridable per agent; this repo declares nothing, so it silently takes the default. Make
  the resolved window a declared, reviewable value, and record on each dispatch which source it came
  from - the same declared-versus-measured discipline `decompose.BUILD_FACTOR_SEED` and
  `forecast_source` already follow.
- **Gate the constant against the ledger.** The contradiction above is mechanically detectable:
  a recorded `context_tokens` greater than the declared window for that spec is a proof the
  declaration is wrong. Add a check that fails on it and names both figures - the same stance the
  evidence-bound ceiling gate already takes, which fired correctly twice on 2026-08-03. Had it
  existed, it would have caught this the first time a lane recorded 210721.
- **Then re-derive the trigger, not the fraction.** `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_CEILING = 0.6` is a behavioural
  guard below the real window (design D8) and is not what is broken; leave it alone. The trigger
  follows from the corrected window.

**A regression test must be proven red first** (basicly-kjc5.49): assert that a run whose recorded
occupancy exceeds the declared window for its spec fails the check, with a control that passes at an
occupancy inside the window. The six records above are the fixture - this is not a hypothetical
input.

## What this bead is NOT

**Separate from basicly-tcmy.34.** Three quantities exist, not two: the scope proxy
(`forecast_tokens`, 18780 to 66780 across these records), final window occupancy (`context_tokens`,
80211 to 223221) and whole-lane spend (`tokens`, 2393339 to 23963089). tcmy.34's 269x is the proxy
against *spend*. This bead is the declared window against *measured occupancy*.

**The band is a second-order question and is deliberately left out.** `decompose.py:792` states that
`working_set_max` is a context-window ceiling, so `DEFAULT_WORKING_SET_MAX = 132000` and
`ceiling_tokens` are the same quantity and should not disagree. Against a corrected 600000 trigger
they no longer contradict outright, but the proxy still runs 3.16x to 7.21x low against measured
occupancy, so a lane admitted at 132000 lands near 495000 at the median ratio and near 950000 at the
worst - over the corrected trigger at the tail. `config.py:455-466` records that 132000 was derived
by re-reading the tree and re-applying the estimator to its own output, which
`run_record.py:164-171` explains was unavoidable before `context_tokens` existed. That field now has
seven samples, so the derivation can be replaced by a measurement - but only after the window is
right, because calibrating a band against a trigger that is itself wrong by 5x fits the error.
**File that as the follow-on; do not widen this bead into it.**

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `basicly.toml`
- `tests/test_runner.py`
payload.title: The declared claude context window is smaller than measured lane occupancy so the finalize protocol truncates healthy lanes

payload.close_reason: wontfix: NO-GO on the land-after-ship redesign. CI-cost driver already solved by flp; c9e5 and 4psl removed loop friction; residual governance+efficiency gains do not justify a high-risk reorder of phase-derivation/fan-in/rework/concurrency on a just-stabilized loop (P3). Full go/no-go analysis recorded in the design comment.
payload.description:
Follow-up design track from basicly-flp. Today the loop lands a worktree at the build->verify transition, BEFORE the verify phase gate and the human ship checkpoint, and closes the bead in a separate post-ship tracker-only commit; merge_worktree also verifies twice (in the worktree post-rebase, then again on base via _record_verify, an identical tree). Proposed redesign: reorder to build -> verify (gate recorded from the worktree run) -> ship checkpoint -> land+close in one step, where the merge uses git merge --no-ff --no-commit, then closes the bead, flushes, stages .beads/issues.jsonl, and commits - one tracker-carrying merge commit per track, nothing lands on main before gates and human approval, and the duplicate base re-verify disappears. Must be designed against: feature fan-in (children land through the queue when all closed - their self-landing order changes), rework semantics after a landing failure, multi-track concurrency (base working-tree jsonl carrying another track's uncommitted claim at merge time), and loop_state phase derivation (verified currently implies a bound worktree + green gates; landing evidence moves). See the investigation and decision comments on basicly-flp.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A design comment (or architecture.md section update) covers phase reorder, fan-in, rework, concurrency, and phase-derivation impacts with a go/no-go recommendation; if go, implementation is decomposed into child beads. Full gate suite passes for anything landed.
payload.title: Design: land after ship approval and fold the bead close into the merge commit

payload.text: Scoped down by basicly-c9e5 (br redirect worktrees + engine-owned tracker commits): once c9e5 ships, the residual value here is governance only - landing before ship approval, and folding the close into the merge commit saves one CI-free engine commit. Re-evaluate go/no-go after c9e5.

DESIGN GO/NO-GO: NO-GO (wontfix). Analysis of the proposed reorder (build -> verify[gate from worktree run] -> ship checkpoint -> land+close in one --no-ff --no-commit merge commit) against the required impact areas:

- Driver reassessment: the original motivation (pointless CI builds from tracker commits) was already solved by flp via paths-ignore .beads/** on the workflows + consumer template. c9e5 then made worktrees share the tracker via br redirect (no diverging issues.jsonl copy), and 4psl made the landing rebase conflict-free when work is committed. The loop is now stable and frictionless, so only two residual benefits remain: (1) governance - today code lands on main at build->verify, BEFORE the human ship checkpoint, so ship approval gates only teardown/close, not the merge; (2) efficiency - one fewer commit (fold close into the merge) and dropping the duplicate verify (worktree pre-merge check + base post-merge recorded run on an identical tree).

- Phase reorder impact: moving the merge to after the ship checkpoint inverts the state machine. loop_state currently derives 'verified' from a bound worktree + green required gate + a landed branch; landing evidence would move, so phase derivation and the _worktree_landed backstop (ship refuses an unlanded branch) both need reworking.
- Feature fan-in impact: children currently land through the serial merge queue at the parent build phase, and a child driven through its own loop self-lands at ITS ship. Landing the parent after ship changes when children land relative to parent approval - fan-in ordering and the 'already self-landed' accounting must be redesigned.
- Rework impact: a landing that fails AFTER a human has approved ship is a new failure mode (today landing precedes approval, so a landing failure reworks before any human gate). Recovery semantics post-approval are undefined.
- Concurrency impact: the --no-commit merge + stage .beads/issues.jsonl + commit would sweep any other in-flight track's uncommitted tracker claim sitting in the base working tree at merge time - a cross-track contamination risk the current commit_tracker_state path avoids.

- Decision: NO-GO. The CI-cost driver is solved; c9e5+4psl removed the friction; the residual wins are modest governance + efficiency on a P3, against a high-risk reorder spanning phase-derivation, fan-in, rework, and concurrency, on a loop that was just stabilized. Rejected alternative kept as-is. The one reason to revisit: if 'nothing lands on main before human ship approval' becomes a hard governance requirement (e.g. a production-agent/Foundry principle), reopen and decompose - but note deterministic verify gates already pass before landing, so the ship checkpoint is effectively a final formality today.

The release workflow runs `uv build` then uploads `files: dist/*` (.github/workflows/release.yml:156). `uv build` writes a 1-byte `dist/.gitignore` (contents `*`) into the output dir, and the wildcard glob sweeps it onto the GitHub release page as a stray attachment alongside the real wheel and sdist.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Tag a release (push a `v*` tag) so the release job runs.
2. Open the published release and look at the Assets list.
3. A 1-byte `.gitignore` appears as an asset next to `basicly-<v>-py3-none-any.whl` and `basicly-<v>.tar.gz`.

Reproduced locally: `uv build --out-dir <dir>` emits a `.gitignore` (1 byte, contents `*`) beside the wheel and tarball.

## Root Cause
`files: dist/*` matches every file uv drops in `dist/`, including its scratch `.gitignore`, so the glob is too broad.

payload.description:
## Context

Claude Code output styles modify the system prompt to set role, tone and default response
format. This repo had none, so every session ran the built-in Default style.

The owner's standing preference - answer first, brevity, structure over prose, disagree when
warranted, flag the claims most likely to be confidently wrong - existed only as a hand-pasted
chat prompt. A committed project output style makes it the default for everyone working in the
repo instead.

## Decisions

- **`keep-coding-instructions: true` is mandatory here.** A custom style *omits* Claude Code's
  built-in software-engineering instructions by default (verified against the vendor doc
  2026-08-06: "Custom output styles leave out Claude Code's built-in software engineering
  instructions, such as how to scope changes, write comments, and verify work, unless
  keep-coding-instructions is set to true"). In a repo whose whole subject is verification
  discipline, losing 'how to verify work' would be the worst possible regression.
- **Mermaid is excluded, tables and ASCII are not.** Claude Code renders markdown in a
  terminal, so a mermaid block shows as source. The style names the formats that actually
  render.
- **Length was the binding constraint.** The source chat prompt is ~600 words; the style is
  ~175. Every clause of the original was mapped before cutting, and the six that had been
  abstracted away were restored. Shorter is likelier to bind, and output styles get periodic
  adherence reminders that reinforce a short instruction set.
- **Phrased affirmatively.** Prohibitions cost context and read as noise; each rule states what
  to do.

## Why settings.json is safe to hand-edit

`.claude/settings.json` is committed but not projected: it is absent from
`.basicly/generated-manifest.json`, carries no generated marker, and `claude_settings.py`
merges only `permissions`, `hooks` and `worktree.bgIsolation` into it. Verified by running
`basicly permissions-build` and `basicly hooks-build` and confirming `outputStyle` survived
both.

## Scope

- `.claude/output-styles/tired-engineer.md`
- `.claude/settings.json`

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a completed copilot dispatch when its usage is read then the run record carries the per-model input output cache-read and cache-write token counts and the AI-credit cost taken from the session shutdown model metrics rather than the chars-over-four transcript estimate, and given a dispatch whose session store is absent or unreadable then the estimate fallback is used and recorded as an estimate rather than reported as measured, with tests
payload.description:
## Context

Reopened and re-prioritised 2026-07-29 after probing the live copilot CLI. The premise
recorded in `src/basicly/runner.py:153` is wrong and must be corrected with this work:
copilot does report token usage. The comment says its result event "carries premium-request
counts, not tokens", which is true of that one event and false as a generalisation.

Verified against `copilot -p ... --output-format json` plus the persisted session store:

- `result.usage` carries only `premiumRequests`, `totalApiDurationMs`, `sessionDurationMs`
  and `codeChanges` - no tokens. This is what the earlier probe saw.
- `session.usage_checkpoint.data` carries `totalNanoAiu` and `totalPremiumRequests`.
- `assistant.message.data` carries `model` and `outputTokens`.
- `model.call_start.data` carries `model` per call.
- `session.shutdown.data.modelMetrics.<modelId>` carries the whole thing, keyed by model:
  `requests{count,cost}`, `usage{inputTokens,outputTokens,cacheReadTokens,cacheWriteTokens,
  reasoningTokens}`, `totalNanoAiu`, and `tokenDetails`.

Observed on a one-word probe: inputTokens 24210, cacheWriteTokens 24208, outputTokens 4,
totalNanoAiu 6056400000 - that is 6.0564 AI credits.

The extraction wrinkle: `session.shutdown` is **not** emitted on stdout in headless `-p`
mode. It is persisted to the session store. So the reader is two-step - take
`result.sessionId` from the stream, then read that session's `events.jsonl`. The store path
is machine-local and must never be committed; it needs a config-overridable base rather than
a hardcoded home-relative path.

Because `modelMetrics` is already keyed by model id, this is the richest calibration carrier
of any adapter we have - it supplies the per-model token counts and a native cost figure that
basicly-jr0l.21 needs, for a family where nothing is recorded today.

Scope: `src/basicly/runner.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a completed copilot dispatch when its usage is read then the run record carries the
  per-model input output cache-read and cache-write token counts and the AI-credit cost taken
  from the session shutdown model metrics rather than the chars-over-four transcript estimate,
  and given a dispatch whose session store is absent or unreadable then the estimate fallback
  is used and recorded as an estimate rather than reported as measured, with tests
payload.design: Do not discover the state path - dictate it. RunnerSpec gains a state_env naming the variable that relocates the family's state root: COPILOT_HOME for copilot and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for claude, both verified present in the shipped binaries; unset for codex, which is not installed here and must not be guessed. run() already injects dispatch env (BR_MODEL at runner.py:568, GIT_AUTHOR and GIT_COMMITTER for the bot identity), so set state_env to a harness-owned directory under the gitignored .basicly/usage tree and read usage from a location known by construction. Verified 2026-07-29: with COPILOT_HOME pointed at a scratch dir the session landed in that dir's session-state and not in the real home, and the dispatch still exited 0 because copilot auth comes from the gh credential store rather than from COPILOT_HOME. This removes the platform path table entirely - no home-directory guessing across Windows, Linux, macOS and WSL, and no wslpath mapping for a Windows binary invoked from WSL - and it makes the path derive from the repo root so nothing machine-specific can reach a committed file. Side benefit: per-dispatch state dirs make concurrent lanes hermetic, which they are not today. Residual risks to handle in the work: a Windows binary reached from WSL needs a Windows-shaped value, which is the one real platform branch and belongs in table-driven test data rather than host-dependent logic per the platform-hermetic rule; a consumer whose auth does live in the copilot home breaks on relocation, so an empty state dir after a failed dispatch must fall back to the default home and record that it did; and a family with no known state_env falls through to usage-unmeasurable, which basicly-jr0l.35 governs.
payload.title: Copilot usage extraction: credits from session usage checkpoint

payload.text: User-supplied rate 2026-07-22 (unverified, AFAIK-grade): 1 copilot credit = 0.01 USD. That resolves the unit question: convert totalNanoAiu to USD as nanoAiu / 1e9 * 0.01 and keep RunRecord.cost USD-denominated - no unit-aware field needed. Verify the rate against GitHub billing docs (or 'copilot billing') before hardcoding; the probe example totalNanoAiu=6044400000 would be 6.0444 credits = 0.060444 USD.

Rate confirmed by official source: GitHub docs, usage-based billing for individuals (docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/billing/usage-based-billing-for-individuals) states 'This total is converted into AI credits (1 AI credit = 0.01 USD)'. Safe to hardcode the nanoAiu/1e9*0.01 conversion; cite this page in the code comment.

[harness-info] Promoted to the release path 2026-07-29. The consequence is not only bad telemetry: policy.session_spend_tokens (the grant meter) sums these recorded token values, so on copilot the autonomy grant's spend ceiling meters a chars-over-four estimate taken over captured output only. Measured 1378 estimated against 24210 real input tokens on a live probe, 17.6 times under with json output and about 24000 times under with text output. Same failure class as basicly-jr0l.22 - a ceiling that cannot fire - reached by a different route. The general case is basicly-jr0l.35.

[harness-info] Codex state root confirmed 2026-07-29 as CODEX_HOME (67 references in codex-cli 0.146.0), plus CODEX_SQLITE_HOME. Important difference from copilot: auth.json lives *inside* the codex home, so pointing CODEX_HOME at an empty directory would break auth - the residual risk flagged on this bead is real for codex specifically. Either seed the harness-owned home with the auth file or relocate only the sqlite state via CODEX_SQLITE_HOME, leaving CODEX_HOME alone. Copilot is unaffected because its auth comes from the gh credential store.

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a design document that tracked open items as a list of bead ids when the sweep is complete then no design or architecture document carries a bead-id list that functions as status and each is replaced by the br query that answers it and a citation explaining why a decision was made is retained
payload.description:
## Context

Attempt 4 of the unattended-run proof failed on `docs/design/tier-injection-kit.md`
§7 'Open', which names `basicly-e3z6` and `basicly-5gn2` as bullets. Both lanes ran
concurrently, each deleted its own bullet, and the two edits hit one anchor — so the
second lane bounced, burned both rework attempts replaying the same rebase, and
escalated to a human.

The list is the tracker's content duplicated in prose. The implementation plan already
states the rule for the same problem one level up (§14): phase membership is a tracker
label and the plan says 'Query it rather than reading a list here', with
`br list --label phase-2`. A design document's open-items list is the same duplication
and creates the same collision.

## The fix

A design document says what the design **is**. What is still open about it is a tracker
query. Replace each hand-maintained bead-id list with the query that answers it —
a label per design area, so `br list --label kit` replaces §7 — and delete the lists.

Two properties follow: the list cannot go stale (it is generated on demand), and two
lanes closing two items in the same design area stop colliding, because neither edits
the document at all.

## Sweep, do not spot-fix

Find every such list rather than only the one that failed: grep the design and
architecture documents for bead-id references that function as status rather than as
citation. A citation of *why* a decision was made is history and stays; a list of what
remains open is state and goes.

## Scope

- `docs/design/tier-injection-kit.md`
- `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md`

Narrowed 2026-08-06 from the original five-file list after the sweep recorded in this bead's
comments. `factory-design.md`, `agent-roster-design.md` and `architecture.md` were checked and
carry citations only, so they are deliberately **out** of scope rather than unexamined. The label
minting the replacement query depends on is a `br` action, not a file.
payload.title: A design document must not carry a list of bead ids the tracker already owns

payload.text:
Swept 2026-08-06 at d58e8e2, before dispatching. Method: extract every `basicly-xxxx` token from
every file under `docs/`, **validate each against the 616 ids in `.beads/issues.jsonl`**, then group
by nearest heading. Validating against the tracker matters - a bare regex also matches
`.basicly-local/`, `basicly permissions-build` and the `basicly-fix-the-thing` example in
work-tracker R5, and a sweep that trusts the regex edits prose that references no bead at all.

Result: **233 real bead references across 14 documents.** Almost all are citations and stay. Two
are the defect.

## Confirmed targets (2, not the 5 files this bead's Scope listed)

1. **`docs/design/tier-injection-kit.md` §7 "Open"** (L189-195) - the instance that failed attempt
   4. A two-line section whose entire content is one bead id as status.
2. **`docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` §14 "Phase labels to epics"** (L603-615) - and this one is
   self-contradicting, which is the sharper finding. Two lines above the table it says *"Query it
   rather than reading a list here"* and prints `br list --label phase-2`. Then it prints a
   15-id table.

   **But the table is not uniformly wrong, so do not delete it.** Phase -> epic is one stable root
   per phase and is the *index into* the tracker, not a duplicate of its contents. What goes is the
   inline **status** in the Release column: ``(`u6jq.1` is all that remains)``, ``(`agzx.1` done)``,
   ``(`m4zv.14` in `v0.7.0`)``. That is the state that rots, and it is what two lanes closing two
   items in one phase would both edit.

## Explicit exclusions - a sweep that takes these is destructive

- **`docs/archive/**` - 45 references, do not touch.** Its own banner: *"Archived - spike complete
  (kept for design provenance) ... nothing here is maintained, and a claim in it is evidence of
  what was true in 2026-07 rather than of current behaviour."* Its dimension numbering is cited by
  `src/basicly/permissions.py` and `src/basicly/rubrics.py`. Archive is history by declaration,
  which is exactly the category this bead says stays.
- **`docs/design/work-tracker.md` §2.1, R1-R9** - each id is the citation for a paid-for
  dependency defect, and R9 is held by a completeness test
  (`test_r9_a_publish_that_would_shrink_the_export_is_refused_not_silent`). Deleting these deletes
  the provenance of a gated register.
- **`docs/design/factory-design.md` §3 components 10-11, §6 configuration defaults, §8** -
  citations: which pre-existing bead a component absorbs, and why a default has the value it has.
- **`docs/design/agent-roster-design.md` §8** - citations of which bead builds a mechanism this
  design depends on (`kjc5.16` confinement, `kjc5.4` decision queue).
- **`docs/architecture/architecture.md` §11 and §15** - checked and neither qualifies. §11 states
  outright *"None is tracked as an open issue"*; §15 keys rows on capability and design document,
  carrying no bead ids.
- **`docs/design/tier-injection-kit.md` §1** - the `Bead` table row identifies which bead each
  *approach* is, which is identification, not status.

## Blocking prerequisite: the replacement query returns nothing today

This bead's fix says *"a label per design area, so `br list --label kit` replaces §7"*. **That
label vocabulary does not exist.** The only labels in the tracker are `phase-0`..`phase-7`,
`phase-meta`, `phase-multi`, `bookkeeping`, `owner-decision`, `zero-dep`. `basicly-a3yi` - the one
bead §7 names - carries `phase-1` and nothing else.

So replacing §7 with `br list --label kit` as written would point the document at an **empty
result**, and an empty query is indistinguishable from "nothing is open". That is strictly worse
than the stale list it replaces: the list was wrong and looked wrong, the query is wrong and looks
authoritative.

**Order the work accordingly:** mint the label on the beads that belong to the design area, run the
query and confirm it returns them, and only then delete the prose. A doc pointing at a query is
only honest once the query answers.

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a corpus of recorded dispatches when the operator asks for a tuning report then it names per governed parameter the value in force the outcome distribution observed under it a recommended value with its sample size and whether the recommendation is measured or seeded and it changes no configuration itself
payload.description:
## Context

Almost every number that governs the factory is currently set by judgment and then never
revisited against what actually happened. The one exception proved the point twice in a single
session: the first measured lane actual (4079243 tokens, 3.657368 USD, 519.6s) corrected a cost
estimate that was wrong by ~2.4x, and then supplied the bound that basicly-vz78 needed. Both were
decisions a measurement changed. Nothing else in the config has that feedback loop.

The owner's framing (2026-08-01): the per-lane budget is changeable, so it should be *learned*
rather than set — and the same applies to the other parameters. Gather the observations, pair them
with the parameters in force, and let the configuration adapt to evidence.

There is already scaffolding to build on rather than invent: run records carry per-dispatch facts,
`decompose.calibrated_build_factors` already replaces its seeds from measured samples past
`calibration_min_samples`, `run_record.SpendCalibration` already keeps a measured ratio beside the
prior it displaced, and `WaitEvent` already meters human wait. This bead is about extending that
pattern to the parameters that have no loop yet, and about making the resulting recommendation
readable.

## The parameters that are currently guesses

- `[runner] runner_timeout` - the owner's example. Set to 1800 today as a cost control, with no
  evidence about what value maximises landed work per token.
- `[worktree] concurrency` - now 5, exercised at 1. Throughput against tracker-write and CPU
  contention is exactly an empirical question.
- `[runner] max_agent_processes`, `stall_after`
- `[sizing] working_set_min` / `working_set_max` - the band that refuses a package
- `[sizing] build_factors` per task class, `context_ceiling`, `calibration_min_samples`,
  `calibration_window`
- `[policy] max_rework`, `max_subtasks_per_lane`, `decider_max_decisions`
- `decompose.UNSIZED_LANE_TOKENS_SEED` and the choice of statistic behind
  `unsized_lane_tokens` (median today, chosen against a bimodal sample of 13 - see basicly-vz78)

## Observations to record per dispatch, so the above can be learned

Outcome signals (what "best results" means, and it is not one number):

- landed on the first attempt, versus rework consumed before landing
- gate failures per lane, split deterministic versus flaky (a flake distorts every other
  measurement - basicly-5h0g, basicly-55yh)
- tokens, cost, wall clock (recorded today)
- final context occupancy against `context_ceiling`, and whether the overrun follow-up fired
- whether the lane hit `runner_timeout`, and what it had produced when it did
- whether it wrote `needs-input.json`, and on what class of missing fact
- declared scope versus files actually touched (relates to basicly-jr0l.44)
- merge-queue events: bounces, D5 base-moved cancellations, retries
- human interventions with cause and kind, and the wait each one cost (`WaitEvent.waited_s`)
- forecast against actual, once basicly-vz78 makes pairs obtainable at all

Each observation has to be stored beside **the parameter values in force for that dispatch**, or
the pairing cannot be reconstructed later - which is the same mistake that left 5 forecasts and 13
actuals with no pair between them.

## Constraints this must respect

- **Advisory, not self-modifying.** Deterministic checks block, judged checks advise, and the
  engine disposes. A tuner proposes a configuration change and reports the evidence; a human or a
  gate applies it. Nothing here may rewrite `basicly.toml` on its own.
- Recommendations must name their sample size and never present a seed as a measurement, the way
  `SpendCalibration` already does.
- Telemetry that never leaves the machine is half useless: `.basicly/usage/` is self-ignored, so a
  measurement that should inform a shared decision has to reach the tracker (basicly-kjc5.50 made
  calibration read both).
- No new runtime product dependency; this is arithmetic over records we already write.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a corpus of recorded dispatches when the operator asks for a tuning report then it names,
  per governed parameter, the value in force, the outcome distribution observed under it, a
  recommended value with its sample size, and whether the recommendation is measured or seeded -
  and it changes no configuration itself
payload.title: Learn the factory parameters from recorded outcomes instead of setting them by judgment

payload.description:
From spike basicly-zv48 dimension 2. Captured runner stdout/stderr is never inspected/filtered/egress-limited. Redact secrets from persisted/surfaced runner output and optionally assert a network-restricted sandbox for headless runs.

Investigation (2026-07-18): run_record.py already never persists output (only a redacted command), so the gap is the surfaced/live RunResult.stdout/stderr, emitted raw by the CLI runner run and read by the loop/rubrics. The yzyd secret-scan hook (.basicly/core/hooks/secret-scan.py) has a high-signal pattern set to reuse, but it is a standalone stdlib hook (not importable), so a sibling redact module in src/basicly mirrors its patterns. Egress: basicly cannot portably network-sandbox a generic subprocess; that is agent-layer (codex sandbox = basicly-t0kt, claude/copilot config), so this task documents the egress posture rather than building a speculative seam (user-scoped 2026-07-18).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new redact module redacts high-signal secret patterns (private-key header, aws/github/slack/google/openai tokens, slack webhook, and the generic secret-named assignment with placeholder filtering) from arbitrary text, replacing each hit with a labeled placeholder; secret-free text is returned unchanged.
- runner.run applies redaction to captured stdout and stderr so every surfaced/persisted RunResult carries redacted output (guardrail at the source); dry-run and handoff results (empty output) are unaffected.
- The redaction patterns mirror the secret-scan hook (basicly-yzyd) as the sibling detector, noted in a comment so the two stay in step.
- Egress is documented as delegated to the agent-layer sandbox (codex basicly-t0kt, claude/copilot config); basicly redacts output but does not sandbox a generic subprocess. No speculative seam is added.
- Deterministic tests cover each secret pattern class, secret-free passthrough, and run() redacting both stdout and stderr.

payload.description:
Open question surfaced by basicly-x5gh: pre-commit as the hook runner forces every consumer to have pre-commit provisioned (uvx works, but it is a Python tool with an activation seam that just bit us on a fresh repo). Evaluate whether lefthook is objectively a better fit for basicly's hook distribution, or whether pre-commit stays.

Produce a decision doc that objectively lists the positives and negatives of each across the dimensions that actually matter for basicly, then recommends one:

- Consumer runtime cost: lefthook is a single static binary (no Python/runtime dep); pre-commit needs Python + provisioning (uv/uvx). basicly consumers reliably have uv, not necessarily pip/pre-commit.
- Cross-platform including Windows and WSL (a hard basicly constraint).
- Hook stage coverage basicly relies on: pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push.
- Config format and projection fit: how cleanly each maps to basicly's catalog -> generated wiring (.pre-commit-config.yaml today) and the managed-block rewrite (ruamel round-trip, basicly-wd7u).
- Speed and parallelism of hook execution.
- Ecosystem, maturity, maintenance, and migration cost off pre-commit.
- Whether either removes the auto-activation footgun entirely (e.g. lefthook install vs pre-commit install).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written comparison (docs or tracker comment) enumerating pros and cons of lefthook vs pre-commit against the dimensions above, ending in a clear objective recommendation with rationale and a migration-cost estimate if it recommends switching. Decide scope of any follow-up implementation beads when picked up.
payload.title: Research spike: lefthook vs pre-commit as the basicly hook runner

payload.text: [harness-policy] checkpoint=classify approved

Decision: KEEP pre-commit (see docs/hook-runner-decision.md). Decisive factor: every projected hook runs 'uv run python', so Python/uv are required regardless of runner - lefthook's static-binary advantage is nullified, and it would add a Go-binary acquisition seam with no uv-native path while not removing activation (already fixed in basicly-x5gh). No implementation follow-up bead: recommendation is status quo. Reconsider triggers recorded in the doc (consumers lose uv; checks go Python-free; measured speed complaint; provisioning seam regresses). The runner-agnostic seam in hooks.yaml is kept so reopening stays cheap.

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given the recorded dispatch history when the band ceiling is set then it is derived from measured lane outcomes with the derivation recorded and a gate fails naming the required value whenever a completed lane would have been refused by the configured ceiling
payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

```
uv run python -c "
from pathlib import Path
from basicly import run_record, br, config
root=Path('.'); s=config.load_sizing_config(root)
ex={str(r['id']):r for r in br.export_records(root)}
f={'task':3.0,'bug':2.0,'chore':1.5}
rows=[(e['scope_tokens'], b, ex.get(b,{}).get('issue_type','?'), ex.get(b,{}).get('status','?'), e.get('returncode'))
      for b,h in run_record.dispatch_history(root).items() for e in h
      if isinstance(e.get('scope_tokens'),int) and e['scope_tokens']>0]
print('lanes with recorded scope:', len(set((b,st) for st,b,_,_,_ in rows)))
print('would be refused today  :', len({(b,st) for st,b,t,_,_ in rows if st*f.get(t,3.0)>s.working_set_max}))
print('closed                  :', len({(b,st) for st,b,_,stat,_ in rows if stat=='closed'}))
"
```

Observed - 47 lanes carry a recorded scope cost, 46 of them closed and none failed, and 18 of them are above the ceiling the band enforces today. Expected - a ceiling that refuses work has at least one recorded instance of that work failing.

## Context

`working_set_max` is 64000. `config.py:392` states the intent: "the govern band is absolute tokens of material to reason over, NOT a fraction of the context window (the 50-70 percent folk rule was researched and refuted)". The refutation of the folk rule is sound. What never happened is validating the replacement constant against an outcome.

Measured over every dispatch that recorded its scope cost:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| lanes with a recorded scope cost | 47 |
| closed | 46 (the 47th is still open, none failed) |
| **refused by today's band** | **18** |
| true headless executions (returncode 0) | 7, all succeeded |
| largest scope on a headless success | **35,106** (`basicly-tcmy.31`) |
| band's effective ceiling for a task | **21,333** (64000 / 3.0) |

So the largest lane a headless agent has actually completed is **1.6x the largest lane the band will allow one to start**, and there is not one recorded failure attributable to scope size in either direction. The ceiling has a 0-for-18 record against the only evidence available.

Honest limit on that evidence: 40 of the 47 are `handoff` outcomes, where a driving agent or human did the work rather than a headless CLI, so they bound what a *session* can carry, not what a dispatched lane can. The 7 executed lanes are the clean sample and n=7 is small. This bead is therefore not "raise it to 152377"; it is "the constant is unvalidated, the only evidence contradicts it, and the engine must start recording what would settle it".

Second, deeper half. `scope_read_cost` is "tokenized size of the existing files matching the declared scope globs" - the WHOLE of every named file. The band compares that to a budget of "material to reason over". Those are the same quantity only when a change reads every line of every file it touches, and this repo's own `tool-usage` fragment forbids exactly that: "find files by name, localize with focused search, read only the ranges you need; don't bulk-load unrelated files". The harness sizes lanes by a cost its own instructions tell agents not to pay, so a one-line fix in a big module and a rewrite of it are indistinguishable to the gate.

This is the same defect shape as `basicly-z2wi`: a measure compared against a ceiling denominated in a different quantity. z2wi fixed the multiplier; this is the measure and the ceiling.

Consequence for the product: `architecture.md` alone is 32,519 tokens of scope, `cli.py` 91,839 and `supervise.py` 71,222, so any child naming one of them is refused whatever the change is. The engine cannot chunk work that touches its own largest files, which is the core capability basicly exists to provide.

## Split

This bead is now **only** the ceiling half. Narrowed 2026-08-02 after measuring: the
original four-file scope costs 39,986 tokens and the band refuses it at 79,972, so the
bead about the band could not be dispatched by the band. The measure half - that
`scope_read_cost` sizes whole files when a lane reads ranges - is a separate bead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the recorded dispatch history when the band ceiling is set then the value is derived from measured lane outcomes and the derivation is recorded rather than asserted
- Given a completed lane whose estimate exceeds the configured ceiling when the gate runs then it fails and names the value the evidence requires so the constant can never again refuse work that demonstrably succeeded
- Given the eight headless executions on this tree when the new ceiling is applied then none of them would be refused and the gate passes

## Scope

- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `tests/test_decompose.py`

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a declared verify check that the engine has run and passed when the exercised-or-unproven gate evaluates a release then that check counts as exercised and does not block the tag and given a declared check that nothing has ever run then the gate still refuses and names it and a test fails if a wrapper executable rather than the check itself is accepted as the witness
payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Measured 2026-08-05 on `main` @ `d31f6bd`, a clean tree, immediately after
`uv run basicly verify --mode full` reported **PASS, 16 checks — `vulture: PASS`**:

```
uv run python -c "
from pathlib import Path
from basicly import release
print(release.unexercised_capabilities(Path('.')))"
```

Observed — one refusal, for a check that had just run and passed in the same session:

```
unexercised capability: verify check 'vulture' - the usage ledger records no
execution of 'vulture'; exercise it or drop the claim before tagging
```

The per-capability read, over 17 declared checks against a ledger holding 544 keys:

| witness | count | capability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vulture` | **0** | verify check `vulture` |
| `uv` | 6091 | verify check `wired-or-deleted`, `docs-claims` |
| `ruff` | 711 | verify check `ruff`, `ruff-format` |
| `pytest` | 785 | verify check `pytest` |
| `basicly` | 2963 | the five `projection-*` checks |

Expected — a declared check that the engine ran, and that passed, counts as exercised.

## Consequence: v0.7.0 cannot be tagged

`release.blocking_reasons` extends with `unexercised_capabilities` (`release.py:382`),
and by that function's own docstring the reasons are checked **before anything is
written**. So `basicly release` refuses the cut, and no amount of re-running `verify`
changes the answer. This is a release blocker for `basicly-yc0x`, not a cleanup item.

## Cause: the witness is a typed shell command, not an execution

`shipped_capabilities` derives each witness as the check's own `command[0]`
(`release.py:252`). `recorded_executions` (`release.py:257`) reads two ledgers, and
neither one can see a check the engine ran:

- `usage.load_usage` reads `.basicly/usage/tool-usage.json`, written by the
  `tool-usage` hook (`.basicly/core/hooks/hooks.yaml:80`), which counts **pipeline
  heads of Bash commands an agent executed**. `vulture` is never typed at a shell —
  it exists only as a `[[verify.checks]]` entry — so its counter is never created.
- `tracker_usage.surface_executions` is the committed half and carries tracker
  surfaces, not verify checks.

`src/basicly/verify.py` records nothing: it has no reference to `usage` at all. So the
one component that actually executes a declared check is the one component that never
witnesses it. Every other check passes only because a human or an agent happened to
type its executable for unrelated reasons.

## The same defect makes the gate vacuous in the other direction

`wired-or-deleted` is declared as `uv run python .scripts/...`, so its witness is `uv`
with 6091 executions — a count that would stay healthy if the check were deleted
outright. `shipped_capabilities`' docstring already names this ("witnessed by the
*wrapper*, which is weaker evidence") and defers the fix to the declaration. It is not
a declaration problem: both facets are one cause, a witness that measures who typed a
word rather than whether the capability ran. A gate that is simultaneously
unsatisfiable for one check and unfalsifiable for another is measuring the wrong event.

## Fix shape

- **`verify` records an execution for each check it runs**, and `recorded_executions`
  reads that as a third ledger half. The engine running the check is the strongest
  available evidence that the capability works — it is the only evidence that the
  check *passed* rather than merely being invoked — and it makes the witness the
  check's `name`, which is unique per declaration, instead of `command[0]`, which is
  shared and wrapper-prone.
- **Do not satisfy this by typing `vulture` once at a shell.** That mints a false
  witness for a capability the gate cannot otherwise see, and leaves the next
  engine-only check blocked in exactly the same way. **Do not drop the claim either** —
  `vulture` is a live gate that `basicly-uexy` shipped deliberately.
- Keep the fail-closed stance on a missing ledger: that half is correct and
  `unexercised_capabilities`' docstring gives the reason.
- Regression test proven red first (`basicly-kjc5.49`): a declared check the engine has
  run is exercised; a declared check nothing has ever run still refuses the tag.

## Context

`basicly-uexy` (which declared `vulture`) and `basicly-irrm` (which built this gate)
shipped in the **same four-lane pass** on 2026-08-04. Neither lane could see that one
was declaring a capability the other's witness model cannot record. This is Phase S's
own shape one turn later — an instrument built and connected to the wrong signal — and
it is the fourth instance of the rule that a closed bead proves code exists, not that a
gate binds. Here the gate does bind; it binds on the wrong event, and it binds against
us.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/release.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `src/basicly/usage.py`
- `tests/test_release.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given recorded pipeline heads containing heredoc delimiters and language keywords when usage report runs then the tool table lists only resolvable command names and unparsed heads are counted to a named bucket and the counter file is not reset
payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

```
uv run basicly usage report | head -40
```

Observed 2026-08-04 - the terminal-tools table counts things that are not tools. Among the top
entries: `t` (123), `-` (121), `-d` (120), `def` (90), `assert` (83), `create` (70), `run` (65),
`from` (51), `p` (43), `PYEOF` (33), `return` (31), `EOF` (28). These are heredoc delimiters, Python
keywords and flag fragments picked up as pipeline heads. Expected - the table lists commands.

## Context

`usage report` exists to support a decision: the `session-finish` skill reads its **never-used**
list as the culling candidates for catalog skills. Pollution on the tools half undermines that in
both directions - it invents tools that were never run, and a real command parsed as a fragment is
undercounted or missed entirely, so a genuinely-unused tool can look used.

The skills half of the report is clean and its finding is sound and worth keeping: **8 skills used
ever, 27 never used**, including every `tool-*` skill. That is the same shape as
`basicly-irrm`'s inventory result (221 dispatch records hold only `claude` and `manual` while the
README advertises three agents), and it is real evidence for the culling `basicly-a3ab.1` and
`basicly-tcmy.21` carry.

This is the defect class `basicly-never-used-can-be-fabricated` names: in a usage audit the
never-used side is the only one a measurement bug can invent. So the *tools* half of this report may
not be cited as evidence until the parser is fixed; the *skills* half may.

## Fix shape

- Extract pipeline heads by parsing the command, not by splitting on whitespace: skip heredoc bodies
  and their delimiters, and skip anything that is not a resolvable command name.
- A recorded head that matches no known executable and no catalog entry is a parser miss - count it
  to a bucket the report names, rather than into the tool table as if it were real.
- Do **not** reset the counter file to clear the noise; it accumulates across sessions by design and
  the historical rows are the fixture for the fix.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/hooks/`
- `src/basicly/usage.py`
- `tests/test_usage.py`

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given three concurrent lanes that each record a changelog entry when the pass lands them then no lane hits a rebase conflict on any changelog path and basicly release assembles every fragment into the dated section in a deterministic order and removes them and a curated Unreleased body still publishes alongside them
payload.description:
## Context

Four unattended-run attempts on 2026-08-05/06 failed, and three of them on the same
shape: two lanes editing one anchor in a shared prose file.

| Attempt | Blocked on |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | `CHANGELOG.md` — three lanes at the same `### Fixed` anchor |
| 3 | `.basicly/generated-manifest.json` — fixed by `basicly-lyro` |
| 4 | `docs/design/tier-injection-kit.md` §7 Open — two lanes each removing their own entry |

`basicly-o8p0` and `basicly-lyro` each fixed one instance by declaring the path. That
approach cannot finish: nobody predicted a design document's Open list, and detection
will always trail the next unenumerated file.

## The fix

**One file per lane, assembled at release.** A lane writes `changelog.d/<bead-id>.md`
instead of editing `CHANGELOG.md`. The filename carries the bead id, so it is unique by
construction and two lanes cannot touch the same file — collision becomes impossible
rather than detected. `basicly release` assembles the fragments into the dated section
in a deterministic order and deletes them.

This is the established news-fragment pattern; the point here is not novelty but that it
removes the cause instead of reporting it.

## What it composes with, and what it costs

`basicly release` already promotes the `[Unreleased]` body into the dated section, so
assembly replaces that read rather than adding a step. The costs are real and accepted:
the landing convention changes for every lane, the release runbook changes, and
`[worktree] append_only_paths` loses its only entry — which is the point, not a
regression.

Keep `[Unreleased]` working for hand-written entries during the transition: a release
assembles fragments **and** any curated body, so an operator editing the changelog
directly is never broken.

## Acceptance evidence to produce

A supervised pass of three lanes that each add a changelog entry must land all three
with no rebase conflict on any changelog path — the direct inverse of attempt 1.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/release.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `basicly.toml`
- `tests/test_release.py`
- `.basicly/core/skills/harness-loop/skill.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/skills/release-process/skill.yaml`
payload.title: Give every lane its own changelog fragment so two lanes can never collide on one anchor

payload.text:
Doc check 2026-07-16 (VS Code 1.129, code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/agent-skills):
- Workspace roots scanned: .github/skills, .claude/skills, .agents/skills (user-level: ~/.copilot, ~/.claude, ~/.agents). Still NO documented dedup/precedence across roots. One secondary source claims .github/skills wins over .claude/skills on duplicates - unverified, and irrelevant here since we retired .github/skills; the pair that matters is .claude vs .agents.
- chat.agentSkillsLocations only ADDS locations; no documented setting to exclude a built-in root, so the copilot-side root-restriction option may not exist.
- 1.129 surfaces skills as slash commands and in a Configure Skills menu (/skills), plus the Agent Customizations editor (Chat: Open Customizations) - duplicates are now user-visible in three places.
- 1.129 also starts migrating prompt files (*.prompt.md) to skills (chat.customizations.promptMigration.enabled) with deprecation direction: validates the skills-first catalog design; basicly projects no prompt files, nothing to migrate.

Updated test procedure (basicly repo open in VS Code >= 1.129):
1. Copilot Chat: type / and look for conventional-commits - listed once or twice?
2. Run /skills (Configure Skills menu) - count entries per skill and note the source path shown for each.
3. Chat: Open Customizations - check the skills section the same way.
4. Context-level check: invoke one skill, expand the Used n references dropdown - did one or both SKILL.md paths load?
Record the VS Code + Copilot Chat versions with the result.

RESOLVED empirically 2026-07-16 by the user (VS Code 1.128.1, current Copilot Chat, WSL remote): Agent Customizations shows 27 of our skills - exactly 26 catalog skills (present byte-identically in BOTH .claude/skills and .agents/skills, 52 SKILL.md files on disk) plus the claude-only release-process skill. No duplicates listed, so VS Code dedups (or merges) same-named skills across roots. Keeping both roots stands: Claude Code reads only .claude/skills, Codex only .agents/skills, and Copilot presents one entry. No basicly-side change needed.

Bonus finding: the VS Code agent harness also consumes .claude/settings.json - our protect-generated PreToolUse hook and the user-level settings both appear under Hooks in Agent Customizations, so the 84v.3 tool-time guard gates Copilot's agent too, not just Claude Code.

- Existing violations in hand-authored markdown are fixed (docs/architecture.md MD060/MD049 auto-fix; the line-714 accidental "+"-list unwrap).
