payload.acceptance_criteria: Given the test suite running concurrently with other br activity on the same machine when the pytest gate runs then no test fails on the machine-global beads write lock or such a failure is recognised by signature and does not consume a rework attempt and the cause is recorded as a requirement on the replacement tracker
payload.description:
## Context

Two transient gate failures in one session (2026-07-30), both from the same cause, both passing on
a plain re-run with no code change:

1. The `basicly-imnu.12` landing merged the worktree and then failed `verify` on `pytest`, recording
   rework 1/2. Re-ran the suite twice by hand - serially and with `-n 4`, the form the gate uses -
   and got **1557 passed both times**. Recovered with `basicly verify --mode full --issue` from
   base, which re-recorded the gate green.
2. `git push origin main` was rejected by the `pre-push` hook. The identical command succeeded on
   the immediate retry with `pre-push-script ... Passed`.

`basicly.toml` already documents the mechanism on the `pytest` check: every `br init` takes a
**machine-global** write lock at `~/.beads/.write.lock` with a 30s timeout, so xdist worker count is
contention on one lock rather than parallelism, and `basicly-9s59` capped workers at 4 for exactly
this reason. Two failures in one session says the cap reduced the rate without removing the cause -
which is expected, because the lock is global to the machine and this session was also running `br`
commands continuously outside pytest (tracker commits, gate records, comment writes). The
contention is not just between workers; it is between the suite and whatever else is driving the
harness.

Why this matters more than an occasional retry: a transient failure inside a *landing* is not free.
It consumes a rework attempt against a cap of 2, and `basicly-55yh`'s re-run test only forgives a
failure that does not reproduce - so a second unlucky landing on the same node escalates to a human
for a defect that does not exist. That is the same class of waste `basicly-kjc5.56` addressed for the
clock defect, and the same argument applies: a gate that fails for reasons the work did not cause
corrupts the merit signal.

This is also a **requirement on the replacement tracker**, and belongs alongside the six already in
`docs/design/work-tracker.md` §2.1: a machine-global write lock is a scaling defect we inherited, and
an in-process store with a per-repo writer would not have it. Consider whether it becomes R7.

Options to weigh, not a chosen design:

- Serialise the tests that call `br init` into one xdist group (`--dist loadgroup`) rather than
  capping global worker count, so the rest of the suite keeps its parallelism.
- Give the test fixtures a private `BEADS_DIR`/`HOME` per worker so they never touch the global lock.
  This is the fix that removes the cause rather than reducing its rate, if br honours it.
- Widen the `pre-push`/landing retry: distinguish a lock timeout from a real failure by signature and
  do not charge rework for it - the register in `verify.py` already exists for exactly this shape.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Drive a harness loop landing while other `br` commands run against the same machine.
2. Observed: the landing's `pytest` gate fails, rework increments, and the suite passes on a manual
   re-run with no change. Same for a `pre-push` rejection that succeeds on retry.
3. Expected: a lock-contention timeout is either prevented, or recognised and not charged as a
   merit failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the test suite running concurrently with other br activity on the same machine when the pytest gate runs then no test fails on the machine-global beads write lock, or such a failure is recognised by signature and does not consume a rework attempt, and the cause is recorded as a requirement on the replacement tracker

## Scope

- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`
- `docs/design/work-tracker.md`

The signature register `verify.py` already carries for this shape is the intended home; the
work-tracker document is in scope only to record the cause as a requirement on the replacement
(the R7 question the body raises). The two other options the body lists - xdist grouping and a
private `BEADS_DIR` per worker - are **out** of this bead: they change the cause rather than the
accounting, and the root fix is the v0.8.0 flip.
payload.title: Stop the machine-global beads write lock making gates flaky and burning rework

payload.text:
[harness-info] Attempted reproduction 2026-08-01 on br 0.2.16, 32-core WSL2. The documented failure does NOT reproduce. Recording this as a measurement, not a closure: the incidents on 2026-07-30 were real, and this says the cause is gone on the current br, not that it never existed.

Probes, in order:

1. `~/.beads/` does not exist on this machine at all, and a `br init` run under a private HOME created no lock file anywhere under it. Suggestive only - a transient lock would already be released by the time the directory is listed - so it was not treated as an answer.

2. Positive control, the config's own stated stampede: `pytest -q -n auto` (32 workers, against the "13-core workstation" the basicly.toml comment describes). Result: 2119 passed in 17.54s, zero occurrences of "write lock", "Timed out after", or lock_timeout in the output. The suite's own integration fixtures call `br init`, so this is already 32-way concurrent br init contention.

3. The bead's actual scenario, which probe 2 does not cover - the suite running concurrently with other br activity on the same machine. A background driver ran 1297 iterations of `br init` (fresh git repo + temp dir each) interleaved with `br show` against the real tracker, for the whole duration of `pytest -q -n auto`. Result: 2119 passed in 19.28s, zero lock failures, 1297 churn iterations completed.

Two consequences.

First, AC clause 1 ("no test fails on the machine-global beads write lock") currently holds by measurement under deliberately hostile conditions. Clause 2 ("the cause is recorded as a requirement on the replacement tracker") is still owed, and basicly-vkh0.6 is the natural home - the requirement is worth carrying even though the defect no longer reproduces, since the point of vkh0.6 is to not re-inherit defects we already paid for. This bead stays open on clause 2.

Second, and actionable now: basicly.toml pins `pytest -n 4` and justifies it with "every br init takes a machine-global write lock ... `auto` stampedes it and the integration fixtures die". That justification is stale on br 0.2.16. Measured cost of the stale cap: `-n 4` takes 28.26s / 46.28s across two runs this session; `-n auto` takes 17.54s / 19.28s. The comment's own release condition is "Raise only if br stops serialising globally", which these probes indicate is met. Every lane's verify gate pays this, so it also affects factory wall-clock.

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given the projected catalog when the routing eval runs in CI then a positive prompt ranks its owner in the top-k and a negative prompt owner outranks the entry under test and no description pair exceeds 75 percent pairwise similarity with a warning at 50 and the rank-1 rate is reported against a floor that the gate refuses to lower
payload.description:
## Context

Plan §4 Phase 2 item 2b. Depends on 2a. Architecture §14.4 calls the routing tier the highest-value single deliverable and the thing nobody else in the field has.

Stemmed TF-IDF over descriptions, pure Python, no new dependency. Verified absent 2026-07-26 at c175c1a - no tf-idf, tfidf, stemmer or porter anywhere in src/.

Three assertions:
- a positive prompt ranks its owner in the top-k;
- a negative prompt declares an owner and the assertion is that the owner outranks this entry - a bare "must not rank first" passes vacuously when the prompt matches nothing;
- no two descriptions exceed a pairwise similarity ceiling - error at 75 percent, warn at 50.

The CI metric is rank-1 rate, with the floor set below a measured baseline, raised as routing improves, and never lowered to make a regression pass - lowering it is deleting the test while looking like maintenance. The floor value is plan §7.5, an owner decision after the baseline is measured, and is deliberately not guessable.

Refuse embeddings: they would make this semantic and therefore non-deterministic, network-dependent and unownable. Semantics are the Tier 3 job.


## Scope

- `src/basicly/catalog_lint.py`
- `src/basicly/catalog.py`
- `tests/test_catalog_lint.py`
payload.title: Gate catalog routing with stemmed tf-idf rank-1 evals

payload.text: [harness-info] Design input from the 2026-07-30 oh-my-agent analysis (reference-repos/_analysis/oh-my-agent.md). oma skills audit is a dependency-free TF-IDF/cosine analysis over skill DESCRIPTIONS that flags near-duplicate pairs, black-hole skills whose mean similarity to the whole library is a statistical outlier, and sprawl by reference-doc count (cli/commands/skills/audit.ts:9-36; cli/utils/text-similarity.ts:105-129). Relevant because our routing rests entirely on 33 descriptions and we currently have NO cross-skill check of any kind - every catalog lint skill rule inspects one file in isolation (src/basicly/catalog_lint.py:219-292). So this bead's rank-1 eval should be paired with a pairwise-similarity check: a rank-1 failure tells you routing missed, while a near-duplicate pair tells you WHY, and the second is cheaper to compute than the first.

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given the catalog entry set derived at build time when an entry has no colocated eval case file then the catalog gate fails as a tier-1 failure and catalog new scaffolds the case file so coverage can only grow by adding entries to the enforced set and never by lowering a threshold
payload.description:
## Context

Plan §4 Phase 2 item 2c. Depends on 2b.

An eval case file per entry, colocated with the catalog source so a reviewer sees the entry and its evidence in one diff, enforced as a Tier-1 failure from the start.

Surface measured 2026-07-26 at c175c1a: 19 fragments (16 core plus 3 overlay) and 28 projected skills = 47 projected entries, from 32 skill sources. Derive the enforced set at build time rather than hard-coding the plan §2 figure of 48, or the gate goes stale the first time an entry is added.

Stage it rather than attempting one pass, and scaffold from catalog new. Plan §8 names the failure mode: coverage stalls partway and the gate is quietly relaxed. Stage by adding entries to the enforced set, never by lowering a threshold.

Accept the consequence deliberately: this raises the cost of adding a catalog entry, which is the intended brake on accretion.
payload.title: Require an eval case file per catalog entry as a tier-1 failure

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a judged verdict with no severity of BLOCKER or IMPORTANT or MINOR when it is recorded then it is rejected as a schema violation rather than complained about and given an assembled reviewer bundle containing a finding-suppressing directive then the engine refuses to emit it
payload.description:
## Context

Plan §4 Phase 2 item 2d. Gates Phase 5.

Two deterministic checks, both currently absent - verified 2026-07-26 at c175c1a, severity appears nowhere in src/.

Severity as a required field on judged output - BLOCKER, IMPORTANT, MINOR - rejected as a schema violation rather than complained about. A judged verdict with no severity cannot pass a required gate.

Plus the no-pre-judging lint. Because dispatch prompts are assembled by code, the engine can refuse to emit a reviewer bundle containing a finding-suppressing directive. A rule an observer can mechanically check beats ten rules of good intent.

Note the plan lists a D4 prerequisite here. It is already satisfied: factory-design.md §D4 carries the 2026-07-25 amendment and loop.py implements it, so build against the shipped shape.


## Scope

- `src/basicly/rubrics.py`
- `src/basicly/review.py`
- `tests/test_rubrics.py`
- `tests/test_review.py`
payload.title: Require a severity on judged output and refuse a pre-judging reviewer bundle

payload.text:
[harness-info] Owner decision, 2026-07-26. Gated on basicly-imnu.1 (the D4 amendment) by explicit ruling.

Plan section 4 Phase 2 states the prerequisite - build 2d and 2e against the amended shape, not the current one - but the decomposition wired imnu.1 to m4zv.6 only, leaving this bead unblocked. Ruled: imnu.1 lands first.

Why it matters here specifically. Severity is BLOCKER, IMPORTANT, MINOR on judged output, and what a BLOCKER *does* is exactly what D4 defines: whether the judged half of validate fails the lane or enqueues a decision. Building severity against the un-amended shape risks making a judged verdict fail a required gate directly, which contradicts the invariant that no persona passes or fails a required gate.

m4zv.5 was deliberately left unblocked - comparing open-finding sets between iterations does not depend on the composite gate shape.

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given consecutive rework iterations when the open-finding set is unchanged once then the bead is warned and when it is unchanged twice consecutively then the node escalates immediately without consuming the remaining cap and when the set grows then it escalates on first occurrence with tests
payload.description:
## Context

Plan §4 Phase 2 item 2e first half. Gates Phase 5.

Compare the open-finding set between consecutive iterations, not the count - a round that fixes one finding and introduces one is not progress. Verified 2026-07-26 at c175c1a: policy.py has no convergence check at all. runner.StallWatchdog exists but is dispatch-level (no file activity for n seconds), a different mechanism entirely.

Re-verified 2026-08-06 at d58e8e2: `policy.py` still has no convergence check. `record_rework`
writes a bare `[harness-policy] rework gate=<gate>` marker carrying no signature, so nothing
anywhere can compare one iteration against the previous one.

Escalation shape:
- one stalled round warns on the bead;
- two consecutive stalled rounds escalate immediately without consuming the remaining cap;
- a diverging round escalates on first occurrence.

Coupling to Phase 0. This rewrites the same rework accounting that 4tjt (clear the counter on an answered retry) and 55yh (do not charge an infrastructure failure) change. Both must land first or the three will collide in policy.py. Both are closed.

## What basicly-bdd4 already covers, and what is left

`basicly-bdd4` landed at d58e8e2 and implemented the **merge** gate's half of this, because
its own acceptance criterion required it: `supervise.conflict_signature` reduces a landing to
`(status, sorted conflicting paths)`, a `[harness-conflict]` marker carries it across passes,
and `_escalate_repeat_bounce` escalates and refunds through
`policy.grant_rework_allowance`.

So do **not** rebuild that. Two things are left.

**1. The general check, for the gates that report findings rather than paths.** A verify gate
reports `verify.VerifyReport.failures`; a rubric gate reports its failed rubric names. Neither
is covered today, and `loop._rework` (loop.py:1435) is the single funnel every one of them
passes through - the merge gate included (loop.py:1111 passes `landing=`). That is the seam.

**2. One mechanism, not two.** bdd4's signature history is `supervise`-local and
merge-specific. Lift the *storage and comparison* into `policy.py` next to the rework counter
that already owns this accounting - a per-`(bead, gate)` signature history plus a verdict -
and have the merge path delegate to it. `_marker_matches` (policy.py:395) already accepts the
marker plus a space-separated suffix, which is how `record_unreliable_gate` carries its
detail, so a signature rides on a marker without disturbing `rework_attempts` or
`rework_charged`.

**The thresholds stay different per gate, deliberately.** bdd4 escalates on the *first*
repeat because re-applying one branch to one anchor is provably non-converging - there is
nothing a second attempt could do differently. A repeated *finding set* is only probably
stalled, since an agent may have changed something the gate does not report, so it warns
first and escalates on the second. Keep both: the verdict is shared, the threshold is the
caller's.

## Divergence needs set semantics, so do not store a digest

"The set grows" cannot be read off a hash. Store the signature as its canonical sorted
member list so the previous set can be recovered and compared:

- previous == current -> stalled
- current is a strict superset of previous -> diverging
- anything else -> progressing

Bound the stored length; the design's 16 KiB event cap is derived, not measured, so keep the
record small rather than treating that number as a constant.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Take a bead whose verify gate fails on a fixed set of checks.
2. Run the rework loop twice without changing what the gate reports.
3. Observe that the second attempt is charged in full and nothing anywhere compares its
   finding set against the first. At `max_rework=2` the node escalates having spent its whole
   budget re-deriving a verdict attempt 1 already reported verbatim.

Observed for the merge gate on 2026-08-05 (see this bead's comment); the finding-set gates
have the same gap and no coverage at all.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `tests/test_policy.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`
payload.title: Detect a non-converging rework loop from the open-finding set

payload.text:
First observed instance, 2026-08-05, on the basicly-u6jq.1 proof run. This bead's own framing notes the rework subsystem had never fired - 286 gate results, 0 failed. It has now fired, and it burned the cap on a condition that could not converge.

  routed:  basicly-3ymj -> bounced - merge failed: rebase of harness/basicly-3ymj onto
           main hit conflicts in: CHANGELOG.md (rework 1/2)
  routed:  basicly-3ymj -> decision - merge failed: rebase of harness/basicly-3ymj onto
           main hit conflicts in: CHANGELOG.md (rework 2/2)

Both attempts failed on the **same file with the same cause**, and nothing between them could have changed the outcome: the conflict is between the lane's changelog entry and two sibling entries already on main, so re-attempting the identical rebase re-derives the identical conflict. Attempt 2 was spent to learn what attempt 1 already reported verbatim.

This is precisely the bead's stated rule ('compare the open-finding set between iterations, not the count; one stalled round warns, two consecutive escalate immediately without consuming the cap'), and the evidence sharpens it in two ways:

1. **The comparable unit here is not a finding set but a failure signature.** A merge bounce carries a cause and a file list, not findings. So the convergence check needs to key on whatever the gate reported - for merge that is (cause, conflicting paths) - or it will not cover the gate that actually fired first. A finding-set-only implementation would have missed this instance entirely.
2. **A byte-identical repeat is the cheapest possible detection**, and it is available before any judgement: if attempt N's failure signature equals attempt N-1's, the round is stalled by definition. That case needs no rubric and no model, which matters because this subsystem is meant to be a free deterministic gate.

Cost of the gap on this run: one rework attempt, and the pass ended with a human decision pending - which is what made basicly-u6jq.1 fail its zero-intervention criterion. The root cause of the conflict is filed separately as basicly-o8p0 (a convention-shared path no bead declares); this comment is only about the cap being spent on a non-converging retry.

payload.description:
## Context

Plan §4 Phase 2 item 2e second half, split out from the convergence detector because it touches every gate call site, gates nothing downstream on its own, and is the piece the D4 composite-gate typing feeds.

Classify every existing gate into the four types - pre-flight, revision, escalation, abort - so "what happens when this fails" is answered by the type rather than per call site.

Then enforce the rule that a pre-flight gate writes nothing. The plan records why this earns its own enforcement: our two worst recorded incidents were both checks that recorded state where they should have blocked entry. See the loop-verify-gate-strands-merge and loop-ship-approve-wedges-phase histories.

Depends on the Phase 3 bead that records validate as a composite of a pre-flight and an escalation component, since that is the first gate to be typed and its typing sets the pattern.


## Scope

- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `tests/test_policy.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a user-invoked skill when it is projected then no generated-marker text occupies the advertised description slot and drift detection still reports a hand-edited projection and the byte-for-byte frontmatter of a model-invoked entry is unchanged and the design doc records the re-measured saving rather than the superseded 430 char figure
payload.description:
## Problem

Found immediately after basicly-m4zv.1 landed, by observing the effect in a live session rather than in a test.

basicly-m4zv.1 makes a user-invoked entry project no `description:` line. The intent is that the entry stops paying context load for reach it does not have. But the host does not simply omit a description - it falls back to the **first body line**, and our first body line is the generated-drift marker. So the three projected user-invoked skills are now advertised as:

    tool-bat: <!-- Generated by `basicly skills-build` from skill.yaml. Do not edit; edit the source. -->

Observed directly: the available-skills list in a session rooted at this repo showed exactly that for tool-bat, tool-fzf and tool-git-delta.

Two consequences.

The saving is about a third of what was claimed. The marker is 91 chars and is emitted per entry, so removing 430 chars of descriptions bought back 3 x 91 = 273, for a net 157 chars rather than 430. catalog-efficacy-design section 3-5 records 430 and about 107 tokens and is therefore wrong; correcting it is part of this bead.

The advertised string is now useless rather than merely cheaper. A description at least told the agent when to route; the marker tells it nothing while still costing tokens. That is a worse trade per character than what it replaced.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Project a user-invoked skill (`basicly skills-build --all-default-roots`).
2. Read `.claude/skills/tool-bat/SKILL.md` - frontmatter is name only, then the marker line.
3. Open a session rooted at the repo and inspect the advertised skill list.

Observed: the marker text occupies the description slot.
Expected: a user-invoked entry advertises no description text at all, or at worst its own short heading.

## Notes

The obvious fix is to move the marker for a user-invoked entry so it is not the first line after the frontmatter - a YAML comment inside the frontmatter block is one option and keeps the drift marker present. Whatever is chosen must keep `check_synced_skills` drift detection working and must not change the byte-for-byte fidelity contract for model-invoked entries, which the existing test asserts.

Re-measure after the fix and correct the figure in the design doc rather than restating the old one.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/skills.py`
- `tests/test_skills.py`
- `docs/design/catalog-efficacy-design.md`

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given the Tier-3 isolation requirements when they are read then they forbid naming the entity under test in an elicitation prompt and given the catalog-authoring skill when it is read then it requires verifying a guidance change against what the agent is actually told rather than the projected file naming the description fallback as the concrete case
payload.description:
## Context

Retro findings from the 2026-07-26 session, approved by the owner. Both are about measurement discipline and both come from real incidents in that session, not from general caution.

### A. An elicitation prompt must not name the entity under test

While probing whether a description-less skill still loads, the prompt said "if a skill named probe-hidden is available to you, include it". The skill appeared - which proved nothing, because the prompt had supplied the answer. Caught and re-run neutrally; the result happened to hold, but the first run was worthless and read as a confirmation.

`catalog-efficacy-design.md` §4.3 already enumerates isolation requirements for Tier-3 arms and exists for exactly this class of bug (the ponytail SessionStart contamination). Add the rule to that requirements list.

### B. Verify what the agent is told, not the file you edited

basicly-m4zv.1 measured "430 chars of descriptions removed" from the source, wrote that figure into `catalog-efficacy-design.md` §3.5, and committed. The delivered saving was 157 chars, because the host fills an absent skill `description` from the first body line - which is our generated drift marker. The error surfaced only when the change appeared in the authoring sessions own skill list, by accident, after the commit. Tracked as basicly-m4zv.7.

The `quality-gate` fragment already says to exercise the change as it will really be used and read the output. The gap is narrower than that: for a guidance change the projected file is not the delivered artifact, because the host may substitute or fall back.

Put this on the `catalog-authoring` skill rather than the always-on baseline. It fires exactly when catalog sources are edited, which is when it applies, and it costs no always-on context - the recall measurement under basicly-agzx.1 removed the argument that the baseline is too dense to attend to, but not the argument that every always-on word is billed per turn to every consumer.

## Notes

Per the ceremony threshold the owner chose this session (by touched path), finding B touches `.basicly/**` so this goes through the loop; finding A alone would have qualified for the lightweight path.

## Scope

- `docs/design/catalog-efficacy-design.md`
- `.basicly/core/skills/catalog-authoring/skill.yaml`

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given the owner has ruled on whether invocation defaults to model for a consumer when the decision is recorded then the schema and lint match the ruling and a consumer catalog with no invocation field either upgrades clean with a warning or is documented as a required migration in the changelog before the next tag
payload.description:
## Context

Raised 2026-07-26 while assessing release readiness. Not yet decided.

basicly-m4zv.1 made `invocation` a **required** field on every skill source. Verified by building a throwaway consumer catalog with one hand-authored skill and running the lint:

    .basicly/core/skills/mine/skill.yaml: invocation is a required property

So every consumer who authors their own skills gets a red `catalog lint` on upgrade, with no migration command and nothing explaining why. At 0.x that makes the next release a minor bump rather than a patch, and it puts a migration burden on every install.

## The question

Should an absent `invocation` default to `model` and emit a projection warning, instead of failing the lint?

Arguments for defaulting:
- The breaking change disappears. Consumers upgrade clean; our own catalog still declares the axis explicitly on every entry, so nothing is lost here.
- `model` is the safe default and the same one the scaffold uses, for the same reason: over-declaring `model` only wastes a description, while over-declaring `user` silently removes an entry from the agent reach.
- For a distribution whose value is being installed by other repos, a hard lint failure on upgrade is a bad trade for a field the consumer has never heard of.
- The lint can harden to required in a later version once consumers have had a release to adopt it.

Arguments for keeping it required:
- A warning that nobody reads is how an unmeasured entry keeps paying context load forever, which is the exact waste the axis was introduced to find. A default means most consumer entries stay `model` by inertia.
- The plan calls 2a an immediate win; a default makes the win opt-in rather than forced.
- basicly-m4zv-2 (Tier-2 routing evals) is built on the axis being reliably declared, and a defaulted field is weaker evidence than a declared one.

## Also part of release prep, and not yet done

Nothing has audited the other commits since v0-5-1 for consumer-breaking changes. The invocation axis was found only because it was built this session; 488 commits have landed since the tag and a release must check them properly rather than assume this was the only one.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/schemas/skill.schema.json`
- `src/basicly/skills.py`
- `src/basicly/catalog_lint.py`

payload.text:
OWNER RULING 2026-07-27: keep invocation REQUIRED. No default, no deprecation window. Document it as a breaking change in the release changelog and ship it.

Rationale (owner): there are no or very few consumers today, so the goodwill cost of a hard break is near zero now and rises with every release. Better to fix a critical thing at the start of implementation than to carry backwards compatibility forward. This rejects options A (default to model), C (migration command) and D (default now harden later).

Consequences accepted:
- Every consumer with a hand-authored skill gets a red catalog lint on upgrade. The break is total, not partial: the field is schema-required and skills.py hard-errors on it.
- v0.6.0 release notes must carry a Migration section. That is now a release blocker, not a nicety.
- No basicly catalog migrate command will be built.

Work this ruling implies, verified by probe rather than assumed:
1. The missing-field message is a raw jsonschema string - '.basicly/core/skills/mine/skill.yaml: invocation is a required property' - reproduced 2026-07-27 against a throwaway consumer catalog holding one pre-m4zv.1 skill plus the projected schemas. It names neither the two valid values nor the pairing rule. bc3add9's commit message claims the lint says what to do, but that is true only of _check_invocation_axis, which a missing field never reaches. If the break stays, this message must be actionable.
2. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] needs the breaking entry with the one-line fix a consumer applies.

Also recorded: because bc3add9 REPLACED description with invocation in the schema required list, every catalog valid on v0.5.1 already carries a description on every skill. That fact was the strongest argument for defaulting and is now moot, but it stays useful for the migration note: adding 'invocation: model' is sufficient for any previously-valid source, with no second edit needed.

Unchanged by this ruling: m4zv.7 remains a release prerequisite. Declaring 'user' today projects the generated drift marker into the description slot, so the axis cannot be advertised to consumers until that is fixed.

payload.description:
Deterministic, token-free usage telemetry: count which terminal tools (rg, fd, bat, jq, yq, uv, ...) the agent actually invokes, so idle skills/tools can be culled from the catalog with real data. Requested 2026-07-16; design delegated and settled below after researching both platforms.

## Design
- New catalog hook script .basicly/core/hooks/tool-usage.py (stdlib only, never blocks: every path ends exit 0). Reads the hook JSON from stdin, accepts BOTH shapes: Claude Code PostToolUse (tool_name == Bash, tool_input.command) and Copilot postToolUse (toolName/tool_name in {bash, Bash, shell}, toolArgs/tool_input command field). Splits the command string on shell operators (pipes, &&, ||, ;, newlines), takes each segment head token, skips env assignments and shell builtins (cd, echo, exit, ...), normalizes to basename.
- Persistence: .basicly/usage/tool-usage.json mapping tool -> {count, last_used date}; atomic replace (tmp + os.replace), tolerant of a missing/corrupt file (restart from empty). The hook writes .basicly/usage/.gitignore containing '*' on first run (self-ignoring dir, like .beads) so the data survives sessions but never enters git. Per-repo-folder by design (worktrees accumulate their own).
- Claude wiring: hooks.yaml entry (id tool-usage, manager claude, stage posttooluse, matcher Bash). claude_settings.py currently hardcodes PreToolUse + the Edit|Write matcher — generalize: derive the settings event from the spec stage (pretooluse -> PreToolUse, posttooluse -> PostToolUse) and add an optional matcher field to hooks.yaml (default stays the current write-tools matcher).
- Copilot wiring: hooks live in .github/hooks/*.json ({"version": 1, "hooks": {"postToolUse": [{type command, bash/powershell/command keys, optional matcher}]}}). Add manager 'copilot' to HOOK_MANAGERS with a projection to .github/hooks/basicly-tool-usage.json (bash + powershell keys both run the same python script via uv), wired into hooks-build/hooks-check/uninstall like the claude manager.
- Dogfood: the hook ships in this repo's own projections (hooks-build here).

## Non-functional
- Zero tokens: pure python, no model calls. Resilient: never fails the tool call (async-safe, exit 0 always), atomic writes, corrupt-file recovery. Survives sessions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Piping a recorded Claude PostToolUse Bash JSON into the script increments counts for each pipeline segment head (e.g. 'rg foo | jq .x' -> rg+1, jq+1) and writes the self-ignoring .gitignore
- The Copilot stdin shape is parsed by the same script (unit test with both payload shapes)
- A corrupt or missing usage file never fails the hook (exit 0) and the next write starts clean
- hooks-build projects the Claude PostToolUse group into .claude/settings.json and the Copilot hook file into .github/hooks/, both idempotent; hooks-check flags drift; uninstall removes both
- Existing pretooluse protect-generated behavior is unchanged (matcher default preserved)
- Dogfooded: this repo's projections carry the hook after hooks-build; git status stays clean after a counted command runs
- Regression tests cover parsing, counting, atomicity fallback, both stdin shapes, and both projections

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a committed non-manual runner default when an operator drives basicly loop run or basicly loop advance interactively then a documented per-invocation override restores the manual handoff without editing any committed or gitignored config
payload.description:
## Problem

`--runner` and `--autonomy` exist only on `basicly loop supervise`. `basicly loop run` and
`basicly loop advance` accept neither, so the runner cannot be chosen per invocation on the
single-track path — the committed `[runner] default` is the only answer available to it.

That forces one committed key to serve two incompatible modes. Autonomous mode wants a real
headless agent so a supervised pass dispatches at all. Interactive mode wants the `manual`
handoff, because the driving agent is already in the worktree and a build-phase dispatch
re-implements the node in a second process. There is no per-invocation escape on the
interactive path, so the only way to hold both is a gitignored `basicly.local.toml` override —
which is precisely what this repo does today, and why the committed default reads `manual` with
a comment explaining that autonomous dispatch would double-run the loop.

The consequence is that the committed default cannot express the product's intent. A repo that
wants supervised runs must either commit a default that sabotages its own interactive sessions,
or keep the real default in an uncommitted file no consumer inherits.

## Steps to Reproduce

```sh
uv run basicly loop supervise --help   # shows --runner and --autonomy
uv run basicly loop run --help         # shows neither
uv run basicly loop advance --help     # shows neither
```

Observed - `_apply_session_overrides` in `src/basicly/cli.py` is called only from
`_cmd_loop_supervise`; `loop run` and `loop advance` have no equivalent, so both read
`[runner] default` through `load_runner_config` with no override seam. With
`[runner] default = "claude"` committed, an interactive `basicly loop run <id>` at build phase
dispatches a headless agent and there is no flag that restores the handoff.

Expected - the runner and autonomy overrides are available on every path that can dispatch, so
a committed default that suits supervised runs does not have to be countermanded by an
uncommitted file to keep interactive driving usable.

## Scope

- src/basicly/cli.py
- tests/test_cli.py

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a committed non-manual `[runner] default` when an operator drives `basicly loop run` or
  `basicly loop advance` interactively then a documented per-invocation override restores the
  manual handoff without editing any committed or gitignored config
payload.title: Only loop supervise can override the runner so one committed default must serve two incompatible modes

payload.description:
Team-rollout hardening for basicly-c9e5: the harness loop now depends on br honoring .beads/redirect - the first br CAPABILITY dependency (not just presence). An older br silently ignores the redirect, auto-imports the worktree's checked-out issues.jsonl into a fresh local DB, and runs a divergent tracker (lost gates/claims) with no error. Add a behavior probe to worktree provisioning: after writing the redirect (moved early, before the slow dep install), run br where --json from the worktree; if br runs successfully but resolves a path other than the base .beads, abort provisioning with guidance (br upgrade, floor br 0.2.16 known good, cleanup command). A missing br or a non-workspace .beads skips the probe - br-less repos remain a supported state. Document the br floor in architecture 12.6.1.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Provisioning fails with a clear upgrade message when br resolves the worktree .beads instead of following the redirect (test), skips the probe when br is absent or errors (test), and passes silently on a redirect-capable br (existing tests). The redirect+probe step runs before dependency provisioning so the failure is fast. architecture.md names the br redirect capability as a loop requirement with 0.2.16 as the known-good floor. Full gate suite passes.
payload.title: Probe br redirect capability at worktree provisioning

payload.description:
Retro from basicly-45ld: recording the verify gate out-of-band (basicly verify --issue / br gate report) makes derive_phase jump past the build->verify landing (loop._on_build -> _verify_and_land), which is the only step that merges the worktree. The loop then shipped+closed the bead with the feature commit stranded on the harness branch, unmerged. Two complementary fixes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Engine guard: loop._on_ship refuses to close/teardown a leaf whose bound worktree branch is not merged into its base (branch tip not an ancestor of base HEAD); it blocks with a clear reason naming the branch and base instead of closing. A branch that no longer exists (already merged + cleaned) is treated as merged. The guard runs before worktree.cleanup and before br close.
- Deterministic and side-effect-free on the block path: no close, no teardown, no tracker commit when the guard trips.
- Regression tests: a bound-but-unmerged worktree blocks at ship (issue stays open, not closed); a merged worktree ships normally; a missing branch ships normally.
- Skill doc: the harness-loop skill warns never to record the verify gate by hand during an active leaf build because the build->verify advance is the only step that merges the worktree; let loop advance record it. Projected SKILL.md regenerated.
- pytest, ruff, and the projection checks (skills-check) stay green.

## Scope

loop._on_ship guard + a small reachability helper + tests; harness-loop skill.yaml note + skills-build. No change to merge.py, no new gate mechanism.

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given the working set band when its maximum is resolved for a pass then it is bounded by the resolved runners trigger divided by an ambient ratio sourced from recorded context_tokens at a high quantile with its sample count recorded and a configured maximum above the resolved trigger fails a check and a lane can no longer move the bound by rewriting its own scope declaration
payload.description:
## Context

Second-order half of basicly-23ep, split out so the window fix does not carry it. **Blocked on
basicly-23ep**: calibrating a band against a finalize trigger that is itself wrong by 5x fits the
error rather than removing it.

`decompose.py:792` states the relationship: the band compares against `working_set_max`, **a
context-window ceiling**. So `DEFAULT_WORKING_SET_MAX` and `supervise.ceiling_tokens` are the same
quantity and must not disagree. Two problems survive the window fix.

**1. The band gates on a proxy measured 3.16x to 7.21x low.** The band does not gate on occupancy; it
gates on `seed x scope_read_cost`. Seven paired records:

| lane | forecast_tokens | context_tokens | ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| basicly-vkh0.10 | 26780 | 193096 | 7.21 |
| basicly-jr0l.64 | 34780 | 170530 | 4.90 |
| basicly-8ry8 | 18780 | 80211 | 4.27 |
| basicly-tcmy.6 | 50780 | 190177 | 3.75 |
| basicly-tcmy.22 | 49716 | 171029 | 3.44 |
| basicly-tcmy.5 | 66780 | 223221 | 3.34 |
| basicly-gczc | 66780 | 210721 | 3.16 |

A lane admitted at the band maximum of 132000 therefore lands near 495000 at the median ratio and
near 950000 at the worst - inside a corrected 600000 trigger at the median, over it at the tail.

**2. The maximum was derived from its own estimator's output.** `config.py:455-466` records that
132000 was licensed by one lane completing at that declared size, and
`run_record.py:164-171` records why that could not be checked at the time: **no field measured the
quantity the band is denominated in**, so the value was derived twice (basicly-3w44,
basicly-ipx2) by re-reading the tree and re-applying the formula to itself. `context_tokens` now
exists and carries the seven samples above, so the derivation can be replaced by a measurement for
the first time. This also subsumes **basicly-qorx's ratchet half**: once the bound stops being a
function of the largest completed self-declared scope, a lane can no longer move a global constant by
editing its own bead.

## Fix shape

**Do not hand-derive a new constant and do not fit a calibration on the proxy alone** - that is how
basicly-z2wi reached 216.65 against a seed of 3.0.

- Bound the admitted band by the resolved runner's trigger: the maximum in force for a pass is
  `min(working_set_max, ceiling_tokens(spec, sizing) / ambient_ratio)`, so it is a function of the
  runner rather than a constant that can disagree with it. A configured maximum above the resolved
  trigger is a configuration contradiction and must fail a check, the stance `config.py:831` already
  takes on `working_set_min >= working_set_max`.
- Source the ambient ratio from recorded `context_tokens` at a high quantile, matching
  basicly-jr0l.58's stance for the unsized-lane bound at `DEFAULT_UNSIZED_LANE_QUANTILE = 0.9`, and
  record the sample count so a seed reads as a seed. Seven samples is below
  `DEFAULT_CALIBRATION_MIN_SAMPLES = 10`, so the honest first landing is a **declared seed ratio with
  the gate wired**, replaced by the measured quantile once the sample crosses the minimum. State
  which of the two shipped.

Pair with basicly-jr0l.54 (verify the declared scope at landing rather than trusting it at decompose)
- an accurate ratio is meaningless if the declaration it divides is unverified.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `tests/test_decompose.py`
- `tests/test_config.py`

## Eighth pair, and it widens the tail (2026-08-04)

`basicly-23ep`'s own lane adds a pair that lies **outside** the range this bead was filed on:
forecast **31688**, recorded occupancy **403051** - a ratio of **12.72**, against the 3.16-7.21 the
first seven samples showed. So the tail is materially worse than the seven-sample view, and the
median is the wrong statistic to bound a ceiling with.

Two consequences for the fix:

- **A high quantile is not optional.** At 12.72x a lane admitted at the 132000 band maximum would
  occupy ~1.68M tokens - over the corrected 600000 trigger and over the 1000000 window itself. Bound
  on the observed maximum or a 0.9-plus quantile, per basicly-jr0l.58's stance, never the median.
- **The sample is now eight, still below `DEFAULT_CALIBRATION_MIN_SAMPLES = 10`.** Ship the declared
  seed with the gate wired and record it as seeded; do not fit on eight.

Worth noting *why* this lane ran so much larger than its declaration predicted: it was driven
single-track, where the ceiling turned out to be inert (basicly-7kxq), so nothing bounded it at all.
A ratio measured on an unbounded run is the honest input for a ceiling, but it is not
interchangeable with one measured on a run the finalize protocol was policing - record which each
sample is.

## Ninth pair corrects the eighth (2026-08-04)

`basicly-7kxq`: forecast **26780**, occupancy **128113** - a ratio of **4.79**, back inside the
original 3.16-7.21 band. So the note above overstated the case: **12.72 is one outlier across nine
pairs, not a new tail**, and the honest summary is a range of 3.16-12.72 with a single point above
7.3. Bound on a high quantile of the nine rather than on the maximum, and say which.

The outlier has a plausible cause worth recording rather than smoothing away: `basicly-23ep` ran on
the single-track path while the ceiling was inert there (basicly-7kxq, now closed), so **nothing
bounded it**. `7kxq` itself ran on that same path *before* its own fix landed, so it too was
unbounded - and still came in at 4.79. Two unbounded runs 2.7x apart says the spread is work-shaped,
not guard-shaped. Keep recording whether each sample ran bounded or unbounded; with the meter now
wired on both paths every future sample is bounded, which changes what the population means.
payload.title: Calibrate the working set band against measured occupancy instead of its own estimator

payload.description:
From spike basicly-zv48 dimension 6 (D5/D6 convergence). basicly's context contribution is static projection; the "I don't know" contract is soft prose in the knowledge-priming/decision-protocol fragments the model may ignore. The loop owns a hard block-and-resume outcome (`_blocked` in loop.py) but it fires only on runner failure/checkpoints/gates, never on the agent itself signalling "iteration budget spent, fact not found".

Make a structured needs-input / I-don't-know a first-class loop outcome the HEADLESS runner can signal, mapping to the loop's existing block-and-resume contract (`_blocked(..., needs_input=<fact>)`) so the loop blocks and surfaces the missing fact instead of landing a confident wrong answer.

Signal carrier (decided): a self-ignored sentinel file the agent writes into its worktree, `.basicly/usage/needs-input.json` = {"fact": ..., "detail": ...}. The loop reads it after a clean (exit 0) dispatch, blocks with needs_input, and consumes it. Robust against output redaction/truncation and agent-neutral. The manual/handoff runner is unchanged (the driver already surfaces missing facts); a manual-driver CLI is explicitly out of scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A headless dispatch that finishes exit 0 with a valid `.basicly/usage/needs-input.json` in the worktree blocks the loop with a needs-input result (populated `needs_input`), does NOT land the worktree, and consumes (removes) the sentinel so a re-dispatch starts clean.
- A malformed or empty sentinel is tolerated (no crash) and falls through to the normal "finished; advance again to land it" block; a missing sentinel keeps today's behaviour exactly.
- The dispatch prompt and a projected catalog fragment document the protocol (when to write the sentinel and its shape), turning the prose escalation policy into an enforced seam.
- The needs-input reason/fact is surfaced by `loop status` / advance output the same way other blocks are.
- Full suite, ruff, ruff format, pyright, bandit, and projection gates (basicly check / skills-check / agents-check / hooks-check) pass; verified by exercising a real dispatch (not just unit tests).

## Notes

- Scope is the headless dispatch path in `loop._dispatch_runner`; the sentinel lives in the already self-ignored `.basicly/usage/` dir (same convention as run-records, tool-usage, checkpoint-confirms).
payload.title: Retrieval: structured I-dont-know / needs-input as a first-class loop outcome

payload.close_reason: Pinned to br 0.2.16 (fc8f319), version single-sourced with drift warning, and the discarded gate verdict now blocks (0cd6f30). Full gate green: 8/8, 1487 passed. Upstream br 0.2.19 remains broken and beads_rust#398 blocks moving forward; the sibling harness repo still needs an enforced pin, tracked there.
payload.description:
br 0.2.19 rejects the harness verify-gate call: 'br gate report <id> --gate verify --provider by-hand --status pass' fails with 'no configured transition from open requires gate verify; add a workflow.gates rule'. Reproduced on origin/main a2cdf23, so it predates the privacy-hardening work and is a tracker-version regression, not a code change.

IMPACT, two levels. Tests: 4 integration tests in tests/test_integration_loop.py fail, which blocks every push because pre-push runs the full-mode verify checks including pytest. CI never caught it because CI does not install br, so all 14 needs_br tests skip there - the gate only fires on a developer machine. Engine: verify.report_gate uses try_run_br and degrades gracefully, so the loop does not crash - it silently stops recording the verify gate. That silent degradation is arguably worse than the test failure and is the part to fix deliberately.

WHAT IS KNOWN about the policy shape, established empirically: it lives in .beads/policy.yaml, not .beads/config.yaml; workflow.gates is a map, not a sequence; its values must be a struct GateRule (serde error: 'invalid type: sequence, expected struct GateRule'); unknown fields are ignored rather than rejected, so a wrong field name parses and still fails validation. Roughly 17 candidate shapes were tried (keys: target status, gate name, from->to string; fields: require, required, requires, gates, all_of, any_of, require_all, required_gates, gate) and none satisfied validation. Passing --to explicitly does not help: --to closed and --to in_progress both fail with 'workflow does not require gate verify for transition'.

WHY IT IS NOT JUST A CONFIG LINE: GateRule is documented nowhere reachable - not br robot-docs guide, not br capabilities, not br schema (which exposes no gate or workflow schema). The obvious next step, reading the beads_rust implementation, is barred by the clean-room boundary recorded in docs/design/work-tracker.md section 7: that licence is MIT with a rider naming analyzing as restricted use for this class of user. So resolving this needs the sanctioned MIT upstream gastownhall/beads, upstream docs, or a design decision instead.

OPTIONS, none chosen: (a) find the schema in the sanctioned MIT upstream and ship a policy.yaml via basicly install; (b) pin a br version floor/ceiling and document 0.2.19 as incompatible; (c) make the 4 tests not depend on br gate report succeeding, accepting reduced coverage; (d) make verify.report_gate fail loudly instead of silently when the tracker rejects a gate, so the degradation is visible. This is a concrete instance of the unowned-external-binary risk that work-tracker.md was opened about.
payload.title: br 0.2.19 breaks gate report; pin to 0.2.16 (CI installs the pin, so CI stayed green)

payload.text:
CORRECTION + resolution (2026-07-29).

The original diagnosis was wrong on one point: CI *does* install br. quality-gates.yml:105
runs .scripts/install_br.py, and all 14 needs_br tests run there. CI stayed green because it
installs the *pinned 0.2.16*, while this machine had drifted to 0.2.19 (installed 2026-07-28
11:16 into ~/AppData/Local/Programs/br). Same commit, same test file, only the binary differs:

  br 0.2.19  ->  4 failed, 10 passed
  br 0.2.16  -> 14 passed

Reproduced outside the harness in a throwaway repo: 0.2.16 records the gate, 0.2.19 answers
'no configured transition from open requires gate verify' and exits 4. Note we ship no
.beads/policy.yaml at all, so this is 0.2.19's *default* behaviour, not a strict-policy opt-in.

CHOSEN: option (b) pin, plus option (d) fail loudly. Not (a): upgrading forward is foreclosed
by beads_rust#398 - current main targets schema 17 and its reviewed migration accepts only
13->17 and 14->17. Our .beads/beads.db is at user_version 16, outside that matrix. Verified on
a COPY that 0.2.16 reads the schema-16 DB (424 issues), records the gate, creates issues, and
leaves user_version at 16 - the downgrade is safe in both directions.

Shipped:
- br.PINNED_VERSION is now the single source; .scripts/install_br.py imports it, and the probe
  warns on ANY difference from the pin, not just below a major.minor floor.
- loop.py no longer discards report_gate's verdict. It blocked nothing before: derive_phase
  keys off gates.can_advance, so a refused gate derived back to build and advance re-ran
  build->verify forever, silently.
- .beads/.gitignore gains *-fsqlite-* - 0.2.19 writes beads.db-fsqlite-ns-{gate,use}, which
  the existing *.fsqlite-* glob misses.

LEAD for anyone who retries the policy schema: beads_rust#399's repro shows workflow.transitions
is a 'from: [to,...]' map with an 'initial:' key, per-transition gates are keyed 'in_review ->
closed' WITH SPACES around the arrow, and a TRANSITION_ANY_FROM ('any') exists. The 17 shapes
tried here used an unspaced 'from->to'. Untested - recorded only so the next attempt starts
further along.

Related upstream, neither of them this bug: #399 (br close skips validate_transition - too
permissive, opposite direction) and #398 (schema 15/16 cannot migrate to 17).

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a multi lane pass whose lanes all append to a convention shared path that no bead declares when the pass is planned then the grouping serialises those lanes and preflight warns naming the path and a control pass whose lanes share no such path still runs fully parallel
payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Measured 2026-08-05 on the `basicly-u6jq.1` proof run: a three-lane supervised pass over
`basicly-ky5z`, `basicly-1piy` and `basicly-3ymj`, whose declared scopes are disjoint —
`src/basicly/schema.py`, `src/basicly/config.py`, `src/basicly/usage.py` and their tests.
`loop preflight` reported all three `in band` and `VERDICT: ready`.

Observed — two lanes landed, and the third could not:

```
routed:  basicly-3ymj -> bounced - merge failed: rebase of harness/basicly-3ymj onto main
         hit conflicts in: CHANGELOG.md (rework 1/2)
routed:  basicly-3ymj -> decision - merge failed: rebase of harness/basicly-3ymj onto main
         hit conflicts in: CHANGELOG.md (rework 2/2)
blocked: 1 decision(s) await a human
```

Expected — a pass whose lanes declare disjoint scopes does not serialise on an undeclared
file, and does not spend a rework budget discovering that it does.

## Cause: every lane writes a file no lane declares

`CHANGELOG.md` is written by essentially every code lane in this repo — the landing
convention expects a `[Unreleased]` entry — and it appears in **no** bead's `## Scope`. So it
is invisible to `decompose`'s grouping and to the band table, and three lanes each inserted an
entry at the same `### Fixed` anchor. The first two landed; the third rebased onto a `main`
whose anchor had moved twice and conflicted.

The mechanism is already documented and was already known. The `harness-loop` skill's
decompose row says a plan should list in `shared` any literal path from a child's scope that
the child only *appends its own entry to* — "a manifest, a lockfile" — "otherwise that one
path serializes every child that declares it". `CHANGELOG.md` is exactly that shape, and the
rule cannot fire for it because **it is not in any scope to begin with**. `shared` can only
de-conflict a path a child declares.

Aggravating factor recorded honestly: the driving session also curated `[Unreleased]` in the
base checkout between the pass being planned and the lanes landing, which moved the anchor a
second time. That was avoidable, but it is not the root cause — three lanes appending to one
anchor collide regardless.

## Why this is not the `qorx` defect

`basicly-qorx` fixed a *tracker* gate charging siblings for one lane's declaration. This is a
*git* conflict on a real shared file, and bouncing to the lane is correct behaviour. What is
wrong is that the collision was undetectable in advance while being entirely predictable.

## Fix shape

Two halves, and the first is nearly free:

- **Declare the convention-shared paths once, in config, not per bead.** A
  `[worktree] shared_paths` (or `[loop] append_only_paths`) list naming `CHANGELOG.md`, fed
  into the same grouping `shared` already feeds, so the sizer serialises lanes that would
  collide on it instead of discovering the collision in the merge queue. A per-bead
  declaration cannot work for a path every bead touches and no bead mentions.
- **Report it in `preflight`.** The band table already names a path that collapsed the
  grouping; it should also warn when a pass of N lanes will contend on a known append-only
  path, because that is the one collision knowable before any lane starts.

Deliberately **not** proposed: teaching the merge queue to auto-resolve a `CHANGELOG.md`
conflict. A union merge of two prose entries produces text nobody reviewed, and the entry is
consumer-facing release copy.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_decompose.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`
- `.basicly/core/skills/harness-loop/skill.yaml`

payload.text:
NEXT-SESSION PLAN (loop state machine, onb.6.3). 3rd of onb.6's four children; READY now (.1 state-model + .2 classify closed). This is the INTEGRATION HUB — it composes every module built so far. THIN CONDUCTOR: the engine advances phases + enforces gates; the AGENT supplies inputs (work type, decomposition plan) and does the actual coding in worktrees. State is read from br every time (resumable); nothing is cached.

MODULE: new src/basicly/loop.py + tests/test_loop.py.

CORE SHAPE — a single-step, resumable transition:
- advance(repo_root, issue_id, *, config=None, work_type=None, children=None) -> AdvanceResult.
- It FIRST reads loop_state.read_node_state(issue_id) to get the current phase (resume point), then dispatches on phase via a HANDLER DICT (phase -> _handler), mirroring cmd_worktree/cmd_policy dispatch so we stay under PLR0911 (<=6 returns) / PLR0913 (<=5 args) — pass agent inputs in a small frozen Inputs dataclass, not as many kwargs.
- AdvanceResult(frozen): from_phase, to_phase (== from_phase when blocked), action ("classified"/"decomposed"/"built"/"merged"/"verified"/"shipped"/"tore-down"/"blocked"/"escalated"), blocked_reason|None, needs_input|None (what the agent/human must supply next). No exceptions for normal blocks — return a blocked result.

PHASE -> ACTION MAPPING (each composes an already-tested module):
- intake: requires work_type; absent -> blocked(needs_input="work_type"); present -> classify.classify(repo,id,work_type) -> to "classify".
- classify: gated by the classify human checkpoint (policy.checkpoint_approved) AND DoR (classify returns can_leave_classify / policy.definition_of_ready). Both true -> to "decompose"; else blocked(needs classify checkpoint approval and/or DoR sections).
- decompose: requires children plan; absent -> blocked(needs_input="children"); present -> decompose.decompose(repo,id,children); then gated by the decompose checkpoint -> to "build".
- build: for each dependency-unblocked child (loop_state.ready_ranked, concurrency-capped by WorktreeConfig), worktree.create(name) and stash the binding via br update --external-ref loop_state.format_worktree_ref(name,branch). Agent builds + verifies each child (that is child-level advance recursion — see design Q3). When children are green -> to "merge".
- merge: merge.merge_queue(repo, [(name,bead)...], config) in the decomposer's serial/topological order; on a node failure the queue already records rework + escalation (policy) -> surface as blocked/escalated.
- verify: verify.run_verify(repo, mode) + verify.report_gate(repo,id,report); gate_status must show the required gate green (policy.gate_status.can_advance) -> to "ship"; fail -> policy.record_rework + should_escalate (bounded n=2, config.max_rework) -> blocked/escalated.
- ship: gated by the ship human checkpoint -> to "teardown".
- teardown: worktree.cleanup for the node's worktrees + br close the issue -> "done".

DESIGN QUESTIONS TO RESOLVE IN-SESSION:
(Q1) Single-step advance() core vs a run() loop. RECOMMEND: advance() is the primitive (resumable, agent/human re-invokes each step); add a thin run_until_blocked(repo, issue_id, inputs) driver that loops advance() until it blocks/checkpoints/finishes. The CLI (onb.6.4) wires both; one-shot mode (arch 12.2) = auto-approve the middle checkpoint in the driver.
(Q2) Where agent inputs live: pass work_type/children into advance() (or an Inputs dataclass); when a phase needs one and it is absent, block and report needs_input. Keeps the engine agent-agnostic (no prompting inside the engine).
(Q3) Fractal recursion (epic->feature->task, arch 12.1/12.2). RECOMMEND scope onb.6.3 to the SINGLE-TRACK linear machine; children advance via the SAME advance() invoked per child by the driver over ready_ranked. Full auto-recursion inside one advance() call is deferred (leave a clear hook + a note); the AC only requires the linear phase machine + checkpoints + rework + resume. Confirm this boundary.

payload.description:
## Context

`basicly loop preflight <root>` answers "what would a pass cost" in aggregate only. Twice in one
session (2026-08-01) the operator had to hand-write a python query against
`decompose.resolve_dispatch_sizing` to answer the question that actually decides a run: **which
candidate lanes would the band admit, and at what size**.

`supervise.band_coverage` already produces exactly this report, but preflight reaches it only via
`_print_preflight_spend`'s `if lanes:` branch — i.e. only when lanes are *already dispatchable*.
With a halted grant, or any root whose children are not yet ready, `lanes` is empty and preflight
prints just the fallback line:

```
per-lane:  16002352 tokens assumed for an unsizeable lane (measured)
forecast:  ~80011760 tokens if all 5 lanes start (cap x per-lane)
```

That 80M is the fallback assumption multiplied by the concurrency cap. It is not a measurement, and
it reads exactly like one. Measured on this repo's own tracker the same moment, over the 16 open
`basicly-jr0l` children: 1 lane in band, 1 below `working_set_min`, 3 above `working_set_max`, and
11 with no parseable scope. A grant minted against the 80M line would be minted against a number
describing none of that.

This is the same class of failure as basicly-jr0l.60 and basicly-tuy6: the information exists, the
gate computes it, and nothing surfaces it to the person deciding. Preflight is the documented
pre-run command (`basicly loop preflight` is what the operating notes say to run instead of
recalling a checklist), so it is the right place.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a session root whose candidate lanes are not dispatchable when `basicly loop preflight` runs then it reports each candidate's band verdict and working-set size, and names the ones with no parseable scope, instead of only the aggregate fallback forecast

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `tests/test_cli_loop.py`

payload.description:
Retro finding (v0.5.0 and v0.5.1 this session): the release changelog generator produces the new section in the wrong place and with a lint violation, so it needs hand-fixing every release.

Root cause: .scripts/generate_release_changelog.py _insert_index returns the index of the first "## " heading, which is "## [Unreleased]". The new "## vX.Y.Z" section is therefore inserted ABOVE [Unreleased] instead of below it, and the join leaves two consecutive blank lines before the following section (markdownlint MD012). Both releases this session required a manual reorder plus a blank-line fix.

Proposed fix: insert the new release section immediately AFTER an existing "## [Unreleased]" section (keeping [Unreleased] on top), and never emit a double blank line at the seam. Fall back sensibly (insert after the intro) when no [Unreleased] section exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- generate_release_changelog.py inserts a new "## vX.Y.Z - DATE" section immediately after an existing "## [Unreleased]" section so [Unreleased] stays at the top; when none exists it inserts after the header intro.
- The output has no consecutive blank lines at the insertion seam (markdownlint MD012 passes on the generated CHANGELOG.md without hand-editing).
- A regression test covers insertion order with an [Unreleased] section present and asserts no double blank lines.
- Once correct, trim the "reordering/curation" caveat in the release-process skill to only the genuine curation step (grouping raw commits into Added/Fixed).
payload.title: Fix the release changelog generator ordering and double-blank seam

payload.description:
WHY: basicly currently authors a skill as .basicly/core/skills/<name>/skill.yaml (fields: name, description, instructions, technologies) and renders ONLY a single SKILL.md via skills.py:render_skill_md/sync_skills. It does NOT copy references/, scripts/, assets/, or any additional files to the skill roots. The Agent Skills spec (https://agentskills.io/specification) allows a skill directory to contain SKILL.md (required) plus scripts/, references/, assets/, and '... Any additional files or directories'. To author powerful skills (e.g. a python skill with a long references/ style guide + a fixer scripts/), the engine must project the whole skill directory.

SCOPE / FILES:
- src/basicly/skills.py: sync_skills / check_synced_skills / discover_skills / render_skill_md — copy every file & subdirectory of the source skill dir (except the skill.yaml source, which renders to SKILL.md) into each destination root (.claude/skills/<name>/ and .agents/skills/<name>/), verbatim, preserving structure. Prune on technology deselection. Add/verify freshness in check.
- src/basicly/schema.py + .basicly/core/schemas/skill.schema.json: extend the skill source to support the spec's optional frontmatter passthrough — license, compatibility, metadata (map), allowed-tools — rendered into SKILL.md frontmatter. Keep 'technologies' (basicly-internal scoping; NOT emitted into SKILL.md frontmatter, or emitted under metadata — decide and document).
- Generated-marker / protect-generated hooks (.basicly/core/hooks/protect-generated*.py): SKILL.md stays generated (marker), but bundled reference/script/asset files are HAND-AUTHORED sources that must be copied but NOT carry the generated marker and NOT be clobbered/pruned wrongly. Define the rule and enforce it.
- .basicly/generated-manifest.json: track projected skill files (including copied resources) so build/check/uninstall stay consistent.
- catalog-lint (.basicly/core/hooks/catalog-lint.py + src/basicly/catalog_lint.py): validate skill dirs against the spec — name matches dir (1-64 chars, lowercase a-z0-9 and single hyphens, no leading/trailing/consecutive hyphen), description non-empty <=1024 chars, SKILL.md body kept small (warn > ~500 lines per spec progressive disclosure), file references one level deep.
- basicly build / skills-build / skills-check / install / uninstall: end-to-end still green with resource files present.
- docs/architecture.md: document the full-spec skill layout and the source->projection mapping.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. A skill authored as .basicly/core/skills/<name>/ with skill.yaml + references/REF.md + scripts/x.sh + assets/y + an arbitrary extra file/dir projects ALL of them (unchanged bytes) into BOTH .claude/skills/<name>/ and .agents/skills/<name>/, alongside the rendered SKILL.md.
2. Optional frontmatter (license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools) round-trips from skill.yaml into SKILL.md frontmatter per spec; omitting them yields today's minimal frontmatter.
3. Technology deselection prunes the whole projected skill dir (all resources), not just SKILL.md.
4. basicly check / skills-check --all-default-roots / hooks-check / catalog lint all pass; protect-generated does not flag hand-authored resource files, and does not allow manual edits to generated SKILL.md.
5. New unit tests cover: full-dir copy, extra '...' files, frontmatter passthrough, prune-on-deselect, and check-detects-drift for a resource file.
6. 'skills-ref validate ./<projected-skill>' (https://github.com/agentskills/agentskills/tree/main/skills-ref) passes for a projected skill, or a documented reason if that tool is unavailable in-repo.

SPEC: https://agentskills.io/specification (directory structure incl. the '...' line; frontmatter table; progressive disclosure: metadata ~100 tokens, SKILL.md < ~5000 tokens / < 500 lines, resources on demand; file references one level deep; validation via skills-ref).
payload.title: Rich-skill engine: full Agent Skills spec compliance (bundle references/scripts/assets + extended frontmatter)

payload.description:
## Re-scoped 2026-08-04

**The derivation half of this bead moved to basicly-o486.** That bead replaces
`DEFAULT_WORKING_SET_MAX`'s derivation-from-the-largest-completed-estimate with a bound computed
from the resolved runner's trigger and a quantile of the measured `context_tokens` samples, which
removes the self-declared input this bead was filed about. It is itself blocked on basicly-23ep,
because the trigger it divides is currently wrong by a factor of five. Both halves in one lane would
put two diffs on the same constant in `config.py`, so they are separated by file rather than by
intent.

**What survives here is the half the bead never actually carried.** `config.py:455-457` records
it: a pass shares one `.beads` through the redirect, so when basicly-tcmy.5's finishing record
failed the tracker-wide ceiling gate, basicly-tcmy.6 and basicly-tcmy.22 failed verify on
tcmy.5's declaration too and **each was charged a rework attempt for a defect in neither
diff**, against a cap of 2. That is a gate-accounting defect, not a sizing one: a shared
tracker-wide gate must attribute its failure to the lane whose declaration invalidated it, and
must not consume a sibling's bounded rework budget. It is the same shape as basicly-m4zv.14,
where a machine-global lock charged rework for a flake, and it should be resolved consistently
with it.

The original filing follows unchanged, as the evidence for both halves.

---

## Steps to Reproduce

```
rg -n "DEFAULT_WORKING_SET_MAX = " src/basicly/config.py
uv run python -c "
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tests')
import test_decompose as T
c = T.completed_lane_estimates(T.REPO_ROOT)
print(sorted(c.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:3])"
```

Observed - the largest completed estimate, which is the sole input to the ceiling, is whichever lane declared the widest `## Scope` and finished. Expected - a lane cannot move a global constant by editing its own bead.

## Context

`DEFAULT_WORKING_SET_MAX` is derived from the dispatch record: the largest estimate on a completed headless lane, rounded to a floor-unit. The estimate is `seed x scope_read_cost(repo_root, globs)` where the globs come from the lane's **own** `## Scope` section, which the lane itself may rewrite while it runs.

`basicly-fcls` did exactly that. It was dispatched with three globs and an estimate of 94912 under the old measure; it finished having rewritten its scope to nine globs, which under its own new read-capped measure records as 72000 - larger than the 53004 of `basicly-tcmy.31` it had just derived 56000 from. The gate fired against the constant the same lane had committed minutes earlier, which is the gate working correctly.

Two distinct defects sit here, and only the second is about the number.

1. **The derivation is a ratchet with a self-declared input.** It can only ever be dragged upward, and the lever is a field the lane controls. A lane that names ten files it barely touches raises the ceiling for every future lane, with no human deciding and no evidence that a lane that size can actually run. Nothing bounds this.

2. **A lane's scope may change after it is admitted.** The band admits a lane on the scope it declared at dispatch, and the record is written against the scope it declared at finish. Those are different quantities and are compared as if they were one - the defect class of `basicly-z2wi`, `basicly-3w44` and `basicly-ipx2`. `basicly-jr0l.54` already covers verifying the declared scope at landing and is the natural home for the enforcement half.

The honest counter-argument, so it is not lost: widening the scope was *correct behaviour*. The lane genuinely did need `runner.py` to record `context_tokens`, and declaring it is what the scope field is for. The defect is that an honest declaration silently moved a global constant and made the bead undispatchable at 329606 - so the current design punishes accurate scope reporting.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `tests/test_policy.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`
payload.title: A shared tracker gate charges every sibling lane rework for one lanes declaration

payload.text: First measurement from RunRecord.context_tokens, which landed with basicly-fcls - and it is a 5x gap, not a 1.5x one. basicly-8ry8 declared a scope costing 8000 read-capped tokens, so the band sized it at 16000 at the bug seed of 2.0, and the lane recorded context_tokens=80211. Occupancy is 5.01x the estimate the band gates on. Three session lanes for the record: 8ry8 est 16000 cost 2393339 occupancy 80211; ipx2 scope 29884 cost 3986470; fcls scope 46066 cost 15245717. This is the first (estimate, measured-occupancy) pair the repo has ever held for the quantity the ceiling is denominated in, and it says the ambient term basicly-fcls declined to invent is the dominant one - consistent with its R^2 of 0.095 for scope against occupancy versus 0.863 for turn count. Do not fit a factor to this single pair; it is one sample and the point of the field is to stop declaring what should be measured. Collect pairs first.

basicly-tcmy.5 was admitted on eight globs at 66780 working-set tokens. Found while landing basicly-lelg (2026-07-31) and deliberately left out of scope there, because it is
not among that bead's seven enumerated defects. Same class of error, same file, and it will mislead the
same way.

`docs/architecture/architecture.md` §14 (around line 1320-1325) makes two claims that are now wrong:

1. **"the path-scoped tier is already built ... and no fragment declares one"** — stale. Two fragments
   declare a scope today (`external-review` on `docs/research/**` + `docs/design/**`, and the
   platform-hermetic tests fragment on `tests/**`). The equivalent line at
   `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md:125` was already corrected; this one was missed.
2. **"it improves both cost _and_ adherence"** — contradicts the finding basicly-lelg just recorded.
   Scoping is only a cost *reduction* for Claude and Copilot. For codex it is a strict cost
   *increase*: scoped fragments are inlined into `AGENTS.md` at ~1500 chars each (measured 1462 and
   1614), because codex has no glob scoping and nested `AGENTS.md` below the cwd is never loaded. So the
   claim is true for two of three families and false for the third — which is exactly the asymmetry
   `implementation-plan.md:403-409` is careful about and this sentence flattens.

The adherence half of the claim also deserves a look rather than a copy: basicly-agzx.1 measured recall
at 98% / 93%, and Phase 4's own exit criterion was weakened to "recall **not degraded**" precisely
because there is no headroom left to improve. A sentence asserting scoping "improves adherence" sits
badly next to that.

1. Read `docs/architecture/architecture.md` around lines 1320-1325.
2. Compare against `.basicly/core/fragments/` (two fragments carry `scope`), against
   `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md:125`, and against §7 detail 4 as corrected by basicly-lelg.
3. Observed: the architecture reference says no fragment declares a scope, and that scoping improves
   cost and adherence for everyone. Expected: it names the two fragments that do declare scopes, and
   states the asymmetry — cost falls for claude and copilot, rises for codex — instead of a blanket
   improvement claim.

- Given the architecture reference section on the path-scoped tier when it is read then it no longer claims that no fragment declares a scope, and the cost claim names the asymmetry between claude and copilot on one side and codex on the other rather than asserting a blanket improvement, with the adherence claim either evidenced against the agzx.1 measurement or dropped
