payload.text:
[harness-info] the entry point landed, 2026-08-14

## The acceptance transcript, run on merged main

```text
$ uv run basicly tracker --help
  {import,shadow}
    import         Bring the owned ledger up to the committed export (§5 step 1)
    shadow         Compare the owned ledger against the live br, read-only (§5 step 2)

$ uv run basicly tracker import --dry-run
ledger 643 records, export 843
would add 200 records, 0 tombstones
```

Both halves of the criterion, and the shape matches the consumer transcript in
`factory-loop.md` §8.1 line for line.

## What was built, and where it could not go

`migrate.py` has **+3 tokens of size headroom and 0.0pt of density**, and
`tests/test_kit_tracker_migrate.py` has **+0 tokens**. So no `main()` was added to the kit and no
test was added to that module. The entry point is `basicly tracker import` - which is what the
acceptance criterion names - plus an `import_preview` seam in `br.py`, which had the headroom.

**A kit-level `main()` is therefore still absent**, and that matters for §4`s promise that the kit
is consumable with zero basicly imports and nothing on PATH. It is not this bead`s criterion and
it is named here rather than left as a silent gap.

## The refusal `basicly-c357` requires

Once the ledger holds a record the dual write created, the import refuses: re-importing would close
the historical gap the differential is judged against and the agreement would prove nothing
(`u4xu`). The `--dry-run` reports the **same** refusal rather than a count, because a preview
saying "would add 200" for a run that will refuse is worse than no preview - and both go through
one `import_preview`, so they cannot answer differently.

## No actor is recorded

`basicly-r166` is open on the ledger committing a username in every event, so this entry point
does not become a second producer of that defect. The original hand-run import wrote
`actor: <redacted:machine-username>` on all 3775 events.

## Deliberately not run on this repo

The 200-record gap stays open. Closing it is a **cutover step** and `u4xu` owns the cutover - the
sequence that makes the import and `u4xu`s "do not re-import" consistent is recorded on that bead:
import while still `external`, declare, then flip. Running it here would have pre-empted that
decision.

## Verification

`pytest -q` 3992 passed, six new in `tests/test_cli_tracker.py` including a real export-in,
ledger-out round trip against the live kit - a mocked import cannot carry "a fresh consumer can
build one". module-size, comment-density, test-naming, wired-or-deleted, docs-claims and
`basicly check` all green.

payload.description:
## Context

`supervise.py:2700` enqueues a decision of kind `stall` whose question literally offers
three routes: "runner {name} stopped on {bound}: retry, re-dispatch, or park?".

`cli.py:3582` (`_carry_out_rework_hold`) returns `None` unless
`item.kind == policy.REWORK_ESCALATION_KIND`, and `policy.py:634` sets that constant to
`"escalation"`. A `stall` decision therefore never reaches `policy.hold_lane`.

Answering `park` on a stall prints `answered <id> by human` and changes nothing: the bead
stays `open`, stays inside `loop_state.DISPATCHABLE_STATUSES`, and the next supervised pass
dispatches it again.

Observed 2026-08-13 on `basicly-ca42#155136fefc`. The lane had to be parked by calling
`policy.hold_lane` directly.

This is the same defect `_carry_out_rework_hold`'s own docstring says it fixed - "every
escalation this engine raises offers `park` as a route and nothing anywhere took it" - still
live one decision kind over. The docstring even claims "Every escalation kind, not only the
rework cap", while the guard binds to exactly one kind.

## Proposed check

A test that enqueues a `stall` decision, answers it `park`, and asserts the issue status is
`policy.HELD_STATUS` and that `supervise.ready_lanes` refuses it. Assert the same for every
kind whose question text offers the route, so the guard cannot drift from the question again.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Find a queued decision of kind `stall`:

   ```sh
   uv run basicly loop decisions <epic>
   ```

   Its question reads "runner <name> stopped on <bound>: retry, re-dispatch, or park?"
   (`supervise.py:2727`).

2. Answer it with the route the question offers:

   ```sh
   uv run basicly loop answer '<decision-id>' "park - <why>"
   ```

3. Observed 2026-08-13 on `basicly-ca42#155136fefc`: it prints `answered <id> by human` and
   **nothing else**. The bead stays `open`, stays inside `loop_state.DISPATCHABLE_STATUSES`, and
   the next supervised pass dispatches it again. The lane had to be parked by calling
   `policy.hold_lane` directly from Python.

4. The cause, read rather than inferred: `_carry_out_rework_hold` (`cli.py:3603`) returns `None`
   at `:3589` unless `item.kind == policy.REWORK_ESCALATION_KIND`, and `policy.py:634` sets that
   constant to `"escalation"`. The same guard repeats at `:3623` and `:3653`. A `stall` decision
   can therefore never reach `policy.hold_lane` (`policy.py:729`), which is the only writer of
   `HELD_STATUS` (`policy.py:709`).

**There is no test coverage for this route at all.** A search of `tests/` for
`_carry_out_rework_hold`, `answer_holds` and `hold_lane` returns nothing, against a positive
control where the same search shape finds three files for `repair_brief`. The retry route is
covered in `tests/test_cli_policy.py`; the hold route never was, which is why a guard that
contradicts its own docstring survived.

That docstring is the sharpest evidence that this is a regression rather than an omission: it
says "**Every escalation kind, not only the rework cap**, because `park` is offered by all three
question shapes `supervise._capped_dispatch` raises" - while the guard binds to exactly one kind.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a queued decision whose question offers `park`, when a human answers it `park`, then the
  issue's status becomes `policy.HELD_STATUS` and the reason is recorded - check: a test enqueues
  a `stall` decision, answers it `park`, and asserts both the status and the recorded reason.
- Given that same answer, when the command reports what it carried out, then it names the park
  rather than printing only `answered <id> by human` - check: assert the printed line, because an
  answer that changed nothing must not read identically to one that did.
- Given every decision kind whose question text offers the route, when each is answered `park`,
  then each is held - check: a test derives the kinds from the question shapes rather than
  hard-coding one, so the guard cannot drift from the question again.
- Given a delegated answer (`answered_by` carrying the decider prefix), when it says `park`, then
  the lane is **not** held and the refusal is reported - check: the existing human-only rule is
  asserted to survive, since a model parking its own lane could drop a requirement.
- Given a held lane, when a supervised pass runs, then `supervise.ready_lanes` refuses it - check:
  assert the lane is absent from the ready set.

## Demonstration

```sh
uv run basicly loop answer '<stall-decision-id>' "park - <why>"
```

prints that it parked the lane, and `br show <id>` reports `DEFERRED`.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_cli_policy.py`
- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `changelog.d/basicly-vkjt.fixed.md`
- `tests/test_cli_policy_hold.py`
- `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md`

payload.description:
## Context

`docs/requirements/factory-loop.md:1290-1306` and `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md:224`
record `--resume --fork-session` at "19x on a cache hit", pinned to claude 2.1.226.

Re-measured 2026-08-13 on claude 2.1.231: the headline **reproduces** at 19.06x (cold seed
`cache_create 20,850 / cache_read 0 / $0.125771`; fork `31 / 20,850 / $0.006597`), and two
concurrent forks of one seed each read the same prefix at `$0.006591` with distinct session
ids. The mechanism is sound and parallel-safe.

Two things the recorded claim does not say, and a lane design would be sized against it:

1. **The 19x denominator is the host floor, not a corpus.** The 20,850 cached tokens are the
   system prompt plus tool definitions. Cache reads bill at roughly 10% of the standard input
   rate, so forking a *repo corpus* is about 10x on that corpus - not 19x.
2. **A fork from a different working directory degrades to 5.4x** (`cache_read 18,071 /
   cache_create 2,928 / $0.0231`). The vendor names the cause: cwd, platform and a git-status
   snapshot are inside the cached prefix, and that "includes worktrees of the same
   repository". So fork-per-lane combined with worktree-per-lane recovers about 87% of the
   read, not all of it.

A documented remedy exists - `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections` on the binary,
`exclude_dynamic_sections` in the Python SDK - but **whether it composes with `--agent` is
unestablished**: `--help` says it is ignored with `--system-prompt`, and `--agent` is
documented as replacing the system prompt the same way. That chain is inference.

## Proposed check

Both documents state the denominator and the cross-directory figure with their dates and the
binary version. A two-directory fork probe with the exclusion flag on and off, comparing
`cache_read_input_tokens`, settles the composition question and is recorded as evidence.

payload.close_reason: fixed: the repair brief carries per-lens reviewer findings, unmerged and unranked (d520860)
payload.description:
## Context

`basicly-feje` made `reviewer` reachable. It dispatches once per lens at VALIDATE and records each lens as a `[harness-review]` marker on the unit.

Nothing reads those markers. They reach a human who opens the bead.

The lane that built it named this and deliberately did not start it, on the grounds that a half-wired path reads as covered. That judgment is correct and this bead is the other half.

## Why it matters more than an unread record usually would

`docs/requirements/factory-loop.md` §11.1 states the rule this leaves unsatisfied: rework that bounces to the same tier with the same framing every time spends the cap without changing a variable. A repair briefed with the findings that rejected the work is the variable.

The mechanism to carry them already exists. `repair_brief` assembles gate evidence today — the check, the command, the result — and `loop` dispatches the implementer in repair mode with it. A review finding is the same shape of evidence from a judged gate rather than a deterministic one.

## The rule that must not break

§6.4 closes with the reason the lens split exists: lens output is reported per lens and never merged into one ranked list, because a change can pass one axis and fail another and reranking lets the strong axis mask the weak one.

So a repair brief carries the findings **grouped by lens**. It does not rank them and it does not merge them into a single list of things to fix.

## A second consumer worth considering, not required here

Two degenerate reviewers are invisible today: the rubber stamp that approves nearly everything, and the noise generator whose findings are nearly all adjudicated contestable. Both are computable per lens from the recorded markers over a window. That is a separate bead if anyone wants it; naming it here stops it being rediscovered.

## Acceptance

- When a repair follows a failed validate, then its brief carries the review findings recorded for that unit, grouped by lens.
- When a unit has findings on two lenses, then the brief keeps them separate and ranks neither.
- When a lens recorded no finding, then the brief says so rather than omitting the lens.
- When a repair follows a failed verify rather than a failed validate, then the brief is unchanged from today.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/repair_brief.py`
- `src/basicly/lens_review.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_repair_brief.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`

## Depends on

`basicly-feje`, which is closed.

## Demonstration

Seed a unit with findings on both lenses, drive a repair, and read the dispatched brief.

## Context

`basicly-u2hl.54.1` made VALIDATE a phase and `.54.3` gave it a dispatch. Neither gave it a
route back to a landing, and the gap is reachable on the first real use.

Found on `basicly-u2hl.54.3` itself, 2026-08-13. Its own validation found a defect in the code
it had just landed. The repair was committed on the harness branch - and then had nowhere to go:

- `_verify_and_land` is reached only from `_on_build`, so the merge only ever happens on the
  build to verify advance.
- `derive_phase` returns `validate` while the validate gate is outstanding, so the node never
  derives `build` again and the landing is unreachable.
- `_on_ship` correctly refuses to close a node whose branch has not merged, so the work is not
  lost - it is stranded, which is the better failure but still a wedge.

A repair during BUILD has the path: `_repair_in_place` writes into the bound worktree and the
next advance re-lands. VALIDATE has the repair (the worktree is still bound) and not the land.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Drive an L3 bead to `validate` with a green verify gate.
- Commit any change on its harness branch, as a validation-driven repair would.
- Run `basicly loop advance <id>`.
- Observed: the advance dispatches or refuses in validate and never merges; the commit stays on
  the branch. Expected: the repaired work lands before validation is re-asked.

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py

## Context

Found by the lane-B survey 2026-08-14, with a measured dependency scan. `basicly-tcmy.13` owns the split. This names where to cut.

Cross-section edge counts, from an abstract syntax tree walk between the section headers:

```text
section                 lines        inbound edges    prose share
lock and heartbeat      108-310      2                36.9%
outcome routing         2810-3905    0                45.2%
usage meter             978-1158     1                34.2%
telemetry and dispatch  2077-2809    6                48.5%
```

## Why routing goes first

It is a pure dependency sink. Zero inbound references means no symbol in `supervise` needs a forwarding shim. It consumes only the lane outcome, the session state, the found-info record, the ready set, and the `merge`, `loop`, `decisions` and `policy` modules.

The two nameable halves are admit and dispatch a pass, and route and land the outcomes.

## The meter goes second

After the cycle is thinned, the meter at 978-1158 is the only thing `loop` reaches in `supervise`. Extracting it is what removes the layering exemption.

## The ratchet arithmetic

Routing at 45.2% prose sits above the module mean of 43.6%, so extracting it lowers the remainder's share. Both sides sit under the cap on a line-based measure. Re-measure with the gate's own token-based script before the commit, because `supervise.py` is frozen at 55.9.

## Warning

`tests/test_supervise.py` is frozen at 60,132 tokens. Move the routing tests out with the code or the test module's own ratchet blocks the lane.

## Acceptance

- When the routing section is extracted, then no forwarding shim is added to `supervise`.
- When both size gates run, then no baseline is raised and `supervise.py` shrinks in the same diff.
- When a supervised pass runs, then its routed outcomes are unchanged.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- a new module
- `.importlinter`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`

## Depends on

The thinning of the loop to supervise cycle.

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_supervise.py -q`, both ratchet scripts, and `uv run lint-imports`.

payload.description:
## Context

Step 6, the residue after `basicly-s5li` moves the 26 `comments` sites to ledger events.
Measured 2026-08-07 by enumerating every `_run_br` call site in `src/basicly/`.

55 sites total. `comments` is 26 of them and is `s5li`. This bead is the other 29, and
the finding is that they fall into four classes of very different cost - a quarter of
them delete themselves.

## Class 1 - the ledger already models these (11 sites)

Each maps onto an event kind `events.py` already declares:

| Call | Sites | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update -t <type>`, `update --external-ref` | `classify.py:54`, `loop.py:370`, `loop.py:1994` | `field` |
| `close --reason` | `loop.py:433` | `status` |
| `dep add -t blocks` | `supervise.py:899`, `supervise.py:1043`, `decompose.py:2056`, `merge.py:1117` | `edge` |
| `dep cycles --blocking-only` | `decompose.py:2019` | derived from `edge` |
| `create` | `supervise.py:1041`, `decompose.py:1815` | `created` |

Note `edge` is already in the ledger - the step-1 import wrote 658 of them - but `fsck`
reports it as an unfolded kind because the fold applies no state for it and a sibling
module derives it directly. Folding `edge` is a prerequisite for answering `blocked` and
`dep cycles` from the ledger.

## Class 2 - the ledger can already answer these (4 sites)

`show --json` (`br.py:1159`, `decompose.py:1988`) is **already flipped** at `MODE_OWNED`
via `read_record`. `blocked --json` (`loop_state.py:308`) and `dep cycles` derive from
folded edges. `gate list --robot` (`policy.py:424`) reads gate records, which are
`[harness-policy]` markers and therefore land with `s5li` rather than here.

## Class 3 - these disappear when br does (4 sites)

They exist only to serve br and have no owned equivalent to build:

- `sync --merge`, `sync --flush-only` (`merge.py:466`, `merge.py:520`) - br database to
  JSONL reconciliation. No second store, no sync.
- `init --prefix` (`cli.py:924`) - creates a br tracker.
- `where --json` (`worktree.py:208`) - probes the `.beads/redirect` file, which exists so
  a worktree shares the base checkout br database.

Deleting these is the measurable end of the dependency, not a migration.

## Class 4 - the one open question (1 site)

`br lint --json` (`policy.py:195`) feeds the Definition-of-Ready. It is br validating a
bead body shape, not a fact about our work graph. Decide deliberately: reimplement the
shape check we actually rely on, or drop it and let the DoR sections gate alone. Do not
port it by reflex - `required_sections` already encodes what the DoR needs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the engine at tracker mode owned with br absent from PATH when a bead is created or typed or closed or given an edge and when the ready set and blocked set and dependency cycles are computed then every one succeeds from the ledger alone and the four br-only call sites named in class 3 no longer exist in src

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/loop_state.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/worktree.py`
- `src/basicly/classify.py`

payload.description:
## Context

`basicly-e2mz.6` landed `.github/workflows/improvement-loop.yml` with `workflow_dispatch` only, by
owner decision 2026-08-14. That decision is explicit that it confirms `workflow_dispatch` and
**not** a cron trigger.

So one half of `e2mz.6` acceptance bullet 1 is deliberately unmet: "then `basicly loop improve`
runs **without a human invoking it**". `workflow_dispatch` cannot satisfy it by construction. The
other half - `wired-or-deleted` crediting the command from an independent entry rather than from
the script own docstring - is met and carries a control assertion.

## What this is

A `schedule:` trigger on the existing file. It would be this repository first scheduled workflow:
`.github/workflows/` holds `basicly.yml`, `improvement-loop.yml`, `pages.yml`, `quality-gates.yml`
and `release.yml`, and none carries `schedule:`.

## The precondition the owner named

"Watching it file a few more under a human hand before it runs unattended is cheap, and the
one-lane bound means an unattended loop that misbehaves would still only produce one bad bead at a
time - **but only if the bound holds, which is itself only observed once**."

The bound has now been observed holding twice, both against real tracker state. That is not the
few the decision asks for. Do not read this bead as ready on the count alone.

## The second question a schedule forces, which dispatch did not

The workflow dry-runs, because a live run files a bead into an ephemeral checkout and persisting
it needs `contents: write` and a push to `main` from CI. A scheduled dry run reports into a log
nobody reads, so a schedule is only worth having if the actuator can persist - which makes the
push the real design question behind this bead rather than the cron line.

CI files are on the confirmation list and this needs its own confirmation.
payload.title: give the improvement loop a schedule trigger so it runs without a human pressing a button

Nothing binds: no fragment mentions comments, ERA001 only catches commented-out code, and python-guidelines currently forbids deleting a comment. A purge hook cannot be the instrument - it would strip the 64 pragma comments the lint gates read, and ruff D mandates docstrings so the prose would relocate.

Deliver:
1. .scripts/check_comment_density.py - a frozen-baseline ratchet on prose tokens (comments excluding pragmas, plus docstrings) as a share of module tokens, cap 50%, waiver marker counted, mirroring check_module_size.py.
2. [tool.comment_density] in pyproject.toml with the go-live baselines.
3. A [[verify.checks]] fast entry in basicly.toml.
4. A core-rules fragment line making code the authoritative source, and an amendment to python-guidelines so the do-not-delete rule does not license the density.

payload.close_reason: fixed: one downstream phase set, and the grant root reaches both supervised drives (6ca4e04)
payload.description:
## Context

Two modules define the downstream population and they disagree. Found by the lane-A architectural survey 2026-08-14 and verified by hand.

```text
wip.py:45           DOWNSTREAM_PHASES = ("verify", "validate", "ship")   counts 3
supervise.py:3427   if phase not in ("verify", "ship"): continue         drives 2
config.py:141       max_downstream_wip = 5
```

`wip.py:15` states the two populations are the same:

> That is the same population `supervise.advance_parked` drives each pass, on purpose: what drains the bound is exactly what the bound counts, so a blocked pass is not a wedged one.

That claim is false. A unit whose derived phase is `validate` is counted by `wip.downstream_units` (wip.py:140-144), is never dispatched (`supervise.py:1577` takes `phase == "build"` only), and is never advanced. Five such units refuse every further dispatch. The queue item raised then (`WIP_QUESTION`, wip.py:50) tells the operator to land the finished lanes, which `advance_parked` cannot do for this population.

## Why it is one day old

VALIDATE became a real phase on 2026-08-13 under `basicly-u2hl.54`. That bead carried five acceptance criteria. All five concerned the phase, its gate, its refusal and its dispatch. None named the supervisor's parked-lane driver. The close was correct against the criteria and the work was incomplete against the system.

## The decision the implementer must take

`advance_parked` calls `loop.run_until_blocked`, which passes no `grant_root` and defaults `repair_dispatch=True` (loop.py:2444-2462). Adding `"validate"` to the tuple naively would run `_dispatch_validation` outside the spend gate. The acceptance criteria pin that.

## Acceptance

- While a supervised session holds a unit whose derived phase is `validate`, when a pass runs, then the engine advances that unit or enqueues a decision naming it, and never skips it silently.
- When the phase set that `advance_parked` drives is compared with the set that `wip` counts, then one definition exists and the other imports it.
- If a validation dispatch is reachable from a supervised pass, then it checks `policy.spend_status` under the session grant root before it spawns.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/wip.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`
- `tests/test_wip.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_supervise.py tests/test_wip.py -q` with a new test that parks an L3 unit in validate and asserts a supervised pass routes it.

## Warning

`supervise.py` and `wip.py` are both density-frozen at zero headroom. Move the tuple. Do not add prose.

payload.description:
## CORRECTED 2026-08-13 — read this before the text below
**The title is refuted as written.** "Instead of spawning a headless CLI" cannot be delivered:
the Python Agent SDK (`claude-agent-sdk`) drives the installed CLI as a local subprocess -
`CLINotFoundError` and its own transport documentation say so. What changes is **how a
definition is loaded**, not whether a subprocess exists. Restate as: *spawn the role definition
as a subagent so its declared `skills:` preload and per-subagent usage is emitted.*

**A third of the text below argues a settled point.** The section "The decision this
contradicts, stated so it is not overturned by accident" attacks `agent-roster-design.md:210`
and `factory-loop-requirements.md:602`. **Neither file exists** - all six design notes were
absorbed and deleted in `28257e9` on 2026-08-08, one day before this bead's last edit. And the
position was reversed *in this bead's favour* on 2026-08-09: **D27** (`factory-loop.md:105`)
decides "thin engine: the catalog defines, the host executes... the host runtime spawns the
subagent, resolves its tier and fires the boundary hooks", and **D28** amends the Conductor
refusal because "both installed runtimes contradict it by construction".

**Its gating open question is now answered, and the answer changes the scope.** An externally
spawned process is always a separate session and can **never** appear as a subagent row inside
a live interactive session. Non-interactive host dispatch: yes. Nested in the driving session:
never. So the bead's own re-scope branch - the engine emits work a session executes - is a
genuinely different design that must be chosen deliberately rather than fallen into.

**The plan's justification for this row does not survive checking.**
`implementation-plan.md:225` says the question is "answered twice over", citing a competing
harness that "runs exactly this split in production". `factory-loop.md:1115` says that
harness's loop does **not** call any LLM and emits a prompt to stdout - which is an existence
proof for the re-scope branch, not for engine-driven host dispatch.

**The real content is the spawn mode**, and it is measured: `skills:` is honoured for a spawned
subagent and **not** under `claude --agent <name> -p`, this repo's only dispatch shape. That is
`basicly-ey58`, which this bead should depend on. One sub-claim below is also stale: `.claude/`
agents are no longer inert - `roles.py:93-105` stats them and `runner.py:547-570` injects
`--agent` - but **0 of 346 recorded dispatches carry it**, against a positive control of 163
carrying `-p`, so the effect is still nil.

The four non-negotiables below - D1's singleton supervisor, D9's `prompt_sha256`, metering, and
agnosticism as contract - are all still current and survive the restatement.

---

## Context

Every dispatch in this engine ends at one `subprocess.Popen` (`runner.py:1469`) of a CLI
binary — `("claude","-p",PROMPT)`, `("codex","exec",PROMPT)`, `("copilot","-p",PROMPT)`
(`runner.py:275-308`). **No code path anywhere asks the host to run a subagent.**

Measured 2026-08-08: flags actually passed are `--output-format`, `--verbose`,
`--forward-subagent-text`, `--session-id`, `--disallowedTools`, `--model`. **Zero hits**
for `--agents`, `--append-system-prompt`, `--mcp-config`, `--permission-mode`, `--resume`.

And the agents we do project are inert: `.claude/agents/` holds three files written by
`agents.sync()`, and **no dispatch code reads that directory** — its only other consumer
is `cli.py:1261`, which globs it to *delete* files.

## The decision this contradicts, stated so it is not overturned by accident

`agent-roster-design.md:210` refuses this by name:

> role prompts *"cannot be Claude subagent files — the factory is agent-agnostic and
> dispatches headless Claude, Codex, and Copilot alike."*

And `factory-loop-requirements.md:602` treats host nesting as a **hazard** ("can fan out
inside itself, unmetered and outside the supervisor's model"), never a capability.

**Two measurements undercut the premise rather than the principle.** First, the
agnosticism is hollow in practice: of 338 run records, `claude` 156 and `manual` 182 —
**codex and copilot have zero dispatches, ever**, while the README advertises all three.
Second, D6's decisive row — light mode has *"one window shared by everything"*, therefore
*"light cannot replace dark"* (`factory-loop-requirements.md:629,634`) — is contradicted by
this repo's own measurement at `steering-surfaces-design.md:25`, which records a subagent
body as *"never enters the parent … low — isolated context"*. **Subagents are isolated, not
shared.** The stated reason for refusing host-native dispatch does not hold.

## What must survive any replacement

Not everything in D6 is refuted, and these are the non-negotiables:

- **D1's singleton deterministic supervisor** owning the base checkout and the serial merge
  queue (`factory-design.md:47-61`). A host fan-out must not become a second writer.
- **D9's prompt-hash reproducibility** — *"two runs of the same node are diffable"*
  (`factory-design.md:295`). `prompt_sha256` is already recorded and must stay meaningful.
- **Metering.** The hazard `flr:602` names is real: a host-spawned agent that fans out
  inside itself is invisible to `run-records.json`. Whatever replaces `-p` must record
  spend per unit of work or the spend ceiling (5 correct firings) stops working.
- **Agent-agnosticism as a contract**, even if unexercised: the host path must be one
  runner among several, not a hard dependency on Claude.

## Open question this bead must answer before it builds

Whether the host runtime can be driven **non-interactively from the engine** at all, or
only from a live session — because the supervisor is a subprocess, not a session. If only
the latter, this becomes "the engine emits work the session executes", which is a
different design and should be re-scoped rather than forced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a unit of work, when it is dispatched through the host runtime, then its spend is
  recorded in `run-records.json` exactly as a `-p` dispatch is - check: a test asserts a
  record with non-zero tokens and a `prompt_sha256` exists after a host dispatch.
- Given concurrent host dispatches, when they land, then the serial merge queue and the
  singleton supervisor lock still hold - check: a test asserts two host lanes cannot both
  write the base checkout.
- Given a repo whose configured runner is not claude, when a dispatch is requested, then
  the engine still dispatches - check: a test asserts the host path is one runner among
  several and does not become mandatory.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly loop run <bead> --runner host` completes a unit of work without spawning
`claude -p`, and `uv run basicly usage` shows its spend.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `tests/test_runner.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `150000`
- depends on: none
payload.title: Dispatch through the host agent runtime instead of spawning a headless CLI

payload.text: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-13 - dispatch shape is HYBRID: host runtime for same-vendor, subprocess for cross-vendor. Claude lanes spawn as real subagents so declared skills: preload and per-subagent usage is emitted; codex and copilot stay subprocess. This is the shape factory-loop.md section 11.7 records a competing harness running in production - an existence proof, not a design. Do not re-litigate. Named failure mode, to be watched: two dispatch paths where the vendor-specific one carries the features, so cross-vendor parity rots quietly - any lane touching this must say what the copilot path loses.

basicly-ey58 shipped 2026-08-13 by PROMPT INJECTION rather than the Agent SDK, so this bead no longer inherits ey58's skills-preload justification - that problem is solved for all three families without a dependency. What remains here is the hybrid dispatch shape decided today, and per-subagent usage emission, which prompt injection does NOT provide. Re-scope accordingly before dispatching: the remaining case is observability and the host-runtime spawn, not skill preloading.

payload.close_reason: fired only on a special cause: a c-chart with a Poisson floor, dispatching retrospector from _rework and not as a phase rung (383eaba)
payload.description:
## Context

`retrospector` is authored, projected to both agent roots, vendored to consumers, loads the `root-cause` skill, and has a `ROLE_BY_PHASE` entry (`roles.py:69`, `retrospective -> retrospector`). It can never be invoked, because RETROSPECTIVE is not a phase: `loop._HANDLERS` has seven keys and `retrospective` is not among them, and `config.LOOP_PHASES` does not carry it.

So the harness ships a role, a skill and a map entry for a state that does not exist. That is a dead definition of the same shape the catalog eval exists to catch, one layer up.

## Why this is the mechanism half of the architectural work, not a loop nicety

`factory-loop.md` section 3.2 is explicit that RETROSPECTIVE is **not a lane state**: it is a conditional process over the gate-failure ledger, fired by a *computed* signal.

- Special cause - a point beyond three sigma, or a non-random run or trend inside the limits - fires it.
- Common cause - a single failure inside the limits - **does not**. Acting on that is tampering, which Deming's funnel experiment shows *increases* variation in a stable process.

That guard is the thing the architectural work actually needs. Without it every smell is worth a bead, which is how a backlog of thirteen findings accumulates and never drains. With it, the system answers *is this shape worth acting on* deterministically, from its own ledger, before any judged dispatch is paid for.

This repo has the anti-pattern on record: beads were filed off single occurrences during the very session that produced the requirements document, and `basicly-jr0l` carries twelve follow-ups that named one truncation while none asked why the trigger fired.

## What must be built

1. The state, with an entry predicate that is the computed signal rather than a phase transition - so it is not a rung in the lane ladder and a lane never sits in it.
2. The signal itself, over the recorded gate-failure history: a point beyond three sigma, or a non-random run or trend within the limits.
3. The dispatch of `retrospector` when it fires, metered like every other dispatch.
4. The output contract already specified in section 3.2: a named control, its tier (control / warning / documentation), and the class of defects it covers - never the why-chain. A documentation-tier outcome is recorded as a downgrade with the reason no stronger control was available.
5. Under D25, the output lands as a **diff against catalog YAML**, never as prose advice, and never reaches the catalog without a human at any grant level.

## Acceptance

- Given a gate-failure history with no special-cause signal, when the ledger is evaluated, then RETROSPECTIVE does not fire and no dispatch is made.
- Given a recorded point beyond three sigma, when the ledger is evaluated, then RETROSPECTIVE fires and names the point that triggered it.
- Given a non-random run or trend inside the control limits, when the ledger is evaluated, then RETROSPECTIVE fires and names which of the two patterns it detected.
- Given RETROSPECTIVE fires, when the engine resolves the role, then `roles.resolve_role` returns `retrospector` and it reaches the dispatch argv.
- Given a completed retrospective, when its output is read, then it carries a named control, a tier from control/warning/documentation, and the defect class it covers, and it is expressed as a diff against a catalog source rather than as prose.
- Given the same output, when it is applied, then a human approves it regardless of the autonomy level in force.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/loop_state.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`

Retro finding, session 2026-08-13. Proposed by the agent, not self-applied. Two rejections, three
lost commits between them.

## Context

**1. `br update --status closed` is refused.** Terminal transitions must go through
`br close <id> --reason "..."` so close-policy (close reason, acceptance criteria, attribution) is
enforced. The error names the remedy, but only after the command has failed inside a chained
command - and this repo rule is that a rejected step in a chain leaves the chain half-run.

**2. Any hand-run `br` write re-exports machine-specific absolute paths** into
`.beads/issues.jsonl`, and the `tracker-path-scan` pre-commit hook then blocks the commit naming
hundreds of lines. A `basicly loop advance` repairs it automatically, which is exactly why it only
ever appears on commits made by hand after tracker work done outside the loop. Repair:

```sh
uv run python -c "from pathlib import Path; import basicly.br as b; print(b.scrub_export(Path(.)))"
```

then re-stage. It reports the number of lines scrubbed.

**The diff shape is the tell, and it matters because it mimics a known catastrophe.** Before
scrubbing, a commit filing one bead plus two comments showed as `752 insertions, 752 deletions`;
after scrubbing, `+3 -2`. A whole-file tracker diff reads exactly like the WAL corruption the
skill already warns about, and the two are told apart by comparing the id SETS either side, not
the line counts.

This session hit both. The second fired twice, in the same session in which its remedy had already
been written down elsewhere - which is the argument for it being in the skill rather than in a
note.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Run `br update <id> --status closed` - refused, naming `br close`.
- Run any `br create` or `br comments add`, then `git add .beads && git commit` - the
  `tracker-path-scan` hook blocks with `machine-specific path(s) in the staged tracker export`.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/skills/tool-br/skill.yaml`

The owner's first answer was option 2, strike the two architecture rows. The repo's own rule says a
capability claim on a consumer surface is exercised before it is published. Exercising it first is
what changed the answer.

`uv run basicly health` at main ceedc3c:

```text
Agent health
agent    runs   fail   rework   score
claude    163    18%      17%    0.78
manual    194     0%       2%    0.99
drift: behavioral regression flagged for claude (recent 5-run failure rate up >= 20%)
```

`--json` emits `schema_version: 1` with per-agent `failure_rate`, `rework_rate` and `health_score`.

Three things follow.

The architecture rows at `architecture.md:929` and `:1561` are **not** a false claim. The command
runs, reads the run-record log, and returns real numbers. Striking them would delete a true
description of a shipped CLI surface, which is the opposite defect from the one the bead names.

The survey's finding stands unchanged and is narrower than it read: nothing in the engine invokes
the report. That is the absence of an operational consumer, not the absence of a capability. The
bead's own Context says the module is clean, pure and read-only and that nothing is wrong with the
code, so the two are separable and only one is true.

The report produced a live finding on its first run. The claude runner carries an 18 percent
dispatch failure rate and a 17 percent rework rate over 163 runs, and the drift check flagged a
recent regression. A signal that fires on the first invocation is evidence for wiring a caller, not
for retiring the surface. Note the population is still two agents, claude and manual, against a
README advertising three.

Recommendation for the owner, replacing the strike: take option 1 and wire one operational caller,
the supervisor pass report the bead already names. The dead-code baseline entry at
`wired_or_deleted.py:153` and the seven field entries at `:184-190` are then removed by the wiring
rather than left standing under a struck claim.

Nothing was edited under this comment. The architecture rows are untouched and the bead stays open.

[harness-decision] the owner answers option 1 — wire an operational caller, 2026-08-14

The bead offered two answers. The owner takes the first: name the health report as an input and wire
one operational caller. The two architecture rows at `architecture.md:929` and `:1561` stay, because
exercising the command showed them to be true rather than aspirational.

The evidence that decided it is the comment above this one. `basicly health` runs, reads the
run-record log, and returned a finding on its first invocation: claude at an 18 percent dispatch
failure rate and a 17 percent rework rate over 163 runs, with the drift check flagging a recent
regression. A report that fires on its first run has a consumer; what it lacked was a caller.

## What the implementation owes

The caller is the supervisor pass report, which the bead already names. The signal belongs beside
the band line and the tree-growth line, on the same pass line an operator reads, so a regression in
a runner's own reliability is visible where every other pass-level number already is.

Two things the wiring must not do, each because this repository has paid for the opposite.

It must not block. `basicly health` is a sizing-adjacent signal with no recorded correct firing, so
under D23 it is observability: recorded on the run, surfaced in the pass line, falsifiable against
the ledger, and never a gate. A prediction that blocks is a prediction that must be right.

It must not spawn anything or cost a token. The report is a pure read over a log the engine already
writes. If the wiring reaches a model, it is the wrong wiring.

payload.acceptance_criteria: When test-discipline states its fixture rule then it requires at least one test to drive a live capture of a format wherever one exists in the tree, so a hand-built fixture cannot be the only evidence a parser is right.
payload.description:
## Context

Session 2026-08-14, `basicly-ejdm.2`. Nine unit tests over hand-built transcript turns all passed
against a pairing rule that was **wrong on every real transcript**. The demonstration caught it,
not the suite.

The rule paired a turn's tokens against the immediately preceding line. A real claude transcript
forwards the tool result as a `user` event carrying no usage, which sits between the call and the
turn that pays for the answer:

```text
assistant  tokens= 26234 tools=[Agent]   <- the call
user       tokens=     0 tools=[]        <- the forwarded result, no usage
assistant  tokens=     0 tools=[]
assistant  tokens= 26635 tools=[]        <- the turn that pays for the answer
```

So the rule reported a real captured lane as **100% unattributed** - a confident figure measuring
nothing. Every hand-built fixture had an assistant turn adjacent to its predecessor, because that
is the shape a person writes when they are thinking about the rule rather than the format.

## Why the existing guidance did not catch it

`test-discipline` covers isolation, order-independence and asserting on observable behaviour. All
nine tests satisfied every one of those and were still blind, because the defect was in the
**shape of the input**, not in the shape of the test.

The repo already had the evidence: `tests/test_runner_subagent_stream.py` holds a stream captured
from a live Claude Code 2.1.226 dispatch, with a comment saying every field is verbatim from that
capture. Driving it took one scratch script.

## Proposed change, for a human to apply

Add one rule to `test-discipline`: **where a live capture of the format exists in the tree, at
least one test must drive it.** A hand-built fixture encodes what the author believes the format
is, and the interesting defects are in the difference between that and what the format does.

The related rule this repo already learned from the other direction - "a dependency's error text
must be observed, not composed" (an invented fixture made a retry path dead code through two
fixes) - is the same finding for error strings. This generalises it to formats.

D25 forbids an agent amending the catalog, so this is filed rather than applied.

payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

`br close` accepts `[IDS]...` — its own `--help` says so. `mirror._close_drafts`
refuses anything but one id:

```text
TrackerDivergenceError: br close names no single issue: close basicly-a basicly-b ...
```

Under `dual`, `br.run_br` spawns br **before** it mirrors, and `_mirror_write`
re-raises `TrackerDivergenceError`. So a multi-id close through the seam closes every
named bead on br, then fails the command with the two stores already diverged — the
guard producing the state it exists to prevent.

`_create_drafts` is the same defect one translator over, and it fired on this bead's
own sibling: it parses `stdout` as JSON, so a `br create` without `--json` creates the
record on br and then raises. `basicly-e2mz.23` was filed that way and its create event
had to be backfilled by hand. `_update_drafts` needs the same check, since `br update`
also takes multiple ids.

The general shape: a translator that refuses **after** br has accepted the write turns a
caller's ordinary argv into a divergence. Either the argv is validated before the spawn,
or the seam normalises it (split the ids, add `--json`) rather than refusing it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a `br close` naming more than one issue when the write is mirrored then one
  status draft is emitted per id rather than a refusal — check:
  `uv run pytest tests/test_mirror.py -k multi_id_close -q`
- Given an argv the mirror cannot translate when the write is attempted then it is
  refused before br is spawned rather than after — check:
  `uv run pytest tests/test_br_seam.py -k refused_before_spawn -q`

## Scope

- `src/basicly/mirror.py`
- `src/basicly/br.py`
- `tests/test_mirror.py`
- `tests/test_br_seam.py`

This bead read the nine fixture commits on `harness/basicly-rn0o` as call sites that
"ran with the live worktree as their repo root", and asked for a gate asserting the
fixture root is under `tmp_path`. Both halves are wrong, and `basicly-e2mz.15` had
already established why: git resolves which repository it is talking to from `GIT_DIR`
first and from `cwd` only afterwards, so one inherited variable retargets every fixture's
git call whatever tmp path it passes. That bead's own words - "the cause is not in the
call sites ... they correctly pass cwd=<fixture repo>".

So the proposed gate would have passed while the damage happened. That is now a test
rather than an argument: `test_a_fixture_root_under_tmp_path_is_not_what_protects_the_
repository` asserts the fixture root IS under tmp_path and then watches the victim
repository take the commit anyway.

The timing settles that this is a second observation and not a second defect. The nine
commits are 2026-08-14 19:51:21-19:51:42; the scrub that fixes the class, `c0dc86d`,
landed at 20:26:25 - 35 minutes later. The damage predates its own fix.

What shipped anyway, because the coverage gap under it was real: `e2mz.15`'s guard binds
the scrub against **two** named incident sites in a subprocess, while four modules commit
a fixture repository. `tests/conftest.py` gains an autouse assertion that no forbidden
`GIT_*` survives into a test or is left behind by one, so the whole population is bound
for the cost of a dict scan, and a test that sets the variable itself is caught where it
happened rather than in whatever runs next. Probed rather than assumed: a throwaway test
setting `GIT_DIR` fails on the after-check and names the variable.

`INCIDENT_SITES` is deliberately not extended. The scrub is process-wide at import, so a
third and fourth subprocess run would re-prove one mechanism at the price of two more
full pytest spawns.

Demonstration: the criterion names `tests/test_landing_anchors.py -k fixture_root`, which
selects nothing - the test belongs to the module that owns the concern. Corrected check:
`uv run pytest tests/test_repo_isolation.py -k fixture_root -q`.

Verified: 4092 passed; `[verify] PASS (mode: fast)`, 21 checks. `tests/conftest.py`
density fell 67.4% to 64.3% against a frozen 68.7.

Decision 6a - reset `harness/basicly-rn0o` to `ea37fe2` and force-push - is unblocked on
the merits rather than on this gate: the hazard was fixed on 2026-08-14 and the branch is
carrying the evidence of an incident that can no longer recur.

[harness-info] closed under owner decision 3a — stop writing it **and** scrub history.

The open question this bead said it had to settle first is answered by that decision:
R6 binds the `actor` field, and the non-identifying form is no form at all. Nothing in
the live path was writing a person there — `br.import_export` defaults `actor` to `""`
and the CLI passes none — so the 3,775 values were the 2026-08-07 hand-run import's.

**The leak was wider than filed, and the wider half is the one still being written.**
The bead measured the ledger. The committed `.beads/issues.jsonl` carried the username
on **813 of 876 records**, because br writes `created_by` on every record it mints and
`migrate._plan_record` copies every non-structural field into the `created` payload
verbatim. So a fresh `basicly tracker import` re-published it. Inside the ledger it sat
on `asserted_by` (3,176), `created_by` (736), `assignee` (56) and 4 free-text values —
not only on `actor`, which is where the bead looked.

**Stop writing it.** `redact.redact_committed` = paths, then identity, and the four
ledger/export write sites in `br.py` use it. The order is load-bearing: the placeholder
holds characters the path rules' tail class excludes, so identity first would leave the
directory layout published. Identity is deliberately outside `MACHINE_PATH_RULES` — a
username is not a shape, only the running machine knows the string — so the mirror test
that holds the hook's rule tuple equal to the module's is untouched.

**Scrub history.** `br.scrub_ledger` rewrote **4,812 of 5,079** events, and
`scrub_export` **811 of 876** records. This is the one place the design edits a line
rather than appending one (work-tracker §4.4); an append cannot un-publish a string,
which is why §4.2 reserves it for an explicit owner decision.

The re-minting is the part that could have gone wrong quietly. An event id covers kind
plus payload, so a redacted payload has to be re-minted or `fsck` reads every scrubbed
event as inconsistent — and the generation the id folds in is **not written on the
line**. It is derived as the occurrence count of an identical (record, kind, payload),
and the derivation was proved before it was used: it reproduced **all 5,079** stored ids
exactly. After the rewrite, all 5,079 re-mint from their own content and there are 0
duplicate ids. `basicly tracker shadow` reports 372 disagreements, **every one
`query='gates'` and excused as history** — the gate-import gap decision 1a covers — and
zero on records, phase or ready.

**The gate.** `tracker-path-scan` now covers `.basicly/ledger/events-*.jsonl` beside
`.beads/*.jsonl`, and reports a `machine-username` rule built per run from
`getpass.getuser()`. Positive control, run against the pre-scrub ledger kept for it: the
gate reports **4,812 findings**, which is exactly the count the scrub repaired, and 0 on
the repaired file. Its stated limit: it cannot see a *teammate's* username already in
the file — that is `[[privacy.denied]]`'s job, and this repo configures none.

**What is deliberately left.** 75 occurrences of the git handle `niksavis` survive in
each file. The rule is word-bounded, so a name the username merely prefixes is not
touched — and that handle is this project's own published identity, in the
`git+https://github.com/...` install URL architecture §9 ships. A gate that redacted it
would fight the README.

Verified: 4106 passed; `[verify] PASS (mode: fast)`, 21 checks.
Demonstration: `uv run pytest tests/test_tracker_path_scan_identity.py tests/test_br_scrub_ledger.py -q`
(13 tests). `scrub_ledger` is wired at `merge.commit_tracker_state`, beside `scrub_export`
and on the same commit path, so `wired-or-deleted` and vulture both bind it.

[harness-info] cutover state at 2026-08-15 close, measured rather than claimed.

Steps 1-3 have run. `basicly tracker import` is re-runnable (`vkh0.23`), the shadow
differential ran on `dual` with an **empty** declared baseline, and `[tracker] mode` is
`dual` (`u4xu`, closed here - it had landed and stayed open). The ledger holds **5,081
events over 873 records** against an 876-record export; the residual 3 are beads filed by
hand through `br`, which is `vkh0.24` demonstrating itself and is deliberately not repaired.

**Step 4 is not dispatchable and the whole of the gap is one query.** `basicly tracker
shadow` reports `conclusive: yes`, `clean: no`, on **372 disagreements of which every one
is `query='gates'`** - zero on records, phase or ready. The owned side reports `missing`
for every gate because gate *history* was never imported. That is decision 1a's one-shot
`br gate list --robot` dump, not a defect hunt.

**Two defects in the dual write are open and both were found by using it**, not by a
survey: `e2mz.23` (P0) the mirror fails **open** when the tracker-mode reader is
unregistered - a caller importing `basicly.br` without `basicly.config` writes to br and
appends nothing; `e2mz.24` a translator that refuses *after* br has taken the write, on a
multi-id `close` and on a `create` without `--json`. Both were hit here and both
backfilled from `mirror.drafts`. Read them before writing through the seam.

**R6 is discharged on both halves** (`r166`, closed): the OS username is out of the ledger
(4,812 of 5,081 events rewritten) and out of the export (811 records), redaction is at the
write seam, and `tracker-path-scan` covers the ledger with a positive control measuring
4,812 findings before and 0 after.

`run_br` call sites outside the seam: **28 across 12 modules**, down from 32.

[harness-info] backlog state at 2026-08-15 close.

`e2mz.20` and `e2mz.21` closed. `.20` had landed and stayed open. `.21` closed with its
**premise refuted**: it asked for a gate asserting a fixture repo root is under `tmp_path`,
which would have passed while the damage happened, because `GIT_DIR` retargets git whatever
path a fixture passes - `e2mz.15` had established exactly that. The timing confirms a second
observation rather than a second defect: the nine fixture commits are 2026-08-14 19:51:21-42
and the scrub that fixes the class landed at 20:26:25. What shipped instead is the real gap
under it - an autouse `GIT_*` assertion in `tests/conftest.py`, binding the scrub over the
whole test population instead of the two sites `test_repo_isolation.py` names.

Two filed from measurement: `e2mz.23` (P0) and `e2mz.24`, both dual-write mirror defects,
both hit while closing the beads above.

**One finding cuts across the epic and is worth a gate of its own.** Five beads touched this
session named a demonstration check that selects **zero** tests, against positive controls
collecting 210, 142, 87 and 23 in the files they name. D18's plan gate refuses a field that
is absent or names nothing runnable; a backticked span matching nothing passes it. The
remedy is to run the criterion's own command and read the collected count. Recorded in
`factory-loop.md` §3.3 and in the plan's standing constraints.

payload.description:
## Context

The plan gate refuses a `demonstration` field that is absent, multi-line, or names
nothing backticked. `plan_gate.demonstration_fault` checks the field's **form** and
never runs the command, so a backticked span that selects **zero** tests passes.

Measured 2026-08-15: five beads were closed or worked in one session naming a
demonstration of the form `uv run pytest <file> -k <expr>` where the expression
selects zero tests, against positive controls collecting 210, 142, 87 and 23 in the
very files they name. Every real regression existed under another name and passed.
So the field was refused for being absent or unquoted, and accepted for being wrong.

Confirmed against the tree 2026-08-16: `plan_gate.py` contains no `subprocess` and no
`run(`, against a positive control of 5 occurrences in `verify.py`.

## Why a third form rule is not the answer

A form rule cannot tell a command that selects nothing from one that selects
everything. Running the criterion's own command and reading the collected count is
free, deterministic, and impossible to satisfy by rewording.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a planned child whose demonstration names a pytest selector matching no test
  when the plan gate runs then the child is refused at the same rung as an absent
  field - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_plan_gate.py -k zero_selection -q`
- Given a planned child whose demonstration selects at least one test then the gate
  admits it - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_plan_gate.py -k zero_selection -q`

## Scope

- `src/basicly/plan_gate.py`
- `tests/test_plan_gate.py`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/plan_gate.py`
- `tests/test_plan_gate.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_plan_gate.py -k zero_selection -q`

## Context

`docs/requirements/factory-loop.md` records, as a measured finding dated 2026-08-09,
that agent definitions hot-reload and are not read once at process start, with two
named exceptions. That claim does not hold for the path the engine and an operator
actually use.

Measured 2026-08-16. `.basicly/core/agents/architect/agent.yaml` gained `Write` and
`Edit`; `basicly agents-build` wrote `.claude/agents/architect.md` and

## Why this matters beyond one dispatch

The catalog is the source and the projection is the delivery, so a projection that a
running host ignores makes every roster change invisible until a restart nobody
schedules. It is also the second instance of the shape this repo keeps paying for: a
capability asserted in a document, believed, and never probed.

is the same defect `basicly-wbsz.3` was filed for.

payload.description:
Filed 2026-08-15 after the gate `basicly-miqr` shipped that morning fired four times in
one afternoon, on one changeset, all from the same cause.

## Observed

A single change adding 18 lines to `src/basicly/loop.py` invalidated **20 citations** across
`docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` and `docs/requirements/factory-loop.md`. Trimming a
docstring in the same file later moved two of them back and invalidated two more. None of
the underlying claims became false: every one still named the right symbol.

## The gate is right and the citation form is the defect

`check_docs_citations.py` already resolves the symbol - its own failure text reads
`outside the symbol named here - `foreign_dirt` is at :509`. So it knows the answer it is
asking the author to write down. A `file.py:line` citation is a claim that decays on every
insertion above it, while `file.py::symbol` would not.

Two rules it already enforces stay exactly as they are: a cited line must be live code, and
a cited line must fall inside the symbol named beside it. A symbol form satisfies both by
construction and removes the churn.

## Why the churn is worse than noise

Bulk-fixing them invites the failure the standing constraints already name. A fixer written
from the gate output rewrote `loop.py:1637` to `loop.py:749` because two citations shared one
document line and the regex took the first suggestion. The wrong number was caught by hand,
which is the audit the "a bulk find-replace needs a line-by-line audit" rule requires - and
the reason to remove the need for the fixer rather than to improve it.

## Not a request to weaken the gate

The one real correction found in the same afternoon is the argument for keeping it: the plan
cited `loop.dispatch_prompt` at a line, and that symbol had moved to `dispatch_brief`
entirely. A symbol-form citation would have failed on the missing symbol rather than
silently pointing at whatever now occupies the line.

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_docs_citations.py`
- `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md`
- `docs/requirements/factory-loop.md`
- `tests/test_check_docs_citations.py`

`_on_verify` now resolves the ship checkpoint through `policy.approve_checkpoint_guarded`
with `ctx.grant_root`. The supervisor passes `session.root_issue`, so the supervised path
reaches the grant. `basicly loop advance` accepts no `--root`, so `ctx.grant_root` is None
and the guarded call defaults to the issue itself - which carries no grant when the grant is

Observed - `basicly loop advance basicly-b2n2` returns
`[blocked] verify -> verify: ship checkpoint awaiting human approval` while
`basicly loop preflight basicly-u2hl` reports `ship pending - the live L3 grant delegates
it`, because the grant is on `basicly-u2hl` and nothing tells `advance` so.

This is not the same defect as `u2hl.56`, which was the parked path not asking at all. This
is the hand path having no way to say which session it belongs to. `loop run` already takes
`--root` for exactly this.

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a tracker write made outside the engine seam when dual write is active then either it reaches the owned ledger or the record carries a marker the shadow differential excludes it by - check: uv run pytest tests/test_br_seam.py -k hand_write -q
payload.description:
Measured 2026-08-15, the day dual write was activated.

`br._mirror_write` sits in the engine seam, so a write made by spawning the `br`
binary directly never enters it. Demonstrated on `basicly-b2n2`: three hand writes
were made after the flip - `br update --description` adding a scope block, `br
update --add-label`, and `br dep add` - and the ledger still holds exactly four
events for that record, all four carrying `provenance: EXTRACTED` from the import.
None of the three arrived.

```
grep record=basicly-b2n2 .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl  ->  4 events
  seq 1 created   seq 2 status   seq 3 edge   seq 4 comment
  scope text present: False
```

The positive control is the same session: a write driven through `br.add_comment`
landed immediately, `seq 9`, `provenance: dual-write`.

## Why this is a defect rather than the documented human carve out

Section 5 step 5 of work-tracker.md deliberately leaves **human prose comments** on
the external side, and that is fine - a comment is evidence, not structure. This is
different in kind: `create`, `update` and `dep add` are the record and the graph, and
a hand write silently moves one store and not the other. The shadow differential then
reports a real divergence it cannot distinguish from a dual write failure, which is
the exact confusion `basicly-c357` narrowed the scoping rules to remove.

It also cannot be repaired indefinitely. `basicly tracker import` refuses a ledger
holding a post flip record, so once any bead is created under `dual` the import stops
being available as a way to close a hand write gap.

## What the answer probably is, stated as options rather than a decision

Either the harness grows an owned write surface a human is expected to use, or the
seam moves down so the binary is never spawned outside it, or the divergence is
declared acceptable and the differential learns to exclude hand written records -
which needs a marker on the record saying so, and nothing writes one today.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/br.py`
- `tests/test_br_seam.py`
payload.title: A hand run br write bypasses the dual write mirror and diverges the two stores

payload.description:
## Context

`pre-commit` snapshots the working tree before each hook and compares it after. A file
that changed during a hook is reported as **modified by that hook**. A concurrent
writer is indistinguishable from a hook write, so the blame lands on whichever hook was
running when the write arrived.

Measured 2026-08-16. Three commits in a row failed with
`catalog-lint: files were modified by this hook`, while `catalog lint: OK` printed in
the same output. A whole-tree probe cleared the command:

```
git ls-files -z | xargs -0 md5sum | sort > before
uv run basicly catalog lint
git ls-files -z | xargs -0 md5sum | sort > after
diff before after   ->  no output
```

The real writer was a background agent editing `docs/architecture/architecture.md`.
Its diff went from 416 to 528 insertions between the second and third attempts, so it
wrote inside the commit window. An hour went into the wrong hook.

## Why the framework cannot answer this and we can

`pre-commit` has no way to tell a hook's write from anybody else's, and it is not ours
to change. `basicly commit` already wraps `git commit`, so it is the one place that can
snapshot the tracked tree before the gate and compare after a failure. A file that
changed but is touched by no hook is a concurrent modification, and saying so turns an
hour of hunting into one line.

Post-hoc diagnosis on failure only. Not a refusal, and not a pre-flight heuristic on
file age - a human editing in another window is a false positive, and a gate that cries
wolf gets waived.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a tracked file changes while the commit gate runs when the commit fails then
  the output names that file as concurrently modified rather than leaving the hook
  blamed - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_commit.py -k concurrent -q`
- Given no file changes during a failing gate then the output says nothing about
  concurrency - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_commit.py -k concurrent -q`

## Scope

- `src/basicly/commit.py`
- `tests/test_commit.py`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/commit.py`
- `tests/test_commit.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_commit.py -k concurrent -q`
payload.title: a concurrent write is blamed on whichever hook was running

payload.description:
## Context

`loop preflight` forecasts a pass at `per_lane x min(concurrency, open_children)`.
Provisioning does not use `concurrency`; `loop._ensure_child_worktrees` computes
`room = wt_config.concurrency - len(existing)` and seeds at most that many. So the
forecast over-states by exactly the number of worktrees already live.

Measured 2026-08-16 on `basicly-e2mz`, with 2 live worktrees and `concurrency = 5`:

```
worktrees: 2 live
forecast:  ~110949235 tokens if all 5 lanes start (per-lane x min(cap 5, 39 open))
```

The pass can seed 3 lanes, not 5. The honest forecast is ~66,569,541.

## Why the size of the error matters rather than the error

The figure exists to size a grant. An operator reading 110,949,235 against a
100,000,000 grant concludes the pass cannot run and either mints a larger grant than
the work needs or does not run it. Both were nearly done here. `admit_pass_spend`
totals the pass and refuses the whole thing on one violation, so the number a human
compares against the grant is the number that decides whether anything is dispatched
at all.

The preflight's own docstring states the intent — "the interesting number is what a
*full* fan-out would need, because that is what a budget has to be minted for" — and a
full fan-out is bounded by room, not by the cap.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given live worktrees exist when the preflight forecasts a pass then the lane count
  is the room provisioning would use rather than the raw cap - check:
  `uv run pytest tests/test_cli_loop.py -k forecast_room -q`
- Given no live worktrees then the forecast is unchanged - check:
  `uv run pytest tests/test_cli_loop.py -k forecast_room -q`

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_cli_loop.py`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_cli_loop.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_cli_loop.py -k forecast_room -q`
payload.title: the pass forecast counts the cap where provisioning counts the room

Observed 2026-08-16 during a supervised pass on basicly-e2mz.

The pass landed basicly-e2mz.13 and dispatched the curator at SHIP at 16:41. The log's last write was 16:41. Eleven minutes later the pass looked dead from outside. It was not.

Evidence taken at 16:48: the supervisor pid was alive since 16:19; the curator pid was state S with 19 threads; rchar moved 10.96 GB to 13.32 GB over 25 seconds; a tool subprocess was spawned mid-sample.

Why it matters: every lane dispatch prints a running line with elapsed seconds and a token count. A ship dispatch prints nothing. The architecture document also records that the ship dispatch carries no watchdog and no stream meter, so a wedged curator hangs the pass until the caller's own outer timeout, and an operator cannot tell that apart from normal work.

Adjacent to basicly-8veb but not the same defect. 8veb was the supervisor hiding progress when stdout is a pipe; lane progress reached the redirected file here without trouble.

Acceptance criteria. Given a supervised pass that dispatches a role at ship, when that dispatch is in flight, then the pass shall print a progress line carrying the role, the elapsed seconds and the token count, on the same cadence as a lane dispatch. Given that dispatch exceeds its bound, then a watchdog shall terminate it and record the reason rather than leaving the pass to the caller's outer timeout.

Found 2026-08-16 while filing basicly-e2mz.29 and basicly-e2mz.31 through the seam.

The seam refused two update fields, each with a precise remedy in the message:

  br update --acceptance-criteria has no owned-ledger equivalent, so mirroring it would drop the field br just wrote; add it to br_argv.UPDATE_FIELD_FLAGS
  br update --description has no owned-ledger equivalent, so mirroring it would drop the field br just wrote; add it to br_argv.UPDATE_FIELD_FLAGS

Measured: br_argv.UPDATE_FIELD_FLAGS holds only --external-ref, --type and -t. A seam-routed filing can therefore set a title and nothing else.

This is the seam behaving correctly. It stopped rather than diverging the two stores, which is the stated invariant. The defect is the narrowness of the translator, not the refusal.

Consequence today: basicly-e2mz.29 and basicly-e2mz.31 carry their evidence and criteria as comments, and neither has a structured acceptance_criteria field, so the definition-of-ready lint will block both until this lands. That is why both declare a blocks dependency on this issue.

Acceptance criteria. Given a seam-routed br update that names a field the owned ledger can hold, when the write runs, then the seam shall translate and mirror it rather than refuse. Given a field the owned ledger genuinely cannot hold, then the refusal shall stand and shall name the field.

Observed 2026-08-16 during a supervised pass on basicly-e2mz.

docs/architecture/architecture.md, section Roles at dispatch, states:

  The curator and the retrospector are both inert on the supervised landing pass, which has no watchdog and no stream meter of its own. Under the supervisor they run only after the ship approval, on the interactive driver.

The run contradicts the second sentence. After basicly-e2mz.13 landed, the curator was dispatched with the supervisor process itself as its parent, not an interactive driver. Preflight had reported 'ship pending - the live L3 grant delegates it', so the supervisor approved the ship itself and dispatched.

The first sentence appears to hold: the dispatch showed no progress line and no watchdog, which is basicly-e2mz.29.

Acceptance criteria. Given the architecture document is read at the Roles at dispatch section, when it describes where the curator runs under a supervised pass, then it shall state that the supervisor dispatches the curator itself once a grant delegates the ship approval, and it shall not claim an interactive driver is required.

payload.title: a second teardown of an already cleaned worktree fails the whole pass

payload.text:
Observed 2026-08-16 on a supervised pass over basicly-e2mz with --max-passes 3.

Both lanes landed and both worktrees were cleaned. The pass then attempted a SECOND teardown of one of them and exited 1. The final three lines of the run:

  Cleaned up worktree 'basicly-e2mz-16' (worktree + branch + metadata).
  no worktree named 'basicly-e2mz-16': no session record and no registered worktree matches it. Run `git worktree list` to see them.
  SUPERVISE EXIT 1

Two consequences, and the second is the expensive one.

1. The pass reports failure after a fully successful round. basicly-e2mz.13 merged as 8ccf6d5 and closed; basicly-e2mz.16 merged as ada298a with verify green.

2. basicly-e2mz.16 was left OPEN at phase ship with a worktree binding to basicly-e2mz-16, which no longer exists on disk. `basicly loop status basicly-e2mz.16` reports that binding against a `git worktree list` that does not hold it. An open bead whose work has landed is the exact trap recorded on basicly-u6jq.1: the next pass adopts it and provisions a worktree for work that already shipped.

The teardown is not idempotent, and it should be. A teardown of an already absent worktree states the same fact as a teardown that ran.

Acceptance criteria. Given a lane whose worktree has already been torn down, when teardown runs again, then it shall report the worktree as already absent and exit zero rather than raising. Given a lane that has merged and passed verify, when its teardown raises for any reason, then the pass shall still clear the lane's worktree binding and shall not leave the bead open at ship.

payload.description:
## Context

On 2026-08-16 every lane failure in the session was operator error, not an engine defect. The engine refused correctly and named the cause every time. The owner asked for a remedy, and the remedy is not simply more prose in the always-on files.

This repository already states the hierarchy: git hooks are the deterministic floor, and guidance is what you use when a gate cannot express the check. The always-on baseline is also measured at 7014 to 7343 characters and is at its cap, so a new always-on rule costs something real and must earn it.

## The four failures and the tier each one belongs in

1. A stray 7.6 MB file under the tracker directory was committed by the tracker-state rollup, which stages the whole directory. CODE. Filed as basicly-vkh0.31.
2. The ignore list missed the file because it is a denylist of suffixes and the name ended `.recovered` rather than `.db`. CODE, same bead: stage known paths instead of relying on ignore rules.
3. `basicly loop run` on a child defaults the session root to the child, so a grant on the parent is never consulted, and the refusal does not name the `--root` flag that fixes it. Two dispatch attempts died on this. CODE: either default a child root to its parent, or name the flag in the refusal text.
4. A subagent was told to write its output into `docs/architecture/` inside the base checkout. An actively written file in the base checkout blocks every lane landing, and it blocked three. GUIDANCE: no gate can see the intent behind a subagent brief.

## What this bead must not become

A fragment that says be careful. Each item above either becomes a check that refuses the thing, or it does not land. Item 4 is the only guidance candidate, and it should be authored as a catalog source, never a hand-written discoverable markdown file, per the catalog-authoring rule.

## Sequencing

Run after the architecture rewrite is verified and swapped in. The rewrite renumbers sections that code cites, and doing both at once would tangle two unrelated diffs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given each of the four failures when its remedy has landed then three are deterministic checks that refuse the failing input and name the cause, and the fourth is a catalog-authored guidance entry scoped to the narrowest tier that reaches the reader
- Given a proposed remedy that is only prose advising more care then it is rejected and the bead records why

## Scope

- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `.basicly/core/fragments/**`
- `tests/**`

## Steps to Reproduce

`FORCE_COLOR=3` is set in this machine shell environment. Measured 2026-08-16:

    uv run pytest tests/test_ui.py -q
    10 failed, 3 passed

    env -u FORCE_COLOR -u COLORTERM uv run pytest tests/test_ui.py -q
    13 passed

Observed: ANSI escapes such as `\x1b[32m` and `\x1b[2m` leak into output the tests assert as plain text.

Expected: the suite gives the same verdict whatever the ambient colour configuration.

## Why this is worse than one flaky file

A lane spawned from a shell carrying the variable inherits it, so its verify run fails on code that cannot affect colour. Two lanes burned rework on exactly that: `basicly-vkh0.28`, a kit CLI, and `basicly-e2mz.30`, the tracker seam.

**The whole suite passed while the single file failed.** A green `uv run pytest -q` therefore does not clear this, and the order dependence is itself the defect: some other test disables colour globally, and whichever runs first decides the verdict. That is a shared-state leak between tests.

## Do not fix this in the shell

The repository rule is that a fix lives in the repo. Stripping the variable at dispatch is a workaround for today, not the remedy. The suite must neutralise the ambient value itself, and a test must not depend on another test having done so.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given any value of FORCE_COLOR CLICOLOR_FORCE or NO_COLOR in the environment when the suite runs then every test gives the same verdict as it does with those variables unset
- Given tests/test_ui.py runs alone when the environment forces colour then it passes, without relying on any other test having run first

## Scope

- `tests/conftest.py`
- `tests/test_ui.py`
