## Steps to Reproduce

Dispatch a lane whose diff adds an engine module or a test file. `basicly-vkh0.28` adds `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py` and `tests/test_kit_tracker_cli.py`; `basicly-e2mz.30` is the same shape.

At the landing:

    [escalated] build -> build: merge failed: verify full failed: pytest, docs-claims (rework 2/2)
    docs-claims: docs/plan/implementation-plan.md [plan-current-state]: generated block is stale
      run `uv run python .scripts/docs_claims.py --fix`

The pytest half is not a second cause: the failing tests are `tests/test_docs_claims.py` and `tests/test_docs_claims_consumer.py`, which assert the same check.

Measured 2026-08-16: the base checkout is clean before the merge (`docs_claims.py --check` prints 4 generated blocks current, 5 assertions current, exit 0). The block goes stale only in the merged tree, because `plan-current-state` counts engine modules and test files.

`basicly-vkh0.26` landed cleanly on the same base at the same time. The difference is that it modified existing files and added none.

## Why the lane cannot fix it

`docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` is outside every lane scope, and correctly so. A lane that widened into it would take a path other lanes also touch. So the lane is refused for a defect it is not permitted to repair, and it burns its whole rework budget discovering that.

## The engine already knows the file is regenerable

Preflight prints it:

    regen: generated: a landing conflict confined to these is rebuilt and continues, spending no rework
           `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` <- `uv run python .scripts/docs_claims.py --fix --block plan-current-state`

That path covers a merge CONFLICT confined to those files. It does not cover a generated block going stale because the merge changed the tree the block is derived from. Those are the same class and only one is handled.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a lane whose merge leaves a declared-regenerable file stale when the landing runs verify then the engine shall regenerate that file after the merge and before verify, and shall not charge the lane rework for it
- Given regeneration does not make the file current when the landing runs then the failure shall be reported against the file with the command that would fix it, rather than as a plain verify failure

## Scope

- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `tests/test_merge.py`

payload.description:
## Context

`comment` is a br construct and it is overloaded. In the owned ledger today 2447 of 5176 events are comments, and they carry two unrelated things:

1. Prose a human or an agent wrote about the work.
2. Every machine marker the loop derives state from - checkpoints, gate results, handoff artifacts, decision-queue items, scope violations, telemetry, worktree bindings.

The second group only lives in comments because br offered no other extensible field. We own this store and are not bound by that.

## Why now

`basicly-vkh0.26` is modelling the gate event in `events.py` while this is filed. A gate result is precisely one of the machine markers that should stop being a comment. The two decisions are the same decision.

## The naming, and one caution

The owner proposed `work log`. Recommendation is the kind name `note` for the prose case: every record in an append-only log is already a log entry, so a kind called `log` reads ambiguously at the call site. `note` is short, is not a br word, and leaves `work log` free as the name of the rendered view a human reads.

## The migration constraint

An append-only log is never rewritten. A rename is therefore not a rename: 2447 existing `comment` events stay on disk unchanged and the fold must keep deriving the same state from them. The reader needs an alias, not the unknown-kind skip path - a skipped comment event would silently drop checkpoint and gate state for every issue older than this change.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/snapshot.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_events.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_snapshot.py`

## Steps to Reproduce

On 2026-08-16 a stray 7.6 MB SQLite file was left at `.beads/beads.db.recovered` during a tracker repair. It was never staged by hand. The next ship advance committed it:

    git log --oneline -- .beads/beads.db.recovered
    910b0dd chore(beads): close the shipped track (basicly-e2mz.16)

    git cat-file -s $(git rev-parse HEAD:.beads/beads.db.recovered)
    7.6 MB

Observed: the engine tracker-state rollup stages the whole `.beads/` directory, so any file under it that the ignore rules miss enters a commit.

Expected: the rollup stages the known tracker paths only, and never a directory glob.

## Why the ignore rules missed it

`.beads/.gitignore` carries `*.db`, `*.db-shm`, `*.db-wal`. A name ending `.recovered` matches none of them, confirmed with `git check-ignore -v` returning NOT IGNORED. The ignore list is a denylist of suffixes, so it can only ever catch names someone predicted.

## The second-order damage

Deleting the stray broke 37 tests at once. The `work_repo` fixture copies tracked files, so a tracked-then-deleted path raises FileNotFoundError during fixture setup, and every test using that fixture errors. The blast radius of a stray file is therefore the whole suite, not one assertion.

The 7.6 MB blob remains in git history. Removing it needs a history rewrite, which is the owner decision, and is probably not worth it for one blob.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a file under the tracker directory that is neither tracker state nor ignored when the tracker state rollup runs then the rollup shall not stage it, and shall name it as unexpected rather than committing it
- Given the known tracker state paths are dirty when the rollup runs then it shall stage exactly those paths

## Scope

- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `tests/test_merge.py`

payload.text:
## Steps to Reproduce

Measured 2026-08-16, after filing six beads with raw br create and raw br dep add rather than through the seam.

    uv run basicly tracker adopt
    adopted 6 record(s): basicly-e2mz.28, basicly-e2mz.33, basicly-e2mz.34, basicly-e2mz.35, basicly-vkh0.30, basicly-vkh0.31

    uv run basicly tracker shadow
    31 record(s) in scope, 9 of them adopted; 866 imported, 0 declared
      disagreement: record='basicly-vkh0.27', query='ready', owned=True, reference=False
      disagreement: record='basicly-vkh0.29', query='ready', owned=True, reference=False
    clean: no · conclusive: yes

Adoption removed every record absence. The two survivors are both the same shape: the owned store reports the issue ready, the reference reports it blocked, because the blocker EDGE is in br and not in the ledger. Adopt reconciles records and not edges.

## Why no seam-routed command can repair it

    uv run basicly tracker write -- dep add basicly-vkh0.27 basicly-vkh0.26 --type blocks
    Dependency already exists: basicly-vkh0.27 → basicly-vkh0.26

The mirror writes only on an ACCEPTED br write. br rejects the duplicate, so nothing is mirrored, and the ledger stays short of the edge forever. Once br holds an edge the ledger never saw, the seam is structurally unable to reconcile it.

## Evidence that this is the operator bypass and not a mirror defect

Records filed through the seam carry the full event set; records filed with raw br create carry none of it. Measured over the ledger:

    seam-routed  e2mz.29  created 1, status 1, edge 2, comment 1
    seam-routed  e2mz.31  created 1, status 1, edge 2, comment 1
    raw br       vkh0.27  field 1
    raw br       vkh0.29  field 1
    raw br       vkh0.30  NONE

The mirror is behaving exactly as designed. The gap is that adopt, the verb whose stated job is reconciling what a hand-run br created, covers only half of what a hand-run br creates.

## Why it matters now

These two disagreements are the whole distance between the differential reading clean and not clean, and a clean conclusive run is what licenses the flip. The cutover is blocked on a reconciliation gap rather than on any remaining engineering.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a dependency edge the reference holds and the owned ledger does not when tracker adopt runs then the edge is appended to the ledger and the differential reports no disagreement for that record
- Given an edge present in both stores when adopt runs then nothing is appended, so a second run changes nothing

## Scope

- `src/basicly/tracker_cutover.py`
- `tests/test_tracker_adoption.py`

## Second occurrence of the same defect, 2026-08-16

The session-root flag has now cost two separate stalls, hours apart, and the second was after the first was already understood and filed. That makes it a control problem, not an attention problem.

Occurrence 1. `basicly loop run <child>` defaults the session root to the child, so the grant on the parent is never consulted:

    [blocked] intake -> intake: classify needs an agent-proposed work type; no active grant
    on basicly-vkh0.26 to delegate it under

Two dispatch attempts died before the `--root` flag was read.

Occurrence 2. `basicly loop advance` has NO `--root` flag at all - only `loop run` does. Shipping three landed beads with `loop advance` therefore produced:

    [blocked] verify -> verify: ship checkpoint awaiting human approval

on all three, from an L3 grant that delegates ship, because the grant was looked for on the child.

## Why the refusal text is the fix

Both messages are accurate and neither is actionable. The first names the missing grant without naming the flag that supplies it. The second reports a human checkpoint without saying that a grant exists one level up and was not consulted.

Two candidate remedies, and the second is cheaper:

1. Default a child's session root to its parent when the child carries no grant of its own.
2. Name `--root` in both refusals when the issue has a parent that carries a live grant, and give `loop advance` the flag it lacks.

A reader who hits either message should not have to run `--help` to discover the mechanism that would unblock them.

## Bearing on the tier question this bead exists to settle

This is the clearest case yet for the bead's own rule. No fragment saying remember the root flag would have helped: I knew about the flag when occurrence 2 happened, and it still cost a dispatch, because `loop advance` does not accept it. Guidance cannot fix a missing flag.

## The bead leak, measured 2026-08-16

The owner asked how far the external tool's vocabulary has spread, so that the rename lands once with the event-kind split rather than twice.

**1,985 occurrences of `bead*` across the tree**, by surface:

| Surface | Occurrences |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/` | 872 |
| `src/basicly/` | 725 |
| `.basicly/core/` (projected to consumers) | 183 |
| `docs/` | 179 |
| `.scripts/` | 26 |

Engine concentration: merge 85, supervise 58, decompose 53, cli 52, policy 51, run_record 49, commit 43, loop 39.

By kind, inside the engine: 43 function parameters or arguments named `bead`/`bead_id`, 15 attribute or key accesses, **106 user-visible strings**, and 5 uses of the `chore(beads)` commit scope.

## It reaches four of the five frozen consumer surfaces

| Frozen surface | Occurrences |
| --- | --- |
| the CLI commands and flags (`cli.py`) | 58 |
| `basicly.toml` and its overlay (`config.py`) | 31 |
| **the owned ledger format (`run_record.py`)** | 52 |
| the catalog source schemas | 4 |
| the generated-file and manifest contract | 0 |

**The one that matters most is the third.** `run_record.py:713` writes `"bead": bead_id` — a field key in the format of the store we own, the store whose entire purpose is to replace the external tool. Our replacement already speaks the vocabulary of the thing it replaces, in a surface declared frozen for semantic versioning.

`cli.py:4399` exposes it directly: `--bead`, required, helped as "Bead id for the merge commit message".

## What this does to the shape of the work

A rename is no longer a tidy-up. Four frozen surfaces means a deprecation window and a changelog fragment, exactly as the two-ladder rename in the architecture backlog already needs. It cannot be a bulk find-and-replace either: a scripted replace across 1,985 sites is precisely the failure recorded on this project before, where a find-replace rewrote a helper's own body and turned 23 failures into 80.

Three populations, and they should not move together:

1. **Internal identifiers** (43 parameters, 15 accesses) — free to rename, no consumer sees them.
2. **User-visible strings and the CLI flag** (106 + `--bead`) — need a deprecation window; the old flag keeps working for one minor.
3. **The ledger field key** — needs a reader that accepts both spellings, for the same reason this bead already states about the `comment` kind: an append-only log is never rewritten, so the reader needs an alias, not a migration.

The third population is the same problem this bead was filed for. That is the argument for folding it in here rather than filing it apart: one alias mechanism in the fold serves both the renamed event kind and the renamed field key, and shipping them separately means building it twice.

## Naming, unchanged from the recommendation above

The kit already answers this. `kit/tracker/cli.py` says `record` 27 times and `bead` zero, and the event schema keys on `"record"`. So the unit is a **record**, its prose entry is a **note**, and the rendered history is a **work log**. Nothing new needs inventing; the engine simply has to catch up with the kit.

payload.value:
## Steps to Reproduce

On 2026-08-16 a comment body was passed to the shell inside double quotes with backticks in it. zsh ran the backticked words as command substitution, and one expanded the whole shell environment into the comment: 152 environment variable assignments, 40325 characters, including a live 32-character CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN.

The write went through the seam, so it reached both stores.

Redaction was then run explicitly and changed nothing relevant:

    uv run python -c "... b.scrub_export(...), b.scrub_ledger(...)"
    scrubbed: 898 0

    grep -c CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN .beads/issues.jsonl .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl
    .beads/issues.jsonl:1
    .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl:1

Expected: a NAME=value block carrying a token-shaped value is redacted at the write, before it enters either store.

## Why the existing rules missed it

The architecture states three rule sets: high-signal secret shapes, machine path shapes, and the running user's own name. An environment dump matches none of them. The token is not in a recognised credential format, the assignment is not a path, and the variable names are not the username.

The value that leaked was 32 characters of hex with no prefix. A shape-matcher keyed on known credential prefixes cannot see it. What identifies it is the CONTEXT - an uppercase identifier ending in TOKEN, SECRET, KEY or PASSWORD, followed by an equals sign and a non-trivial value.

## What did not leak

Checked by name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN and OPENAI_API_KEY were all absent. The exposure was a local session IPC token, plus machine paths and environment variable names.

## Why this was recoverable, and why that is luck

Nothing had been committed. HEAD held zero occurrences, so the repair was an edit to two uncommitted working files. Had a commit intervened, the remedy would have been a history rewrite.

A lane was running at the time and the loop commits tracker state at arbitrary points, so the window was minutes wide. Recovery depended on noticing before an unrelated process committed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a write whose body contains an uppercase identifier ending in TOKEN, SECRET, KEY or PASSWORD followed by an equals sign and a value when redaction runs then the value is replaced with a labelled placeholder before the write enters either store
- Given a write body carrying a large block of NAME=value lines when redaction runs then the block is refused or redacted rather than stored verbatim
- Given a body with no such pattern then redaction changes nothing, proven by a positive control

## Scope

- `src/basicly/redact.py`
- `tests/test_redact.py`

## Steps to Reproduce

A comment written on 2026-08-16 carried a leaked environment dump into both stores. Removing it was necessary and neither store offered a way.

    uv run br comments --help
    Commands: add, list, help

There is no delete. The owned ledger is append-only by design, so it has no removal either.

The repair was a hand edit of two uncommitted working files, verified afterwards:

    .beads/issues.jsonl        898 valid records, 0 occurrences
    .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl  5294 valid events, 0 occurrences

That is only defensible because nothing had been committed. Had it been, the remedy would have been a history rewrite of a tracked store, which is an owner decision and a bad one to be forced into.

## The tension, stated rather than resolved

Append-only is the ledger's integrity property and the reason a fold has authority. The architecture is explicit: repairs are corrective appends, a broken log is reported and never rewritten in place. That rule is right for a wrong FACT.

It is not sufficient for a wrong DISCLOSURE. A corrective append leaves the secret readable in the file. Redaction after the fact needs the bytes to change, which is exactly what append-only forbids.

So the two properties genuinely conflict, and the resolution is a design question rather than a bug fix. Candidates, none chosen here:

1. A redaction event that the fold honours, plus a compaction step that is the only writer permitted to rewrite history, run deliberately and leaving evidence that it ran.
2. Refuse at the write. If nothing unredactable can enter, nothing needs removing. This is basicly-vkh0.33 and it is the cheaper half, but it only covers shapes someone predicted.
3. Accept that removal requires a rewrite, and make that a first-class, audited operation rather than a hand edit under time pressure.

Option 2 alone is not enough: it fails exactly when the shape is novel, which is the case that produced this bead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a record or event whose content must be withdrawn when the withdrawal path runs then the content is unreadable in the store afterwards and the fold reports that a withdrawal occurred, with its time and reason
- Given the withdrawal path when it runs then it is the only code permitted to rewrite the log, and a consistency check afterwards reports the log as sound

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/fsck.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_events.py`

## Third rename folded in: the two ladders, measured 2026-08-16

The owner asked to fold the autonomy and integrity ladder rename in here, so one deprecation window covers every vocabulary change instead of three.

This replaces an earlier attempt at this comment which was mangled by shell expansion and withdrawn. See basicly-vkh0.33.

### The state

The architecture reference names both ladders. The code implements neither.

| Ladder | The document says | The CLI accepts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| autonomy | attended, assisted, supervised, unattended | L0 to L3 |
| integrity | docs-and-tests, engine, consumer-surface | L1 to L3 |

Measured occurrences of the bare L0-L3 spelling:

| Surface | Occurrences |
| --- | --- |
| tests | 384 |
| src/basicly | 142, of which policy.py and integrity.py hold 75 |
| .basicly/core, projected to consumers | 18 |
| config.py and basicly.toml, a frozen surface | 10 |

The named levels appear ZERO times in policy.py or integrity.py as identifiers, against a positive control of 21 and 13 hits for L3 in those same two files. A tree-wide search finds 49 hits for the words and every one inspected is ordinary English prose, such as "a supervised pass". The names live in the document and nowhere else.

### The finding that should change the design

The word "supervised" is already taken, and it means something else.

    src/basicly/cli.py:3611   | {"supervised": view.supervised}
    src/basicly/cli.py:3655   if not view.supervised or view.holder is None:
    src/basicly/cli.py:3657   f"stop: refused - {args.issue} is not supervised"

view.supervised is a derived boolean: whether a session currently has a supervisor holding its lock. That is unrelated to how much a grant lets the engine approve. Adopting "supervised" as the name of autonomy level 2 would give one word two meanings in the same codebase.

That is precisely the test the document's own rejected-names table applies. It rejected none/decompose/classify/ship because each already names a loop phase, and local/engine/contract because "local" already names the per-machine overlay. The same test rejects "supervised", and the table missed it because the collision is in the code rather than in the document.

This needs an owner decision before any rename lands: pick a different word for autonomy level 2, or rename view.supervised. The first is cheaper. The boolean is older, is used at three sites, and its meaning is the more literal one.

### Why one window, not three

Renaming bead to record, comment to note, and the ladder levels are the same shape: a spelling change across surfaces declared frozen for semantic versioning, each needing the old value accepted with a deprecation message for one minor release. Building that machinery once and running three renames through it costs far less than three windows, and it spares consumers three separate migrations.

The ladder rename is also the smallest of the three by consumer exposure, at one CLI flag and one config key, so it is the natural first pass through the mechanism.

## Second occurrence of the same defect, 2026-08-16

The session-root flag has now cost two separate stalls, hours apart, and the second was after the first was already understood and filed. That makes it a control problem, not an attention problem.

Occurrence 1. `basicly loop run <child>` defaults the session root to the child, so the grant on the parent is never consulted:

    [blocked] intake -> intake: classify needs an agent-proposed work type; no active grant
    on basicly-vkh0.26 to delegate it under

Two dispatch attempts died before the `--root` flag was read.

Occurrence 2. `basicly loop advance` has NO `--root` flag at all - only `loop run` does. Shipping three landed beads with `loop advance` therefore produced:

    [blocked] verify -> verify: ship checkpoint awaiting human approval

on all three, from an L3 grant that delegates ship, because the grant was looked for on the child.

## Why the refusal text is the fix

Both messages are accurate and neither is actionable. The first names the missing grant without naming the flag that supplies it. The second reports a human checkpoint without saying that a grant exists one level up and was not consulted.

Two candidate remedies, and the second is cheaper:

1. Default a child's session root to its parent when the child carries no grant of its own.
2. Name `--root` in both refusals when the issue has a parent that carries a live grant, and give `loop advance` the flag it lacks.

A reader who hits either message should not have to run `--help` to discover the mechanism that would unblock them.

## Bearing on the tier question this bead exists to settle

This is the clearest case yet for the bead's own rule. No fragment saying remember the root flag would have helped: I knew about the flag when occurrence 2 happened, and it still cost a dispatch, because `loop advance` does not accept it. Guidance cannot fix a missing flag.

| Surface | Occurrences |

| `tests/` | 872 |
| `src/basicly/` | 725 |
| `.basicly/core/` (projected to consumers) | 183 |
| `docs/` | 179 |

Engine concentration: merge 85, supervise 58, decompose 53, cli 52, policy 51, run_record 49, commit 43, loop 39.

By kind, inside the engine: 43 function parameters or arguments named `bead`/`bead_id`, 15 attribute or key accesses, **106 user-visible strings**, and 5 uses of the `chore(beads)` commit scope.

| --- | --- |
| the CLI commands and flags (`cli.py`) | 58 |
| `basicly.toml` and its overlay (`config.py`) | 31 |
| **the owned ledger format (`run_record.py`)** | 52 |
| the catalog source schemas | 4 |
| the generated-file and manifest contract | 0 |

**The one that matters most is the third.** `run_record.py:713` writes `"bead": bead_id` — a field key in the format of the store we own, the store whose entire purpose is to replace the external tool. Our replacement already speaks the vocabulary of the thing it replaces, in a surface declared frozen for semantic versioning.

`cli.py:4399` exposes it directly: `--bead`, required, helped as "Bead id for the merge commit message".

## What this does to the shape of the work

A rename is no longer a tidy-up. Four frozen surfaces means a deprecation window and a changelog fragment, exactly as the two-ladder rename in the architecture backlog already needs. It cannot be a bulk find-and-replace either: a scripted replace across 1,985 sites is precisely the failure recorded on this project before, where a find-replace rewrote a helper's own body and turned 23 failures into 80.

Three populations, and they should not move together:

1. **Internal identifiers** (43 parameters, 15 accesses) — free to rename, no consumer sees them.
2. **User-visible strings and the CLI flag** (106 + `--bead`) — need a deprecation window; the old flag keeps working for one minor.
3. **The ledger field key** — needs a reader that accepts both spellings, for the same reason this bead already states about the `comment` kind: an append-only log is never rewritten, so the reader needs an alias, not a migration.

The third population is the same problem this bead was filed for. That is the argument for folding it in here rather than filing it apart: one alias mechanism in the fold serves both the renamed event kind and the renamed field key, and shipping them separately means building it twice.

## Naming, unchanged from the recommendation above

The kit already answers this. `kit/tracker/cli.py` says `record` 27 times and `bead` zero, and the event schema keys on `"record"`. So the unit is a **record**, its prose entry is a **note**, and the rendered history is a **work log**. Nothing new needs inventing; the engine simply has to catch up with the kit.

## Third rename folded in: the two ladders, measured 2026-08-16

The owner asked to fold the autonomy and integrity ladder rename in here, so one deprecation window covers every vocabulary change instead of three.

This replaces an earlier attempt at this comment which was mangled by shell expansion and withdrawn. See basicly-vkh0.33.

### The state

The architecture reference names both ladders. The code implements neither.

| Ladder | The document says | The CLI accepts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| autonomy | attended, assisted, supervised, unattended | L0 to L3 |
| integrity | docs-and-tests, engine, consumer-surface | L1 to L3 |

Measured occurrences of the bare L0-L3 spelling:

| Surface | Occurrences |
| --- | --- |
| tests | 384 |
| src/basicly | 142, of which policy.py and integrity.py hold 75 |
| .basicly/core, projected to consumers | 18 |
| config.py and basicly.toml, a frozen surface | 10 |

The named levels appear ZERO times in policy.py or integrity.py as identifiers, against a positive control of 21 and 13 hits for L3 in those same two files. A tree-wide search finds 49 hits for the words and every one inspected is ordinary English prose, such as "a supervised pass". The names live in the document and nowhere else.

### The finding that should change the design

The word "supervised" is already taken, and it means something else.

    src/basicly/cli.py:3611   | {"supervised": view.supervised}
    src/basicly/cli.py:3655   if not view.supervised or view.holder is None:
    src/basicly/cli.py:3657   f"stop: refused - {args.issue} is not supervised"

view.supervised is a derived boolean: whether a session currently has a supervisor holding its lock. That is unrelated to how much a grant lets the engine approve. Adopting "supervised" as the name of autonomy level 2 would give one word two meanings in the same codebase.

That is precisely the test the document's own rejected-names table applies. It rejected none/decompose/classify/ship because each already names a loop phase, and local/engine/contract because "local" already names the per-machine overlay. The same test rejects "supervised", and the table missed it because the collision is in the code rather than in the document.

This needs an owner decision before any rename lands: pick a different word for autonomy level 2, or rename view.supervised. The first is cheaper. The boolean is older, is used at three sites, and its meaning is the more literal one.

### Why one window, not three

Renaming bead to record, comment to note, and the ladder levels are the same shape: a spelling change across surfaces declared frozen for semantic versioning, each needing the old value accepted with a deprecation message for one minor release. Building that machinery once and running three renames through it costs far less than three windows, and it spares consumers three separate migrations.

The ladder rename is also the smallest of the three by consumer exposure, at one CLI flag and one config key, so it is the natural first pass through the mechanism.

payload.value:
## Steps to Reproduce

Measured 2026-08-16, after six records were filed with raw br create and raw br dep add rather than through the seam.

    uv run basicly tracker adopt
    adopted 6 record(s)

    uv run basicly tracker shadow
    31 record(s) in scope, 9 of them adopted; 866 imported, 0 declared
      disagreement: record=basicly-vkh0.27, query=ready, owned=True, reference=False
      disagreement: record=basicly-vkh0.29, query=ready, owned=True, reference=False
    clean: no · conclusive: yes

Adoption removed every record absence. Both survivors are the same shape: the owned store reports the issue ready and the reference reports it blocked, because the blocker EDGE is in br and not in the ledger.

Expected: adopt reconciles an edge the reference holds and the ledger never saw, exactly as it reconciles a record.

## Why no seam-routed command can repair it

    uv run basicly tracker write -- dep add basicly-vkh0.27 basicly-vkh0.26 --type blocks
    Dependency already exists: basicly-vkh0.27 -> basicly-vkh0.26

The mirror writes only on an accepted br write. br rejects the duplicate, nothing is mirrored, and the ledger stays short of the edge permanently.

## This is the operator bypass, not a mirror defect

Records filed through the seam carry the full event set. Records filed with raw br carry none of it:

    seam-routed  e2mz.29  created 1, status 1, edge 2, comment 1
    raw br       vkh0.27  field 1
    raw br       vkh0.30  NONE

The gap is that adopt, whose stated job is reconciling what a hand-run br created, covers only half of what a hand-run br creates.

## Why it matters now

These two disagreements are the whole distance between the differential reading clean and not clean, and a clean conclusive run is what licenses the flip.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a dependency edge the reference holds and the owned ledger does not when tracker adopt runs then the edge is appended to the ledger and the differential reports no disagreement for that record
- Given an edge present in both stores when adopt runs then nothing is appended, so a second run changes nothing

## Scope

- `src/basicly/edge_adoption.py`
- `src/basicly/br.py`
- `src/basicly/tracker_cutover.py`
- `.importlinter`
- `tests/test_edge_adoption.py`
- `tests/test_tracker_adoption.py`
- `tests/test_tracker_cutover.py`

## Scope correction

The first declaration named `src/basicly/tracker_cutover.py` and `tests/test_tracker_adoption.py` only. That was wrong: adoption lives in `br.py`, and the reconciliation earned a module of its own. The landing gate refused with "the plan is wrong, not the merge", which was exact. `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` is not listed because it is declared regenerable and the landing rebuilds it.

payload.title: a lane with no commits holds ground the scope gate treats as occupied

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Steps to Reproduce

Measured 2026-08-16. `basicly-vkh0.32` was refused at the landing:

    [blocked] build -> build: basicly-vkh0.32 changed .importlinter, docs/plan/implementation-plan.md,
    src/basicly/br.py, src/basicly/edge_adoption.py, tests/test_edge_adoption.py,
    tests/test_tracker_cutover.py outside its declared scope
    (src/basicly/tracker_cutover.py, tests/test_tracker_adoption.py), and basicly-b2n2 declared
    that ground: the plan is wrong, not the merge.

Half of that refusal was correct and is not this bead: the scope declaration really was wrong, and the gate said so precisely.

The other half was a collision with a lane that had produced nothing:

    git log --oneline main..harness/basicly-b2n2 | wc -l    -> 0
    git -C <worktree> status --short | wc -l                -> 0

Zero commits ahead of main, clean worktree, sitting on a base from an earlier session. `basicly-b2n2` had held `src/basicly/br.py` and a worktree slot since before the session while writing no code.

Tearing the worktree down released the ground and the lane landed. Nothing was lost, because there was nothing to lose.

## The gap

The architecture defines live deliberately: "Live means the worktree session records on disk, not the tracker export." The reason is good and should not be reverted - a freshly provisioned lane is the one most likely to be mid-edit, and the export would not show it.

But presence of a worktree record is a weak proxy for occupancy. It cannot distinguish:

- a lane mid-edit with uncommitted work, which must hold its ground;
- a lane with commits, which must hold its ground;
- a lane with no commits and a clean tree, which is holding a claim and a concurrency slot and nothing else.

The third case cost a landing, a rework attempt, and an operator decision today. It also occupied one of five worktree slots, which separately blocked a dispatch earlier in the same session.

## What this is not

Not an argument for reading the tracker export instead. Not an argument for auto-reaping a lane: a human parked it for a reason, and deleting work is the one thing a scope gate must never do. A lane with no commits but a dirty tree is genuinely mid-edit and must keep its ground.

The remedy is discrimination and a better message, not eviction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a scope collision with a lane that has no commits ahead of the base and no uncommitted changes when the landing gate reports the collision then it names that lane as holding no work, and names the command that releases it
- Given a collision with a lane that has commits or uncommitted changes then the refusal is unchanged
- Given the preflight runs when a provisioned lane has no commits and a clean tree then it reports that lane as holding a slot without work

## Scope

- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/contention.py`
- `tests/test_merge.py`

payload.title: edge adoption made the differential reference a derivative of the owned ledger

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Steps to Reproduce

Measured 2026-08-16, immediately after `basicly-vkh0.32` landed as `e69a61b`.

    uv run basicly tracker shadow
    35 record(s) in scope, 9 of them adopted; 866 imported, 0 declared
      refused: Refusal(rule='derived-from-owned-ledger', detail="the reference's answers
      moved when one synthetic event was added to the owned ledger, so it is a function of
      that ledger rather than an independent source")
    clean: no · conclusive: yes

Earlier the same day, before that landing, the same command reported two disagreements and NO refusal:

    31 record(s) in scope, 9 of them adopted; 866 imported, 0 declared
      disagreement: record=basicly-vkh0.27, query=ready, owned=True, reference=False
      disagreement: record=basicly-vkh0.29, query=ready, owned=True, reference=False
    clean: no · conclusive: yes

## Why this is not a false positive

The audit is a perturbation probe. It appends one synthetic status event to the event set the reference is handed and refuses a reference whose answers move with it. The kit's own module docstring states the discriminator:

    A genuinely live source ignores the argument, so it cannot false-fire.

The reference moved. By the audit's own construction that means the reference is now reading the owned ledger rather than being independent of it.

## Why it matters more than the two disagreements it replaced

The differential is the instrument that licenses the flip. A refusal is worse than a disagreement: a disagreement names two records to fix, while a refusal says the comparison cannot discriminate at all. Step 4 of the cutover waits on a clean AND conclusive run, and a refused reference can never produce one.

The work that caused it is the work that was meant to remove the last blocker. That inversion is the finding.

## Where to look, not yet established

`edge_adoption.shortfall` is pure by construction - its own docstring says nothing there loads a kit, reads a file or runs a process, and the kit modules arrive as parameters. It is called from `br.py:1499` on the adoption path, not the read path. So the module import alone does not explain it, and the mechanism has NOT been traced.

Two candidates, neither confirmed:

1. The reference callable the differential builds now threads ledger events into a path that reaches a br view.
2. Adoption changed the reference's own inputs, so the perturbation reaches it indirectly.

Do not assume either. Trace the reference callable the differential constructs and find which argument now carries ledger events.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the shadow differential runs when the reference is audited then the reference is independent of the owned ledger and the run reports no refusal
- Given a reference that genuinely derives from the owned ledger then the refusal still fires, proven by a deliberate derivative as a positive control

## Scope

- `src/basicly/tracker_cutover.py`
- `src/basicly/br.py`
- `tests/test_tracker_cutover.py`

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Steps to Reproduce

A durability review of docs/architecture/architecture.md on 2026-08-16 found the systemic defect behind most of its individual ones. The document declares status out of scope at line 138 and then carries roughly twenty status paragraphs and four capability-status columns.

The two files had already diverged on one surface. Three gradings of the tool-call boundary existed at once:

    architecture.md  layer 1                     partial
    status.md        enforcement at the boundary designed
    status.md        agent hooks for two families shipped

Architecture defines `designed` as "decided, sequenced behind a later phase, and nothing is built". Four hooks exist and are projected, so `designed` was false while a `shipped` row described the same four hooks.

A second contradiction sat inside architecture alone: two gates were graded `partial` for behaviour a later section argues for as a deliberate design decision, in the section the grading links to.

## What was fixed immediately, and what was not

Fixed in the same session: both status columns deleted from the two gate tables, so only one file can be wrong about a grade. Also the four falsehoods the review found - the lens vocabulary never named, a module count that did not reproduce from its cited source, a census figure copied in defiance of the decision record that forbids copying it, and a dependency register omitting the dependency with its own decision record.

Not fixed, and the reason this issue exists: the pattern will recur. The review identifies roughly 420 lines that go stale when the CODE changes rather than when a DECISION changes, spread across many sections.

## The prerequisite the review names, which is the useful part

Most of the content that should leave architecture lands in `status.md`. `status.md` itself records that **nothing gates it**. Moving a stale row from a file nobody gates into another file nobody gates does not reduce the risk; it relocates it.

Architecture decision **D-30** proposes one source rendered into every surface by a generated block. It is recorded as `proposed`, not accepted, and not built. **D-30 is therefore a prerequisite of the cleanup, not an item beside it.** Decide D-30 first.

## Why this matters more than a tidy-up

An agent reads the architecture folder at the start of every session and builds its working context from it. A false statement there is not a documentation defect; it is a wrong premise under every unit of work that follows. That is the owner's framing and it is the right one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a capability with a status when the reader looks for it then exactly one file states that status, and the architecture document states only what the capability is and what it must satisfy
- Given the architecture document is read after a routine refactor that changes no decision then no sentence in it has become false
- Given D-30 is decided when the cleanup runs then the destination of every moved row is a surface something gates

## Scope

- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `docs/architecture/status.md`
- `.scripts/docs_claims.py`

Owner decision 2026-08-17: D-30 is accepted. One source for the capability status view, rendered into all three surfaces by a docs-claims generated block. The architecture cleanup this bead asks for is unblocked by that acceptance.

The decision record itself is not edited yet, because an architect pass owns docs/architecture/ right now and two writers on one file is how a clean merge drops a field. Edit D-30 to accepted in the same change that lands the generated block.

Owner decision 2026-08-17: the board goes on the release ladder at v0.10.0, not deferred. Recorded in docs/plan/implementation-plan.md section 4, and a section 12 row now maps this epic to a release.

Why it needed a decision: this epic was on no ladder row, carried no phase label, and appeared in no status table, while its consumer half was already built. rn0o.1 and rn0o.9 are closed, so the snapshot schema and its validator exist and basicly board validate runs. Nothing produces a snapshot, so rn0o.2, rn0o.3 and rn0o.7 are the next work.

This epic has no phase label and none was invented for it: phase membership is a tracker label, and the label write surface is currently refused by the dual-write seam.

Owner decision 2026-08-17: go on the flip, in the order vkh0.27 then this bead. vkh0.27 is dispatched as a lane on the vkh0 grant.

This bead is not dispatchable as written. basicly loop preflight refuses it: 1487370 working-set tokens against a band of 8000 to 264000, verdict REFUSED - too large, split it. Every other ready vkh0 child sits in band, the largest at 77454, so the refusal is this bead's scope and not the band.

Two further constraints on it, both measured today:

1. Its declared scope includes docs/architecture/architecture.md, which an architect pass is rewriting for the comment-kind split. Dispatching it now would put two writers on one file.
2. The grant on vkh0 has 46489485 tokens remaining and a lane costs about 33 million measured, so one lane at a time. The full five-lane fan-out forecast is 105672805, which the grant cannot pay.

Next action on this bead is a decompose, not a dispatch.

payload.description: Four modules each declare part of the closed event-kind set and they disagree: events.py declares six KIND_ constants, migrate.py declares KIND_EDGE, and gates.py and differential.py each declare KIND_GATE. events.KNOWN_KINDS reads like the authority, omits two of the six kinds actually in the log, and has no consumer anywhere including the suite. Adding five kinds to that set is how spellings six and seven appear. Full plan-gate-shaped entry: docs/architecture/backlog.md B8.1. Design: architecture section 32.8.

payload.description: The alias table the reader needs is keyed on the harness marker families, and the list of families has drifted three times. requirements/work-tracker.md said twelve; the answer is eleven. It named [harness-side], which is a phrase from commit.py prose and not a family, and omitted [harness-retro]. The load-bearing consequence: [harness-overrun] has twelve ledger rows and no producer, so a table derived from live marker constants drops them. The table must be a frozen literal over every family ever written, gated. Full entry: docs/architecture/backlog.md B8.3.

payload.text:
A third upstream defect, observed 2026-08-17 during the architecture pass. br exited with CONFIG_ERROR: Invalid JSON at line 562, naming .beads/issues.jsonl. Line 562 of that file parses without error under Python. The failure was intermittent: an earlier invocation in the same session read the same file successfully.

That makes three, and the pattern is the argument rather than any one of them: the binary's own reader, its own health check and its own repair path have each now been observed to misreport or destroy state that the owned ledger holds correctly. None is fixable in place.

Not investigated further, and no reproduction is recorded. It is handed on as evidence for this bead, not as a bug to chase upstream.

## Context

The flip. Step 4 of the cutover.

The acceptance criterion is deliberately harsh: with the external binary absent from the machine entirely, the loop still runs a unit of work from intake to a merge. Nothing weaker proves the dependency is gone rather than merely unused.

Three defects in the external binary are the argument for finishing this, and all three are upstream so none can be fixed in place:

- br doctor health printed db=ok while sqlite called the image malformed.
- br doctor --repair rebuilds the database from the JSONL export, and that export carries zero gate results against 386 in the database, so the vendor's own repair path destroys the gate ledger.
- br exited CONFIG_ERROR: Invalid JSON at line 562 on an export line that parses without error under Python, intermittently. Recorded in this bead's comments 2026-08-17.

## Why the scope was narrowed rather than split

This bead was REFUSED by the working-set band at 1487370 tokens, and the refusal was over-declaration and not size [measured 2026-08-17 with read_cost.scope_read_cost]:

- declared as filed, with tests/** : 497551 read tokens
- the same scope without tests/** : 9803
- tests/** alone accounts for 487748 of it, which is 98 percent

The named test files below cost 21913 read tokens, which is about 65739 working-set tokens at the task factor of 3, inside the band of 8000 to 264000. So the remedy was to name the tests this work actually touches. A split would have cut one unit of work into parts that each carry the same over-declaration.

If the build finds a test file this list does not name, add it here and re-check the band. Do not widen it back to a glob.

## Scope

- `basicly.toml`
- `src/basicly/tracker_cutover.py`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `tests/test_tracker_cutover.py`
- `tests/test_br_seam.py`
- `tests/test_owned_store.py`
- `tests/test_mirror.py`
- `tests/test_tracker_invocation.py`

basicly loop preflight prints an advisory every pass: no append-only path declared, a path every lane writes is invisible to the grouping until it is listed. The path is .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl - every lane writes tracker events, they mirror into the owned ledger, and the ledger is committed.

Declaring it in [worktree] append_only_paths is the wrong remedy. That list is empty on purpose: its own comment records that CHANGELOG.md was the whole list and that serializing every lane was the cost of detecting a collision the repo created for itself. decompose serializes every child that does not declare the path and call it shared, and no bead declares it, so declaring it today serializes every plan.

basicly-4746 is the precedent: it removed the cause rather than describing it, by giving each lane its own changelog.d fragment file that basicly release assembles. The ledger already has the same shape available - events.LOG_GLOB folds every events-*.jsonl, snapshot.rotate exists and has no caller, and the lexicographic ordering rule is written down. A per-lane segment would make the log a set of files no two lanes share, so nothing contends and the advisory disappears because the fact behind it is gone.

Open question the build must answer: whether a segment is per lane or per period, and how a segment name sorts against the year-period rotation names the kit already reserves.

Operator reading of the acceptance criterion, recorded before dispatch so the build does not have to guess.

"With the external binary absent from the machine entirely" is not satisfiable by a lane and must not be attempted literally. Removing br from the machine is not a change to this repository, and under dual mode the base checkout's tracker still depends on it, so a lane that uninstalled it would break the store its own claim is written to.

Read it as hermetic absence inside the lane: the loop runs a unit of work from intake to a merge with the binary unreachable from the environment the engine spawns into. A PATH that excludes it, or an equivalent injected lookup failure, satisfies the criterion. The proof must be a committed test, not a manual session, because the criterion has to keep holding after the lane closes.

If hermetic absence turns out to be untestable at this layer, block with needs-input rather than weakening the criterion to "unused".

Observed 2026-08-17 on basicly-vkh0.27, one layer over from the teardown case this bead names. A redundant ship advance on a unit already at done exits non-zero with an upstream error rather than reporting that there is nothing to do:

  Error: br close basicly-vkh0.27 --reason shipped by the harness loop failed: Warning: Skipped basicly-vkh0.27: already closed
  Error: Nothing to do: all 1 issue(s) skipped

The unit had already shipped correctly in the previous advance. Nothing was lost. The cost is that an operator reading exit codes cannot tell a redundant advance from a failed one, which is the same failure mode as the second teardown.

Same remedy shape if this bead is widened: an advance whose work is already done reports it and exits zero.

## Context

The cost rollup under-reports a landed unit, and the shortfall is one whole dispatch rather than a rounding difference. Measured on basicly-vkh0.27 the day it landed, 2026-08-17, from the owned ledger.

The unit's own [harness-cost] record:

    {"actual": {"cost": 11.7265305, "dispatches": 1, "estimated": false, "rework": 0,
                "tokens": 15810802, "wall_clock_s": 1567.63111574},
     "forecast": {"cost": null, "tokens": null, "wall_clock_s": null},
     "scope_tokens": null, "task_class": "task"}

The same unit's [harness-run] records, three of them:

    run-921dfc68e1 phase=build   15810802 tokens
    run-3baf1603bf phase=ship     1780766 tokens
    run-3baf1603bf-2 phase=ship   1793781 tokens

So `tokens` in the cost record is the build run alone, and `dispatches: 1` counts one of three. The sum of build plus the first ship run is 17591568, which reconciles exactly with the grant ledger's own delta across the lane: 51102083 minus 33510515. Two independent instruments agree on 17591568; the cost record says 15810802, which is 10.1 percent low against the grant and 18.5 percent low against all three runs.

The `cost` figure of 11.73 US dollars is presumably build-only for the same reason, and nothing in the record says so.

## Why it matters

Cost per landed unit is the instrument the tier claims rest on. An instrument that silently drops the ship phase makes every landed unit look cheaper than it was, and the error is not constant: it scales with how much ship work a unit needs.

Two further gaps in the same record, both visible above: `forecast` is null on all three fields for a unit that was forecast at preflight, and `scope_tokens` is null although the bead declares a scope. So forecast against actual cannot be computed for this landing at all, which is the comparison the record exists to support.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cost_rollup.py`
- `tests/test_cost_rollup.py`

## Context

Cost per landed unit is the instrument the tier claims rest on, and it is not recording what it claims to. Two defects, measured 2026-08-17 over all 202 cost records in the owned ledger. The second is the headline; the first is what led to it.

## 1 · The forecast is absent from 185 of 202 records, which is 91.6 percent

`[harness-cost]` exists to carry a forecast beside the actual it produced. In 185 of 202 records `forecast.tokens` is null, and `scope_tokens` is null with it, so forecast against actual cannot be computed for that population at all.

The cause is a content-key miss and not a missing write. `cost_rollup.record` calls `decompose.forecast_for(repo_root, task_class, scope)`, which builds a key from the work type plus the globs and then searches the export for a frozen sizing marker under that key. The estimate is frozen on the feature, priced over its **working set**; the rollup looks it up with the bead's **ownership scope**. Different globs give a different key, so the lookup misses and returns None. `forecast_for`'s own docstring predicts exactly this: "A caller holding only the ownership scope therefore misses on a bead declaring its own `## Working Set`, and gets a null rather than a forecast over the wrong material."

The population supports it: the ledger holds 35 sizing markers against 202 cost records.

Probe, reproducible on any bead:

    decompose.forecast_for(repo_root, *decompose.bead_class_and_scope(repo_root, 'basicly-vkh0.29'))  ->  None

## 2 · The curator's dispatch is never in the total, in the units that had one

On basicly-vkh0.27 the cost record says `dispatches: 1, tokens: 15810802` while the unit holds three run records: build 15810802, ship 1780766, ship 1793781. Build plus the first ship run is 17591568, which reconciles exactly with the grant ledger's delta over the same lane, 51102083 minus 33510515. Two independent instruments agree on 17591568 and the cost record is 10.1 percent below it.

The cause is ordering, and it is structural rather than intermittent: `loop._on_ship` calls `cost_rollup.record` at line 641 and `_dispatch_curation` at line 642. The rollup is written before the curator has spent anything, and it cannot simply move later because the comment above it records why it must precede `merge.commit_tracker_state` - a marker written after that commit sits in the local database only.

**The undercount is bounded, not universal.** Of 202 units, 194 agree with their run count and 8 do not: e2mz.16 (3 against 6), vkh0.27 (1 against 3), e2mz.13 (3 against 4), vkh0.26, vkh0.28, e2mz.30 and two more at one run each. None over-counts. The 194 agree because curation is skipped under the supervisor's landing pass, so most units have no ship dispatch to miss. An earlier draft of this bead claimed the shortfall was general; the measurement above refuted it.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cost_rollup.py`
- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `tests/test_cost_rollup.py`

Fresh observation that settles this bead, 2026-08-17 on basicly-vkh0.27, a single-lane loop run rather than a supervised pass.

The curator ran and produced its artifact. The unit's own ledger events, in order:

    comment  [harness-policy] checkpoint=ship approved under grant L3
    comment  [harness-cost] id=basicly-vkh0.27#cost
    comment  [harness-run] id=basicly-vkh0.27#run-3baf1603bf phase=ship
    status
    comment  [harness-run] id=basicly-vkh0.27#run-3baf1603bf-2 phase=ship
    comment  [harness-artifact] kind=release-record {"claims":[{"claim":"feat(tracker): read gate state from the owned fold ...

The release-record artifact is the curator's output, and two ship-phase run records carry its dispatches: 1780766 and 1793781 tokens. So the curator is reachable and does work on a landing.

What this does not establish: the claim being corrected is about the curator under the **supervisor**, and this observation is from `basicly loop run`, not `basicly loop supervise`. `loop._dispatch_curation` documents itself as skipped under the supervisor's landing pass, which has no watchdog or stream meter of its own. So the honest correction is narrower than "the curator runs": it runs on a direct advance and is deliberately skipped on a supervised landing, and the architecture text should say which.

Supporting population figure: of 202 cost records in the ledger, 194 report a dispatch count equal to their run-record count and 8 report fewer. Those 8 are the units that curated - which is also the measure of how rare a curated landing is.

The architecture edit is held: `docs/architecture/architecture.md` is inside the declared scope of the running basicly-vkh0.29 lane, and two writers on one file is how a clean merge drops a field.

The redundant advance is not free, which is worth adding to the argument for this bead.

The third advance on basicly-vkh0.27 described in the previous comment spent 1793781 tokens before it failed on the already-closed bead. Its run record is basicly-vkh0.27#run-3baf1603bf-2, phase=ship.

So a redundant advance re-dispatches an agent at about 1.8 million tokens and then exits non-zero with an upstream error. Reading it as a failure and retrying costs the same again. That moves this bead from a legibility complaint to a measured spend leak.

{"detail": "MEASURED IN THIS WORKTREE 2026-08-17, at harness/basicly-vkh0-29 tip 0bef11d, with two probes over a temp consumer repo carrying the kit, a ledger seeded through the kit CLI, [tracker] mode = "owned", the manual runner, and one required verify gate.

WHAT IS LICENSED. `uv run basicly tracker shadow` from this worktree prints '43 record(s) in scope, 9 of them adopted; 866 imported, 0 declared (2026-08-15)' / 'clean: yes' / 'conclusive: yes'. So step 4's own precondition in basicly.toml -- a differential clean AND conclusive over a non-empty scope -- is met, and basicly-vkh0.35's 'derived-from-owned-ledger' refusal is gone. The config flip itself is licensed. This is not the blocker.

AC CLAUSE 1 ALREADY HOLDS, measured per phase. With `br.which()` forced to None, loop_state.read_node_state derives the right phase and the right gate verdicts at all seven points of a leaf's walk: intake, classify, build, build(after the agent commit), verify (passed=('verify',)), ship, done. Nothing is spawned for the derivation. vkh0.19/.20 (record, ranking), s5li (markers) and vkh0.27 (gate view) delivered this between them.

AC CLAUSE 2 FAILS, and not marginally. With br genuinely off PATH the FIRST advance raises `RuntimeError: br is not on PATH; the harness requires the beads tracker` from classify.py:73. Stubbing the spawn below br._mirror_write so the walk continues, the same intake-to-merge-to-ship walk spawns 6 distinct br surfaces at 9 spawn events, every one a write except `lint`:

  update <id> -t <type>            1 spawn   classify.py:73
  lint <id> --json                 2 spawns  policy.py:200 (definition_of_ready, fires on every advance)
  sync --flush-only                3 spawns  merge.py:520
  update <id> --external-ref <ref> 1 spawn   loop.py:2497
  sync --merge                     1 spawn   merge.py:466
  gate report --gate verify        1 spawn   verify.py:424
  close <id> --reason              1 spawn   loop.py:643

WHY THIS IS A PLAN DEFECT AND NOT A REPAIR. Under owned mode every engine READ is behind a flipped seam, and every engine WRITE still goes to br and reaches the ledger only through br._mirror_write. Remove br and the write lands in neither store -- which is why clause 2 needs the write seams flipped, in the five modules above. basicly.toml's own comment already says it: 'the rung above it is not a config edit'. The bead was filed on the premise that it is one; its band-narrowing note only ever narrowed tests/**, and records the src side as 9803 read tokens, i.e. tracker_cutover.py plus the config plus the doc.

THE COLLISION THAT MAKES THIS AN OWNER CALL RATHER THAN MINE. basicly-wpc8 ('Retire the remaining engine br surfaces after the marker migration', OPEN, P2) declares exactly these call sites, and its acceptance criterion is all but identical to clause 2: 'Given the engine at tracker mode owned with br absent from PATH ... every one succeeds from the ledger alone'. Widening this lane into those five modules would duplicate an open bead and collide with any lane dispatched on it. One correction for wpc8 either way: its 29-site figure overstates what clause 2 needs -- `where --json`, `blocked`, `dep cycles`, `dep add`, `create`, `show` and `comments` do NOT fire on a leaf's intake-to-merge path. It is 6 surfaces across 5 modules.

WHAT I DID NOT DO, deliberately. I did not flip [tracker] mode to owned. ## Context

Deleting the external store today would destroy the body of nine records, four of them the cutover's own beads. The differential does not see it, and reports clean.

Measured 2026-08-17 over `.basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl` and `.beads/issues.jsonl`. Both stores hold **910 records**. The owned ledger holds a `created` event for **901** of them. The nine without one:

    basicly-e2mz.20   comment, edge, status
    basicly-e2mz.21   comment, edge, status
    basicly-u2hl.55   comment, edge, status
    basicly-u2hl.56   comment, edge, status
    basicly-vkh0.25   comment, edge, status
    basicly-vkh0.26   comment, edge, field, gate, status
    basicly-vkh0.27   comment, edge, field, gate, status
    basicly-vkh0.28   comment, edge, field, gate, status
    basicly-vkh0.29   comment, edge, field

The `created` event is the only carrier of a record's title, description, type, priority and acceptance criteria. For these nine the owned store holds the work log, the status, the edges and the gates, and nothing that says what the work was.

The arithmetic points at the cause. The import took 866 records. 910 minus 866 is 44 created after it, of which 35 have a mirrored `created` event and nine do not. So the nine were created in the window before the mirror covered the `create` surface, or by a direct spawn that never entered the mirror at all.

## Why the differential says clean anyway

`differential.QUERIES` is `(phase, ready, gates)`. Three derived answers, and not one of them reads a record's body. So a clean and conclusive verdict is a statement about three queries agreeing, not about the owned store being able to reproduce a record. The verdict is not wrong; it is narrower than the sentence a reader takes from it, and the gap is exactly the data the flip is supposed to make safe to delete.

## Why this blocks the deletion rather than the flip

The flip changes which store answers. Deleting the external store removes the only copy of these nine bodies. So this is a precondition of the deletion and of the fresh-consumer criterion, not of the mode change.

One ordering trap sits behind it: the import path deliberately refuses a ledger that already holds records created after the import, so a reconciling re-import cannot simply be run later. Whatever backfills these nine has to be either a corrective append per record or a widened import that is allowed to run on a live ledger, and that choice is the design question here.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/tracker_cutover.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/differential.py`
- `tests/test_tracker_cutover.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_differential.py`

Landed in 5d109d0 as session work, not a lane, per the below-floor sizing on the bead.

What changed. The gate resolves its id set from the owned ledger first and the external export second, and reports which file it read. An empty store counts as no source rather than as an empty id set, so a store that exists and holds nothing falls through instead of refusing every commit. The tracker root is resolved once, following the redirect, and both stores hang off it, so the ledger obeys the same one-store-per-repository rule the export does.

Exercised as the gate runs, not only in tests. With a known id: exit 0, "Issue id reference is valid." With an unknown id: exit 1, and the message names `.basicly/ledger/events-*.jsonl` as the file it checked, which is the proof the source switched.

Gates: 4293 passed in the full suite, verify --mode fast PASS, ruff clean.

One deviation from the second acceptance criterion, stated rather than hidden. It asked that the refusal carry no reference to the deleted directory. The message names the file it actually read, so on the fallback path it does name the export. That path exists only while the export is the sole store, which is the case for a consumer before the cutover, and naming a file the reader can open is worth more than a message that hides which store answered.

Two traps this hit, both worth the next reader's time. The kit owns the log glob as events.LOG_GLOB and a hook may not reach into the kit, so the hook carries its own spelling and a test now pins the two together - a drifting glob matches nothing, reads the ledger as empty, and would fail open onto a store that is about to be deleted. And loading a kit module through spec_from_file_location without registering it in sys.modules first raises inside dataclasses on the first decorated class, because a dataclass resolves its annotations through sys.modules[cls.__module__].

Wording changed in two places outside the hook: tests/test_git_hooks/test_beads_commit_msg.py and tests/test_kit_tracker_ids.py:486, the second of which is a positive control in another module that asserted the old message text. The whole suite found it; the hook's own tests did not.

Ordering found 2026-08-17, after the epic was filed: this must not land before the flip, so it now blocks on basicly-vkh0.29.

Until the mode flips, every engine write still reaches the owned ledger through the external binary, and a human tracker write goes through the seam as an argv for that binary. So an agent working in this repository today still needs the guidance this skill carries. Retiring it first would remove the instructions for the tool the harness is still using, which is worse than a stale skill.

The corollary for whoever does the work: the replacement is not a deletion. It is a skill for the owned tracker, and it needs the kit CLI surface to be worth documenting first.

Ordering found 2026-08-17, after the epic was filed: the installer deletion must not precede the CI change, so this now blocks on basicly-vkh0.42.2.

quality-gates.yml:106 and improvement-loop.yml:45 both run .scripts/install_br.py. Deleting the script while either workflow still calls it turns every CI run red at that step, and the failure would look like a CI defect rather than an ordering mistake.

The two repointing halves of this bead - the improvement controller spawn site and the corpus drift check - carry no such constraint and could be done first if a smaller unit is wanted.

| field empty, but the description carries an `## Acceptance Criteria` heading | 32 |
| criteria nowhere at all | **55**, of which 52 are not epics |

The discriminator is proven rather than assumed, with one probe per population:

    basicly policy dor basicly-vkh0.36   ->  DoR: READY          (field populated)
    basicly policy dor basicly-e2mz.35   ->  DoR: READY          (heading in the description only)
    basicly policy dor basicly-y8el      ->  DoR: NOT READY - missing: ## Acceptance Criteria

So the heading in the description is sufficient and the field is not required. The 55 have neither, and every one of them stops at classify with the same refusal. 24 of them are priority 1.

The count is a floor rather than a ceiling: the readiness check answers more than the criteria question, so a record that passes this filter can still be refused for another missing section.

## Why it is worth a bead rather than an afternoon

Two reasons, and the second is the one that makes it a mechanism problem.

A dispatch on any of the 55 costs a worktree provisioning and an intake advance before the refusal, so the cost of the gap is paid per attempt rather than once.

And the readiness rules are not ours yet. `policy.definition_of_ready` spawns the external binary's `lint`, which is the first of the operations with no owned equivalent, and porting it is inside `basicly-wpc8.1`. Whoever owns those rules chooses whether the description heading keeps counting. That choice moves this number in either direction, so the report has to read the live rule rather than restate it.

## What to build

A report that names every open record the readiness check refuses, with the reason it gives, so the gap is one command rather than 221 probes. It reads the live check rather than re-implementing its rules.

Then the authoring pass itself, which is the improvement controller's kind of work: 52 small edits, each writing criteria for a record whose intent is already in its title and description.

## Contention to respect

Folding this into `basicly policy dor --all` would touch `src/basicly/policy.py` and `src/basicly/cli.py`. Both are inside the declared scope of open beads, `basicly-wpc8.1` and `basicly-wpc8`, so the report starts as a script instead. Adding a `[[verify.checks]]` entry touches `basicly.toml`, which `basicly-vkh0.29` declares and `basicly-vkh0.37` is amending, so sequence it after those rather than beside them.

## Scope

- `.scripts/report_readiness.py`
- `tests/test_report_readiness.py`

payload.description:
## Context

A lane that hits the runner timeout tries a salvage commit. When that commit is rejected, the advance prints a **passing** hook line as the reason, so an operator reading the message goes to the wrong gate.

Observed 2026-08-17 on basicly-wpc8.1, verbatim:

    [blocked] classify -> classify: runner 'claude' stopped on runner_timeout after 3600s
    in worktree 'basicly-wpc8-1'; the salvage commit was rejected:
    protect-generated-commit.................................................Passed;
    inspect the worktree and re-dispatch

`protect-generated-commit` passed. So did every hook in that list. The actual cause was one stale citation, found by running the commit by hand and reading the whole output:

    docs/requirements/factory-loop.md: 1 stale citation(s); this document has no recorded debt
      - line 85: merge.py:509 - past end-of-file or a blank line

The lane had moved a function in `merge.py`, so a parenthetical line reference in another document landed on a blank line. A one-line fix, hidden behind a message naming a gate that was fine.

## The defect

The reporter appears to take the **last** line of the hook output rather than the failing one. A pre-commit run ends with its passing hooks after the failing one has already printed, so the last line is almost always a pass. The message is therefore not merely unhelpful, it is reliably wrong whenever more than one hook runs.

## Why it costs more than it looks

A timed-out lane is already the expensive case: the tokens are spent and the work is uncommitted. The operator's next decision is whether to salvage by hand or re-dispatch, and that decision needs the real cause. Pointing at a passing gate argues for re-dispatch, which pays the whole lane cost again to arrive at the same one-line fix.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`

payload.description:
## Context

`loop run` refuses to advance when the base checkout has **any** uncommitted change, including changes in files the incoming merge cannot touch. So one piece of unrelated work in progress blocks every lane landing, and the operator's only remedies are to commit work that is not ready or to discard it.

Observed 2026-08-17. basicly-wpc8.1 was green in its worktree — 4295 passed — and committed at 89a5436. The build-to-verify advance, which is the only step that merges, refused:

    base checkout has uncommitted changes; commit or stash first:
    M .basicly/core/kit/tracker/differential.py
    M src/basicly/cost_rollup.py
    ... 13 more, none of them in the lane's commit

Not one of the dirty paths appears in the lane's commit, so `git merge` itself would not have refused. The precondition is broader than the operation it protects.

## Why the broad form was chosen, and why it is still worth narrowing

The broad check is safe and cheap, and it prevents a class of confusion where a landing silently mixes an operator's work into a lane's merge. That reason is real. What it does not distinguish is dirt that **could** conflict from dirt that provably cannot.

The narrowing is checkable rather than judged: the merge's own file set is known before it runs, and so is the dirty set. Refuse on the intersection, on the engine tracker paths the advance itself commits, and on anything the rebase would regenerate. Admit the rest, and say in the advance detail which dirt was admitted, so nothing is silent.

## The operating cost this has today

Parallel work in the base checkout serialises against lane landings. An operator running several agents in one checkout - which is the obvious way to keep a backlog moving while a lane runs - discovers only at the landing that none of it may land until all of it is committed. The repo's own answer is a sibling worktree per unit of work, and that answer is right; the point here is that the precondition makes the failure appear at the worst moment rather than at the start.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`

A fourth upstream defect, observed 2026-08-17 on basicly-wpc8.1's landing, and this one is about the dual write itself.

The landing merged and shipped, but the advance reported:

    [merged] build -> verify: merged harness/basicly-wpc8-1 into main @ 2c7386d;
    WARNING tracker NOT reconciled - br sync --merge exited 7:
    Error: Configuration error: Merge conflicts detected:
      - basicly-jr0l.71: ConvergentCreation
      - basicly-a3yi: BothModified
      ... 13 records in all, 12 ConvergentCreation and 1 BothModified

**All thirteen records are identical in both stores.** Compared record by record on status, updated_at and title length: every one matches. A matching updated_at means neither store holds a later write, so there is nothing to reconcile. A full-content comparison is confounded by fields only one store carries, source_repo_path among them, which is why the comparison was made on those three.

So the reconciliation refuses on the shape a dual write necessarily produces. ConvergentCreation is "the same record was created independently on both sides", which is the literal description of a mirrored create. Twelve of the thirteen are that.

Nothing was lost. Both stores hold 922 records, br reads them, `basicly tracker shadow` is clean and conclusive, and the working tree is clean. The cost is that a real reconciliation failure and this noise are now indistinguishable, and the advance prints a warning an operator must investigate by hand every time.

Do not reach for `br doctor --repair` here. It rebuilds the database from the export, and the export carries zero gate results against the database's own, so the vendor's repair path would destroy the gate ledger to fix a conflict that does not exist.

Four defects now, in the binary's reader, its health check, its repair path and its reconciliation. Each was found by using it rather than by auditing it.

Detection landed 2026-08-17 in a99859f. Backfill designed, proven on a copy, and blocked on one line in another bead's file.

## What landed

`.scripts/ledger_bodies.py` names every record the ledger holds no `created` event for and exits 1, with six tests. Against the live ledger:

    ledger-bodies: 9 of 922 record(s) in .basicly/ledger have no body; deleting the
    external store would destroy the only copy

And `basicly tracker shadow` now states what it did not compare:

    not compared: a record's title, description, type, priority or acceptance criteria
    - the three queries read its status, comments, edges and gate rows only, so a clean
    verdict does not say the owned ledger can reproduce a record

## Why a check beside the differential rather than a fourth query

Three reasons, and the third is decisive. A body query needs `br._live_views` to populate body fields, and that module belonged to a live lane. Comparing body *content* across the stores would manufacture disagreements, because the committed export is redacted and the live tracker is not — while the defect here is **presence**, answerable from the owned ledger alone. And `differential.py` has **zero** size headroom, 10950 of 10950 frozen, as does its test module at 7212 of 7212, so any addition fails `module-size` and the honest remedies are an extraction or a waiver, both their own track.

## The backfill: mechanism chosen, proven, and one line short

`migrate._plan_record` already appends a `created` event whenever `held.created is None`, so **no relaxation of the import refusal is needed** — and relaxing it was rejected outright, because `import_preview.native`'s refusal exists to stop the historical gap being closed by re-import and would absorb genuine dual-write failures into history.

The gap is purely selection, in `br.adopt_hand_writes`:

    undeclared = {ids} - {records in the ledger} - {baseline records}
    wanted = undeclared | held

A bodyless record is in the ledger's record set, so it is subtracted out of `undeclared`; it has no `created` event, so it is not in `held`. It falls in neither set. The fix is `wanted = undeclared | held | bodyless`.

Proven on a copy under /tmp, never the real ledger: 9 bodyless before, 0 after; 5485 lines before, 5595 after; every original line unchanged and in place; each backfilled record arrives with its title, type, priority, description and acceptance criteria under `hand-write-adoption`.

**Blocked:** that line lives in `src/basicly/br.py`, which `basicly-wpc8.1` was holding. Apply it once that lane has landed.

## Two things deliberately not done

**The check is not wired to a `[[verify.checks]]` entry, on purpose.** Nine records are bodyless today, so a wired gate would exit 1 on every commit in this repository. Wire it in the same change that lands the backfill, as a `basicly.d/basicly-vkh0.41.toml` drop-in — the mechanism `basicly-vkh0.37` proved works.

**`basicly tracker shadow` still prints `clean: yes` over the nine.** `br.scoped_differential` wraps the report in `baseline.scope`, which builds a fixed-field `ScopedReport` reading only `disagreements`, `unknown` and `refusals`, so any new finding field on `DifferentialReport` is dropped before the command sees it.
