## Context

`docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` §7 names the `v1.0.0` row of the release ladder as "stabilize and declare": `1.0` is a promise, so the last release proves it instead of adding capability. On 2026-08-27 no tracker record existed for any §7 item (search of 254 open records for semver, surface, acceptance test, breaking, forward-version, compatibility: zero hits on the §7 work). The row carries seven items; two are already recorded elsewhere (`basicly-tcmy.24` error-path polish, open; `basicly-u2hl.46` scope precedence, closed) and are referenced, not duplicated.

The exit criteria are the §7 exit criteria verbatim: the acceptance test passes on a machine that has never seen this repo; the compatibility policy is published; a surface-breaking commit without a `!` marker fails deterministically; `v1.0.0` is tagged by `basicly release` with both pushes owner-approved.

## Success Criteria

- The five consumer surfaces are enumerated in one machine-readable place and frozen: CLI commands and flags, `basicly.toml` plus the `.basicly-local/` overlay contract, the catalog source schemas, the generated-file contract, and the owned ledger event format.
- A commit that changes a frozen surface without a `!` marker is refused by a deterministic gate (hook and `basicly verify`), with a test that trips it.
- A published compatibility policy states what `1.x` promises for each surface and how a break is announced.
- A fresh consumer repository (git plus a uv-provisioned interpreter, nothing else) installs basicly, runs every gate green, and drives one unit of work to a landed commit; this runs as a test, not as prose.
- The next Python minor is exercised in CI so the `3.14+` floor claim is tested, not asserted (CI edits need explicit owner confirmation; the child names that).
- The two requirements documents are folded into the architecture and deleted. `docs/requirements/work-tracker.md` is owned by `basicly-vkh0.42.6` (a `blocks` edge on this epic, not a child); `docs/requirements/harness-board.md` is deleted when `basicly-rn0o` closes (plan §9). Neither is re-filed here. §3 of the plan is refreshed once; the plan file itself is deleted when the ladder is spent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the frozen-surface manifest when `basicly verify --mode full` runs then a diff to any listed surface in the commit under test without a `!` in the subject fails the `surface-freeze` check naming the surface.
- Given a clean machine with git and uv when the acceptance test runs then it installs the packaged basicly into a new repository, every projection gate passes, and one task record advances intake to a landed commit.
- Given `docs/` when the release is cut then a compatibility policy document exists, is linked from the README, and names each of the five surfaces.
- Given `basicly release 1.0.0 --issue basicly-kosxhm --dry-run` when run on main then release-notes, release-fragments and docs-claims are green and the dry run prints the assembled notes.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/**`
- `tests/**`
- `.basicly/core/**`
- `.scripts/**`
- `docs/**`
- `README.md`
- `basicly.d/**`
- `changelog.d/**`

## Context

Owner retro 2026-08-23: a fresh context is right for review, architecture and analysis - independence is the point - but an implementer working the same feature re-derives the repo from zero every dispatch, 1-3M tokens before the first edit, measured on every lane today. The mechanism is already measured: --resume --fork-session gives ~10x cheaper warm starts, one-time penalty per working directory (plan row ejdm). What is missing is the policy: per-role inheritance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a dispatch role is implementer or repair on a feature with a seeded session, THE DISPATCH SHALL fork the seeded session instead of starting cold.
- WHEN the role is a reviewer, validator, decider or retrospector, THE DISPATCH SHALL stay cold, and the policy names why.
- WHEN no seed exists, THE FIRST DISPATCH SHALL create it.
- Demonstrated by: two consecutive implementer dispatches on one feature, the second's cache-read share and cost against today's cold baseline.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/roles.py`
- `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md`
- `tests/test_roles.py`
- `tests/test_runner_session_seed.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`

payload.description:
## Context

Observed 2026-08-27 on `basicly loop supervise basicly-zq9i2m --tier high --max-passes 8`. Passes 4 to 8 were identical: `carried: basicly-2kh170 - landing without a new dispatch`, then `routed: basicly-2kh170 -> rework` on the same scope collision, then the pass spend gate refused (`89259646 tokens forecast; 87452222 remaining`), then `decider: basicly-zq9i2m#3018546b66 [escalation] to human` with a fresh decider rendering each time. The ledger holds 5 `[harness-run] phase=decide` records for that one decision id. Nothing changed between the passes: no lane dispatched, no landing succeeded, the queue held the same item. The session ended `stopped: --max-passes 8 reached`, so five of eight passes bought nothing and the operator read a full pass count as work.

Two defects share the root that a pass has no notion of "this pass changed nothing":

1. `record_pass_refusal` is idempotent per (issue, kind, question), so the queue item was correctly re-enqueued once, but the decider was dispatched again on every pass for an item it had already routed to a human. A human-routed item is pending until a human answers; re-deciding it spends a decider run per pass and cannot change the answer.
2. A pass whose only outcomes are a repeated landing refusal and a repeated queue item is a stall. The supervisor kept looping until `--max-passes`, and a session without that flag would loop until the operator noticed.

## Steps to Reproduce

Root with one carried lane whose landing bounces on a stable cause (a scope collision with a live sibling), and ready children whose forecast exceeds the remaining grant. `basicly loop supervise <root> --max-passes 4`. Observed: 4 identical passes, 4 decider runs on one decision id. Expected: after the first pass that changes nothing, the session ends with a `stalled:` narrative naming the pending decision and the bounced lane, and the decider runs at most once per queue item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a queue item the decider already routed to a human when the next pass finds it still pending then no decider dispatch runs for it and the pass narrative names it as `pending (human)`.
- Given a pass that dispatched no lane, landed no lane and enqueued no new item when the pass ends then the supervisor ends the session with `stalled:` naming every pending item and bounced lane, and exits non-zero.
- Given a pass that dispatched or landed at least one lane then the session continues as today.
- Demonstrated by: `uv run pytest tests/test_supervise.py -q` with a test that drives two identical no-progress passes through the supervisor and asserts one decider dispatch and a `stalled:` ending.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/decisions.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`
- `tests/test_decisions.py`
- `changelog.d/*.md`

## Context

Read-only survey on 2026-08-26 of the nine loop skills (`.basicly/core/skills/*/skill.yaml`) and the four always-on fragments that mention the loop, the tracker, worktrees or gates, 61 claims checked against the code. Eleven are refuted; ten CONFIRMED by reading the code or `--help`, one SUSPECTED. Two would make an agent act wrongly (2, 4). Edit the YAML sources only, then `basicly skills-build --all-default-roots`, `basicly build`, and the projection gates.

1. `harness-client/skill.yaml:54-56` says `board serve` binds the loopback only and answers GET alone, a POST is 405. `src/basicly/board_cli.py:136` (`actions=not args.no_actions`, default on), `board_serve.py:402,411`, `board_actions.py:349` (405 only with `--no-actions`), `--bind` on `board serve --help`. Replacement: "It takes no lock and writes no file, but by default it registers one POST route that runs the basicly command an operator submits - pass `--no-actions` for an unattended wall, and leave `--bind` unset so it stays on the loopback."
2. `fragments/project/harness-loop.fragment.yaml` body: phases "(intake → classify → decompose → build → verify → ship → teardown → retro)". `src/basicly/loop_state.py:31` PHASES = intake, classify, decompose, build, verify, validate, ship, done; the `harness-loop` skill description itself says teardown and retro are not phases. Replacement: "(intake → classify → decompose → build → verify → validate → ship → done)".
3. `harness-loop/skill.yaml:5` and the phase table `:186-194` omit `validate`. `loop.py:451` `_on_validate`, `:470` blocks with `needs_input="validation"`; `validate-as-consumer/skill.yaml:12` covers phase `validate`. Add a table row between verify and ship: "| **validate** | the merged unit owes the consumer check its integrity level requires; the engine dispatches a validator and blocks on `needs input: validation` until a verdict is recorded | `basicly policy gate <id>` to inspect; a failed validate repairs in the lane's worktree and re-lands (see `validate-as-consumer`, `repair-in-place`) |" and fix the description's arrow chain.
4. `catalog-authoring/skill.yaml:41` "Project + verify: `basicly skills-build` then `basicly skills-check`." `src/basicly/skills.py:181-183` writes `.claude/skills` only without a flag; `basicly.toml:415-416` `projection-skills` checks both roots. Replacement: "Project + verify: `basicly skills-build --all-default-roots` then `basicly skills-check --all-default-roots` - bare, both touch only `.claude/skills`, and the `projection-skills` gate checks both roots."
5. `harness-loop/skill.yaml:54-55` "one `chore(ledger)` commit". `merge.py:654` commits `chore(beads): ...`. Replacement: "one `chore(beads)` commit".
6. `decompose-plan/skill.yaml:24` "Acceptance criteria | absent, **or not in EARS**". `plan_gate.py:194` checks presence only; `grep -ri ears src/` is empty (positive control: `demonstration` has many hits). Replacement row: "| Acceptance criteria | absent | The gate checks presence only, so the EARS discipline is yours to keep |".
7. `harness-loop/skill.yaml:401-404` "Two `VERDICT` lines mean fix this first". `cli.py:2966-3269` joins at least eight blockers with `; ` on one line. Replacement: "A `VERDICT: not ready - ...` line joins every blocker it found with `; ` - a dirty base, an unrecognised config key, a metered runner with no token budget, a spent or unmeterable grant, an unapproved root checkpoint, or no open child in the band. Read the whole line."
8. `release-process/skill.yaml:19-21` enumerates four pin files. `release.py:81-86` has `PIN_FILES` plus `PIN_GLOBS = ("docs/how-to/*.md",)`, with the comment that the enumeration is what failed. Add "and every page under `docs/how-to/`".
9. `harness-loop/skill.yaml:194` ship row omits the demonstration guard. `loop.py:646-648` blocks ship with `needs_input="demonstration"` before the not-landed guard. Add: "Two guards run first and both block with no side effects: the recorded demonstration must still select something (`needs input: demonstration`), and the branch must already be merged."
10. `harness-loop/skill.yaml:408` "`supervise.py:_band_verdict`". `src/basicly/working_set.py:285`. Replacement: "`working_set.py:_band_verdict`".
11. SUSPECTED. `decompose-plan/skill.yaml:65` "skills project to **three**" against `:84` "writes two roots"; `skills.py:47-50` has two default roots. Replacement: "the YAML source plus both projected roots - `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills`".

Verified correct, no change: `--runner` on run/advance/supervise, the 15-minute confirm TTL, rework n=2, `dep add` without `-t` refused, the label-write refusal, `needs-input.json`, the redirect file, the changelog categories, the four band verdicts, dot-to-hyphen worktree names.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN each finding is applied to the YAML source, THE PROJECTED SKILLS AND INSTRUCTIONS SHALL be rebuilt, and `uv run basicly check`, `uv run basicly skills-check --all-default-roots`, `uv run basicly agents-check`, `uv run basicly catalog lint` SHALL pass.
- WHEN the always-on fragment is corrected, THE PROJECTED `AGENTS.md` AND `.claude/CLAUDE.md` SHALL carry the eight-phase chain and no `teardown` or `retro` phase.
- WHEN finding 11 is checked, THE RECORD SHALL say which reading was right before the edit.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/skills/harness-loop/skill.yaml`

## Context

Measured 2026-08-27: `docs/tutorial/first-loop.md:35` pins `@v0.8.0` while `README.md:59,94,202,203` pin `@v0.9.0` and `src/basicly/__init__.py:3` says `0.9.0`. `src/basicly/release.py:89-91` leaves the tutorial out of `PIN_FILES` on purpose: its recorded transcripts quote the engine version, so bumping the install line alone would make the page inconsistent with itself. The result is a consumer page two releases behind with nothing that detects it. The plan §7 acceptance test (epic `basicly-kosxhm`) drives a fresh consumer through one unit of work, which is the tutorial's own path; the tutorial should be re-recorded against the release it will ship in and then either join the pin set or carry a gate that fails when its pin lags `__version__`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN `basicly verify --mode fast` runs, THE `docs-claims` CHECK (or a new check declared in `basicly.d/`) SHALL fail when any `@vX.Y.Z` pin under `docs/tutorial/` differs from the latest tag in `CHANGELOG.md`, naming the file and line.
- WHEN the tutorial is re-recorded, ITS TRANSCRIPTS SHALL quote the version the install line pins, and `README.md` SHALL link it.
- Demonstrated by: `uv run basicly verify --mode fast` green on main, then red after `sed -i 's/@v0.9.0/@v0.8.0/' docs/tutorial/first-loop.md` in a scratch copy.

## Scope

- `docs/tutorial/first-loop.md`
- `.scripts/docs_claims.py`
- `tests/test_docs_claims.py`
- `basicly.d/*.toml`
- `changelog.d/*.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- The repository shall carry one committed machine-readable snapshot at `.scripts/frozen_surfaces.json` keyed by the five clause names of `integrity._CONSUMER_SURFACES` (cli-surface, config-surface, catalog-source-schemas, generated-file-contract, ledger-format), each entry derived from the code that defines it: the argparse tree of `cli._build_parser()` (commands, subcommands, flags), the accepted section and key names of `config.CONFIG_SCHEMA` for basicly.toml and basicly.local.toml, the `$id` and `required`/`properties` of `.basicly/core/schemas/{fragment,skill,agent}.schema.json`, the generated-manifest `version` and the projected output set, and `events.KNOWN_KINDS`, `events.KNOWN_FIELDS`, `events.EVENT_FAMILY` and `events.LOG_GLOB` from `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`.
- When `uv run python .scripts/check_surface_freeze.py --check` runs on a tree whose derived surfaces equal the committed snapshot, it shall print `surface-freeze: 5 surfaces current` and exit 0.
- When a derived surface differs from the committed snapshot, `--check` shall exit 1 and print one line per drifted surface naming the surface clause and the first differing entry (for example `surface-freeze: cli-surface drifted: +flag verify --frobnicate`), and the same finding shall appear in `basicly verify --mode fast` and `--mode full` as a failing check named `surface-freeze` declared in `basicly.d/basicly-kosxhm.1.toml`.
- When `--fix` runs, it shall rewrite `.scripts/frozen_surfaces.json` from the code and print `surface-freeze: snapshot regenerated`; the verify entry shall declare no `fix_command`, so the fast set never regenerates the freeze on the author's behalf.
- The snapshot shall be byte-identical when generated on Linux, macOS and Windows (sorted keys, LF, posix paths), asserted in `tests/test_check_surface_freeze.py` together with a positive control that a mutated parser produces a drift naming `cli-surface`.
- The `ledger-format` clause of `integrity._CONSUMER_SURFACES` shall also claim `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`, and `tests/test_integrity.py`'s exactly-one-level property shall still hold over every tracked file.

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_surface_freeze.py`
- `.scripts/frozen_surfaces.json`
- `tests/test_check_surface_freeze.py`
- `src/basicly/integrity.py`
- `tests/test_integrity.py`
- `basicly.d/basicly-kosxhm.1.toml`
- `changelog.d/basicly-kosxhm.1.added.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `12000000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: `uv run python .scripts/check_surface_freeze.py --check` prints `surface-freeze: 5 surfaces current` and exits 0; then `uv run pytest tests/test_check_surface_freeze.py tests/test_integrity.py -q` collects more than 0 tests and passes; expected reading: the check line names exactly five surfaces and the pytest summary line ends in `passed`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- This child edits `.github/workflows/quality-gates.yml` (and nothing else under `.github/`) plus CONTRIBUTING.md; editing a CI workflow requires explicit owner confirmation before the first write, and the lane shall stop with a `needs-input.json` naming that confirmation if it has not been granted.
- When the `quality-gates` workflow runs on `main` or a pull request, it shall include one additional job that installs the next Python minor (`3.15`, pre-release if no final exists, via `astral-sh/setup-uv` with `python-version: 3.15` or `uv python install 3.15` and `UV_PYTHON=3.15`) on `ubuntu-latest`, runs `uv sync`, `uv run python -m basicly.cli catalog lint` and `uv run python .basicly/core/hooks/pre-push.py`, and reports its own result under a job name containing `3.15`.
- The new job shall carry the same 30-minute `timeout-minutes` as the existing matrix job and `continue-on-error: false`, so a red result on the forward interpreter blocks like every other gate.
- If `3.15` is not installable by uv on the runner, the job shall fail naming the interpreter it could not install rather than silently fall back to 3.14; the lane shall verify this by reading the job log of one real run, not by reasoning about the YAML.
- CONTRIBUTING.md (lines stating `Python 3.14+` and `CI runs the same set`) shall name the two interpreters CI exercises (3.14 and the next minor), so the contributor-facing claim matches the workflow; `pyproject.toml`, `.python-version`, `uv.lock` and README.md shall not be edited by this child.

## Scope

- `.github/workflows/quality-gates.yml`
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `8000000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: `gh run list --workflow quality-gates.yml --branch main --limit 1 --json databaseId,conclusion` then `gh run view <databaseId>` lists a job whose name contains `3.15` with conclusion `success`; locally, `uv run --python 3.15 python -c 'import sys, basicly; print(sys.version_info[:2], basicly.__version__)'` prints `(3, 15) 0.9.0` when uv can provision 3.15.

payload.description:
## Context

Observed 2026-08-27: `basicly tracker write -- update basicly-tjhjmk --status deferred` recorded, then `update basicly-tjhjmk --status open` answered "already recorded, so nothing was appended ... the ledger already holds this exact event; the record still reads as it did", and `tracker show` kept `deferred`. The same for `basicly-n5jvhh`. `src/basicly/tracker_write.py:44-47` explains the rule: event ids are content digests, so a fact the ledger already holds is skipped as a replay. A `status=open` event exists on every record from its creation, so no record can ever be returned to `open` by a status write once it has left it. The workaround was `--status in_progress`, a status the record had not held yet, which is in the ready set by `differential.is_ready`.

The replay guard is right for a repeated command and wrong for a state that recurs: a status transition is a fact about *now*, and its identity has to include its position in the record's sequence (or a nonce), not only its payload. The guard also masks itself: the command exits 0 and prints prose, so a script reading the exit status sees success (the failure mode basicly-kn4rip recorded from the other side).

## Steps to Reproduce

```
basicly tracker write -- create "probe" -t task -p 3 -d "## Acceptance Criteria\n- x\n## Scope\n- \`README.md\`" --json   # -> <id>
basicly tracker write -- update <id> --status deferred
basicly tracker write -- update <id> --status open      # observed: already recorded; show -> deferred
```
Expected: the record reads `open`. Run against a scratch ledger directory; the live one keeps every probe.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a record at `deferred` (or any status it left) when `update <id> --status open` runs then the record reads `open` and the command prints `recorded:`.
- Given the same write repeated twice in a row with no other event between when the second runs then it is still skipped as a replay and says so.
- Given a write that appends nothing when the command exits then its exit code is non-zero, so a script cannot read a skipped write as success.
- Demonstrated by: `uv run pytest tests/test_tracker_write.py tests/test_kit_tracker_events_durability.py -q` with a test that defers, reopens, and reads `open` back, and a test that repeats one write and asserts the second is skipped.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/tracker_write.py`
- `src/basicly/tracker.py`
- `src/basicly/owned_write.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`
- `tests/test_tracker_write.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_events_durability.py`
- `changelog.d/*.md`
payload.title: a status a record once held can never be written again because the replay guard keys on content alone

## Context

Re-measured 2026-08-27 against `reference-repos/deepseek-harness` at `origin/master` = `b150a551b8` (`dsh-v0.1.1-rc.2`, the §13 pin; the mirror advances only at release commits, so no fetch between releases moves it). Every concept in §3, §4, §5 and §12 holds; the five dispositions P1–P5 in §11.3 do not move. Ten citations in `docs/research/2026-08-17-deepseek-harness.md` are wrong at the pin they name:

- line 484-485: `run-gates.ts` "909 lines … topologically sorts them (`visit` at `:694`)" — `visit` is the DFS inside `findDependencyCycle` (:744/:750), a cycle detector; ordering is the scheduler loop at :813; 968 lines.
- lines 917-918 (`:618`, `:633`), 1191 (`:668`, `:683`), 1104 (`:672`) — the gate wiring is at :674 (model-experience), :684 (limitations), :677 (archived-agent-notes).
- line 494: "219 non-test `invariant*.ts`" — 227 at master (219 reproduces only at rc.7).
- line 579: "`code-mode.ts` (503+ lines)" — 681 at rc.7, rc.8 and master.
- line 354: `types.ts:82` — :81.
- line 1166: `QUOTA_EXCEEDED_CODE` at `llm/src/error.ts:94` — `packages/llm/llm/src/error.ts:28` at all three pins; wrong when written.
- lines 461, 539, 562: `AGENTS.md:104`, `:122`, `:127-128` — :105, :123, :128.
- line 649: "14 CI workflows" — 18 (§13.4 already says so); line 978 "exactly two tags" — 4 (§13 already corrects it).

The `docs-citations` gate reports 29 of 41 citations unverifiable; a citation into an external repository is one of them, so this class recurs on every pin move with nothing to catch it. One new mechanism worth a line in §7's cost row: PR #2730 splits session projection state from client views with a `stateSchema` that refuses a cached fold before it seeds — the shape P3 refused had no consumer that could refuse; this one has.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the ten citations are corrected, EACH SHALL name the pin (`b150a551b8`) it was verified at, and the `visit` sentence SHALL describe cycle detection, not sorting.
- WHEN §7's durable-state or cost row is read, IT SHALL mention the PR #2730 state/view split in one sentence with its Agent Note path, and §11.3 SHALL record that P3's basis is unchanged by it.
- WHEN `uv run basicly verify --mode fast` runs, `docs-citations` SHALL be green and its unverifiable count SHALL not rise.
- Demonstrated by: `uv run python .scripts/docs_citations.py` (or the check's own command from `basicly.toml`) on the edited document.

## Scope

- `docs/research/2026-08-17-deepseek-harness.md`
- `changelog.d/*.md`

payload.description:
## Context

Measured 2026-08-27 over the owned ledger: 265 open records (258 open, 3 deferred, 2 in progress, 2 blocked) under 20 epics plus 38 with no parent. Of 240 open leaf records, 103 carry no `## Acceptance Criteria` and 70 no `## Scope`, so the loop cannot dispatch them (`basicly policy dor` refuses, the band cannot size them). Several were filed against requirements, designs or module names that later work replaced (the external tracker is gone; the board moved from wall display to cockpit; the release ladder was rewritten 2026-08-08). Nothing today detects an undispatchable record, so the count grows with every session.

The owner asked (2026-08-27) for a backlog analysis that decides whether every record is still actual, not obsolete, and not in conflict with the changed requirements, design and architecture. The doctrine is that code, not prose, is the authority: the result of the triage is therefore a gate that refuses a new undispatchable record, plus a frozen allowlist of today's offenders that the triage lanes shrink to zero, one root epic at a time. A record that is obsolete is closed with a reason naming what replaced it; a record that is real gets acceptance criteria in EARS form and a scope of backticked globs; a record that waits on a decision is deferred with a comment naming the decision.

## Success Criteria

- A verify check refuses any open leaf record (bug, chore, task, feature) that lacks `## Acceptance Criteria` or `## Scope`, except those named in a committed allowlist keyed by root epic, and the allowlist is validated against the population it exempts (an entry naming a closed or missing record fails).
- Every root epic's allowlist key is emptied by a triage lane that read each record against the current architecture document and plan, and closed, deferred or completed it with a reason on the record.
- The count of open leaf records without acceptance criteria or scope is 0 on main after the epic closes, and a new offender fails `basicly verify --mode fast`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the gate when a record under an allowlisted key is closed then the check fails until its entry is removed.
- Given an open leaf record with both sections when the check runs then it is not reported.
- Given a triage lane's epics when the lane lands then `uv run python .scripts/check_backlog_hygiene.py` is green with those keys removed from the allowlist.

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_backlog_hygiene.py`
- `.scripts/backlog_hygiene_allowlist.json`
- `tests/test_check_backlog_hygiene.py`
- `basicly.d/*.toml`
- `changelog.d/*.md`

unsupported.claim: Implementer and repair inherit
unsupported.why: The implementer half holds. The repair half is unqualified and only holds under supervision. The one dispatch site that runs phase="repair" is loop.py:1705 via loop._run_agent, and that function's runner.run call (loop.py:910-922) passes role= but no seed=; `grep -rn 'seed=' src/basicly/loop.py` returns nothing at any dispatch site. Under the supervisor the claim is rescued only indirectly: supervise.py:4084 calls loop.advance(..., repair_dispatch=False), so rework is dispatched by _dispatch_lane as phase "build" with the repair prompt swapped in at supervise.py:959, and the seed gate there is hardcoded roles.phase_inherits_context("build"). unsupported.claim: Fork against the cold baseline on the identical question: 6.1x cheaper, both answering correctly.
unsupported.why: This is the record's demonstration criterion ("the second's cache-read share and cost against today's cold baseline") and it appears only in the commit message for 2a640140, not in changelog.d/basicly-2kh170.changed.md — so no consumer reads it and I am not asking for it to be dropped. Naming it because no second reader can re-run it: the four-row table is a one-time live billing measurement against claude 2.1.247, with no committed instrument, fixture or replay, and the run's own note concedes the baseline was generous ("it answered by grep rather than by reading the corpus the seed read"). The mechanism is tested; the ratio is not reproducible.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN `uv run python .scripts/check_backlog_hygiene.py` runs on a ledger holding an open leaf record (issue_type bug, chore, task or feature) whose description lacks a `## Acceptance Criteria` heading or a `## Scope` heading with at least one backticked glob, THE CHECK SHALL exit non-zero and print the record id, its root epic and the missing section, unless the id is listed under its root epic's key in `.scripts/backlog_hygiene_allowlist.json`.
- WHEN an allowlist entry names a record that is closed, tombstoned or absent, THE CHECK SHALL fail naming the stale entry, so the allowlist is validated against the population it exempts.
- WHEN the check first lands, THE ALLOWLIST SHALL hold exactly today's offenders keyed by root epic, records with no parent under the key `none`, so the tree is green on landing and the count is the frozen baseline.
- WHEN the gate is wired, IT SHALL be declared in `basicly.d/basicly-uz3m68.1.toml` as a `[[verify.checks]]` entry in modes fast and full, never by editing `basicly.toml`.
- WHEN the root epic of a record is resolved, THE CHECK SHALL follow parent-child edges read through the kit tracker module, not a regex over the event file.

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_backlog_hygiene.py`
- `.scripts/backlog_hygiene_allowlist.json`
- `tests/test_check_backlog_hygiene.py`
- `basicly.d/basicly-uz3m68.1.toml`
- `changelog.d/basicly-uz3m68.1.added.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `14000000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: `uv run python .scripts/check_backlog_hygiene.py` prints the offender count per root epic and exits 0 on main; run against a scratch ledger copy holding a probe record with no sections it exits non-zero naming the probe

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the lane finishes, THE ALLOWLIST KEYS for basicly-e2mz basicly-a4q3 SHALL be removed from `.scripts/backlog_hygiene_allowlist.json` and `uv run python .scripts/check_backlog_hygiene.py` SHALL exit 0.
- WHEN a record under those roots describes work already delivered, a module or product that no longer exists, or a requirement that `docs/architecture/architecture.md` or `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` has since replaced, THE LANE SHALL close it with `basicly tracker write -- close <id> --reason "<what replaced it, with a path or record id>"`.
- WHEN a record is still real, THE LANE SHALL write `## Acceptance Criteria` in EARS form and `## Scope` as backticked globs with `basicly tracker write -- update <id> -d "<full body>"`, keeping the existing context text.
- WHEN a record waits on an owner decision, THE LANE SHALL set it `--status deferred` with a comment naming the decision; `--status open` is refused by the replay guard (basicly-bj8kks), so reactivation uses `in_progress`.
- WHEN two records describe one change, THE LANE SHALL close the later one naming the survivor.
- WHEN the lane commits, IT SHALL have touched no file except the allowlist and its own `changelog.d` fragment; every other outcome is a tracker write. About 55 records are in these groups.

## Scope

- `.scripts/backlog_hygiene_allowlist.json`
- `changelog.d/basicly-uz3m68.2.changed.md`

payload.value:
## Context

Observed 2026-08-27 on `basicly-6ajmrc`: the landing failed `pyright-windows`, and the repair brief at `.basicly/usage/repair-brief.json` carried `"evidence": [{"check": "verify full", "command": "basicly verify --mode full", "output": ""}]`; `verify-run.json` recorded `"detail": ""` for the failing check. The next session had to re-run the check by hand to learn the two errors. The ledger shows the pattern repeats: 35 landings failed `verify full` (pytest 44, lint-imports 24, docs-claims 16 by check), and the finding-set warning "the gate reported the same 2 finding(s) as the previous attempt ... this round changed nothing it reports" appears on lint-imports rounds, which is what a repair briefed with no output looks like.

The output exists at the moment it is dropped. `merge.py` re-runs the failures with `verify.rerun_failures(report, worktree_path, verify_mode, capture=True)` for its unreliable-gate test, so `rerun.results[*].output` holds the transcript; `MergeResult` keeps a one-line `detail` and the transcript is discarded. `loop._landing_verify_evidence` documents the gap in its own docstring ("Only the command, not the output ... widening it is merge's contract to change").

## Steps to Reproduce

In a worktree bound to a lane, introduce a type error that only `pyright --pythonplatform Windows` reports, commit, run `basicly loop advance <id>` from base. Observed: the landing fails, the brief's `evidence[0].output` is `""`. Expected: `evidence` holds one entry per failing check with the check's captured stdout+stderr, clipped from the front to the configured brief length.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a landing whose re-run reproduces N failing checks when the repair brief is written then `evidence` holds N entries, each naming the check, its command, and the captured output of the re-run.
- Given a failing check when `verify-run.json` is written then its `detail` holds the check's captured output or a one-line reason, never an empty string for a `fail` status.
- Given a landing with an unreliable or foreign verdict when the brief is written then no evidence entry is fabricated for it (behaviour unchanged).
- Demonstrated by: `uv run pytest tests/test_loop.py tests/test_merge.py tests/test_repair_brief.py -q` with a test that lands a worktree carrying a failing check and reads the captured output back out of the brief.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/repair_brief.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `tests/test_merge.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
- `tests/test_repair_brief.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`
- `changelog.d/*.md`
- `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md`
- `src/basicly/verify_artifact.py`
- `tests/test_loop_repair_evidence.py`
- `tests/test_merge_evidence.py`
- `tests/test_verify_artifact.py`

payload.description:
## Context

The measurement basicly-tjhjmk was opened for, taken 2026-08-27 on this tree with
`.basicly/usage/scratch/baseline.py` (each declared check run exactly as `verify._run`
runs it) and confirmed by a real landing through the new `merge._Landing` instrument.

**A landing runs the full verify suite twice.**

1. `merge._verify_for_landing` runs `verify.run_verify(worktree_path, "full")` after the
   rebase — 132.4s.
2. `loop._record_verify` (`src/basicly/loop.py:2097`) runs `verify.run_verify(repo_root,
   "full")` again in the base checkout *after* the merge has already happened — 132.4s.

That is ~265s of a landing the owner retro clocked at 3-8 minutes. Inside one full run:

| check | seconds | share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pytest | 84.35 | 64% |
| pyright-linux | 10.93 | 8% |
| pyright-darwin | 10.72 | 8% |
| pyright-windows | 10.59 | 8% |
| the other 34 checks | 15.8 | 12% |

`fast` (34 checks, unscoped) is 26.4s, of which `pyright` is 11.0s. The landing also pays
that chain twice more, in the tracker-sync commit and in the merge commit, scoped to the
staged diff — that scoped figure is **not** measured here, and the new per-stage record
answers it on the next real landing (`tracker-commit` and `merge` stages).

## The cut

The second full run is the candidate: it re-runs, in base, the suite that just passed in
the worktree on the same content. `_record_verify`'s job is to *record the gate*, and it
runs a suite to have something to record. Whether the first run's `VerifyReport` can be
carried to the gate record instead is the question — the trees are not identical (the
merge commit exists in base), so this needs an argument, not an assumption.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the cut lands, THE RECORD SHALL carry the before/after from
  `.basicly/usage/landing-timings.json`, measured over real landings, not estimated.
- WHEN the second full run is removed or narrowed, THE VERIFY GATE SHALL still be recorded
  against evidence from a tree that includes the merge commit, or the record shall state
  why that is not needed.
- Demonstrated by: two landings' recorded breakdowns, before and after, with the verify
  stage total named in each.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`

body.post_ship_action: Before the tag: recommend the owner add the missing qualifier to changelog.d/basicly-3oxf0d.fixed.md so the sentence excludes the release-note-debt landing, which still gets the whole-suite command and an empty output. After the tag moves: (1) re-run `uv run basicly verify --mode full` on the tagged commit from a clean tree — on this tree its pytest check reported FAIL and `passed: false` in .basicly/usage/verify-run.json, and re-running the exact argv the artifact named (`uv run pytest -q -n 4 --durations=25`) gave 4992 passed exit 0, so it did not reproduce; if it recurs on a clean tree it is a real red on main and blocks the next landing rather than this ship. (2) File one follow-up record covering the three unsupported items: correct basicly-3oxf0d's Demonstrated-by line to name tests/test_loop_repair_evidence.py, tests/test_merge_evidence.py and tests/test_verify_artifact.py; add a test pinning the MAX_REPAIR_EVIDENCE=5 truncation at loop.py:1659; and either pass `checks=` at merge.py:332 or add a test asserting the whole-suite fallback is what that path is meant to brief. (3) Do not push and do not tag from this review — both pushes are the owner's.

unsupported.claim: Demonstrated by: `uv run pytest tests/test_loop.py tests/test_merge.py tests/test_repair_brief.py -q` with a test that lands a worktree carrying a failing check and reads the captured output back out of the brief.
unsupported.why: I ran it: 265 passed. But grep over those three modules for `result.checks`, `recorded_detail`, `_landing_evidence` and `MAX_REPAIR_EVIDENCE` returns 0 matches, so nothing in them asserts the new behaviour and nothing in them would have failed before the change. The 46 `evidence` mentions in those modules are all `repair_brief.verify_evidence` (tests/test_repair_brief.py:64-97), the pre-existing in-place-repair path, not `loop._landing_evidence`. The test that actually lands a worktree carrying a failing check is tests/test_loop_repair_evidence.py::test_a_landing_briefs_its_repair_with_the_output_the_gate_captured, in a module the declared command does not name — the commit message says the ratchet forced test additions into new sibling modules, and the acceptance criterion was never updated to follow them. The demonstration command as written demonstrates nothing about this change.

unsupported.claim: Given a landing whose re-run reproduces N failing checks when the repair brief is written then `evidence` holds N entries, each naming the check, its command, and the captured output of the re-run.
unsupported.why: src/basicly/loop.py:1659 truncates the generator with `)[: repair_brief.MAX_REPAIR_EVIDENCE]` and src/basicly/repair_brief.py:55 sets `MAX_REPAIR_EVIDENCE = 5`, so for N greater than 5 the brief holds 5 entries, not N. grep for `MAX_REPAIR_EVIDENCE` across tests/ returns zero hits, so no test pins the boundary in either direction. This also weakens the fragment's universal 'each failing check's own command and captured output' for the same N; I looked for a cap test and for a qualifier in the fragment and found neither.

unsupported.claim: instead of the whole-suite command and an empty string
unsupported.why: Read as unconditional it is false on one reachable path. src/basicly/merge.py:332 returns `MergeResult(name, "verify-failed", detail) if owed else None` with no `checks=`, unlike the two sites at merge.py:359 and merge.py:366 which the diff amended to pass `checks=_failed_checks(rerun)`. That verdict carries status `"verify-failed"` which is `repair_brief.LANDING_VERIFY_FAILED` (repair_brief.py:49), so it passes the guard at loop.py:1647 with `result.checks == ()` and takes the whole-suite fallback at loop.py:1656 — the whole-suite command and no output, exactly the old behaviour. loop.py's own docstring concedes this ('The whole-suite command stands in when the failure carries no checks — the release-note debt refuses a landing whose suite was green'). I searched tests/test_merge_landing.py and tests/test_merge_evidence.py for a test that reads a brief off the release-note-debt path; test_merge_landing.py:92 tests the refusal itself and nothing asserts on its evidence. A defence exists — the verify suite was green there, so arguably that landing did not 'fail its verify gate' — but the sentence a consumer reads carries no such qualifier.

## Context

Owner directive 2026-08-28: there is no single point of truth. A session found three stores that disagree: the gitignored `HANDOVER.md`, `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` with `docs/requirements/`, and the ledger. The 2026-08-20 release decision lives only in a ledger comment on basicly-7phc and claims to be recorded in the plan document; it is not. `docs/plan/` and `docs/requirements/` are declared obsolete by the owner. The ledger is the authority for current, in-progress and planned work, and `docs/architecture/` must be cross-checked against the code (basicly-atrqcd).

For the ledger to be the authority its write path must be honest and its read path must be exact, for a human and for an agent alike. Today a write can report recorded when it did not land (basicly-vkh0.50, basicly-wu4w8v), a valid status is refused with exit 0 (basicly-bj8kks), a field cannot return to a value it held (basicly-z9bggw), a whole-file rewrite takes no lock (basicly-cqu7i3), a record can never be removed (basicly-vkh0.34), every count off `tracker show` is inflated by duplicate edges (basicly-vkh0.52), and 44 open records carry single-character labels written by a string-as-list defect.

basicly-uhiq (4/4 children closed) carries the owner ruling of 2026-08-02 that the code is the truth and a spent document is deleted. This epic carries that ruling forward to the stores that outlived it.

## Success Criteria

- Every ledger write either lands or reports failure with a non-zero exit; no write path reports recorded for a write that did not append.
- A human and an agent can create a record, claim it, comment on it, re-record a field it once held, and read the exact folded state back with `basicly tracker show`, with counts that match the event log.
- `HANDOVER.md` is deleted and `basicly` produces the session brief from the ledger (basicly-askx4j), so a new session reads one store.
- `docs/plan/` and `docs/requirements/` are deleted, every surviving citation is repointed, and `docs-claims` stays green.
- Every architecture claim basicly-atrqcd names is either corrected or bound to a tripwire.

## Exit criteria

WHEN a new session starts, IT SHALL be able to answer where the work is, what is in progress and what is planned from `basicly tracker` and `basicly loop status` alone, and no document under `docs/` other than the architecture set and the consumer-facing set exists.
payload.title: single point of truth: the ledger is the one store humans and agents write and read and every other store is deleted

## Context

Measured 2026-08-28 over `.basicly/ledger/snapshot.jsonl`: 72 open records carry labels, and 44 of those labels are single characters (`s` 12, `2` 8, `e` 4, `-` 4, `0` 4, `8` 4). A label is how `basicly loop supervise --label` selects lanes, so a corrupted label set makes lane selection untrustworthy. The shape is a string iterated as a list at a write site: `"phase-2"` becomes `p,h,a,s,e,-,2`. Which writer did it is not yet known; the fold, the import, the seam translator and the kit CLI each touch the field.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `python3 -c "import json;[print(r['record'],(r.get('fields') or {}).get('labels')) for r in map(json.loads,open('.basicly/ledger/snapshot.jsonl')) if 'record' in r and any(len(l)==1 for l in ((r.get('fields') or {}).get('labels') or []))]"`
2. Observe 44 records with one-character labels.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the writer that split a string into characters is found, IT SHALL be fixed and a regression test SHALL write a label through that path and read back the whole word.
- WHEN a label event carries a value of one character, `ledger-fsck` SHALL report it, so the class cannot recur silently.
- WHEN the fix lands, a corrective write SHALL remove every one-character label from every open record through the seam, never by editing the log, and `snapshot.jsonl` SHALL show zero one-character labels.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/**`
- `src/basicly/owned_store.py`
- `src/basicly/tracker_write.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_*.py`
- `tests/test_owned_store.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: the reproduction command in step 1 prints nothing, against a positive control that prints the `phase-7` records.
payload.title: a label writer splits a string into characters so forty four open records carry one letter labels

## Context

Owner directive 2026-08-28: the board must become a cockpit for developers as well as an observability surface for operations. basicly-k6tpep answers the operator question "what is happening right now, and does it need me?". A developer asks a different question: "where is my record, what is being done to it, and what stands between it and main?" Today that answer needs `basicly loop status`, `basicly tracker show` and the worktree list, read separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a developer opens `/record/<id>` on the board, IT SHALL show the record's title, status, priority, derived phase, worktree and branch, the checkpoints held and missing, the rework count per gate, the open blockers and the open dependents, from one snapshot read.
- WHEN a lane is running for that record, the same page SHALL show the agent, the model, the start time, the last progress line and the spend so far, and SHALL say when the snapshot was taken.
- WHEN the record has no lane, the page SHALL say so and SHALL name the next command that moves it, copied from the engine's own remedy text and never composed by the board.
- WHEN the snapshot lacks a field the page needs, the field SHALL render as absent, never as a default value, and the `harness-board/v1` contract SHALL name the added sections.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_*.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/board/**`
- `tests/test_board_*.py`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: `uv run basicly board --out /tmp/board.html` then open `/record/basicly-k6tpep` and read the fields above, and `uv run pytest tests/test_board_lane.py tests/test_board_sections.py -q`.

The ledger already records every dispatch (`[harness-run]` markers with tokens, cost, duration, outcome), every gate result, every rework and every scope violation. Nothing renders them over time. The handover of 2026-08-27 computed the bottlenecks by hand: 95 merge-gate reworks, landing failures by check (pytest 44, lint-imports 24, docs-claims 16), 303 scope violations, a 24 percent lane failure rate over 441 runs. An operator should read those numbers off the board, not off a session transcript.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an operator opens `/ops` on the board, IT SHALL show, for a selectable window of 1, 7 and 30 days: lanes dispatched, landed, failed and reworked; tokens and cost per landed record; the failing verify checks ranked by count; scope violations by path prefix; and median lane duration.
- WHEN a number is shown, IT SHALL name the ledger population it was computed over (record count and event kinds), so a reader can re-derive it with the kit CLI.
- WHEN the ledger holds no event in the window, the tile SHALL say `no data` and never render zero as a measurement.
- WHEN the page renders, IT SHALL read the folded ledger and the `[harness-run]` markers only; it SHALL spawn nothing and hold no lock.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_*.py`
- `src/basicly/usage_*.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/board/**`
- `tests/test_board_*.py`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`

## Context

The first `basicly release` since the release-notes gate landed (basicly-7phc, 2026-08-20) refused its own release commit on 2026-08-28: `FAILED: release-notes` in `pre-commit-script`, 32/33 checks passed, and the tree was restored. Measured with `release.accounted_records` logic re-run without the filename source: 43 closed records with a shipped scope would owe a note after assembly, and every one of them has a fragment named for it whose body never cites its own id in parentheses.

`release.accounted_records` counts a record from three sources: the fragment filename, a parenthetical citation in a fragment body, and a parenthetical citation in `CHANGELOG.md`. Its docstring says `CHANGELOG.md` holds both once assembly has deleted the files. It does not: `release._fragment_body` copies the body verbatim, so a fragment that cited its record by filename alone loses its accounting in the very commit that publishes it. The gate and the assembler disagree about what an assembled note carries, and the release is the only commit where that disagreement is visible.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On a clean main with 149 fragments, `uv run basicly release 0.10.0 --issue basicly-3mr2zg`.
2. Observe `release failed and the tree was restored: ... FAILED: release-notes`.
3. Control: `uv run python .scripts/check_release_notes.py` on the same tree before the release passes, because the filenames still exist.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN `_assemble_fragments` folds a fragment whose body does not cite its own record id parenthetically, IT SHALL append the citation `(<record-id>)` to the fragment's last non-empty line, so the assembled `CHANGELOG.md` accounts for the record exactly as the filename did.
- WHEN a fragment body already cites its own id parenthetically, IT SHALL be copied unchanged, so the section stays byte-identical for every fragment written correctly.
- WHEN `check_release_notes.py` runs on a tree where a fragment named for a closed record has been assembled by the fixed code, IT SHALL report the record as noted, not owed.
- WHEN the regression test runs, IT SHALL assemble one fragment without a self-citation and one with, and assert the first gains `(<id>)` and the second is unchanged, then assert `accounted_records` over the assembled changelog contains both ids with the fragment files deleted.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/release.py`
- `tests/test_release.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: `uv run pytest tests/test_release.py -q -k assembl` green, then `uv run basicly release 0.10.0 --issue basicly-3mr2zg --dry-run` and the real release commit passing `pre-commit-script`.
payload.title: the release commit refuses itself because assembly deletes the fragment filename that accounted for the record

## Context

Second refusal of the v0.10.0 release on 2026-08-28, reproduced in a scratch clone by applying the release steps and running `.basicly/core/hooks/pre-commit.py` over the staged tree: the hook exited 0 and rewrote `docs/architecture/architecture.md`. The pre-commit framework fails a hook that modifies a file, so the release commit was refused and the routed text carried no check name.

The version bump `0.9.0` to `0.10.0` adds one character to the header of every projected instruction file, and `docs/architecture/architecture.md` carries the `always-on-sizes` generated block that states those sizes to the character. `release._regenerate` runs `basicly build` so the projections carry the new version, and nothing regenerates the docs-claims blocks that describe the projections, so the release commit is stale on arrival at its own gate.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Clone this repo at d7860cf4, `uv sync --group dev`, copy `node_modules`.
2. In Python: `release.plan_release`, then `_bump_version_file`, `_regenerate`, `_rewrite_pins`, `_assemble_fragments`, `_write_changelog`; `git add -A`.
3. `uv run python .basicly/core/hooks/pre-commit.py`; exit 0; `git status` shows `docs/architecture/architecture.md` modified by 3 lines of the always-on-sizes table.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN `release._regenerate` runs, IT SHALL also run the `docs-claims` check's declared `fix_command` from `basicly.toml`, so every generated block that describes the projections is current in the release commit.
- WHEN the repository declares no `docs-claims` check, `_regenerate` SHALL run the projection rebuild alone and refuse nothing.
- WHEN a regression test applies a release to a fixture whose `docs-claims` fix command writes a marker file, IT SHALL assert the marker exists after `_regenerate` and that the release commit contains no unstaged change.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/release.py`
- `tests/test_release_assembly.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: the reproduction above ends with `git status --short` empty after the hook, and the real `basicly release 0.10.0` commit passes `pre-commit-script`.

## Context

Third refusal on the v0.10.0 path, 2026-08-28: `git push origin main` from the release commit d2160ce3 was refused by `pre-push-script` on one test out of 5003: `tests/test_check_release_fragments.py::test_the_live_tree_passes_its_own_gate` asserts `inherited + new > 100`. A release deletes every fragment it assembles, so on a release commit the population is legitimately empty and the pre-push refuses every release commit. The gate itself passed on that tree (`release-fragments: 0 fragment(s)`); only the test's positive control failed.

The floor was a population discriminator for the wiring. The release is the producer that legitimately empties the population, so the discriminator must be a marker the release keeps: `changelog.d/README.md` stays, and the count must equal the fragments the gate itself enumerates.

2. Observe `assert (0 + 0) > 100` fail.

- WHEN the test runs on a tree with zero fragments and `changelog.d/README.md` present, IT SHALL pass.
- WHEN the test runs, IT SHALL assert the gate refuses nothing and that `inherited + new` equals the number of paths `fragment_paths` enumerates, so the wiring is still checked against the real population.
- WHEN `changelog.d/README.md` is absent, IT SHALL fail, so an unwired or relocated directory is still caught.

## Scope

- `tests/test_check_release_fragments.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L1`
- demonstration: `uv run pytest tests/test_check_release_fragments.py -q` green on the release commit, then `git push origin main` accepted by `pre-push-script`.

## Context

Windows quality gate, run 33170058900 at fe96b60b (2026-08-28): `tests/test_runner_session_seed.py::test_a_pruned_seed_costs_a_re_read_and_not_the_round` fails with `FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2]` from `subprocess.Popen`. The test puts `stubcli` and `stubcli.cmd` on PATH; `runner.run` hands `argv` to `Popen` without a shell, and Windows `CreateProcess` resolves a bare name only to `.exe`, never through `PATHEXT` to `.cmd`. The same applies to the real `claude` binary on Windows, which npm installs as `claude.cmd`: the runner has never been able to spawn it from a bare name. `runner.py` uses `shutil.which` only for availability checks (lines 785, 976, 2159), not for the dispatch argv. Introduced with basicly-2kh170 (2a640140, 2026-08-27); the gate has been red on every run since.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On Windows: put `x.cmd` on PATH and run `subprocess.Popen(["x"])` - WinError 2. `subprocess.Popen([shutil.which("x")])` starts it.
2. `uv run pytest tests/test_runner_session_seed.py -k pruned_seed -q` on windows-latest.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN `runner.run` spawns a dispatch, IT SHALL resolve `argv[0]` with `shutil.which` before `Popen`, so a `.cmd` shim on Windows and a bare executable on POSIX both start, and IT SHALL report a command that resolves to nothing as a refused dispatch naming the command rather than raising `FileNotFoundError`.
- WHEN the resolved path is used, the recorded `command` on the run record SHALL still carry the spelling the spec declared, so ledger records stay comparable across machines.
- WHEN the regression test runs on any platform, IT SHALL put a `.cmd` twin and a bare shim on a temporary PATH and assert the dispatch starts through `runner.run`.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `tests/test_runner_session_seed.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: the Windows job of `quality-gates` green on the landing commit, read from the job log.

## Context

Owner, 2026-08-28, on https://github.com/niksavis/basicly/releases/tag/v0.10.0: "no one is going to read this wall of text." The workflow published the whole tagged CHANGELOG section as the release body: 124999 characters, 1642 lines. v0.9.0's page is 3050 characters: a summary paragraph, the entry counts, a link to the changelog, the breaking changes, and themed highlights. Measured against the tag: the v0.9.0 CHANGELOG section was 54326 characters, so that page was rewritten by hand with `gh release edit` after publication, and the step lived in no skill, script, workflow or record; `.github/workflows/release.yml` has not changed since 2026-07-22. v0.10.0's page was rewritten by hand the same way on 2026-08-28 and the step now sits in the `release-process` skill, which is guidance, not a gate.

The rule the owner wants: the release page carries the highlights; the changelog carries the record. The deterministic form is a curated summary written under `## [Unreleased]` before `basicly release` (the skill already says a hand-curated body publishes alongside the fragments and keeps its position), and a workflow that publishes only that summary plus the breaking entries and a link, never the whole section.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN `basicly release` runs and the `[Unreleased]` body carries no prose paragraph above the first `###` heading, THE COMMAND SHALL refuse before writing, naming the missing summary, so a release cannot ship without its highlights.
- WHEN the release workflow builds `release-notes.md` from the tagged section, IT SHALL take the prose above the first `###` heading, the entry counts per category, a link to the section in CHANGELOG.md at the tag, every entry whose bold lead starts with `BREAKING`, and the `## Install` block, and nothing else.
- WHEN the published body is compared with the CHANGELOG section, the body SHALL be under 6000 characters for a section over 20000, and every BREAKING entry SHALL appear in both.
- WHEN a regression test runs the extraction over the v0.10.0 section stored as a fixture, IT SHALL produce the three BREAKING entries and the summary and nothing from `### Fixed`.

## Scope

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- `.scripts/generate_release_notes.py`
- `src/basicly/release.py`
- `tests/test_release.py`
- `tests/test_generate_release_notes.py`
- `.basicly/core/skills/release-process/skill.yaml`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- depends on: owner confirmation before the first write to `.github/workflows/release.yml` (CI edit), recorded as a needs-input if not granted
- demonstration: the next release's page under 6000 characters with every BREAKING entry present, read from `gh release view`.

## Context

2026-08-28, truth epic round 1: every landing in the round was refused by `tests/test_decompose.py::test_the_spend_forecast_lands_within_an_order_of_magnitude_of_recorded_spend` because basicly-0cpn51's first run recorded 7,318,875 tokens spent against a forecast of 82,107,017 (0.089x). The test's own docstring says a lane spending less than forecast is not a defect and must not turn main red, and it fails only past `SPEND_RATIO_BAND`. `SpendPair.within_band` is symmetric (`1/BAND <= ratio <= BAND`), so an under-spend past 10x fails the gate against the docstring's intent. The lane whose landing was refused (basicly-6mfhjp) did not produce the marker, and its briefed repair could not converge; it was stopped by hand after 1m17s.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a pair's actual is below its forecast by any factor, `SpendPair.within_band` SHALL be true and `spend_accuracy` SHALL report no violation for it; the pair stays in `pairs` so the under-spend remains readable.
- WHEN a pair's actual exceeds its forecast past `SPEND_RATIO_BAND`, IT SHALL be a violation as today, and the message SHALL say `over the 10x band`.
- WHEN the regression test runs, IT SHALL construct one pair at 0.05x and one at 11x and assert only the second is a violation, in a test file other than `tests/test_decompose.py`, which has 59 tokens of headroom.
- WHEN the change lands, `src/basicly/decompose.py` SHALL not grow: it has 95 tokens and 0.2 prose points of headroom.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `tests/test_decompose_spend.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: `uv run pytest tests/test_decompose.py tests/test_decompose_spend.py -q` green on this ledger, then a landing of basicly-6mfhjp passes verify full.

## Context

basicly-0cpn51, a P1 bug lane with a 225,914-token working set, was forecast at 82,107,017 tokens of spend and spent 7,318,875 in a run that finished normally (returncode 0, 1280 s, 2026-08-28). Preflight admits lanes by that forecast against the grant's remaining budget, so an 11x over-forecast refuses lanes a grant could fund: basicly-tjhjmk was deferred on 2026-08-27 because a forecast of 89.26M exceeded 87.45M remaining. basicly-8gvg records the opposite direction (build factors under-forecast 3x to 11x). Both are one estimator with the wrong shape, calibrated on `[policy.sizing]` seeds that `basicly usage tuning` reports as never measured (`factors: all seeds`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane's forecast is derived, the derivation SHALL be recorded on the run marker (working set, class factor, tier factor, source), so a miss can be attributed to one factor.
- WHEN `basicly usage tuning` runs on this ledger, IT SHALL report a measured build factor per task class where the sample size clears `calibration_min_samples`, and the next forecast SHALL use it.
- WHEN the 0cpn51 pair is re-derived under the calibrated factors, its ratio SHALL fall inside 0.33x to 3x.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `src/basicly/usage_tuning.py`
- `src/basicly/run_record.py`
- `tests/test_decompose_spend.py`
- `tests/test_usage_tuning.py`

- demonstration: `uv run basicly usage tuning` printing a `measured` row for the bug class, and the next dispatched bug lane's marker carrying a forecast within 3x of its actual.

## Context

Recurring shape, third occurrence recorded (memory 2026-08-2x, basicly-85cadb, 2026-08-28 basicly-6mfhjp): a landing runs `verify full`, which runs tests whose population is the whole committed ledger, so a marker written by any other lane's dispatch can refuse this lane's landing. The lane is then charged a rework and briefed a repair for a defect that is not in its diff and cannot be fixed from its worktree. `.scripts/check_release_notes.py` already solved the same shape for its gate with `landing(repo, record_id)`, judged against the lane rather than the tree (basicly-qorx).

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a landing's verify run fails a check or test whose subject is a tracker record other than the landing lane, the landing SHALL report the failure as a base finding naming that record, SHALL not charge the lane a rework, and SHALL not brief a repair in the lane's worktree.
- WHEN the ledger-population tests run inside a landing, THEY SHALL evaluate the landing lane's own records and the base's state separately, so the verdict says which side owes the fix.
- WHEN the failure belongs to the base, the supervisor SHALL hold every landing in the pass with the base finding as the reason, and route one repair to the base rather than one per lane.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `tests/test_merge_landing.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: a fixture landing whose only failure is another record's spend pair is routed as a base finding with rework unchanged.

## Context

2026-08-28, truth epic round 1: every landing in the round was refused by `tests/test_decompose.py::test_the_spend_forecast_lands_within_an_order_of_magnitude_of_recorded_spend`, because basicly-0cpn51's completed run recorded 7,318,875 tokens against a forecast of 82,107,017 (0.089x). The band is two-sided by decision (`test_an_over_forecast_is_reported_too`: money one way, throughput the other), so the pair is a real finding about the estimator (basicly-yjmxjz: one median ratio, 282 over 155 lanes, applied to a working set 8x the median). The recorded forecast cannot change, so the finding is permanent history, and the gate that reads it is the one population gate in the repository with no frozen table: release-notes, module-size, comment-density and noqa-debt each bank a historical red under `[tool.<gate>.frozen]` with a reason, shrink-only, through `.scripts/ratchet.py`. This gate turns main red for every lane until an engine patch lands, three times now (memory 2026-08-06, 2026-08-08, today).

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN `.scripts/check_spend_accuracy.py` runs, IT SHALL compute `decompose.spend_accuracy` over the repository ledger and fail on a violation whose record is not frozen in `[tool.spend_accuracy.frozen]`, naming the record, the ratio and the remedy (fix the estimator or freeze the record with its reason and a `count_delta`).
- WHEN a frozen record no longer violates, the check SHALL fail naming it as graduated, so the table only shrinks, exactly as `[tool.release_notes.frozen]` behaves.
- WHEN the check passes, IT SHALL print the pairs measured, the violations and the frozen count on one line, and the positive-control test SHALL assert the measured population is non-empty.
- WHEN the check is declared in `basicly.toml` `[[verify.checks]]` for `fast` and `full`, the live test in `tests/test_decompose.py` SHALL call the same function, so a landing and a fresh clone agree.
- WHEN this lands, `basicly-0cpn51` SHALL be the one frozen entry, with basicly-yjmxjz named as the reason and the graduation condition.

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_spend_accuracy.py`
- `tests/test_check_spend_accuracy.py`
- `tests/test_decompose.py`
- `basicly.toml`
- `pyproject.toml`
- `basicly.d/basicly-helmej.toml`
- `changelog.d/basicly-helmej.added.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: `uv run python .scripts/check_spend_accuracy.py` green on this ledger naming one frozen record, then a landing of basicly-6mfhjp passing verify full.

## Context

Measured 2026-08-28 over `.basicly/ledger/snapshot.jsonl`: 72 open records carry labels, and 44 of those labels are single characters (`s` 12, `2` 8, `e` 4, `-` 4, `0` 4, `8` 4). A label is how `basicly loop supervise --label` selects lanes, so a corrupted label set makes lane selection untrustworthy. The shape is a string iterated as a list at a write site: `"phase-2"` becomes `p,h,a,s,e,-,2`. Which writer did it is not yet known; the fold, the import, the seam translator and the kit CLI each touch the field.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `python3 -c "import json;[print(r['record'],(r.get('fields') or {}).get('labels')) for r in map(json.loads,open('.basicly/ledger/snapshot.jsonl')) if 'record' in r and any(len(l)==1 for l in ((r.get('fields') or {}).get('labels') or []))]"`
2. Observe 44 records with one-character labels.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the writer that split a string into characters is found, IT SHALL be fixed and a regression test SHALL write a label through that path and read back the whole word.
- WHEN a label event carries a value of one character, `ledger-fsck` SHALL report it, so the class cannot recur silently.
- WHEN the fix lands, a corrective write SHALL remove every one-character label from every open record through the seam, never by editing the log, and `snapshot.jsonl` SHALL show zero one-character labels.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/**`
- `src/basicly/owned_store.py`
- `src/basicly/tracker_write.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_*.py`
- `tests/test_owned_store.py`
- `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: the reproduction command in step 1 prints nothing, against a positive control that prints the `phase-7` records.

payload.description:
## Context

2026-08-28, truth epic: basicly-0cpn51's landing was routed to rework because it changed `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` outside its scope, and basicly-tjhjmk declared that path. The change is the `plan-current-state` generated block re-counting test files, which the landing's own regeneration produces for every lane that adds a test module; `[worktree.regenerate_commands]` already names the path as generated so a conflict there is rebuilt without rework. The scope gate does not read that table, so the same path is generated for the merge and foreign for the scope check. basicly-3oxf0d, basicly-tjhjmk and basicly-0cpn51 each paid a rework and a hand-widened scope for it; basicly-e2mz.18 records the sibling shape for the harness's own per-lane files.

Second half, same round: the supervisor holds every other lane "after an earlier failure this pass" when the first failure is a scope collision, and with no lane to dispatch it repeats the identical pass until `--max-passes` (basicly-n5jvhh's shape). Four built lanes sat unlanded behind one scope finding for three passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a landing's changed paths are compared with the lane's declared scope, a path named in `[worktree.regenerate_commands]` SHALL be excluded from the comparison and reported as regenerated, so no lane declares a generated block as its scope.
- WHEN a lane's landing fails on a scope collision alone, the supervisor SHALL not hold the other lanes of the pass, because the collision says nothing about the base; a held lane is for a failure whose subject is the base.
- WHEN a pass dispatches no lane and every routed outcome equals the previous pass, the supervisor SHALL stop and route the repeated outcome to a human instead of running the pass again.
- WHEN the regression tests run, THEY SHALL cover a regenerated path in a landing diff, a scope collision that leaves siblings unheld, and two identical no-dispatch passes.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/merge_scope.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `tests/test_merge_scope.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: a landing that regenerates `plan-current-state` passes the scope gate with the path reported as regenerated, and a pass with one scope failure lands its other lanes.

## Context

Found 2026-08-22 while probing the swallow on a scratch ledger. Two sites report a tracker write as having happened when it did not, and they are the sites `basicly-kn4rip` left because its own change was additive.

## The kit CLI crashes rather than reports

`.basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py:322` reads `appended[0].record` with no guard. When every draft is swallowed - the ordinary outcome of re-recording a fact the ledger holds - `appended` is `[]` and the CLI raises an unhandled `IndexError` with a traceback. That is the kit-side twin of the engine-seam defect `79bbe0db` just fixed, and that commit does not cover it: the kit is a separate consumer with its own entry point, which is the whole reason it takes a ledger directory as an argument.

A traceback is a worse answer than the wrong one it replaces. An operator reads it as a broken tool rather than as a write that recorded nothing.

## Two engine sites still report a swallowed gate as recorded

`basicly-kn4rip` made `tracker.write` return whether every draft landed. Its own commit message says every other caller discards that return and that the change is therefore additive. That is true, and two of those callers are where it costs something:

- `src/basicly/verify.py:415`
- `src/basicly/rubrics.py:536`

Both discard the boolean and unconditionally print `recorded gate <name>=<status>`.

**`gate report` is the verb with the worst swallow shape.** Its payload is `{provenance, gate, provider, passed}` (`src/basicly/write_verbs.py:227-235`) and carries neither the note nor the actor, so two genuine runs of the same gate with the same verdict are byte-identical and the second is skipped. This is a plain A then A - it needs no intervening B, unlike every other verb. `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/gates.py:222-224` documents the shape as wrong.

So a gate that really ran twice is recorded once, and both call sites say it was recorded.

## Steps to Reproduce

**The kit crash.** On a throwaway ledger under a scratch directory - never `.basicly/ledger/`:

1. `uv run python .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py create <dir> --prefix scratch --title probe --status open`
2. `... update <dir> <id> --status blocked`
3. `... update <dir> <id> --status open`

**Observed.** Step 3 exits with `IndexError: list index out of range` at `cli.py:322`.
**Expected.** It reports that the fact was already held and nothing was appended.
**Control.** Steps 1 and 2 both succeed and print a record and an event id, so the CLI works and step 3's failure is the swallow path specifically.

**The gate report.** Record the same gate, provider and verdict twice on a scratch record and read the record's events: one `gate` event, two reports of success.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN every draft a kit CLI write hands the ledger is skipped, THE CLI SHALL report that and SHALL NOT raise.
- WHEN a gate report records nothing because the ledger already holds it, THE CALLER SHALL NOT print that it was recorded.
- WHEN two genuine runs of one gate produce the same verdict, THE LEDGER SHALL be able to hold both, or the caller SHALL say which one it kept.
- WHERE the engine reports a gate, THE REPORT SHALL rest on what the write returned rather than on no exception having been raised.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `src/basicly/rubrics.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_cli.py`
- `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md`
- `tests/test_gate_report_swallow.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `90000`
- depends on: `basicly-kn4rip`
- demonstration: Drive the kit CLI through a swallowed write and read a report instead of a traceback, then report one gate twice and read the second report against the record's actual event count.
