payload.description:
## What this record is

A completed research spike of 2026-09-04, filed as permanent memory rather than as work. Its
findings are actioned by basicly-hnnmk9.4, which carries the disposition obligation.

The load-bearing result: 41 concepts classified BUILT, REFUSED or UNADDRESSED, each with a
file:line, a commit or the refusal measurement. 22 are unaddressed, 16 harness and 6 execution.
The deleting commit is c73dbef7, not the 78962968 in circulation. Seven limits are named in its
own coverage section, including four rows resting on bounded probes that returned zero without
their own positive control.

---

# Recovering `docs/research/2026-08-17-deepseek-harness.md`

## Verdict

The document is recoverable in full — 1479 lines, byte-identical at the commit D-43 cites — and
D-43 is real, sound, and **narrow**. D-43 (`docs/architecture/architecture.md:4833-4882`) absorbs
exactly five proposals the document's own §11.3 table put forward, and nothing else: those seven
lines are the *only* mention of `dsh` or Cordis anywhere in the 4900-line architecture
(`grep -n "dsh\|Cordis\|deepseek" docs/architecture/architecture.md` returns hits only at
4835, 4843, 4845, 4851, 4857, 4879, 4881). The one adoption is built and its migration window has
closed (`src/basicly/catalog_token_cost.py:62` `REQUIRED_FROM_VERSION = "0.11.0"` against
`src/basicly/__init__.py:3` `__version__ = "0.11.0"`); the narrow surviving half of P4 is also
built and shipped (`basicly catalog dump`, `src/basicly/cli.py:2512`, record `basicly-8kqkxy`
closed 2026-08-23). The four refusals each rest on a measurement I could not re-run — the
`deepseek-harness` clone is not in this tree — but each measurement is a *third-pin* reproduction
(rc.7 → rc.8 → `dsh-v0.1.1-rc.2`), so three of the four refusals are unusually well insulated
against drift; only P4 rests on a fact that has plausibly moved. The valuable finding is what
D-43 left on the floor. The document describes roughly forty distinct mechanisms of a shipped
agent runtime, and the P-list touched five of them. The unexploited residue clusters hard in two
places: **event-log forward-compatibility discipline** (dsh refuses an unknown event by default;
basicly's fold is tolerant by default and its own docstring says the resulting failure mode is
undetectable) and **structured dispatch outcomes** (dsh's workflow result *never rejects* and
carries a `stopReason`; basicly paid for the absence of that with `provider_limit.py`, a
post-hoc discriminator over 110 mis-charged runs). Both speak to the execution-process core, not
the harness core.

## Recovery, and a correction to the brief

| Fact | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Deleting commit is `c73dbef7`, not `78962968` | `git log --all --diff-filter=D --name-only -- 'docs/research/*'` → `c73dbef7 docs(architecture): absorb the research documents as decision records and delete them (basicly-e2mz.46)`, Sat Aug 29 14:57:17 2026. It deleted five research files at once. |
| `78962968` is the last commit at which the file was live | `git log -1 --format='%h %ad %s' 78962968` → `chore(tracker): close the release record and file the macos build cap flake (basicly-kcgptv)`, Sat Aug 29 14:10:12 2026 — 47 minutes before the delete. |
| The brief's command (`78962968^:...`) is wrong by one; D-43's own command (`78962968:...`) is right | `git show 78962968:docs/research/2026-08-17-deepseek-harness.md` → exit 0, 1479 lines. `diff` against `git show c73dbef7^:docs/research/...` → identical (exit 0). |
| Full text used for this report | `/tmp/.../scratchpad/deepseek-doc.md`, 1479 lines |

Sibling documents deleted in the same commit, for context: `2026-07-26-sota-review.md` (absorbed
as D-44), `2026-08-14-harness-board-design.md`, `2026-08-17-archify-visualization.md`,
`2026-08-19-documentation-routes.md`.

## Structure of the recovered document

Thirteen sections, three of them later passes appended to the original review. Everything after
§10 is re-measurement, which is why the document is auditable at all.

| § | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Verdict, with an **amendment** admitting a §1 clause was refuted at rc.8 |
| 2 | "What the paper actually is" — the mis-attribution warning: the paper is about Cordis and Koishi, not about `dsh`; `deepseek` occurs once in it, as an affiliation |
| 3 | The conceptual model: paper constructs (Table 2 dictionary), the fiber lifecycle, the loader, and where the harness's practitioner primer diverges from the formalism |
| 4 | What the harness is built from: shape (226 packages), composition layering, the capability seam, the isolate realm |
| 5 | Mechanisms — work representation (5.1), decomposition *absent* (5.2), dispatch (5.3), the session log (5.4), verification (5.5), landing *absent* (5.6), presets (5.7) |
| 6 | Claimed versus built, split paper (6.1) / product (6.2) / where the harness exceeds the paper (6.3) |
| 7 | A 27-row concept-by-concept comparison table with basicly |
| 8 | Eight open questions, each later annotated SETTLED with a forward link |
| 9 | "Not established" — twelve explicit non-claims |
| 10 | Provenance, pins, licence note, method note |
| 11 | Second pass 2026-08-19: Q1 and Q4 settled; **§11.3 is the P1–P5 disposition table** |
| 12 | Third pass 2026-08-20 at rc.8: five remaining questions settled; §12.8 disposition deltas |
| 13 | Fourth/fifth/sixth passes 2026-08-22 at `dsh-v0.1.1-rc.2`: the instrument recovered, a 40-row evidence table, droppable claims, non-re-measurable claims, and §13.6 — "six commands that do not run" |

## D-43, verbatim in substance

Located at `docs/architecture/architecture.md:4833` (index row at `:4052`:
`| D-43 | The plugin paradigm: four refusals, one adoption, two lessons | accepted | §6, §19, §31, §34 |`).

### The one adoption

**P5 — a catalog source declares its always-on token cost, and `basicly catalog lint` fails a
declaration that drifts past its tolerance.** D-43 at `:4837-4840`: "built as
`catalog_token_cost`, mandatory from 0.11.0 — basicly-e2mz.48.3, basicly-puohe0".

Verified built:

- `src/basicly/catalog_token_cost.py` exists; `:57` `DECLARED_COST_KEY = "token_cost"`; `:62`
  `REQUIRED_FROM_VERSION = "0.11.0"`, with the module's own docstring stating the window is keyed
  on the tree's version, never a date, "because a clock makes a gate's verdict depend on when CI
  happened to run".
- Wired into the lint at `src/basicly/catalog_lint.py:289` (`violations`) and `:450` (`warnings`).
- The authored field is in both schemas: `token_cost` appears in
  `.basicly/core/schemas/skill.schema.json` and `.basicly/core/schemas/fragment.schema.json`.
- Regression test: `tests/test_catalog_token_cost.py`.
- The window is **closed**: `src/basicly/__init__.py:3` is `__version__ = "0.11.0"`, and ledger
  record `basicly-puohe0` is closed with `close_reason` = "64 sources declare the measured token
  cost; lint reports none at version 0.11.0".

Two details of the built form that differ from the source proposal, both from the module
docstring: the declared cost is **measured as a projection delta, never configured**, and it is
declared **per always-on surface**, because `AGENTS.md` inlines scoped fragments and the other two
always-on files do not (the example given: `code-is-authoritative` costs codex 132 tokens and
claude/copilot zero). A skill's surface is the host's *listing*, not a target file
(`LISTING_SURFACE = "listing"`, `:59`).

### The four refusals and their measurements

| # | Refused proposal | The measurement D-43 carries (`architecture.md` line) | Still valid? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | An effect-inverse or undo layer over git or the filesystem | `:4848-4852` — "the reference implementation tracks no filesystem effect itself — 0 `.effect(` sites in `fs-local` against 91 mutation syscalls, and `backup: null` on the one slot its platform offers." Plus the positive claim: basicly's append-only log and bounce-on-conflict landing (§27) "already give what a LIFO inverse gives Cordis, by withholding an irreversible emission rather than compensating for it afterwards." | **Robust.** The source document reproduced this at three pins (§12.8: "Across 536 commits and 7 new packages, not one filesystem inverse was added"; §13.2: `fs-local` `.effect(` = 0 "at a third pin"). The `backup: null` line held at all three. The 91-syscall figure is the weak leg — §13.4 records it as **unverifiable**, because §11.1 never named its syscall set and a substituted ten-name set gives 45. The refusal does not depend on it: 0 effect sites is the load-bearing half, and that one is doubly confirmed. |
| P2 | A dynamic component runtime mounted from configuration | `:4853-4856` — it "abandons §5's rule that `.basicly/` holds no engine code and breaks §34's exhaustive layering contract. `vendor/` saw 0 commits in the measured range against 418 in `packages/`: the dynamic core is not where the harness itself moves." | **Valid, and the measurement is not the reason.** The primary ground is a basicly invariant (§5, §34), which no upstream movement can touch. The 0-vs-418 commit figure is a corroboration over a two-day window (rc.7→rc.8) and has certainly moved by now — but D-43's argument survives without it. The Python-side half (§11.2's two spikes: the descriptor protocol is *not* the `Proxy` analogue; module eviction is advisory) is a fact about CPython 3.14.6, not about `dsh`, so it does not expire on an upstream release. |
| P3 | A `before`-content field on the change-summary artifact | `:4857-4858` — "`FsWriteOutcome.before` is presentation-only in `dsh`. A field with no consumer that can refuse is the anti-pattern §33 names." | **Valid.** The recovered §11.1 gives four consumers, all presentation (`tool-fs/src/write.ts:96-98`, `:126`; `edit.ts:108`, `:144`), and three independent lossiness proofs (null above a 10 MiB basis, null for non-UTF-8, line-ending normalised) that make it unusable as an inverse *even if wired*. §12.8 records the file byte-identical at the next pin. The refusal rests on basicly's §33 contract rule, not on upstream state. |
| P4 | "No privileged core, every row replaceable from configuration" | `:4859-4860` — "measured false as an absolute — three bootstrap rows are privileged in the industrial application." | **The measurement holds at its pin but is the one most exposed.** §12.3 names the three rows (`new Context()`, `ctx.provide('dshHomePath')`, `ctx.plugin(Loader)` at `packages/boot/app-boot/src/index.ts:757-786`) and records that the vendor sentence at `docs/architecture.md:13` "was not weakened at rc.8" and was "still present, still unweakened" at rc.2. That is a claim about a **third party's prose in a pre-1.0 developer preview**, three releases stale as of 2026-09-04; the vendor could have softened the sentence, and the refusal's basis would revert from "measured false" to a design-invariant argument. That would not flip the disposition — D-43's real ground is §6's "the engine disposes, agents propose" and D-01 — but the *stated reason* would be wrong. This is the one refusal whose citation I would re-run before quoting it. |

The narrow half of P4 that D-43 keeps (`:4842-4844`) is **built**: `basicly catalog dump`,
"Print the composed fragment selection: per-item origin and selecting axes"
(`src/basicly/cli.py:4990-4993`), implemented at `src/basicly/cli.py:2512` `_cmd_catalog_dump`
with `_dump_origin` at `:2598`. Ledger record `basicly-8kqkxy` is closed, `close_reason`
"shipped by the harness loop", 2026-08-23T15:31:05Z, verify gate passed at seq 14.

### The two lessons and the one instrument

D-43 `:4862-4870` adopts two lessons, and **neither is built**:

- A budget counter advancing only on attributable units, derived from the durable log by
  validated replay. Carried by `basicly-rhzr6d` — **open** ("grant spend travels in the ledger so
  a fresh clone reads the same budget the origin machine does"). The nearest built thing is
  `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py:52-55`, "One accumulator, called from both sides …
  there is no hand-written increment anywhere", and `.scripts/check_spend_accuracy.py`, which
  gates forecast-against-actual rather than deriving the counter.
- Every exemption list machine-validated against the population it exempts from. Carried by
  `basicly-3enm1o` — **open**. `.scripts/check_waivers.py` does it for the size waivers only
  (its docstring: "A retiring record the tracker does not hold fails too").

`:4871-4874` keeps one instrument for a proposal not made: the namespace-sentinel weakref
eviction probe. It exists as prose in D-43 and in the recovered §11.2; there is no code.

## Reconciliation table

Every concept the document proposed or described as a portable mechanism. `BUILT` is claimed only
where I can name the code.

| Concept (document §) | State | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Declared always-on token cost on a catalog source (§11.3 P5) | **BUILT** | `src/basicly/catalog_token_cost.py:57,62`; `catalog_lint.py:289,450`; `tests/test_catalog_token_cost.py` |
| A command printing the composed selection with each item's origin (§11.3 P4 narrow half) | **BUILT** | `src/basicly/cli.py:2512,2598,4990`; `basicly-8kqkxy` closed |
| Effect-inverse / undo over git or the filesystem (§3.1, §11.1) | **REFUSED** P1 | `architecture.md:4848` — 0 `.effect(` sites in `fs-local`; `backup: null` |
| Withholding an irreversible emission instead of compensating (§3.1 output-commit problem) | **BUILT** (pre-existing, *confirmed* by the refusal) | `architecture.md:4850-4852` cites §27's bounce-on-conflict landing; `src/basicly/landing_gate.py`, `src/basicly/merge.py` |
| Dynamic component runtime mounted from configuration (§3, §4.2, §11.3 P2) | **REFUSED** P2 | `architecture.md:4853` — breaks §5 and §34 |
| Annotation-free transactional HMR with cache rollback (§3.3) | **REFUSED** under P2 | same |
| `before`-content on a handoff artifact (§11.1, §11.3 P3) | **REFUSED** P3 | `architecture.md:4857` — presentation-only, no consumer that can refuse |
| "No privileged core, every row replaceable" (§12.3, §11.3 P4) | **REFUSED** P4 | `architecture.md:4859` — three bootstrap rows |
| Append-only durable log projected by folds (§5.4) | **BUILT** (pre-existing) | `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`; arch §32 |
| Order-independent composition, byte-identical output (§3.3) | **BUILT** (pre-existing) | arch §11, cited by the document's own §7 row |
| Per-session namespace isolation enforced at mount, not by convention (§4.4) | **BUILT** in a different mechanism | sibling git worktree + zero-touch tracker state, arch §27.1; `src/basicly/worktree.py` |
| Provider-per-agent-family delegation seam (§5.3) | **BUILT** (pre-existing) | `src/basicly/runner.py:218` `resume_style`, `:280`; `RunnerSpec` adapters |
| An engine-owned fan-out ceiling invisible to the dispatched script (§5.3) | **BUILT** | `src/basicly/supervise.py`; lane cap at `basicly.toml:368,379` |
| A field/instrument with no consumer that can refuse, as a gate (§12.7 refuse-lesson, P3) | **BUILT** as a gate | `.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py` — "nothing ships with references only inside its own module"; names three past instances |
| Mechanically checkable cross-references between prose and code (§12.5) | **BUILT**, both directions | `.scripts/check_docs_citations.py` (doc→code), `.scripts/check_code_citations.py` (code→doc, 370 marks in 100 modules) |
| Banning a retired marker so it "cannot creep back" (§5.5) | **BUILT** | `.scripts/check_retired_vocabulary.py`, git-baseline ratchet |
| Regenerate-rather-than-reject in a pre-commit hook (§5.5a) | **BUILT** (partial) | `fix_command` on a verify check, `src/basicly/config.py:1075-1080`; "the fix never replaces the verdict". ## The UNADDRESSED analysis

### Harness tools

1. **A dispatch result that never rejects, carrying a `stopReason`.** Touches the runner/dispatch
   seam (`src/basicly/runner.py`, `runner_envelope.py`, `provider_limit.py`) and the routing step
   of a supervised pass. Evidence needed: none, really — the evidence is already recorded.
   `provider_limit.py:1-8` measured 110 of 702 runs where a provider refusal was
   indistinguishable from an agent failure at the routing layer, "70 of them inside 20 minutes on
   2026-08-28 before a human stopped the session". The question is only whether the envelope can
   be made to carry a closed outcome vocabulary instead of an exit code plus discriminators, and
   that needs a census of what today's callers branch on.
2. **Fail-closed confinement that substitutes the argv.** Touches the tool-call boundary (layer 1,
   `.basicly/core/hooks/`) — today a hook says deny or allow; dsh's provider hands back the argv
   to run *instead*. Evidence needed: whether any host in the supported set (Claude Code, Codex,
   Copilot) exposes an input-rewrite decision at the PreToolUse boundary — a vendor-docs fact, and
   `interface-facts` territory, not a recall answer.
3. **A `stopReason`-shaped named refusal for an unsupported option.** Touches the dispatch brief
   and the agent/tool declarations: `DEFERRED_AGENT_OPTIONS` makes "we do not support worktree
   isolation here" a loud error rather than a silent ignore. Evidence needed: a list of options
   basicly's dispatch surfaces accept and silently drop.
4. **A minimal composition kept as a measurement baseline.** Touches the target/axis selection in
   `.basicly/core/targets/` and the adherence work on `basicly-agzx.1`. Evidence needed: whether a
   two-fragment always-on baseline can be projected and dispatched against, so a recall figure has
   a floor to sit above. Note a discrepancy the document introduced: §11.3's "branch not taken"
   asserts the always-on character cap "already exists" as a ratchet that "refuses the last
   straw", but `.basicly/core/targets/claude.yaml:9` and `copilot.yaml:9` declare
   `max_size_warning: 9000` and `codex.yaml:26` declares `16000` — a **warning**, not a refusal.
5. **A capability seam as a three-role completeness rule.** Touches `catalog lint` /
   `wired_or_deleted` and the module-layering contract (arch §34). Evidence needed: a census of
   basicly's own seams to see how many ship a definition and a provider with no consumer that can
   refuse — the same question `wired_or_deleted.py` already answers for names, one level up.

### Gates and verification

6. **A gate dependency graph.** Touches `basicly verify` end-to-end and the `[verify]` config
   contract consumers author against. `VerifyCheck` (`src/basicly/config.py:1066-1080`) has no
   `needs`; the check list is flat and ordered by declaration. Evidence needed: measure how much
   of a full verify run is wasted on checks that run after a cheap prerequisite already failed —
   if the answer is small, this is not worth a schema change to a consumer-facing contract.
7. **Pre-append validation by an independent re-derivation.** Touches the ledger write seam
   (`.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py` `append`, `gates.py:219`). dsh's goal package rejects a
   malformed candidate "before the candidate event enters the durable log"; basicly's `fsck`
   finds the same class afterwards, and `.scripts/check_ledger_fsck.py` had to declare a frozen
   allowance for a lost event precisely because "an append-only log has no undelete". Evidence
   needed: the class of defects the existing `fsck` findings fall into, and which of them a
   second fold at write time would have refused. This is the highest-value item in the report:
   the cost of *not* having it is already paid and recorded in `pyproject.toml`
   `[tool.ledger_fsck.frozen]`.
8. **Required-on-read event kinds with an `ignorable` escape and a structural format version.**
   Touches the ledger event vocabulary (arch §32.3, eighteen kinds) and every cross-version
   reader — a consumer repo on an older kit reading a newer ledger. basicly is tolerant by
   default and says so: "never change a kind's meaning, never reuse a kind name … nothing here
   can detect that" (`events.py:78-80`). dsh inverts the default and makes the undetectable case
   detectable. Evidence needed: whether any consumer repo is actually pinned to an older kit
   version against a shared ledger — if not, the risk is theoretical and the tolerance is right.
9. **A runtime-invariant plane.** Touches every module and the verify runner. dsh ships 219
   `invariant*.ts` companions and a registry service with a regex allow/blocklist. basicly's
   equivalent surface is the gate list. Evidence needed: whether any basicly defect class is
   *only* observable at run time (mid-dispatch, mid-supervise) rather than at commit time — the
   stall watchdog and `contention.py` suggest yes, which would make this a real gap rather than a
   restatement of the gate stack.
10. **A required "declared limitations" field on every catalog source.** Touches the catalog
    schemas and `catalog lint`. The carrier objection D-43 raised is already answered — the
    adopted P5 put a declaration in YAML — so the remaining question is content, not form.
    Evidence needed: a sample of skills to see whether an author who had to state "what this does
    not do" would have written something a reader could act on.
11. **A gate that executes a command a document prints.** Touches `docs-claims` and the
    architecture's own evidence rows. §13.6 found **six** rows whose printed command produces the
    wrong figure, one of them a zero whose positive control also collapsed to zero — "the row's
    own guard against a bad probe fails silently with it". Evidence needed: a count of `sh`-fenced
    commands in `docs/` and `.basicly/core/` that a reader is invited to run, and how many are
    reproducible today.
12. **A positive-control requirement as a gate rather than a fragment.** Touches
    `external-facts.fragment.yaml` and the hook tier. The document hit the same `rg -r` trap
    twice in three passes and concluded the note "belongs in a gate rather than a document"
    (§12.9) — the identical argument `unsplit-loop-guard.py` makes for itself ("the rule already
    exists, always-on … it was in context and did not bind"). Evidence needed: a census of
    probe-shaped Bash calls in recent transcripts whose flags cannot produce the claimed output.

### Instructions and prompting

13. **`What the model sees` and `KV Cache effect` as declared fields.** Touches the catalog
    schemas beside `token_cost` and the projection. `token_cost` answers "what does this cost";
    neither of the other two is asked. Evidence needed: whether the KV-cache question is even
    well-posed for basicly's projection, where always-on files are a stable prefix — if the
    answer is "always zero", the field is noise.
14. **A three-role event-domain rule as an authoring instruction.** dsh states "picking the right
    domain is the first decision in most changes" and encodes it in a primer its plugin authors
    read. The basicly analogue is a fragment or the `catalog-authoring` skill telling an author
    which tier a rule belongs in. Evidence needed: how often a catalog source lands in the wrong
    tier (always-on fragment vs on-demand skill vs hook) — a defect count from the ledger.
15. **A format-adoption pin with exactly one grandfathering comment.** Touches the catalog schema
    version and `catalog lint`. dsh pins `FORMAT_ADOPTED = '2026-07-05'` and permits one
    grandfathering comment per older note; basicly's `token_cost` window already keys on version
    rather than date, which is the same idea done better. Evidence needed: whether any *other*
    catalog field wants a migration window, in which case the pattern should be extracted rather
    than re-hand-written.
16. **A "no central index, path is the metadata" rule for the on-demand corpus.** Touches skill
    discovery and routing (`catalog_routing.py`, `routing_evals.py`). dsh deliberately refuses an
    `INDEX.md` and rests retrieval on a closed class set encoded in the path. Evidence needed:
    whether basicly's routing evals fail more on ambiguous names than on missing descriptions —
    if names carry the routing, path-as-metadata is a real lever.

### Orchestration

17. **A code discriminator on the single blocked state.** Touches every phase that can block and
    the `needs-input.json` protocol. basicly has one `blocked` status (`loop_state.py:45`) and one
    structured stall reason (`needs_input.py`); dsh has one durable `blocked` phase plus a closed
    lower-kebab-case `code` vocabulary that separates provider limits, budgets, execution errors
    and human-input requests. basicly's four dsh-side codes were measured as *dark* (§12.7:
    `round-limit`, `queue-failed`, `prompt-rejected`, `model-reported`, none of them a token or
    quota mapping) — which is the warning, not the model. Evidence needed: the distinct causes
    behind basicly's own `blocked` events in the ledger; if the count is one or two, no vocabulary
    is warranted.
18. **A continuable child with a durable inbox and structural follow-up authority.** Touches
    `loop supervise`, the dispatch brief, and `loop decision answer`. dsh checks follow-up
    authority against "the exact live direct parent recorded in the child's durable header",
    re-checked after cold resume. basicly resumes by session id and forks
    (`runner.py:104-111`); nothing checks *who may deliver* into a lane. Evidence needed: whether
    two concurrent supervisors or a stray session can deliver an answer into a lane that did not
    ask — a reachability question over `board_actions.py` and the decision queue.
19. **A compare-and-set revision fence on a record.** Touches the ledger write path and
    concurrent-lane safety. basicly's lock is staleness-bounded, not compare-and-set. Evidence
    needed: whether any recorded ledger defect was a lost update rather than a lost event — the
    `fsck` findings are the population.
20. **Tombstoned deletes and single-writer cross-assignment on the shared board.** Touches
    `board_actions.py` / `owned_write.py`. Evidence needed: whether a record has ever been
    reassigned by two lanes in one pass.
21. **Withdrawal visible one step early, and staleness checked at two levels.** Touches phase
    advance and rework. The idea is that a dependent recomputes its readiness *before* the thing
    it depends on is torn down, and that a long transition is checked for staleness both at its
    boundary and inside its loop so a rollback can be partial. Evidence needed: whether a basicly
    advance has ever half-completed and left a lane readable-but-invalid — the "stranded merge"
    class in the operator's own notes suggests yes.
22. **Advisory write scopes declared as advisory, with the bypasses enumerated.** Touches the plan
    gate's scope globs and `contention.py`. dsh's `agent-team` states plainly that "Bash,
    formatters, code generators, and direct external writers can bypass filesystem version
    checks". basicly's scope globs have the same property and, as far as I found, do not say so.
    Evidence needed: a single lane that wrote outside its declared globs via a formatter.

## Which core each speaks to

The owner's two cores split the residue cleanly, and the split is itself a finding: **`dsh` has
almost nothing to say about the execution process and a great deal to say about the harness.**

- **Execution process (the state graph).** Only five items: #7 and #8 and #19 (what the durable
  substrate guarantees between states), #17 and #21 (what a state's result carries to the next,
  and what happens when a transition half-runs). #1 is the sharpest of them all, because a
  dispatch outcome *is* the edge between BUILD and VERIFY, and an exit code that cannot separate
  "refused" from "failed" corrupts the edge. This is thin because the document establishes, at
  three pins with a working positive control, that `dsh` has **no decomposition** (`decompos` = 0
  at all three pins) and **no landing** (`worktree` 5 hits, `git commit` 3, against a `session`
  control of 30 624) — the two halves basicly's graph is mostly made of.
- **Harness (tools, gates, instructions).** Everything else — all of #2–#6, #9–#16, #18, #20, #22.
  This is where `dsh` is a mature system and where the mining is worth doing: 219 invariant
  modules, a topologically ordered gate DAG, two gates on *documentation structure*, and a
  sealed-manifest freeze on its design-record corpus.

D-43's own closing paragraph draws the boundary correctly and is worth keeping in view
(`architecture.md:4875-4878`): "It forecasts no cost: it caps a round count … Nothing in it would
have caught this repository's 3-to-11x under-forecast (basicly-yjmxjz)." `basicly-yjmxjz` is
**open**. Nothing in the unexploited residue closes it.

## What could not be established

- **Every measurement behind the four refusals is un-re-runnable from this repository.** The
  `deepseek-harness` clone the document pins
  (`<workspace>/reference-repos/deepseek-harness`, per §10) was not checked for
  existence, because doing so would reach outside the repository under audit; and I ran no
  `git`, `rg` or `curl` against any upstream source. Every figure in the refusal column is
  reported as **the document's claim at its pin**, not as a fact I verified.
- **Whether the upstream sentences the refusals quote still read as quoted.** In particular
  `docs/architecture.md:13`'s "There is no privileged core to patch", which P4 is measured
  against; `dsh-v0.1.1-rc.2` is dated 2026-08-21 and is three releases stale relative to today.
- **The `dsh` runtime, at all.** The document states this itself, three times (§9, §12.9, §13.4):
  no install, no test, no gate, no `dsh` process. Gate *existence* is established throughout;
  gate *outcome* nowhere.
- **Several UNADDRESSED classifications rest on bounded probes that returned nothing.** Named so
  they are not read as absences: an argv-substituting hook decision (probed only
  `.basicly/core/hooks/pre-commit.py` and `check_runner.py` for `updatedInput` /
  `permissionDecision`); a compare-and-set revision fence (probed `owned_store.py`,
  `owned_write.py`, `kit/tracker/events.py`, `gates.py`); a durable child inbox (probed
  `src/basicly/` for `followup|continuable|inbox`). Each returned zero; only the `VerifyCheck`
  zero (#6) carries its own positive control, the printed field list at
  `src/basicly/config.py:1069-1080`.
- **Whether `basicly catalog dump` prints what its help says.** I read the help string and the
  three rendering functions; I did not run the command, per the read-only constraint on a
  repository with a live multi-lane pass.
- **Whether any of the four sibling research documents deleted in `c73dbef7` proposed the same
  concepts.** D-44 (`architecture.md:4884+`) absorbs `2026-07-26-sota-review.md` and its gap
  table overlaps this report at two rows (6.4 stall detection / gate taxonomy / severity, and 6.6
  the trend instrument, `basicly-si89mh`, **open**). I did not recover or read the other four
  files, so a concept I marked UNADDRESSED here may be disposed of in one of them.
- **Whether the always-on size warning was ever a refusal.** §11.3's "branch not taken" describes
  it as a ratchet that "refuses the last straw"; today's targets declare `max_size_warning`. I did
  not check whether a hard cap existed on 2026-08-19 and was later relaxed.

payload.description:
## What this record is

A completed research spike of 2026-09-04, filed as permanent memory rather than as work. Its
findings are actioned by basicly-zq9i2m.2, basicly-zq9i2m.3 and basicly-hnnmk9.2.

The load-bearing result: nine distinct graphs, composing at exactly one point - decompose compiles
file contention into blocks edges once, at plan time. 184 scope-violation events across 160
records, of which 162 recorded the contradiction and landed anyway. Phase is derived and never
stored. No declared gate precedence exists anywhere. Two things it could not establish are named,
including the declared/computed split over the live 418-edge blocks population.

---

# The graphs `basicly` already models — an inventory

Read-only survey of `<repo>`, main. A supervised multi-lane pass was
running throughout: HEAD was `bd5e7900` at the start and `05ffc861` at the end, so the ledger
counts below are a snapshot of a moving log and may be one or two events low.
`git status --short` was empty at the end — nothing here modified the repository.
No file in the repository was created, edited or deleted; no writing git command, no `pytest`,
no `basicly verify/check`, no `pre-commit`, no whole-tree gate was run. Every claim below
carries a `file:line`, a command with its output, or the word **ASSUMPTION**.

---

## Verdict

**basicly maintains nine distinct graph structures, and they compose at exactly one point.**
Seven were named in the brief; two more turned up while establishing them — a
path-glob-to-integrity-level classification graph (`src/basicly/integrity.py:100-155`) and a
declared, gate-enforced module layering DAG (`<repo>/.importlinter:16-45`).
The single composition point is `decompose.decompose`, which **compiles the file contention
graph into `blocks` edges on the record dependency graph** once, at plan time
(`src/basicly/decompose.py:2041-2048`). That one-time compilation is the whole of the
coupling. After it, the two graphs are separate structures a human reconciles by hand: the
contention module is reachable from three CLI sites and nowhere else
(`src/basicly/cli.py:2029`, `:3496`, `:3501`), the supervisor's dispatch path never consults
it, and the ledger's 184 `scope-violation` events on 160 distinct records are the measured
rate at which the plan-time compilation turned out to have been computed from a declared
scope the real diff contradicted. Phase is **derived, never stored** — a six-rung ladder
re-evaluated on every read (`src/basicly/loop_state.py:178-191`) — so the phase graph is a
read-time projection of the gate graph, the ledger and the dependency graph rather than a
structure of its own, and it has no back-edges: rework is a self-loop counted in the ledger,
not a phase transition (`src/basicly/loop.py:472-476`). The owner's framing — *is the result
of one state needed and consumed by the next* — is answerable literally for only three of
eight declared artifact kinds; five carry a schema on disk that nothing produces and nothing
can refuse, and a sixth (`classification`) is produced and consumed **outside** the validated
artifact transport.

---

## Graph 1 — the phase graph

| | |
|---|---|
| **Node** | one tracked record, at one of eight phases. `PHASES = ("intake","classify","decompose","build","verify","validate","ship","done")` — `src/basicly/loop_state.py:31`; the transition-bearing subset `LOOP_PHASES` (no `done`) — `src/basicly/config.py:400` |
| **Edge** | a phase advance, `AdvanceResult` — `src/basicly/loop.py:124`. Handlers keyed by source phase: `_HANDLERS` — `src/basicly/loop.py:2556-2563` (seven entries; `done` has no handler) |
| **Stored or derived** | **DERIVED.** `derive_phase` — `src/basicly/loop_state.py:140-191`. Confirmed independently: zero `field` events named `phase` in the whole log, and the 18 structured `"phase"` hits are `dispatch`-payload supervisor telemetry (`"phase":"lane"`, `"phase":"decide"`), a different vocabulary |
| **Derivation reads** | five inputs, all themselves folds: `status`, approved `checkpoints`, a parsed `external_ref` worktree binding, `policy.GateStatus`, `has_children` — `src/basicly/loop_state.py:140-146`, assembled at `:196-222` |
| **Writes the edges** | nobody. There is no transition table. The ladder is rebuilt inline from booleans each call — `src/basicly/loop_state.py:174-190` |
| **Reads them** | `loop.advance` dispatches on the derived phase — `src/basicly/loop.py:2588,2613`; `supervise._phase_of` — `src/basicly/supervise.py:1710-1712`; `wip.downstream_units` — `src/basicly/wip.py:139-149`; whole-population `phase_map` — `src/basicly/loop_state.py:228-262` |
| **Decision driven** | which handler runs, and therefore whether the next act is a dispatch, a gate, a merge or a close |

**Shape: a linear state machine, evaluated as a priority ladder, with no cycles.** The ladder
is read strongest-rung-first and the first rung whose evidence holds wins —
`src/basicly/loop_state.py:149-150`, rungs at `:181-186`. Rework does **not** create a
back-edge: `_repair_from_validate` states "**The phase does not move**" and re-lands in place
— `src/basicly/loop.py:472-476`. `_rework` records a counter and returns `_blocked`, never a
phase move — `src/basicly/loop.py:2206-2247`. So the cycle a human perceives as "rework" is a
self-loop realised as ledger counters (`[harness-policy] rework`, 119 events measured) plus a
repair brief, not an edge in this graph.

Two rungs are load-bearing and both are documented as bug fixes to the ladder itself:
`landed` requires a **green verify gate**, not merely an approved ship checkpoint, because
`approve_checkpoint` enforces no phase ordering at all — `src/basicly/loop_state.py:167-172`,
and `policy.approve_checkpoint` confirms it validates only the *name* against `CHECKPOINTS`
— `src/basicly/policy.py:1215-1220`, `src/basicly/config.py:391`.

## Graph 3 — the contention graph over FILES

| | |
|---|---|
| **Node** | a **path glob**, not a record. Three populations, each with its own remedy |
| **Edge** | "these two lanes can match a common path", i.e. must serialise. Pure glob intersection, no filesystem lookup, so a file that does not yet exist compares correctly — `src/basicly/decompose.py:19-21`, `globs_overlap` `:293-295`, `scopes_overlap` `:298-300` |
| **Writes** | the **agent**, as a `## Scope` list per child (`src/basicly/decompose.py:130`) and an optional `shared` subset (`:201-240`); a **human**, as `[worktree] append_only_paths` and `[worktree.regenerate_commands]` (`src/basicly/config.py:906,922`); **code**, as the two per-record globs every lane owns by construction (`src/basicly/config.py:959-976`) |
| **Reads** | `decompose.group_children` at plan time — `src/basicly/decompose.py:390-416`; `loop._scope_block` at the landing — `src/basicly/loop.py:1328-1379`; `contention.*` at preflight and in the brief — `src/basicly/contention.py` |
| **Decision driven** | **at plan time, real parallelism** (it becomes the `blocks` chain). **At every other time, advice only.** |

**Three path populations, deliberately separated because the remedies differ:**

| Population | Declared where | Effect on grouping | Live value in this repo |
|---|---|---|---|
| owned globs | agent's `## Scope` | overlap **serialises** — `decompose.py:337-345` | 160 records carry one (see below) |
| `shared` globs | agent's `shared`, must already be in `scope` — `decompose.py:237-240` | overlap through a path **both** declared shared does **not** serialise — `decompose.py:342-344` | not measured |
| contended (append-only) | `[worktree] append_only_paths` | serialises **by default**, escape is a mutual `shared` — `decompose.py:337-339` | **`append_only_paths = []`** — `basicly.toml:102`. **This arm is inert here.** |
| generated | `[worktree.regenerate_commands]` | **no** grouping effect; a landing conflict is rebuilt — `contention.py:79-101` | 2 entries — `basicly.toml:132-142` |
| derived per-lane | `config.lane_scope(record)` | none needed: the record id is in the filename, so two lanes can never write one file — `config.py:959-976` | always active |

**Grouping.** Union-find over pairwise `serializes` — `_group` `src/basicly/decompose.py:350-388`,
public entry `group_children` `:390-416`. Then `chain_predecessors` chains consecutive
same-group members in declared order into one linear `blocks` chain per group, with **no chain
across groups** — `:431-443`. `collapsing_paths` names the one path whose overlaps were
load-bearing, because the collapse is otherwise silent — `:446-530`, rationale `:446-452`.

**The empty-list decision is documented and deliberate**, and it removed the cause rather
than the symptom: `CHANGELOG.md` was the whole list; `basicly-4746` moved to
`changelog.d/<id>.<category>.md` so no two lanes share the file — `basicly.toml:95-101`.

**Where contention is *advisory* rather than admitting.** The module says so:
"the boundary is *advice* against *admission*: nothing here refuses a pass"
— `src/basicly/contention.py:20-23`. Confirmed at the call site: `_print_preflight_contention`
is invoked as a bare statement contributing nothing to `blockers` —
`src/basicly/cli.py:3605`, against `blockers +=` on the two lines above it (`:3602`, `:3604`),
and the `VERDICT` is computed from `blockers` alone — `:3615-3619`. Its own docstring:
"Advisory, never a blocker" — `src/basicly/cli.py:3481-3486`.

**The one place a file collision can refuse.** `loop._scope_block` —
`src/basicly/loop.py:1328-1379`, at the build→verify landing, "the one moment the lane's real
diff exists" (`:1334-1337`). It holds the committed diff against `declared + lane_scope(id)`
(`:1357`), records **every** out-of-scope path as evidence (`:1361`), and refuses **only** when
a path also falls inside another **live** lane's declared scope (`:1360`, `:1362-1363`), under
`[policy] scope_collision`, whose default is `block` — `src/basicly/config.py:425` (not
overridden in `basicly.toml`). "Live" here means a worktree session record on disk, not the
tracker export, because a freshly provisioned lane is not yet flushed —
`src/basicly/loop.py:1305-1326`.

### Does the record dependency graph know anything about the file contention graph?

**Only what was compiled into it at the moment of decomposition, and nothing after.**

`decompose.decompose` unions two sources of `blocks` edges — the agent's declared `depends_on`
and the computed serial chain within a scope-overlap group — and writes them as tracker edges:
`src/basicly/decompose.py:2041-2048`, rationale `:2008-2015`. The design intent is explicit:
"Parallel-safety is encoded in the dependency graph, not a side flag... The absence of a
sibling `blocks` edge *is* the parallel-safe signal" — `src/basicly/decompose.py:10-17`.

**After that write, the answer is no, plainly:**

1. **The edges are never re-derived.** Nothing re-runs `group_children` against an amended
   `## Scope`. `_scope_block` compares the diff to the declaration and **records** —
   `src/basicly/loop.py:1361` — it never adds an edge.
2. **Hand-filed siblings get no edges at all.** `contention.py:14-18` states it: "the lanes that
   collided were hand-filed siblings that no plan ever grouped: nothing in
   `basicly.decompose` runs for them."
3. **The supervisor never asks.** Graph 4, `ready_lanes` — `src/basicly/supervise.py:1683-1704`
   — filters on the blocked set and the rank. Two lanes with disjoint `blocks` edges and
   overlapping real diffs are both admitted and dispatched into
   `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=cap)` — `:2144`.

**The consequence, named and measured.** The system will fund and run two lanes concurrently
whose files collide, and it discovers the collision at the merge queue, after the tokens are
spent. That is not a hypothetical: it is why `contention.py` exists at all — "three lanes,
provably disjoint scopes, `VERDICT: ready`, and the third lane bounced twice on a `CHANGELOG.md`
rebase conflict and spent its whole rework budget getting there"
(`src/basicly/contention.py:5-10`); and again at `:106-112`, observed 2026-08-26, "two of three
siblings edited `board_render.py`, which the third declared; both landings blocked on
`needs input: scope` and a human widened each record by hand". The measured scale of the
reconciliation is 184 `scope-violation` events across 160 records, of which **162 recorded the
contradiction and landed anyway** (Graph 3). The remedy the system currently ships is a warning
a human must choose to read (`basicly loop preflight`) plus a prose fence injected into the
lane's own prompt (`contention.with_scope_fence` — `src/basicly/contention.py:120-129`,
called from `src/basicly/cli.py:2029`) — i.e. advice to an agent, not an edge.

## Answer 2 — where a dependency is IMPLICIT

A real ordering constraint that no declared edge expresses.

1. **Gate-to-gate ordering.** No declaration exists; it is statement order — the probe and its
   positive control are in Graph 5. Concretely, "the merge's internal re-verify precedes the
   recorded verify gate" lives only in the order of statements in `_verify_and_land` —
   `src/basicly/loop.py:1481-1550` — and the two preconditions run in the order of a hard-coded
   tuple, `src/basicly/loop.py:1508`.
2. **The build and ship phases must run from the base checkout.** A genuine ordering/location
   constraint, expressed as a runtime refusal rather than an edge:
   `_BASE_CHECKOUT_PHASES = ("build", "ship")` — `src/basicly/loop.py:105`, enforced at
   `src/basicly/loop.py:2597-2606`.
3. **Generated-artifact contention.** `[worktree.regenerate_commands]` names two paths every
   lane rewrites — `basicly.toml:132-142`, with the measurement in the comment: three lanes
   editing three different skills, two landed, "both of the third's rework attempts" burned
   (`:106-109`); and `87/157/24` vs `86/158/25` against a merged truth of `87/159/25`,
   "a value neither lane could have written" (`:116-120`). This is a real "these lanes contend"
   fact, and it is deliberately kept **out** of the grouping — `contention.generated_report`
   `src/basicly/contention.py:79-101`, `basicly.toml:110-112` — so it induces **no ordering
   edge**. The remedy is a rebuild recipe, which is a defensible choice; the point for this
   inventory is that the contention is real and no edge carries it.
4. **Append-only contention is structurally expressible and currently empty.**
   `append_only_paths = []` — `basicly.toml:102`. The mechanism serialises children when a path
   is listed (`src/basicly/decompose.py:337-339`) but nothing is listed, so every
   append-only-shaped constraint in this repo today is implicit. Two of the three
   `contention.append_only_report` branches return the "nothing declared" line —
   `src/basicly/contention.py:56-59`.
5. **Serial landing.** The constraint "one landing at a time" is a property of one function's
   single-threaded control flow — `src/basicly/supervise.py:3261-3277` — and the lock that
   might have declared it covers only the tracker-state commit
   (`src/basicly/merge.py:626-656`), not the rebase or the merge (`:829`, `:783-786`).
6. **Actual diff → integrity level.** The real dependency is "the files this change touches
   decide which gates it owes". The system reads the *declared* scope at CLASSIFY
   (`src/basicly/loop.py:259-269` → `src/basicly/classify.py:73`) and then explicitly refuses to
   re-derive: "Read back from the marker, never re-derived from scope" —
   `src/basicly/validate_gate.py:60-62`. No edge connects the landed diff to the level.
7. **Checkpoint order.** Nothing orders `classify`, `decompose`, `ship`.
   `src/basicly/policy.py:1215-1220` validates the name against `CHECKPOINTS`
   (`src/basicly/config.py:391`) and nothing else. The hole was closed by adding a *gate*
   requirement to the phase ladder instead — `src/basicly/loop_state.py:167-172`: "a ship
   approval recorded out of order on an unstarted leaf derived `ship` and closed the bead with
   zero work done."
8. **The one implicit dependency proved absent rather than unexpressed** — worth naming because
   it is the model the others lack: `config.lane_scope(record)` derives
   `basicly.d/<id>.toml` and `changelog.d/<id>.*.md` from the record id, and argues that no
   ordering is needed because "the id in the filename is unique to the lane and two lanes can
   never write one file" — `src/basicly/config.py:959-976`.

No filesystem lookup — `src/basicly/decompose.py:19-21` |

sits between those two moments and is, by its own docstring, advice: "nothing here refuses a

### Where a declared edge lying has consequences

1. **A wrong `## Scope` buys parallelism the files do not support** — and this is the measured
   one. The globs are the sole input to the plan-time grouping
   (`src/basicly/decompose.py:390-416`), and the grouping is the sole source of the computed
   `blocks` edges (`:2048`). The declaration is checked against reality only at the landing
   (`src/basicly/loop.py:1328-1379`), which **records** every contradiction and **refuses** only
   a sibling collision. Measured: **184** `scope-violation` events over **160** records; **22**
   named a colliding lane, **162** did not (commands and output in Graph 3).
2. **The same wrong `## Scope` picks the gate set, and the choice is then frozen.**
   `integrity.assign` takes the max level over the *declared* paths
   (`src/basicly/integrity.py:299-302`); an empty declaration takes `_FALLBACK` = L2
   (`:291-297`, `:153`); the level is written to a marker (`src/basicly/classify.py:84-99`) and
   read back "never re-derived from scope" (`src/basicly/validate_gate.py:60-62`). An
   under-declared L3 change is therefore permanently an L2 change, and never owes
   `validate-as-consumer` or a human ship. That this rule bites hard is already recorded in the
   repo: passing no scope at intake made "**every** unit the loop classified record L2 —
   measured on basicly-u2hl.54.1, whose twelve globs classify L3. That made L3, and every
   behaviour gated on it, unreachable" — `src/basicly/loop.py:259-269`.
3. **A false `shared` declaration un-serialises a real collision.** Overlap through a path both
   sides declared `shared` does not serialise — `src/basicly/decompose.py:342-344`. The rule is
   sound for a manifest each lane appends its own entry to; nothing verifies the claim.
4. **A mislabelled record joins a pass with no edge review whatsoever.** In label mode
   `derive_session` builds the lane set from `label_source.labelled` and consults **no** edge —
   `src/basicly/supervise.py:596-607`, `:539-575`.
5. **An unreadable classification marker silently drops the validate requirement.**
   `src/basicly/validate_gate.py:57-80`; the trade is stated at `:72-73`. Combined with (2): the
   input that decides whether validation is owed is agent-declared free text travelling outside
   the validated artifact transport (Graph 7).
6. **The declaration that is safe by construction, for contrast.** `config.lane_scope` derives
   its two globs from the record id, so no lane can claim another's — `src/basicly/config.py:959-976`
   — and `contention._admits` explains to the lane that these "outrank any sibling glob" and are
   not a licence for anything else — `src/basicly/contention.py:203-231`.

---

## What could not be established

- **The disposition of the five L3 records with no validate gate.** Seven records recorded
  `level=L3` and the log holds two `validate-as-consumer` gate events. I did not join the seven
  marker records to their gate rows or to their statuses, so whether the other five are open,
  closed under the fail-open path (`src/basicly/validate_gate.py:57-80`), or predate the gate is
  **not established**.
- **Whether any of the 162 non-blocking `scope-violation` records caused a downstream conflict.**
  The marker records the paths; correlating them to merge bounces would need the
  `[harness-policy] rework`/coupling events joined per record. Not done.
- **Which single commit compiled each of the 418 `blocks` edges.** I did not separate
  agent-declared `depends_on` edges from `group_children`-computed chain edges in the live
  ledger; both are written by the same `dep add ... -t blocks` call
  (`src/basicly/decompose.py:2048`) with no marker distinguishing them. So the declared/derived
  split for the *live* `blocks` population is **not measured** — only the code paths are
  established.
- **Whether the implicit gate ordering has ever produced a wrong verdict.** Not derivable from
  the ledger; would need a counterexample run, which the read-only constraint forbids.
- **Runtime behaviour of any of this.** Per the task constraints I ran no `pytest`, no
  `basicly verify/check`, no `pre-commit` and no whole-tree gate. **No claim in this document
  rests on a green suite.** Every claim rests on a file read, a `jq`/`grep` over the committed
  ledger, or `uv run basicly tracker stats`.
- **The board subsystem.** `src/basicly/board_*.py` (13 modules, ~3300 lines) was not
  inventoried; whether it renders any of these graphs as a view, or maintains a tenth, is
  **not established**.
- **The `related` (59) and `discovered-from` (5) edge types.** Measured in the population but I
  did not trace a reader for either. **ASSUMPTION**, unverified: they are informational and
  outside `DEFAULT_VOCABULARY.blocking_types`, since `dependency_graph` filters on that set
  (`src/basicly/dependency_graph.py:50-51`, `:76-79`) and only `blocks`/`parent-child` appear in
  the paths I read.
