payload.description:
## Context

Parent: basicly-lc2bd3v. The owner: *"be able to easily start, stop work"*.

Nothing on the board starts work. `board_asks.pending` builds one action row per implementable *offer*, and a ready record has no ask - so the 234 records the board says are ready carry no way to begin any of them.

## The verb

`basicly loop supervise <id> --max-passes 1 --detach`, not `loop run`: a killed first run cannot be re-dispatched by `loop run`, because `loop run` dispatches once at provisioning. The board must not offer a verb whose second press does nothing.

## No confirm code, and the reason

`checkpoint-approve` carries one because a checkpoint is the human gate the anti-autopilot rule protects; a board that read the minted code and offered a one-click approve would be relaying the code to itself. Starting a lane is not a gate. It is spend, and spend is bounded by the grant the engine already enforces.

So the guard here is a different one: the action is offered only for a record that is **ready and unclaimed**, so a press cannot start a second lane on work already in flight.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a record is ready and no lane holds it, THE BOARD SHALL offer to start it, on that record`s own row.
- WHERE a record is already claimed or already has a lane, THE BOARD SHALL NOT offer to start it.
- THE PRINTED COMMAND SHALL be built through the action`s own `build`, so the line a reader copies cannot diverge from the argv the button runs.
- WHEN the action returns, THE BOARD SHALL show the CLI`s own exit status and output rather than a generic success.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_asks.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_asks.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: press start on a ready record and watch a worktree appear

## Context

Parent: basicly-lc2bd3v. The owner: *"start, stop work"*.

`lane-kill` is already in `board_actions.ACTIONS` and already works. It has no surface: `board_asks.pending` draws a row per *ask*, and a running lane is not an ask, so the verb is unreachable unless something else happens to be waiting.

That is the whole defect. A verb that exists and cannot be pressed is worse than one that does not exist, because a reader of the code believes it is available.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane is running, THE BOARD SHALL offer to kill it, on that lane`s own card.
- THE REASON SHALL be a required free-text field, so the ledger records why a lane was stopped rather than that it was.
- WHERE `lanes[]` is absent from the snapshot, THE BOARD SHALL offer nothing rather than an action naming an empty id.

payload.description:
## Context

Parent: basicly-lc2bd3v. The owner: *"descope work, scope work"*.

In this harness, descoping a record is deferring it and scoping it back is reactivating it. Both are `tracker write -- update`, and neither is on the board.

## The replay trap this must not walk into

A status the record once held is dropped as a replay: event ids are content digests, so `update <id> --status open` on a deferred record matches the `open` it was created with, appends nothing, exits 0 and prints *already recorded* (basicly-bj8kks). A board that read the exit code would draw a reactivation that never happened.

So reactivate with `--status in_progress`, and read the status back with `show` rather than from the exit code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a record is open or in progress, THE BOARD SHALL offer to defer it, with a required reason.
- WHEN a record is deferred, THE BOARD SHALL offer to reactivate it.
- THE BOARD SHALL confirm the outcome by reading the status back, never from the exit code alone.
- THE BOARD SHALL NOT offer to create a record: the owner keeps that in the terminal.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_asks.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_actions.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: defer a record from the board and read it leave the ready set

The owner has restated the cockpit requirement more than once, and each restatement is evidence the previous one did not hold. A requirement a person has to repeat is a requirement with no gate behind it.

The owner`s own test: *"if you as an agent look at the board, and only have access to the board, would you be able to see what is going on?"*

One test that enumerates the nine questions and asserts each is answerable from the rendered page - not from the snapshot, and not from the model, because both have passed while the page drew nothing (basicly-3qstvw, basicly-yj8hpjr).

1. what work is available
2. what can start now
3. what is in progress, and who holds it
4. what is blocked, and by what
5. what one record actually says
6. how to start a record
7. how to stop a lane
8. how to descope a record
9. when the work will be done

## Acceptance Criteria

- THE TEST SHALL assert against the rendered page, using a fixture whose sections are all present.
- EACH question SHALL be one named assertion, so a failure names the question that stopped being answerable.
- WHERE a question is not yet answerable, THE TEST SHALL name the open record that will answer it and skip on that record alone, so the count of unanswered questions is visible and shrinks.

| 17:03:23Z | the served board: `RUNNING NOW no pass is running - 238 record(s) are ready to start` |

A worktree was on disk, its `worktree:` binding was in the ledger, and the board said nothing was running.

## Cause

`board_facts.py:610-622`:

```python
lanes=(
    lane_facts(repo_root, session.root_issue, phase_map, lane_label=lane_label)
    if in_flight and session is not None
    else ()
    if board_serve.live_holder(repo_root) is None
    else None
)
```

`()` means *"no pass is running"*, and it is chosen whenever no process holds the lock. So visibility is keyed to a **live supervisor process**, not to work in flight. The moment the supervisor exits - because it finished its rounds, because a terminal closed, or because it crashed - every lane it provisioned disappears from the board while its worktree stays on disk.

The second channel does not catch it either. `board_regions.claimed` filters `status == "in_progress"`, and a provisioned child is still `open`, so it is in neither population.

## Not basicly-9guj21

That record is about work with **no** `worktree:` binding at all - a host subagent or a background shell job. This record is the opposite case: the binding exists, the lane was adopted by name, and it is still invisible.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a record carries a live `worktree:` binding and no supervisor holds the lock, THE BOARD SHALL still name it, its branch and its phase.
- THE BOARD SHALL distinguish a lane an agent is inside from a worktree standing open with nobody in it: the second is not a running pass and must not be drawn as one.
- WHERE the lock is held, THE PRESENT behaviour SHALL be unchanged, so a supervised pass still reports its own selector.
- A REGRESSION TEST SHALL provision a binding with no lock and assert the board names it.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`

DECISION, owner, 2026-09-05: the grant system stays as a measurement and stops being a gate. Their words: 'the grant system brings more harm then good... it is great for measuring costs, but it should not be used for blocking work.' Asked about the one sub-question this left open - whether check_pass_spend's pre-dispatch refusal survives - they chose to cut it too and warn loudly instead.

THE LINE. The token budget never blocks anything. The autonomy level still governs checkpoints: L0 meaning every checkpoint is human is the checkpoint design and is not in question. What goes is spend as a term in any permission.

WHAT IT RESTS ON, four measurements:
1. basicly-ncday7 stopped at 36,636,442 tokens against a 17.7M forecast and its uncommitted work landed unreviewed; a later review found four defects, three major, all past a green 5152-test suite. The bound removed the author who would have reviewed the work.
2. The k6tpep grant read 104485469/100000000, so every checkpoint returned to a human and two ships jammed on code already merged.
3. basicly-u6jq.1: a 5,000,000-token ceiling admitted a pass that spent 46,026,602. Nine times over.
4. 2026-09-05: basicly-fiow1sr ran to 17,838,762 tokens while loop session reported 0/10000000. supervise.py:1401 and :1971 test only whether a budget EXISTS, never whether spend is under it, so the ceiling is sampled at lane boundaries and a lane is where the spend happens.

The code already argued the owner's side. check_pass_spend's own docstring: 'the remedy for an over-budget pass is to start nothing, never to interrupt a lane that is already running. Cost is bounded by sizing the work, never by killing a working agent.' policy.py:1345 contradicts it by making a checkpoint approve only 'with... spend under the grant's token budget'.

THE SURFACE IS ONE FLAG. Seven consumers read spend.halted and each refuses something: policy.py:1769 (checkpoint approval), policy.py:1880 (proposal grant), loop.py:805 (dispatch refused before it started, needs_input=grant), decisions.py:384 (the decider abstains), release.py:676 (release refused), supervise.py:1401 and :1971 (a metered pass with no budget), and check_pass_spend (a pass over its forecast). All seven become reports.

WHAT STAYS: the forecast, spend_status as a reading, tokens_under_grant, preflight's figures, the spend-accuracy gate and the board's spend region.

RESIDUAL RISK, stated rather than argued away: with no ceiling an unattended pass is bounded only by --max-passes and the 7200s runner timeout, which is what basicly-vz78 was filed for. The honest replacement is a hard per-lane token kill enforced by the runner, at the place spend happens - the bound the grant never provided. Filed separately rather than assumed.

With `spend.halted` no longer gating anything (basicly-vrgi1jk), an unattended pass is bounded only by `--max-passes` and the 7200s runner timeout. `--max-passes 50` with nobody watching is unbounded in practice. That is the state `basicly-vz78` was filed for: *"an unbounded pass looked exactly like a checked one."*

## Why the grant was never that bound

Measured 2026-09-05. `basicly-fiow1sr` ran to **17,838,762** run-record tokens against a 7,934,065 forecast while `basicly loop session` reported `grant: L1, 0/10000000 tokens under this grant`. if admission.grant is not None and admission.grant.token_budget is not None:
    return None
```

So the ceiling is sampled at lane **boundaries**, and a lane is where the spend happens. That is why it appeared to do nothing until it killed something.

I stopped that lane by hand at 17.8M because the owner had authorised about 8M. The engine would not have.

## What this record is

The bound at the place spend happens: the runner watches its own lane and stops it at a stated ceiling, reporting the figure. Not a permission and not a gate on anyone else - one process, its own spend, its own limit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane passes its token ceiling, THE RUNNER SHALL stop that lane and record why, and SHALL refuse nothing else.
- THE CEILING SHALL be a runner setting, not a grant field, so exhausting it cannot revoke an autonomy level - the coupling basicly-hnnmk9.1 was filed against.
- WHERE no ceiling is set, THE RUNNER SHALL behave exactly as it does today.
- THE STOPPED LANE SHALL leave its worktree and its uncommitted work intact, because basicly-ncday7 showed that landing an unreviewed diff is worse than stopping.
- A TEST SHALL drive a lane past a small ceiling and assert it stopped, the figure was recorded and the worktree survived.

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `tests/test_runner*.py`

1. loop preflight reports 'contend: no append-only path declared ([worktree] append_only_paths) - a path every lane writes is invisible to the grouping until it is listed'. The ledger is exactly such a path: every lane appends to .basicly/ledger/events-*.jsonl, and it is not declared, so it does not group. Two lanes writing the ledger are not seen as contending at all.

2. The memory this repository keeps of its own traps says 'editing base during a pass - a lane records your dirt as its own verify failure, and no push survives the beat'. That is the same defect read from the operator's side: a human working in parallel with a pass is invisible to the grouping for the same reason a lane amending its scope is.

So the owner's question - whether classify and decompose really prepare work so there is no merge conflict afterwards - has a split answer. The partition is real and is computed. It is computed once, and nothing enforces it after that.

## Context

Owner directive 2026-08-28: the board must become a cockpit for developers as well as an observability surface for operations. basicly-k6tpep answers the operator question "what is happening right now, and does it need me?". A developer asks a different question: "where is my record, what is being done to it, and what stands between it and main?" Today that answer needs `basicly loop status`, `basicly tracker show` and the worktree list, read separately.

This record is the inspect half of basicly-lc2bd3v, the cockpit epic, and it answers operator question 5 of nine, "what one record actually says". `tests/test_board_operator_questions.py` xfails that question against this id, so closing this record without moving the question is itself a failure.

## The data path, decided 2026-09-06

The detail renders **from the snapshot**, not from a per-request subprocess. basicly-lc2bd3v argued for the `board_actions.ACTIONS` seam on the ground that "294 bodies would be a snapshot nobody can serve" - that argument is about record **bodies**, and the fields below are metadata. Measured 2026-09-06: `units[]` carries 7 fields for 295 records and the whole snapshot is 172 KB.

The snapshot path is what the demonstration requires: `basicly board --out` writes a self-contained file with no server behind it, so a page that shells out cannot be demonstrated that way.

The `consumer-reads-only-the-snapshot` contract is unaffected either way: it binds `board_actions`, `board_asks`, `board_diagram`, `board_footer`, `board_graph`, `board_loop`, `board_regions`, `board_render` and `board_wall`. `board_serve`, `board_facts` and `board_snapshot` are producers and are not in its source list.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a developer opens `/record/<id>` on the board, IT SHALL show the record's title, status, priority, derived phase, worktree and branch, the checkpoints held and missing, the rework count per gate, the open blockers and the open dependents, from one snapshot read.
- WHEN a lane is running for that record, the same page SHALL show the agent, the model, the start time, the last progress line and the spend so far, and SHALL say when the snapshot was taken.
- WHEN the record has no lane, the page SHALL say so and SHALL name the next command that moves it, copied from the engine's own remedy text and never composed by the board.
- WHEN the snapshot lacks a field the page needs, the field SHALL render as absent, never as a default value, and the `harness-board/v1` contract SHALL name the added sections.
- WHERE the board prints a record id - next up, running now, parked, claimed, events, asks - THAT ID SHALL be the link to that record's page, so the page has a way in from the wall.
- WHERE a row clips a record title to fit its column, THE ROW SHALL carry the untruncated title as a `title` attribute, so a reader recovers it without leaving the board.

## Scope

The previous scope named `.basicly/core/kit/board/**`, which matched no file on disk (measured 2026-09-06); the template lives under `.basicly/core/templates/board/`. The page itself goes in a new module rather than into `board_regions.py` (754 lines) or `board_facts.py` (660), both of which carry frozen `module-size` entries and have open split records against them (`basicly-k6tpep.1`, `basicly-k6tpep.2`).

payload.description:
## Context

`basicly-fiow1sr` (start a ready record from the board) is blocked on a capability the CLI does not have: **no verb starts one ready leaf record detached.**

Measured 2026-09-06:

- `basicly loop run --help` lists `--work-type --children --mode --confirm --root --runner --autonomy --tier`. There is no `--detach`, and the command is synchronous. `board_actions.TIMEOUT_S` is 300s against a lane that runs twenty minutes.
- `basicly loop supervise` is detachable but fans out over parent-child children. A ready leaf has none, so `loop preflight` on a task reports `lanes: 0 dispatchable now, 0 open child(ren)`.

The previous lane on `basicly-fiow1sr` built a board button whose argv was `('loop','supervise',issue,'--max-passes','1','--detach')`. It does nothing, for both reasons above, and its tests passed because they asserted the argv's shape rather than that the argv starts anything.

## The mechanism already exists

`src/basicly/cli.py:3853-3968` holds the whole detached-launch machinery: `_detach_isolation`, `_detach_argv`, `_detach_log`, `_spawn_detached`, `_detach_supervisor`. It is generic apart from one line - `_detach_argv` hardcodes `["loop", "supervise", args.issue]` - and one hand-written forwarding table, `SUPERVISE_FORWARDED_FLAGS`, pinned to the parser by `test_every_supervise_flag_reaches_the_detached_process`.

So this is a verb-aware `_detach_argv`, a second forwarded-flag table for `loop run`, and a second pinning test. The comment above `SUPERVISE_FORWARDED_FLAGS` already names the failure mode a missing table entry produces: the launching process accepts the flag and the process that does the work silently never applies it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an operator runs `basicly loop run <id> --detach`, THE COMMAND SHALL spawn the same invocation without `--detach` in its own session, print the child pid and the log path, and return at once.
- WHERE a flag the `loop run` parser accepts is not forwarded to the detached child, A TEST SHALL fail, in the way `test_every_supervise_flag_reaches_the_detached_process` already does for supervise.
- WHEN the detached child writes output, IT SHALL append to a per-launch file under the detached-log directory, so a second launch inside the same second appends its refusal rather than truncating the first launch's log.
- WHEN `--detach` is combined with `--confirm`, THE COMMAND SHALL refuse, because a one-time confirm code relayed into a process the operator cannot watch defeats the challenge it answers.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_cli_loop.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3` - `loop run` is a consumer surface.
- demonstration: `basicly loop run <a ready leaf> --detach` prints a pid and a log path and returns in under a second, then `basicly worktree list` shows the worktree the detached child provisioned.

## The data path, decided 2026-09-06

The detail renders **from the snapshot**, not from a per-request subprocess. basicly-lc2bd3v argued for the `board_actions.ACTIONS` seam on the ground that "294 bodies would be a snapshot nobody can serve" - that argument is about record **bodies**, and the fields below are metadata. Measured 2026-09-06: `units[]` carries 7 fields for 295 records and the whole snapshot is 172 KB.

The snapshot path is what the demonstration requires: `basicly board --out` writes a self-contained file with no server behind it, so a page that shells out cannot be demonstrated that way.

The `consumer-reads-only-the-snapshot` contract is unaffected either way: it binds `board_actions`, `board_asks`, `board_diagram`, `board_footer`, `board_graph`, `board_loop`, `board_regions`, `board_render` and `board_wall`. `board_serve`, `board_facts` and `board_snapshot` are producers and are not in its source list.

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-05: *"One of the biggest issues with agentic development in the terminal alone is that human has no idea what is going on and when multiple parallel sessions and work is being done, it gets buried under."*

Reproduced in 27 seconds on 2026-09-05 while dispatching a real lane.

## Measured

| time | fact |
| --- | --- |
| 17:02:56Z | `loop supervise basicly-lc2bd3v --label cockpit-first --max-passes 1 --detach` |
| 17:02:5xZ | log: `adopted: basicly-vowpbar (open) -> basicly-vowpbar on harness/basicly-vowpbar [live]` |
| 17:02:5xZ | log: `stopped: --max-passes 1 reached after 1 pass(es), 1 child(ren) still open` |
| 17:03:0xZ | `basicly worktree list`: `basicly-vowpbar: harness/basicly-vowpbar (base main)` |
| 17:03:23Z | the served board: `RUNNING NOW no pass is running - 238 record(s) are ready to start` |

A worktree was on disk, its `worktree:` binding was in the ledger, and the board said nothing was running.

## Cause

`board_facts.py:610-622`:

```python
lanes=(
    lane_facts(repo_root, session.root_issue, phase_map, lane_label=lane_label)
    if in_flight and session is not None
    else ()
    if board_serve.live_holder(repo_root) is None
    else None
)
```

`()` means *"no pass is running"*, and it is chosen whenever no process holds the lock. So visibility is keyed to a **live supervisor process**, not to work in flight. The moment the supervisor exits - because it finished its rounds, because a terminal closed, or because it crashed - every lane it provisioned disappears from the board while its worktree stays on disk.

The second channel does not catch it either. `board_regions.claimed` filters `status == "in_progress"`, and a provisioned child is still `open`, so it is in neither population.

## Not basicly-9guj21

That record is about work with **no** `worktree:` binding at all - a host subagent or a background shell job. This record is the opposite case: the binding exists, the lane was adopted by name, and it is still invisible.

## Widened 2026-09-06, after a second reproduction

Reproduced again while an operator watched, this time with **two** unsupervised processes: a
`loop run` lane building in its worktree, and later a `loop advance` landing running verify for
minutes. The board said `no pass is running` and `NOTHING IS WAITING` through both, with four
worktrees on disk.

The second case matters because `basicly-ncday7` already shipped the state that names it. Every
lane state exists - `board_sections.LANE_STATES` is `queued running waits-to-land landing
refused parked`, the schema carries the enum, and `board_regions.py:92` maps `landing` to a
colour. It is unreachable, because `board_facts.py:621` sets `lanes` to `()` before any state
can be assigned. So this record is not only about naming a worktree: it is the one gate that
makes an entire shipped vocabulary dead code outside a supervised pass.

`ncday7` is not reopened. Its criteria each read `WHEN the supervisor runs a landing`, so it was
closed correctly against what it asked for. The premise was the defect, not the delivery.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a record carries a live `worktree:` binding and no supervisor holds the lock, THE BOARD SHALL still name it, its branch and its phase.
- WHEN a landing runs with no supervisor - `basicly loop advance` driven by a person or another session - THE BOARD SHALL draw that record in the `landing` state, using the vocabulary `basicly-ncday7` already shipped rather than a second spelling of it.
- WHERE a lane state in `board_sections.LANE_STATES` cannot be reached by any unsupervised path, A TEST SHALL fail naming that state, so a shipped vocabulary cannot become dead code again.
- THE BOARD SHALL distinguish a lane an agent is inside from a worktree standing open with nobody in it: the second is not a running pass and must not be drawn as one.
- WHERE the lock is held, THE PRESENT behaviour SHALL be unchanged, so a supervised pass still reports its own selector.
- A REGRESSION TEST SHALL provision a binding with no lock and assert the board names it.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_facts.py`
- `tests/test_board_claimed.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: dispatch with `--max-passes 1`, let the supervisor exit, and read the worktree on the board

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-06, listing the cockpit actions an enterprise board must carry: *"parking, prioritizing, changing scope"*.

Measured 2026-09-06 against `board_actions.ACTIONS`, which is the closed table of everything the board can run: it holds `loop-answer`, `checkpoint-approve`, `record-park`, `record-resume` and `lane-kill`. Parking and resuming already answer *descope* and *scope*. **Nothing changes a priority.**

That leaves the ranked lists the board draws - `NEXT UP`, `THE QUEUE`, the ready set - read-only. An operator who can see that the wrong thing is ranked first must leave the board to move it, which is the exact loss the cockpit exists to stop.

## The verb already exists

`basicly tracker write -- update <id> -p <n>` is the priority write, and it is the same shape the existing park and resume actions use - an argv handed to the installed CLI, never a tracker read. So `consumer-reads-only-the-snapshot` is unaffected.

## No confirm code, and the reason

The rule `record-park` states: a checkpoint carries a code because it is the human gate the anti-autopilot rule protects. A priority spends nothing, starts nothing, and is undone by setting it back. It is the same class as park, so it takes no code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an operator submits a priority for a record, THE BOARD SHALL run `basicly tracker write -- update <id> -p <n>` through the installed CLI and show that command's own exit status and output.
- WHERE the board draws a record in a ranked list, IT SHALL offer the priority change on that record's own row, not only where an ask prefills it.
- THE ACTION SHALL refuse a value the tracker will refuse, before the subprocess runs, and say which values are allowed.
- THE PRINTED COMMAND SHALL be built through the action's own `build`, so the line a reader copies cannot diverge from the argv the button runs.
- A TEST SHALL assert the argv reaches the CLI and changes the record, not that the argv has the right shape - the shape-only test is why `basicly-fiow1sr` shipped an argv that started nothing.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_record.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_record.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_actions.py`
- `tests/test_board_action_wire.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: open a record page on a served board, submit a new priority, and read the record's rank move in the next fold.

## Context

Found by looking at the rendered page of `basicly-62h3x9` on 2026-09-06, minutes after it merged, against the owner's own method: screenshot it and say what a human sees without reading the code.

Two defects, both in what the page omits rather than in what it draws.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `uv run basicly board --out /tmp/board.html`
2. Open `/tmp/board.html`'s record page for an epic, for example `record/basicly-k6tpep.html`.

Observed: `THE TREE` lists fourteen children as bare ids - `basicly-2n5dfe`, `basicly-9guj21`, `basicly-a8jy77` and eleven more - with no titles. And no section anywhere carries the record's description.

Expected: a reader can tell what each child is, and can read what the record says.

## Why each one matters

**Bare ids.** The owner has stated this as a standing requirement: a person cannot read an id, and a record must be named with its title. The board's own ready list already prints `id + title` on every row, so the record page is the one surface that regressed against a rule the rest of the page keeps. `BLOCKED BY` and `BLOCKING` have it too.

**No description.** The owner's words when this surface was asked for: *"inspect work (the info written in the record in a structured way)"*. The page today shows metadata *about* a record and never what the record says, so the question that opened the page is the one thing it cannot answer.

The description was deliberately left out of `basicly-62h3x9` when its data path was decided on 2026-09-06, on the argument that `basicly-lc2bd3v` makes about bodies: 297 of them would be a snapshot nobody can serve. That argument is still true for *every* body at once, and it does not apply to *one*. A record page is one record.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHERE the record page prints another record's id - in the tree, in blocked by, or in blocking - IT SHALL print that record's title beside the id, and the id SHALL remain the link.
- WHEN a record page is opened, IT SHALL render that record's description as markdown, so the headings the Definition of Ready requires read as headings.
- WHERE the description would take the page past what one snapshot can carry for every record at once, THE PRODUCER SHALL carry each body on that record's own page rather than in the shared document, so the wall's snapshot does not grow by 297 bodies.
- WHEN a record has no description, THE PAGE SHALL say so as an absence, never as an empty section.
- A TEST SHALL assert a title appears beside an id in each of the three link sections, and SHALL fail if any of them prints a bare id.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_record.py`
- `src/basicly/board_cli.py`
- `src/basicly/board_serve.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_record.html.j2`
- `.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json`
- `tests/test_board_record_page.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_record.py`
- `src/basicly/board_cli.py`

- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_record.html.j2`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: `uv run basicly board --out /tmp/b.html`, open `record/basicly-k6tpep.html`, and read every child's title beside its id and the epic's own description on the page.

minutes. The board said `no pass is running` and `NOTHING IS WAITING` through both, with four
worktrees on disk.

lane state exists - `board_sections.LANE_STATES` is `queued running waits-to-land landing

colour. It is unreachable, because `board_facts.py:621` sets `lanes` to `()` before any state

makes an entire shipped vocabulary dead code outside a supervised pass.

`ncday7` is not reopened. Its criteria each read `WHEN the supervisor runs a landing`, so it was
closed correctly against what it asked for. The premise was the defect, not the delivery.

- WHEN a record carries a live `worktree:` binding and no supervisor holds the lock, THE BOARD SHALL still name it, its branch and its phase.

- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_facts.py`
- `tests/test_board_claimed.py`

## Plan
- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `80000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: dispatch with `--max-passes 1`, let the supervisor exit, and read the worktree on the board

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-06, listing the cockpit actions an enterprise board must carry: *"parking, prioritizing, changing scope"*.

Measured 2026-09-06 against `board_actions.ACTIONS`, which is the closed table of everything the board can run: it holds `loop-answer`, `checkpoint-approve`, `record-park`, `record-resume` and `lane-kill`. Parking and resuming already answer *descope* and *scope*. **Nothing changes a priority.**

That leaves the ranked lists the board draws - `NEXT UP`, `THE QUEUE`, the ready set - read-only. An operator who can see that the wrong thing is ranked first must leave the board to move it, which is the exact loss the cockpit exists to stop.

## The verb already exists

`basicly tracker write -- update <id> -p <n>` is the priority write, and it is the same shape the existing park and resume actions use - an argv handed to the installed CLI, never a tracker read. So `consumer-reads-only-the-snapshot` is unaffected.

## No confirm code, and the reason

The rule `record-park` states: a checkpoint carries a code because it is the human gate the anti-autopilot rule protects. A priority spends nothing, starts nothing, and is undone by setting it back. It is the same class as park, so it takes no code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an operator submits a priority for a record, THE BOARD SHALL run `basicly tracker write -- update <id> -p <n>` through the installed CLI and show that command's own exit status and output.

## Context

Found by the security reviewer the engine dispatched at VALIDATE on `basicly-62h3x9`, 2026-09-06, with a probe it ran rather than an argument it made. The code is on main.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Pick an output directory a second party can write to, which `basicly board --out` creates itself.
2. Plant a symlink at `record/<any-id-in-units>.html` pointing at a file the board's user can write.
3. Run `basicly board --out <that directory>/board.html`.

Observed, from the reviewer's probe:

```
written,refused: (1, 0)
target head: <!doctype html>|<html lang="en">|  <head
```

The target file lost its content. Expected: the write refuses a path that is a symlink and reports it as refused.

## What is and is not being claimed

**Not path traversal.** `board_record.SAFE_ID` is anchored at both ends and holds; the path stays inside `record/`. `board_serve`'s `/record/<id>` route reaches no filesystem at all - it is a dict lookup - and `board.record("../../etc/passwd", ...)` returns `None`.

**What changed with `basicly-62h3x9`.** The class is pre-existing for the two files `board --out` already wrote. That record made the names **predictable and numerous** - one per record in `units`, 297 today - and made the tool create the directory itself. An attacker plants rather than guesses.

**Exposure is low and stated as low.** The reviewer's own words: *"high that the write follows the link, low that anybody runs the board with a shared output directory outside the demonstration line."* This is filed because the fix is small and the finding is demonstrated, not because the risk is pressing.

## Also unverified, deliberately left as a note

A Windows device name - `CON`, `NUL`, `COM1` - passes `SAFE_ID` and would become `record/CON.html`. The reviewer was on Linux and could not run it, so it is stated as unverified rather than filed as a finding. Settle it on Windows before treating it as either.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a page's destination path exists and is a symbolic link, THE WRITER SHALL refuse that page and count it among the refused, rather than following the link.
- THE COMMAND SHALL report the refusal count it already prints, so a refused page is visible to the operator rather than silent.
- WHERE a destination is refused, THE OTHER PAGES SHALL still be written: one hostile entry must not cost the whole render.
- A TEST SHALL plant a symlink at a destination, run the writer, and assert the link target is unchanged - the shape the reviewer's own probe took.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_cli.py`
- `tests/test_board_cli.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.security.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_cli.py`
- `src/basicly/board_record.py`
- `tests/test_board_cli.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `60000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: plant a symlink at one record's destination, run `basicly board --out`, and read the unchanged target beside a refusal count of one.

## Context

Found in the blind read of the board minutes after `basicly-kqh9dj8` merged, which is the change that introduced it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Land a lane so its branch merges into main, leaving the worktree standing until ship tears it down.
2. `uv run basicly board --out /tmp/board.html` and read its card.

Observed, 2026-09-06, on two cards at once:

```
a developer opens one record on the board ...   QUEUED - VERIFY
  id basicly-62h3x9      a worktree with no commits and no changes
work in a live worktree is invisible ...        QUEUED - VERIFY
  id basicly-kqh9dj8     a worktree with no commits and no changes
```

Both had merged. Their code was on main as the card was drawn.

Expected: a card that says the work landed and the worktree is waiting to be torn down.

## Cause

`board_unsupervised.state_for` reads `ahead` - commits the branch holds that base does not - and treats `0` as "nothing here". `0` is the answer for **two** different lanes: one that merged, whose commits are now in base, and one that has not started. The producer's own docstring says so and calls them the same thing: *"A merged branch answers 0, as does one that did nothing; neither is work in flight."*

That reasoning is right about *work in flight* and wrong about what to draw. Neither is in flight, but only one of them is finished, and `queued` is the wrong word for finished.

## The vocabulary question this raises

`board_sections.LANE_STATES` is `queued running waits-to-land landing refused parked`. None of the six means "merged, waiting for teardown". So this is either a seventh state, or a `state_detail` that carries the distinction under `queued`.

Prefer the detail unless a reader needs to filter on it: the closed set is a schema enum that `basicly-ncday7` established, and widening it is a contract change every consumer must follow. The phase already carries the truth beside the state - both cards read `VERIFY`, which is past build - so the pair is not ambiguous to a reader who knows the loop. It is ambiguous to everyone else, which is who the board is for.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane's branch holds no commits base lacks AND its phase is past build, THE CARD SHALL say the work merged and the worktree awaits teardown, not that the worktree has no commits.
- WHERE a lane's branch holds no commits and its phase is at or before build, THE PRESENT wording SHALL be unchanged: that worktree really has done nothing yet.
- A TEST SHALL drive both cases through one function and assert the two produce different text, because one integer answers for both and only the phase separates them.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_unsupervised.py`
- `tests/test_board_unsupervised.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_unsupervised.py`
- `tests/test_board_unsupervised.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `40000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: land a lane, leave it before ship, and read its card saying the work merged rather than that the worktree is empty.

`board_sections.LANE_STATES` is `queued running waits-to-land landing refused parked`. None of the six means "merged, waiting for teardown". So this is either a seventh state, or a `state_detail` that carries the distinction under `queued`.

channel, so `landed` is a seventh state rather than a footnote on the sixth.

gate that says so: `test_the_closed_state_set_is_spelled_the_same_in_all_three_places`
refused the change until the constant, the bounded set and the schema enum all carried it,

body.post_ship_action: File a bug record against the two consumer-surface sentences and bind them to a gate, before touching either sentence. (1) Narrow both sentences to the six regions the acceptance criterion names, or link the two unlinked regions - board_page.html.j2:1589-1604 and board_regions.py:283-290. Linking is preferable, because the sentence is the capability the owner asked for. (2) Add the gate that would have caught this: a test that renders the whole wall from the shipped fixture, collects every printed id with a units row behind it, and fails naming any that carries no link - the population-wide form, not a per-region list, because the per-region test passed while the claim was false. Until (1) and (2) land, the release notes carry the narrowed sentence and the unmet part is stated in the notes rather than dropped.

unsupported.why: The sentence names one condition; the code requires two. `src/basicly/board_unsupervised.py:128` reads `if ahead == 0 and phase in PAST_BUILD_PHASES:`, so a branch whose commits base already holds still reads 'a worktree with no commits and no changes' at phase `build` or earlier. `tests/test_board_unsupervised.py::test_a_phase_at_or_before_build_keeps_the_present_wording[build]` asserts that exact wording for that exact case, so the lane's own suite refutes the sentence as written. The clause is also self-defeating: a worktree that has done nothing is likewise a branch whose commits base already holds, so the sentence contrasts a set with its own subset. I searched tests/test_board_unsupervised.py, tests/test_board_facts.py and tests/test_board_regions_flight.py for a test or gate that binds the unconditional form, and ran the three files (66 passed); none asserts it.

payload.description:
## Context

Owner, 2026-09-06, reading the board's alarm band: *"i have no idea what these 3 waiting on the person want from me"*.

The band was drawing `1 HOUR - 3 WAITING ON A PERSON`, one record's name, an engine sentence, and `+2 more waiting`. Everything a person needed to act was either absent, truncated, or wrong.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Land three records so each sits at `verify` with its ship checkpoint unapproved.
2. `uv run basicly board --out /tmp/board.html` and read the band.

Observed: one ask named, two hidden behind a count, the offered command cut off as `do:...`, and the question reading `verify is cleared and nothing is scheduled to advance it`.

## The five defects, in the order they cost a person time

**1. The offered command does not do the job.** Each ask carries `actions[].offer = "basicly loop advance <id>"`. Run against a merged record it prints:

```
[blocked] verify -> verify: ship checkpoint awaiting human approval
```

What actually ships it is `basicly loop run <id> --root <epic-with-a-grant>`, which the board never mentions. **This is the serious one**: an operator surface that prints a command which stops one step short teaches the operator that the board is wrong, and the other four defects are cosmetic beside it.

**2. Only one ask of three is named.** The other two exist only as `+2 more waiting`. A person cannot act on a count.

**3. The offer is truncated.** The band has the exact argv and cuts it at the right edge.

**4. The question is written for the engine.** `verify is cleared and nothing is scheduled to advance it` describes a scheduler state. A person needs the consequence: this merged, advancing it closes the record and tears the worktree down.

**5. There is no advance action.** `board_actions.ACTIONS` holds `loop-answer`, `checkpoint-approve`, `record-park`, `record-resume` and `lane-kill`. `advance` is the most common thing waiting on a human on this board and it is not offered.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHERE an ask carries an `offer`, THE BOARD SHALL print a command that reaches the state the ask is waiting for, verified by running it, and SHALL NOT print one that stops at an unapproved checkpoint.
- WHEN more than one ask is pending, THE BOARD SHALL name every waiting record and its own command, rather than naming one and counting the rest.
- THE OFFERED COMMAND SHALL be rendered without truncation, wrapping instead of clipping where the column is narrow.
- THE ASK SHALL state the consequence of acting in a person's terms alongside the engine's own wording, never instead of it.
- WHERE an ask's kind is `advance`, THE BOARD SHALL offer it as an action on that ask's row, through an argv handed to the installed CLI like every other action.
- A TEST SHALL run each offered argv against a fixture at the state the ask describes and assert it reaches the next state, so an offer that stops short fails rather than renders.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_advance.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_actions.py`
- `tests/test_board_advance.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_advance.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_advance.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `80000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: leave three records waiting at ship, read the board, and run each command it prints - each reaches ship without a second command the board did not name.

payload.description:
## Context

Found while shipping four records on 2026-09-06. The console said a gate failed; the ledger recorded that it passed. The ledger is right.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Take an L3 record at `verify` whose validate gate is required.
2. `basicly loop run <id> --root <epic-with-a-grant>` or `basicly loop advance <id>`.

Observed, on two records independently:

```
[blocked] validate -> validate: the validator recorded validate-as-consumer failed;
the unit stays in validate (needs input: validation)
```

Measured against the ledger immediately after, counting every `gate` event for each record:

```
basicly-zq9i2m.6: 2 gate event(s) -> [('verify', True), ('validate-as-consumer', True)]
basicly-62h3x9:   2 gate event(s) -> [('verify', True), ('validate-as-consumer', True)]
```

There is **no failed gate event for either record**. `basicly policy gate <id>` agrees: `required passed: ['verify', 'validate-as-consumer']`, `advance: ALLOWED`. Both records then shipped with no rework and no second validator run.

Expected: the line names the state the ledger holds, or says nothing.

## Why this is worth a record rather than a shrug

It is not a fail-open - the gate is honest and the store is correct, which is the reassuring half. It is the surface disagreeing with the record, and that has a cost this session measured twice over: an operator who reads `failed` on a gate that passed learns to distrust the console, exactly as an operator who runs the board's offered command and watches it stop one step short learns to distrust the board (`basicly-lc2bd3v.3`).

The two defects are the same disease in two surfaces. A harness whose narration and whose store disagree cannot be operated by reading either one.

## What is not yet established

Which of three this is: a message composed before the gate write lands and never re-read; a message keyed on the validator's own exit status rather than on the recorded gate; or a message about the *reviewer* dispatches that follow the validator, mislabelled as the validator's. The reviewers do run in this phase - both records carry `[harness-review] lens=correctness` and `lens=security` comments - so the third is not idle speculation and the three are distinguishable by reading the emitter.

Settle that before writing the fix: the remedy differs for each, and a message patched without knowing which would still be wrong in the other two cases.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a phase reports a gate's outcome, THAT REPORT SHALL be read from the recorded gate event rather than from a dispatch's exit status, so the console and the ledger cannot disagree.
- WHERE a report concerns a reviewer rather than the validator, IT SHALL name the reviewer and its lens, never the gate.
- A TEST SHALL drive a passing validate through the phase and assert the printed line and the recorded gate agree, with a control driving a real failure so the assertion is not vacuous.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/validate_gate.py`
- `tests/test_loop_validate.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/validate_gate.py`
- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `tests/test_loop_validate.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `60000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: run an L3 record through validate with a passing gate and read one console line that agrees with `basicly policy gate <id>`.

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-05: *"symbols on the board are not great (check what bootstrap icons have - it is fine to download that dependency and use it, do not use cdn and access online - web assets must be available without internet access)."*

## The constraint that shapes this

`tests/test_board_render.py` asserts the page carries no `<script`, no `<link` and no `src=`. The board is one self-contained HTML file a wall opens from disk. So an icon font, a stylesheet and a sprite URL are all refused by a gate that already exists.

That leaves **inline SVG paths**, which is also what this repo already decided for its own marks: `board_diagram` states that a mark is *"a `path` and never a codepoint, so it does not depend on a wall display font coverage"* - the owner reported tofu on a wall once already.

## What to vendor

`bootstrap-icons` as a dev dependency, its SVG sources committed under the kit rather than fetched. The build reads the handful of paths the page needs and inlines them; nothing at render time touches the network or the filesystem outside the repo.

## Acceptance Criteria

- THE PAGE SHALL still carry no `<script`, no `<link` and no `src=`, and SHALL still render with no network access.
- EACH icon SHALL be an inline `path`, never a codepoint, so a wall display font cannot tofu it.
- ONLY the icons the page draws SHALL be inlined; the full set SHALL NOT be embedded.
- THE VENDORED SOURCE SHALL be committed with its version and licence, and a test SHALL assert the inlined path matches the vendored file so a silent divergence fails.
- WHERE an icon replaces a drawn shape that already works, IT SHALL NOT be replaced without saying why.

## Scope

- `package.json`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/`
- `src/basicly/board_icons.py`
- `tests/test_board_icons.py`

## Owner authorization, 2026-09-06

*"I also approve onboarding of external dependencies like bootstrap icons and components, as
long as they are FOSS."* bootstrap-icons is MIT. No further approval is needed for the
dependency; the no-network and no-`<link>` constraints above still bind.

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `70000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: open the board with the network down and read every mark

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-06, reading a wall whose lower half was empty: *"maybe we can have a way to click somewhere on the board and see the full backlog list so we can plan what to do next better?"*

## Measured

Taken from the board rendered at 1600x1400 on 2026-09-06:

| what the wall draws | what exists |
| --- | --- |
| `NEXT UP` lists **4** records, then `+233 MORE READY` | 237 ready |
| `THE QUEUE` gives four counts and three blocker ids | 1,251 records, 298 active, 57 blocked |
| blank page below `NEXT UP` | roughly 600 of 1400 pixels, 43% of the wall |

So the one surface an operator plans from shows 1.7% of the ready set, and the space to show more is already there and empty.

## Why a page rather than a bigger region

The wall is a glance surface read from across a room and it is right to cap a list. A plan is a different act: it is done at a desk, it wants every record, and it wants sorting and grouping the wall must not spend space on. `basicly-62h3x9` already established the shape - `board --out` writes 297 record pages beside the wall and `board serve` answers `/record/<id>` - so one more page costs no new mechanism.

This is **not** `basicly-c9crxu`. That record is about the wall's own ready column not reading the viewport, and it stays true whatever this one does.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an operator follows the backlog link from the wall, THEY SHALL reach a page listing every open record, not a capped sample.
- EACH ROW SHALL carry the record's id as a link to its page, its title, its priority, its status, its phase and whether it is ready - the fields a person sorts on when choosing what to do next.
- THE PAGE SHALL group by feature, naming the parent each record belongs to, and SHALL name the records that belong to no feature rather than dropping them.
- THE PAGE SHALL let a reader see the blocked set and what blocks each member, because a plan that ignores blockers plans work nobody can start.
- WHERE the wall prints a count it caps - the ready set, the queue, the blocked set - THAT COUNT SHALL be the link to this page, so the way in is where the reader already looks.
- THE PAGE SHALL be written by `board --out` beside the record pages and served by `board serve`, from the snapshot, so `consumer-reads-only-the-snapshot` still holds.
- A TEST SHALL assert the page lists every record `units` carries, so a cap cannot be reintroduced silently.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_backlog.py`
- `src/basicly/board_cli.py`
- `src/basicly/board_serve.py`
- `src/basicly/board_render.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_backlog.html.j2`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `.importlinter`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `tests/test_board_backlog.py`
- `tests/test_board_serve.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_backlog.py`
- `src/basicly/board_record.py`
- `src/basicly/board_cli.py`
- `src/basicly/board_serve.py`

- `tests/test_board_backlog.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `90000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: `uv run basicly board --out /tmp/b.html`, follow the ready count from the wall, and count the rows on the page against `basicly tracker stats`.

Owner, 2026-09-02: "header is still confusing." Third time the header is raised; basicly-jbd80w and basicly-v8jwf0 moved rows and fixed the alarm band, and the owner still cannot read it. This record states what the header holds today, so the next change is against a measurement and not a feeling.

Measured on the live page at 1712x1345, three lines left and one cell right:

```text
basicly  REPO basicly · main · 1687bc87   RUN basicly-k6tpep · open · L3 [bar] 43%
GATES [GREEN] mode full · recorded 2026-09-01T19:38:28Z   SPEND machine-local · 2,032.19 usd · 36.59 usd largest · 1.4B in · 8.7M out
CLOSED TODAY not measured
                                   as of 11s ago / 2026-09-02T09:18:28Z · stale after 60s · [●] producer basicly · 0.11.0
```

Seven things a reader trips on, each verifiable against the snapshot:

1. `RUN basicly-k6tpep` is an id with no title. The snapshot's `units[]` holds the root's title; the header does not use it.
2. `L3 [bar] 43%` names no figure and no denominator. `session.spent_tokens` 42,966,175 of `token_budget` 100,000,000, and `spent_tokens_live` 55,722,904 already reads higher than the committed figure the bar uses.
3. `GATES GREEN` beside `recorded 2026-09-01T19:38:28Z` says the green is yesterday's, and nothing says whether that is fine.
4. `SPEND machine-local · 2,032.19 usd` is the lifetime spend of this machine, not the run's. It sits on the run's line and reads as the run's cost.
5. `1.4B in · 8.7M out` are lifetime token counts with no reader action attached.
6. `CLOSED TODAY not measured` is a standing row that says nothing, the shape basicly-ibzr0f removed from the cards.
7. The right cell repeats the time three ways (`as of 11s ago`, the timestamp, `stale after 60s`) and carries the boxed glyph from the sibling record.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the header renders, LINE ONE SHALL answer which checkout and which run: repo, branch, short head, the root's title with its id beside it, and the run status.
- WHEN a grant is live, THE HEADER SHALL print `spent of budget tokens` as two figures with the bar, using the live figure where the producer holds one and naming the committed figure as such otherwise.
- WHEN the gates cell renders, IT SHALL carry the verdict and the age of the record in the same phrase form as freshness (`recorded 14h ago`), and SHALL colour amber past the same stale threshold the freshness cell uses.
- Lifetime spend and lifetime token counts SHALL move to the footer beside `agents`, and the header SHALL carry the run's own spend only.
- A header cell whose value is `not measured` SHALL NOT render; the absence SHALL appear in the `not drawn` inventory only.
- THE freshness cell SHALL state the time once as `as of 11s ago`, keep the stale threshold, and drop the timestamp to a `title` attribute.
- `tests/test_board_render.py` SHALL assert the header cell order and the absence of `not measured` cells on the fixture.

Assumption stated: the owner named no specific confusion, so the seven items above are the ones measured on the page. The owner may strike or add items before this is dispatched.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_render.py`
- `src/basicly/board_footer.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_render.py`
- `tests/test_board_footer.py`

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-06: *"lanes should not be killed if they are doing work. lanes must be inspected to determine if they hang, and conditions to kill them must be fulfilled. for example a timeout which we set is a poor condition on its own, because an agent can sometime work for hours on a task."*

**The engine already agrees with that, in writing.** `runner.DispatchBounds` says of the wall clock: *"it is the one signal that carries no information about whether work is happening"*, and `runner.StallWatchdog` is documented as *"A flag, not a kill - and deliberately the earliest of the three bounds, so a human learns about a wedge while it is still theirs to intervene in... A slow-but-working run is never cut short here."*

The defect is that none of it reaches a lane started with `basicly loop run`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `basicly loop run <id> --work-type task` on any record.
2. Read what bounds the dispatch it starts.

Measured 2026-09-06:

```
$ rg -n "StallWatchdog\(" src/basicly
src/basicly/supervise.py:2670

$ rg -n "DispatchBounds\(" src/basicly
src/basicly/supervise.py:2688

$ rg -n "runner_timeout|bounds|watchdog" src/basicly/loop.py
loop.py:891    timeout=config.runner_timeout,
loop.py:911    timeout=config.runner_timeout,
loop.py:1138   timeout=config.runner_timeout,
```

Both informed bounds are constructed in exactly one file, and it is not the one the single-lane path uses. `loop.py` passes the wall clock and nothing else.

Expected: the same three bounds, in the same order, whichever verb started the lane.

## Not hidden - stated, three times, and never closed

`loop.py` already documents its own gap:

* `loop.py:188` - *"the spend gate, the watchdog and the stream meter that only exist there"*
* `loop.py:524` - *"names the session as its grant root but has no watchdog or stream"*
* `loop.py:684` - *"watchdog or stream meter of its own"*

So this is a known asymmetry carried as a comment rather than as a record. It is the same shape as `basicly-kqh9dj8`, where lane *visibility* was keyed on the supervisor and a `loop run` lane was invisible: a capability built for the multi-lane path, absent on the single-lane one, with the difference written down and never gated.

## What this costs, measured today

Every lane driven this session used `loop run`. Each therefore ran with the poor condition alone and no stall flag. Three of them died, and the cause each time was the *host* killing the shell they were children of - which is a fourth failure mode none of the three bounds covers, and which the operator could only diagnose by reading a git worktree by hand.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN `basicly loop run` dispatches an agent, THAT DISPATCH SHALL carry the same `StallWatchdog` and `DispatchBounds` a supervised dispatch carries, so the bound that stops a lane is the one that read whether work was happening.
- WHERE a lane is quiet but its event stream, its commits or its worktree dirtiness has changed, IT SHALL NOT be stopped: the fingerprint is proof of life and restarts the clock.
- WHEN the stall bound is reached, THE ENGINE SHALL flag it for a human and SHALL NOT terminate, keeping `stall_after` below `quiet_after` as the supervised path already orders them.
- THE WALL CLOCK SHALL remain the backstop and SHALL NOT be the first bound reached on any path.
- A TEST SHALL assert the bounds a `loop run` dispatch is given equal the bounds a supervised dispatch is given, so the two paths cannot drift again.
- WHERE a dispatch dies because its parent process was killed rather than because a bound fired, THE RECORD SHALL say so, so an operator is not left inferring it from a worktree.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `tests/test_loop_dispatch_bounds.py`
- `tests/test_runner.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `tests/test_runner.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `90000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: start a lane with `loop run`, watch it idle past `stall_after`, and read the flag raised for a human while the lane is still alive - then let a working lane run past the same bound untouched.

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-05: *"symbols on the board are not great (check what bootstrap icons have - it is fine to download that dependency and use it, do not use cdn and access online - web assets must be available without internet access)."*

## The constraint that shapes this

`tests/test_board_render.py` asserts the page carries no `<script`, no `<link` and no `src=`. The board is one self-contained HTML file a wall opens from disk. So an icon font, a stylesheet and a sprite URL are all refused by a gate that already exists.

That leaves **inline SVG paths**, which is also what this repo already decided for its own marks: `board_diagram` states that a mark is *"a `path` and never a codepoint, so it does not depend on a wall display font coverage"* - the owner reported tofu on a wall once already.

## What to vendor

`bootstrap-icons` as a dev dependency, its SVG sources committed under the kit rather than fetched. The build reads the handful of paths the page needs and inlines them; nothing at render time touches the network or the filesystem outside the repo.

## Acceptance Criteria

- THE PAGE SHALL still carry no `<script`, no `<link` and no `src=`, and SHALL still render with no network access.
- EACH icon SHALL be an inline `path`, never a codepoint, so a wall display font cannot tofu it.
- ONLY the icons the page draws SHALL be inlined; the full set SHALL NOT be embedded.
- THE VENDORED SOURCE SHALL be committed with its version and licence, and a test SHALL assert the inlined path matches the vendored file so a silent divergence fails.
- WHERE an icon replaces a drawn shape that already works, IT SHALL NOT be replaced without saying why.

## Scope

Widened at the landing on 2026-09-06. The first list said `.basicly/core/templates/board/`,
which matches the directory and not the files in it, so every vendored SVG read as out of
scope. Four more follow from gates rather than from the change: `.importlinter` must declare
every module in `basicly`, `docs/architecture/architecture.md` carries a generated layering
block that goes stale when that list moves, `package-lock.json` is what `npm install` writes
beside the pin, and `tests/test_board_render.py` holds the no-`<script>`/`<link>`/`src=`
assertion this record is measured against.

- `package.json`
- `package-lock.json`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/**`
- `src/basicly/board_icons.py`
- `src/basicly/board_render.py`
- `.importlinter`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `tests/test_board_icons.py`
- `tests/test_board_render.py`
- `basicly.d/basicly-e1c4pct.toml`
- `changelog.d/basicly-e1c4pct.changed.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_icons.py`
- `src/basicly/board_render.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_icons.py`

## Owner authorization, 2026-09-06

*"I also approve onboarding of external dependencies like bootstrap icons and components, as
long as they are FOSS."* bootstrap-icons is MIT. No further approval is needed for the
dependency; the no-network and no-`<link>` constraints above still bind.

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `70000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: open the board with the network down and read every mark

payload.description:
## Context

Third instance of one root cause, found 2026-09-06 by watching the header go blank the moment a supervisor exited cleanly.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Work a repository with `basicly loop run` only, so no supervisor lock is ever taken.
2. `uv run basicly board --out /tmp/board.html` and read the header's run line.

Observed:

```
RUN not emitted by this producer
NOT DRAWN  session - not in this snapshot
```

Expected: the run's record, its grant level, its token budget and its spend, which are facts about the repository and not about a process.

## Cause, and why it is a pattern

`board_serve.session_facts` returns None unless `supervise.read_holder` finds a lock file. `board_facts.session_facts` adds the grant on top and inherits the same gate. So the run line, the grant level, the budget bar and the spend figure all exist only while a supervisor process holds a lock.

This is the **third** capability keyed on that lock rather than on the work:

| capability | record | state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lane rows in `RUNNING NOW` | `basicly-kqh9dj8` | fixed 2026-09-06 |
| the six lane states `LANE_STATES` ships | `basicly-ncday7` | shipped, then unreachable, reached by the fix above |
| the run line: record, grant, budget, spend | **this record** | open |

Each was built for the supervised pass and each is absent on the single-lane path, and in every case the absence rendered as an absence of *work* rather than an absence of *a supervisor*.

## Why nobody noticed until now

A stale lock kept it alive. `read_holder` returns the holder whatever its age and the caller marks it `stale = age_s > STALE_AFTER_S`, so a lock left by a dead session still fed the header - the board drew `RUN basicly-k6tpep - open - L3 - 103%` all day with no supervisor anywhere. A detached `loop supervise` run then took that lock and released it cleanly on exit, which removed it, and the header went blank.

So the header was not working; it was being fed by a corpse. That is worse than it having been blank all along, because the figure it drew - a grant bar at 103% - was the only warning anywhere that the session had gone human-only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a repository has an active grant and no supervisor holds a lock, THE HEADER SHALL still name the granted root, its level, its budget and its spend.
- WHERE a supervisor does hold a lock, THE PRESENT behaviour SHALL be unchanged, including the stale marking.
- WHERE the run line is derived without a lock, IT SHALL NOT claim a pass is running: the grant is a fact about the repository and the pass is a fact about a process, and the header must not merge them.
- A TEST SHALL build the header with no lock present and assert the grant figures are drawn, with a control asserting no pass is claimed.
- THE THREE CAPABILITIES ABOVE SHALL share one test naming every board fact that is allowed to depend on the lock, so a fourth cannot be added silently.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_serve.py`
- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_facts.py`
- `tests/test_board_serve.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_serve.py`
- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_snapshot.py`
- `tests/test_board_facts.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `70000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: with no supervisor and no lock file, render the board and read the granted root, its level, its budget and its spend on the header.

payload.description:
## Context

Owner, 2026-09-06, on what a backlog surface must do beyond listing:

> *"get inspired by jira, linear, clickup, asana, youtrack... we need a better dependency visualization system than those tools provide. then I could open a backlog and prioritize it, and during prioritization the dependencies would always be considered, so constraints would be set in place. Example: if moving an item from 5th position to the 1st, and that item has an item dependent on item on 4th position, that means that 4th item must be done before 5th and the 5th cannot be placed before it. The system would in this case visualize what items are connected and in which order when one is selected, and will prohibit sorting the backlog in a way that breaks dependencies."*

And the framing: *"adapt these concepts to the agentic-first development, which also humans, if visualized correctly, used."*

## The design question this forces, which must be answered before any code

**This repository has no rank field.** `basicly tracker ready` reports a rank, and it is *computed*, not stored:

```
$ uv run basicly tracker ready --limit 3 --json
{"rank": 1, "record": "basicly-94bk",   "score": 3001, ...}
{"rank": 2, "record": "basicly-a3yi",   "score": 3001, ...}
{"rank": 3, "record": "basicly-g5ce75", "score": 3001, ...}
```

`scheduler.ranking()` derives the order from priority, dependent count and id, and `Ranking` carries the sort policy beside the rows *"because a rank recorded without its policy is uninterpretable later"*. Three records tie at 3001 today, so the visible order between them is the tiebreak, not a judgment anybody made.

So a drag to position 1 has nowhere to land. Two honest routes, and this is the decision to take first:

**(a) The drag writes `priority`.** No new state. The engine already reads priority and every consumer inherits the change. But priority is coarse - five buckets, 480 records at P1 - so a drag inside a bucket changes nothing and the item springs back. Honest, and visibly weak.

**(b) The ledger gains a stored rank the scheduler reads ahead of its computed score.** A drag means something exact. It costs a new field, a new event kind, a migration for 1,253 records, and it puts a human's ordering above the engine's - which is either the point or the danger, depending on the owner's answer.

**Do not build until this is chosen.** A drag that appears to work and is silently ignored by the dispatcher is worse than no drag, and it is the exact failure `basicly-fiow1sr` already shipped once: an argv that looked right and started nothing.

## What the research already settled, and nobody has used

Two closed spikes from 2026-09-04 are the reading for this, and both are unactioned:

* `basicly-hnnmk9.6` - dependency-ordered scheduling in established practice. Its load-bearing finding is that **this repo orders lanes on write-scope overlap, not on consumed results** (`decompose.serializes`, an anti/output dependence model), while declared `depends_on` edges are carried separately. So there are *two* orderings, and a backlog that honours only the declared graph will let a human order two items that collide at the merge.
* `basicly-hnnmk9.9` - an inventory of the nine graphs this repository maintains, including the record dependency graph and the file contention graph, and where they do and do not compose.

The owner's constraint rule is a topological one, and the spike names its literature: Kahn 1962, CPM, and GNU make's *order-only prerequisite* - an edge that imposes ordering without implying data flow, which is precisely the shape of a contention edge.

## What the named tools do, and where each stops

| tool | ordering | dependency handling | where it stops for us |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Jira | stored `Rank` (LexoRank), drag writes it | blocks/is-blocked-by shown as a badge; ordering is not constrained | a human may rank a blocked item first and nothing objects |
| Linear | stored sort key, drag writes it | blocking relations, and a blocked item is marked | same: the warning is advisory |
| ClickUp / Asana | manual order per list | dependencies with optional date shifting | shifts dates, does not refuse an order |
| YouTrack | saved queries and sort | issue links, `depends on` | sort is a query, not a constraint |

**None of them refuses a reorder.** They warn. The owner is asking for refusal, which is the thing that is actually new here - and it is only defensible because our graph is machine-consumed: an order a dispatcher will really execute is worth constraining, where a human backlog order is advisory anyway.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an operator selects a record in the backlog, THE PAGE SHALL draw that record's dependency neighbourhood - what it waits on, what waits on it, and the order those imply - and SHALL distinguish a declared `blocks` edge from a contention edge derived from overlapping scope.
- WHEN an operator moves a record above one it depends on, THE PAGE SHALL refuse the move and SHALL name the chain that forbids it, rather than accepting it with a warning.
- WHERE a move is legal, THE PAGE SHALL apply it through an argv handed to the installed CLI, and the resulting order SHALL be the order `basicly tracker ready` then reports - or the move SHALL be refused as unrepresentable.
- THE PAGE SHALL NOT invent an ordering the engine does not read: a drag whose effect the dispatcher ignores is a lie the operator will act on.
- WHERE two records are unordered by any edge, THE PAGE SHALL say they are unordered rather than implying the list position is a decision.
- A TEST SHALL attempt a dependency-violating move against a fixture and assert it is refused, naming the chain, with a control asserting a legal move is applied.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_backlog.py`
- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_graph.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_backlog.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_backlog.py`
- `tests/test_board_actions.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_backlog.py`
- `src/basicly/board_graph.py`
- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `tests/test_board_backlog.py`

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: `basicly-lc2bd3v.4`
- demonstration: open the backlog, select a record and read its neighbourhood, then attempt to move a dependent above its blocker and read the refusal naming the chain.

payload.description:
## Context

Owner, 2026-09-06: *"board shows 2 cards in parked - build, which is an indicator to me that nothing is happening and everything is waiting, contrary to the 'nothing is waiting' large text on the board."*

Both readings were the board's fault. The banner said `NOTHING IS WAITING` and the region beneath it said `waits for the next pass - 2 lane(s) parked`, so the page contradicted itself in the two largest type sizes it has.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Leave two worktrees on disk whose records are `parked` - one deferred, one abandoned - and no lane running.
2. `uv run basicly board --out /tmp/board.html` and read the line under `RUNNING NOW`.

Observed: `waits for the next pass - 2 lane(s) parked`.

Expected: no pass exists to wait for, so the region says what a reader can act on.

## Cause

`board_regions._waiting_on` is a ladder, and its third rung fired on any state in `LANE_MARKS`:

```python
stopped = [state for state in held if state in LANE_MARKS]
if stopped:
    return f"waits for the next pass - {len(stopped)} lane(s) {words}"
```

`parked` is in `LANE_MARKS`, so two dead worktrees produced a sentence promising a pass that was never coming. `basicly-3iaw0x` is deferred by owner decision of 2026-09-01 and `basicly-fiow1sr` is an abandoned worktree held on purpose; no pass will adopt either.

`landed` had the same problem the moment it was added (`basicly-k6tpep.4`): finished work would have read as waiting too.

The rung's own docstring already states the rule it broke - *"A rung must not answer a question it cannot"* - written when the blocked count fired on an idle factory (`basicly-9guj21`). This is the same defect one rung higher.

## Fix

`LANE_RESUMABLE = {queued, waits-to-land, refused}` - the stopped states a pass will come back to. `parked` and `landed` are excluded, and the fall-through guard reads the same set, so a board holding nothing but parked and landed worktrees drops to the ready count instead of describing a pass that does not exist.

Measured after: `no pass is running - 239 record(s) are ready to start`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHERE every lane is `parked` or `landed`, THE REGION SHALL NOT say the pass waits for them, and SHALL fall through to what a reader can start.
- WHERE a lane is `queued`, `waits-to-land` or `refused`, THE PRESENT sentence SHALL be unchanged: a pass really will come back to those.
- THE BANNER AND THE REGION SHALL NOT disagree: when the banner says nothing is waiting, no line beneath it may say something is.
- A TEST SHALL drive a board whose only lanes are parked and assert the ready count is reported, with a control asserting a queued lane still reports as waiting.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions_flight.py`
- `changelog.d/basicly-k6tpep.6.fixed.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions_flight.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `30000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: render a board whose only worktrees are parked and read one sentence that names the ready count, with the banner agreeing.
