payload.value:
## Context

Owner, 2026-09-05, restating a requirement they say they have given many times: *"the requirement was also to make the board interactive or a cockpit or a control panel where we can see and control the flow of work. Cool thing would be to be able to easily start, stop work, descope and so on."*

And the reason, in their words: *"One of the biggest issues with agentic development in the terminal alone is that human has no idea what is going on and when multiple parallel sessions and work is being done, it gets buried under. Terminal is fast and no one scrolls up, having multiple terminals does not help."*

And the test they set: *"if you as an agent look at the board, and only have access to the board, would you be able to see what is going on? what work is available, what work can start, is in progress? start work, stop work, inspect work (the info written in the record in a structured way)? descope work, scope work?"*

Explicitly **not** in scope: *"it is not about creating new records - that we can do via terminal. it is about work loop transparency and control."*

And the standing instruction: *"the board, even if it is a byproduct of basicly, it is essential and should grow with the basicly."*

## The gap, measured

Taken against the served board at 127.0.0.1:8788 on 2026-09-05, and against the snapshot it renders.

| the owner's question | answered today | by what |
| --- | --- | --- |
| what work is available | partly | `NEXT UP` draws 3 of 234 ready |
| what can start now | yes | `THE QUEUE`: 262 needs nothing, 24 waits on one, 8 waits on a chain |
| what is in progress | yes | `RUNNING NOW` and `CLAIMED, NO LANE` |
| what is blocked, and by what | yes | `THE QUEUE` names the top blockers and the longest chain |
| **inspect one record** | **no** | `units[]` carries `id, phase, priority, ready, status, title, type` and no body |
| **start work** | **no** | no action offers `loop run` or `supervise` |
| **stop work** | partly | `lane-kill` is in `ACTIONS`, but only reachable when an ask prefills it |
| **descope / scope** | **no** | no action changes status or priority |
| when will it be done | no | `basicly-hymq99` and `basicly-w6vbw61` |

So four of nine. The two channels that are missing are **inspect** and **control**, and they are missing for different reasons.

## The seam already exists

`board_actions.ACTIONS` is a closed table of three argv builders handed to the installed CLI as a subprocess. Its docstring states the design: *"The board is a renderer with a keyboard."* `.importlinter`'s `consumer-reads-only-the-snapshot` contract holds because the board never reads the tracker; it runs `basicly`.

That is the answer to inspect as well as control. A record's body does not have to enter the snapshot - 294 bodies would be a snapshot nobody can serve. The board runs `basicly tracker show <id>` the same way it runs `basicly policy checkpoint`, and renders what comes back. No contract moves.

`board_asks.pending` already prefills a row per implementable offer. What is missing is a surface for an action that no *ask* proposes - a ready record has no ask, so today nothing offers to start it.

## Redefined by the owner, 2026-09-06 — the cockpit is a development environment

> *"the board is the human instrument for implementation of new features. the human will set
> up the backlog with the agent using terminal, and then it will view and control the
> implementation via the board. That is why this board design must look like a development
> environment for a human, where he sees what is going on and can react on it."*

And the reason, which is the same one they have given all session in different words:

> *"I have asked you many times during implementation, and several times in this session,
> where are we now. that is because I cannot see clearly where we are."*

**This supersedes the wall framing.** The board was built as a glance surface read from across
a room, and every design decision followed from that: cap the lists, prefer counts to members,
draw a diagram rather than a backlog. Those were right for a wall and are wrong for a cockpit.
`basicly-a68ggd` is the clearest case - it is closed, and its title is *"the loop region shows
the whole backlog binned by phase instead of the running pass"*. The region was deliberately
made **not** a list of what sits in each phase. The owner is now asking for exactly that list.
It is a reversal on a new requirement, not a regression, and it is recorded here so nobody
re-closes `a68ggd`'s finding on top of it.

**The division of labour, stated by the owner:** the backlog is set up *with an agent in the
terminal*. The cockpit is where a human **views and controls the implementation**. So the
cockpit does not need record creation - it needs seeing and reacting.

**Two surfaces, not one page:**

1. **The loop** - what is happening now, as a kanban of phase columns in the shape Linear and
   Jira use, where each phase names its members and a member is reachable.
2. **The backlog** - what is planned, ordered, with the controls to shape it.

**Titles carry the meaning, ids are the address.** The owner: *"the real titles of features and
tasks are more important than IDs. IDs should be there but focus is on titles, description,
priority, and dependency."* The board leads with ids in most regions today.

**And the case nothing is designed for: N sessions on one repository.** The owner:
*"4-5 terminals, each with an open session, are working on the same repository."* Shared
branch, shared worktrees. `basicly-kqh9dj8` shipped worktree visibility, which is one agent's
answer to "who is inside a lane"; it says nothing about which *session* holds what, whether two
are about to collide, or what a fifth terminal joining should be told.

**Priority:** the owner has made visualization number one, on the ground that the cockpit is
*"the 1st thing a user will see when starting basicly after installation in their repo"*.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an agent has the board and nothing else, IT SHALL be able to answer all nine questions in the table above, and a test SHALL enumerate them so the board cannot drift back into a report.
- WHERE a verb changes the flow of work, THE BOARD SHALL offer it on the row it applies to, not only where an ask happens to prefill it.
- THE BOARD SHALL NOT gain the ability to create a record: the owner keeps that in the terminal.
- `consumer-reads-only-the-snapshot` SHALL still hold: every new capability is an argv handed to the installed CLI.

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- children decompose this; each is a leaf a lane can build

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `uv run basicly board --out /tmp/board.html` and read `THE LOOP`.

Observed: seven boxes carrying a count each - `268 intake`, `2 classify`, `27 decompose`, `1 build`, `0 verify`, `0 validate`, `0 ship`, `954 done`. No box names a record. Nothing is reachable.

Expected: each phase names the records sitting in it, and each is reachable.

## This reverses a closed decision, deliberately

`basicly-a68ggd` is closed and titled *"the loop region shows the whole backlog binned by phase instead of the running pass"*. The region was changed **away** from listing what sits in each phase, because a wall read from across a room should show the pass and not the backlog.

That was right for a wall. The owner has redefined the surface as a development environment a person works at (`basicly-lc2bd3v`), and at a desk the members are the point. **Do not re-close `a68ggd`'s finding on top of this**: its concern - that the running pass must stay legible and not be drowned by 268 intake records - is still true, and is the reason the columns below are capped and ordered rather than dumped.

## The shape, from the tools the owner named

Linear and Jira both draw a column per state with cards in it, a count in the column header, and a card that opens the item. The adaptation here is that our columns are **loop phases**, which are not a workflow a human moves cards between - the engine moves them. So the column is a view, and the actions on a card are the loop's own verbs, not a drag between columns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a reader opens the loop surface, EACH PHASE SHALL be a column naming the records in it, with its count in the column header.

- A CARD SHALL be the link to that record's page, so a phase is a way in and not a dead end.
- WHERE a phase holds more records than the column draws, THE COLUMN SHALL say how many more and SHALL remain readable - `intake` holds 268 and a column that dumps them is the defect `basicly-a68ggd` closed.
- THE COLUMN ORDER SHALL be the loop's own order, so the surface reads left to right as work flows.
- WHERE a record in a column has a live worktree, THE CARD SHALL say so, so a reader can tell a phase a record is parked in from one being worked.

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-06: *"think about what will be shown on the cockpit if multiple sessions and agents are working on the same repo in parallel, using same branch and worktrees? One of the use cases I encounter in projects is that 4-5 terminals, each with an open session, are working on the same repository."*

Nothing in the board is designed for this. It is the case the cockpit exists for - the owner's own reason for wanting one is *"when multiple parallel sessions and work is being done, it gets buried"* - and it is the one case no record covers.

## What the board can see today, and what it cannot

`basicly-kqh9dj8` shipped this session and answers **one** question: which records have a worktree, and what git says about each. Measured against the owner's case, that is a third of it.

| the question a fifth terminal arrives with | answerable today |
| --- | --- |
| what worktrees exist and what state is each in | **yes** - `board_unsupervised.lanes` |
| which *session* holds which worktree | no - no session identity is recorded outside a supervisor lock |
| is anybody editing the base checkout right now | no |
| what did the other four sessions just do | partly - the events ticker, unattributed |
| am I about to collide with one of them | no - the contention graph exists and nothing consults it (`basicly-zq9i2m.3`) |
| may I start work on record X | no - `ready` says the tracker permits it, not that a peer is not already on it |

The last row is the sharp one. Two terminals can both read `ready`, both pick the top record, and both start. The tracker's claim is written at provisioning, so the window is small but real, and the loser finds out at the merge queue.

## What identity already exists to build on

* `supervise.read_holder` writes a lock with a `session_id` and a heartbeat - but only a supervisor takes it, which is `basicly-k6tpep.5`'s finding: three capabilities are gated on that lock and a `loop run` operator takes none.
* Every worktree has a name, a branch and a git state, which needs no cooperation from the session that made it.
* The ledger records who claimed a record and when, and it is shared across worktrees by the `redirect` file - so the ledger is the one place all five sessions already meet.

So the honest design direction is **the ledger and the filesystem, not a session registry**: anything requiring five terminals to register themselves will be wrong the moment one crashes, and a heartbeat nobody writes is the stale-lock defect this session already found feeding the header for a whole day.

## What must be decided before building

**Is a session a first-class thing the ledger records, or is it inferred?** Recording it means a new event kind, a heartbeat, and a liveness rule - and a crashed terminal then lies until its heartbeat expires. Inferring it from worktrees and ledger writes means the board can never name a session that has not touched anything, but it also cannot be wrong about one.

Prefer inference until a question is found that inference cannot answer. State the question if one is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN more than one session is working a repository, THE COCKPIT SHALL name each unit of work in flight and which worktree holds it, without requiring any session to register itself.
- WHERE the base checkout is dirty, THE COCKPIT SHALL say so, because a landing refuses on it and the operator who caused it may be at a different terminal.
- WHEN a reader considers starting a record, THE COCKPIT SHALL say whether a peer already holds it, and SHALL distinguish "the tracker permits this" from "nobody else is on it".
- WHERE two units in flight declare overlapping scope, THE COCKPIT SHALL name the overlap before the merge queue does.
- THE COCKPIT SHALL NOT claim a session is alive on the strength of a marker nobody is refreshing: a stale lock fed the header a false run line for a full day on 2026-09-06.
- A TEST SHALL drive two concurrent units against one repository and assert both are named with their holders.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_unsupervised.py`
- `src/basicly/board_sessions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-06: *"the real titles of features and tasks are more important than IDs. IDs should be there but focus is on titles, description, priority, and dependency."*

This is the fourth session in which a version of it has been said, and it is already a saved rule from an earlier one: *a person cannot read an id, so report the id and the title together.* The board keeps doing the opposite in specific places, and each has been fixed as its own defect - `basicly-a8jy77` for the header, `basicly-lc2bd3v.2` for the record page. Fixing sites one at a time is why it keeps coming back.

## Measured

The wall rendered at 1600x1250 on 2026-09-06 prints **23 record ids in its body, 22 of them unique**. The rows that carry a title alongside are the ready list and the lane cards. The rows that do not:

- `PARKED  P4 basicly-0jiq intake  P3 basicly-3iaw0x build  P2 basicly-kjc5.49 intake  P2 basicly-vkh0.4 intake`
- `THE QUEUE ... unblocks most  basicly-uz3m68.1 4  basicly-7bur 3  basicly-vkh0.42.6 3`
- `longest  basicly-uz3m68.5 -> basicly-uz3m68.4 -> basicly-uz3m68.3 -> ...`
- `EVENTS  basicly-e1c4pct  2026-09-06T16:47:58Z  harness-cost  id=basicly-e1c4pct#cost`
- the header's `RUN` line, when it draws

Five regions, one rule, and no gate. A reader is asked to hold 22 opaque strings.

## Why a gate rather than a sixth fix

`basicly-m8cdnv1` - *"every header and footer line earns its place or is cut"* - is **closed**, and the owner has raised the header twice since. A review that passes and a requirement that keeps failing means the review was of the wrong thing. What survives is a check the page has to satisfy on every render, not a judgment made once.

The gate is cheap because the fact is already there: `units[]` carries a title for every record the board draws, so a region printing a bare id is not missing data, it is choosing not to draw it.

## The exception the gate must allow

A **chain** - `a -> b -> c -> d` - cannot carry four titles and stay one line. That region's job is the shape, not the members. So the rule is not "never print a bare id"; it is "a region that names a record as a thing a reader acts on must name it by title", and a region that draws a shape declares itself as such.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHERE the board names a record as a thing a reader acts on, IT SHALL draw that record's title, and the id SHALL be present as the address rather than as the name.
- WHERE a region draws a shape rather than members - the dependency chain is the case - IT SHALL declare itself exempt in one named list, so the exemption is enumerable rather than implicit.
- A TEST SHALL render the page and fail on any record id outside that exempt list which is not accompanied by its title, naming the region, so a sixth site cannot be added silently.
- THE TITLE SHALL be clipped rather than dropped where a column is narrow, and the untruncated title SHALL remain available on the row.
- WHERE a title is absent from the snapshot, THE ID SHALL stand alone and the absence SHALL read as an absence, never as a record with no name.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_footer.py`
- `src/basicly/board_graph.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_titles.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.changed.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_footer.py`
- `src/basicly/board_graph.py`
- `tests/test_board_titles.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `80000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: render the wall and read every named record by its title, then add a bare id to a region and watch the gate name that region.

## Context

Raised by a waiver taken on 2026-09-06, and filed as the record that retires it.

`src/basicly/board_actions.py` was split at the `module-size` gate's own instruction: the endpoint half - spawn, validation, HTTP, audit - moved to `board_action_surface`, leaving a table of six action declarations and the reason for each. The split fixed the size gate and pushed `comment-density` from 50.1% to 54.1%, because what left was code-dense and what stayed is declaration plus rationale.

Measured across the move: 125 lines left the module and only 31 of them were prose.

## The question

**Is a prose ratio the right measure for a module that is mostly a declaration?** The gate exists to catch narration - a comment restating the statement below it - and it is good at that. A table of six argv builders is different in kind: each entry is two or three lines of data and the reason it is that argv rather than another, which is exactly what the repo's rules ask code to carry.

Three ways this could go, and the record exists to choose one rather than to leave a waiver standing:

1. **The measure is right and the module is wrong.** Then the reasons belong somewhere else - the architecture document, or one block comment rather than eight docstrings - and the waiver retires by moving them.
2. **The measure needs a population discriminator.** A module whose top-level statements are overwhelmingly a literal declaration is a different population from a module of functions, and the cap could read it as such. This is the shape `a-ratchet-needs-a-population-discriminator` describes.
3. **The split was wrong.** Unlikely - the size gate demanded it and the seam was real - but stated so it is refutable.

## What was tried before waiving, so it is not repeated

The module docstring's four paragraphs were split by subject: three described the confirm-code friction, the redaction property and the HTTP trust boundary, all of which had moved to `board_action_surface`, so they moved with the code they describe. Five function docstrings were then rewritten shorter by hand. One mechanical compression pass was attempted, produced sentences truncated mid-thought, and was reverted - a rationale cut to fit a ratio is worse than the ratio.

The figure did not move off 54.1% across all of it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- THE WAIVER on `src/basicly/board_actions.py` SHALL be removed in the same change that resolves this record, whichever of the three ways is chosen.
- WHERE the answer is that the measure needs a discriminator, THAT DISCRIMINATOR SHALL be bound to something the producer of the module writes, not to a name or a path - an absence must not be ambiguous.
- WHERE the answer is that the reasons belong elsewhere, EVERY REASON SHALL survive the move: the count of distinct claims before and after is the check, not the character count.
- A TEST SHALL fail if this waiver outlives the record, so it cannot become a standing exemption.

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_comment_density.py`
- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `pyproject.toml`
- `tests/test_check_comment_density.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.changed.md`

## Working Set

- `.scripts/check_comment_density.py`
- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `tests/test_check_comment_density.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `50000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: run the density gate with the waiver removed and read either a passing module or a discriminator that says why a declaration table is a different population.

[session handover 2026-09-06] STATE: the board is redefined as a cockpit and that is now P0. Board serves detached on 127.0.0.1:8787. No worktrees, no asks, tree clean.

NEXT: the owner redefined the surface on 2026-09-06 and the epic basicly-lc2bd3v carries their words. Two surfaces, not one page: basicly-lc2bd3v.6 the loop as a kanban of phase columns naming their records (this reverses closed basicly-a68ggd deliberately - read that record's concern before building), and basicly-lc2bd3v.4 the backlog page then basicly-lc2bd3v.5 dependency-constrained prioritization. basicly-lc2bd3v.5 is BLOCKED ON AN OWNER DECISION: there is no rank field, ranking is computed by scheduler.ranking, so a drag either writes priority (five coarse buckets, 489 at P1, springs back inside a bucket) or the ledger gains a stored rank the scheduler reads first. Do not build until that is chosen. Also basicly-lc2bd3v.7 multi-session visibility for 4-5 terminals on one repo, and basicly-lc2bd3v.8 titles-first as a gate rather than a sixth wording fix.

OPEN FROM TODAY: basicly-jr0l.75 the console says a validate gate failed while the ledger records it passed, three for three on every L3 record driven through validate, so the line is unconditional. basicly-zq9i2m.7 a loop run lane is bounded by the wall clock alone and gets no stall watchdog - StallWatchdog and DispatchBounds are constructed only in supervise.py. basicly-k6tpep.5 the run line and grant bar exist only while a supervisor holds a lock, and a stale lock fed the header a false 103% all day. basicly-k6tpep.3 the record page writer follows a planted symlink, demonstrated by the security reviewer. basicly-lc2bd3v.3 the board prints loop advance which stops one step short of shipping. basicly-kya2os.1 owns the comment-density waiver taken on board_actions.

Closed by hand 2026-09-07, outside the loop, on the owner's decision.

The work is on main at 3f2ee599 'feat(board): offer a start on a ready record and split the action endpoint out'. Both defects this record's 2026-09-05 comment measured are fixed there: board_actions._start now builds ('loop','run',<id>,'--detach') and carries --work-type and --root, so it is neither 'supervise' (which fans out over children a leaf has none of) nor '--max-passes 1' (which provisions without dispatching). Verified against a served board: 'basicly board serve --port 8787' prints record-start among its six registered actions.

Why the loop could not close it. The lane was landed by hand and its worktree torn down, so the build->verify landing never ran and no verify gate was recorded. 'basicly policy gate basicly-fiow1sr' reports required MISSING: ['verify']. 'loop advance' refuses with 'no worktree session named basicly-fiow1sr' (merge.py:1030) because branch harness/basicly-fiow1sr no longer exists. derive_phase (loop_state.py:170) needs verify in required_passed for every rung above build, so the record derived build off a dead binding, and clearing that binding would have dropped it to intake and re-dispatched a lane to rebuild landed code.

The gap this leaves for the harness: a hand-landed lane whose worktree is gone has no route to ship. clear_worktree_binding is the only disposal the engine offers and it sends a finished record back to intake.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `uv run pytest -q` (the whole suite, 5433 tests, ~230s).

Observed 2026-09-07: `tests/test_supervise_board.py::test_a_tick_emits_a_snapshot_whose_freshness_is_younger_than_the_tick` failed with `assert 0 <= -0.880328`. The test passed on its own immediately afterwards, twice, and the whole module passed.

## The defect

```
stamped = datetime.fromisoformat(document['generated_at'])
age_s = (datetime.now(UTC) - stamped).total_seconds()
assert 0 <= age_s < document['freshness']['stale_after_s']
```

Two wall-clock reads bound a value the *supervisor thread* stamps. Under a loaded run the reader can observe a stamp written after its own `now()`, so the age is negative and the lower bound trips. Nothing is wrong with the product: the snapshot is younger than the tick, which is what the test is named for.

## Why it matters more than one flake

The repo's own rule is to wait for the condition and take elapsed time from a monotonic clock. This assertion does neither, and it is the freshness contract's only guard - a flake here trains a reader to re-run rather than to read, which is how a real staleness regression would land green on the second attempt.

## Acceptance Criteria

- THE TEST SHALL assert the snapshot is younger than the staleness bound without a lower bound that two wall-clock reads can violate.
- WHERE the lower bound carries meaning - a stamp from the future is a producer defect - IT SHALL be expressed with a tolerance the scheduler cannot exceed, and that tolerance SHALL carry the measurement it came from.
- THE TEST SHALL pass under a full-suite run, not only in isolation.

## Scope

- `tests/test_supervise_board.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L1`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: run the full suite and read the summary line

OWNER DECISION 2026-09-07, unblocking this record. A drag writes a STORED RANK FIELD, not a priority bucket.

The ledger gains a rank the scheduler reads before scheduler.ranking computes one; the computed ranking becomes the fallback for records that carry no stored rank, not the answer. ## Context

Owner, 2026-09-07, reading the served board: *"even you mentioned onboarding bootstrap icons and components, i still see a few icons only, and the buttons and components do not look like bootstrap and do not behave like bootstrap."*

And the constraint, in their words: *"you can vendor the bootstrap css, and update the style (css classes) to match our design. i think that bootstrap css can be onboarded using npm as a node package (no CDN, or any internet access for the page to run is allowed)."*

`basicly-e1c4pct` vendored bootstrap **icons** MIT with provenance. Nothing vendored the framework, so every control on the board is hand-rolled CSS: a submit button is a bare `<button>` styled to look like text, and the cards, tables and strips share no component vocabulary.

## Measured

Taken from the served board at 127.0.0.1:8787 on 2026-09-07.

| what a bootstrap page has | what the board has |
| --- | --- |
| `.btn` with size, variant, focus ring and disabled state | a `<button>` with `background: none` and a hover border |
| `.card` with header, body and consistent radius | four different hand-tuned box treatments across regions |
| `.table` with striping and cell padding scale | three tables, each with its own padding literals |
| a spacing scale | ad-hoc px values, ~40 distinct |

## Acceptance Criteria

- THE REPOSITORY SHALL vendor bootstrap's CSS as an npm dependency with its licence and version recorded beside it, as `basicly-e1c4pct` did for the icons.
- WHEN a board page is opened with no network, IT SHALL render fully: no CDN reference, no external font, no remote fetch of any kind.
- WHERE the board draws a control a reader presses, IT SHALL carry bootstrap's button semantics - a visible focus ring, a disabled state, and one size scale.
- THE THREE PAGES - wall, loop and backlog - SHALL share one component vocabulary, so a card on one reads as a card on the others.
- THE PALETTE SHALL stay basicly's own; this record adopts bootstrap's components and spacing scale, not its colours.
- A TEST SHALL assert no page references an external origin, so a CDN cannot be reintroduced silently.

- `.basicly/core/templates/board/vendor/`
- `tests/test_board_offline.py`

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-07, after reading a record page that showed a title and no body: *"how should i then use this to drive test-driven development to write tests first and make them pass later? ... I as human, if that was my backlog i wouldnt even know where to start."*

And the standard they set: *"you can follow the INVEST criteria and benchmark against them every time you write a record (story, task). Also Jeffries C3 for writing stories can also help. I am demanding this because to me it looks like content of the records is not independent, negotiable, valuable, estimable, small, testable - thus it is hard to implement."*

## Measured

Folded from the ledger on 2026-09-07 over the 304 records `units[]` lists, with a positive control on `basicly-lc2bd3v.7` run before the zero was believed:

| active records | 304 |
| --- | --- |
| with a `## Acceptance Criteria` section | 196 (64%) |
| a body but no criteria | 99 |
| no body at all | 9 |

So **108 records can be dispatched with nothing to verify the result against**. `basicly-e2mz.38` filed this at *fifty five*; it has doubled since, which is what says guidance did not hold it.

## Why a gate and not a checklist

`basicly-lc2bd3v.8` established the pattern one surface over: a requirement restated in four sessions and fixed site by site is a requirement no review is holding. The plan gate already checks acceptance criteria for a *decomposed child* - `plan_gate.missing_fields` tests `bool(acceptance)` - and a record created straight from the terminal never passes through it. That is the hole.

## The owner's chosen strength

Gate at dispatch, advise everywhere else. A record may be captured from a terminal in one line; that is how the owner builds the backlog and it must stay cheap. It may not *enter BUILD* without something a test can be written from.

## What is checkable and what is judgement

Checkable, so it gates: **Testable** - an acceptance section with at least one criterion; **Valuable** - a context naming who wants it and why; **Small** - a token budget; **Independent** - dependencies declared or explicitly none. Judgement, so it advises only: **Negotiable** and **Estimable**.

Jeffries' three Cs map onto sections the format already has. Card is the title, Conversation is Context, Confirmation is Acceptance Criteria. A record missing Confirmation is the population measured above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a record is dispatched to BUILD, THE ENGINE SHALL refuse it where it carries no acceptance criteria, and the refusal SHALL name the missing section rather than reporting the record invalid.
- WHERE a record is created or updated outside dispatch, THE ENGINE SHALL record the same finding as advisory and SHALL NOT refuse the write.
- A REPORT SHALL name every active record failing a checkable INVEST condition, grouped by condition, so the 108 are a worked backlog rather than a number.
- THE REPORT SHALL run a positive control, so a zero distinguishes an empty population from a probe that found nothing.
- THE JUDGEMENT CONDITIONS, negotiable and estimable, SHALL NOT gate, and the report SHALL say so where it names them.
- A TEST SHALL drive a record with no criteria at dispatch and assert the refusal names the missing section.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/plan_entry.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `.scripts/check_record_invest.py`
- `tests/test_record_invest.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `110000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: run the report and read the 108 by name, then dispatch a record with no criteria and read the refusal

- WHEN the board is served and no viewport is declared, THE PAGE SHALL fit the reader's viewport at 1440x900, 1600x1000 and 1920x1080.

Owner priority: they read a record page mid-session and could see no description and no acceptance criteria, and said so - "how should i then use this to drive test-driven development ... I as human, if that was my backlog i wouldnt even know where to start."

Both defects fixed.

Titles beside ids. The parent line and the three link lists went through one `named()` macro, so four sites cannot become four spellings of the rule. The context carries the titles map the wall already builds from `units[]` - no new data.

The description. Rendered as markdown by `board_render.markdown`, a Jinja filter using markdown-it-py with `html=False`. That flag is the security boundary and not a formatting choice: every other producer string on the page is autoescaped, so a renderer that passed embedded markup through would be the one hole in that. A test asserts `<script>` in a body reaches the page escaped.

The data path. `board_bodies.bodies()` folds the ledger once and returns 1249 descriptions keyed by id. Not a snapshot section: 304 bodies is a document nobody can serve, which is this epic's argument, and it holds for every body at once and not for one. `harness-board/v1` is unchanged. `board_snapshot` was the first home and crossed the 4000-token cap, so the read moved to its own module along a nameable responsibility rather than taking a waiver.

Measured. `basicly board --out` writes 307 record pages in 3.2s total - one fold, not 307, asserted through the seam rather than by timing. The epic `basicly-k6tpep` renders six body headings and names all fourteen children by title. `check_render_overflow` reports nothing clipped and nothing overlapped.

Four gates fired on the new module and each was fixed rather than waived: `module-size` on `board_snapshot` and on `test_board_record_page` (both split), `comment-density` on the new module (docstring cut to the two facts the code cannot state), `test-naming` (a test file named after it), `noqa-debt` (the first S704 in this tree, declared in `basicly.d/` with its reason), and `docs-claims` (the layering block regenerated for the new tier).

One thing found and not fixed here: `.scripts/check_test_naming.py` cites `§9.4` three times and no document in this tree defines it. I stated the rule in words in my own line rather than carry an unresolvable pointer. Worth a record.

payload.value:
## Context

When a record reaches BUILD carrying nothing a test can be written from, the lane has to invent the requirement it is verifying against, so I want the engine to refuse that dispatch and to name every record already in that state, so I can drive the backlog test-first instead of guessing what each record meant.

Owner, 2026-09-07, after reading a record page that showed a title and no body: *"how should i then use this to drive test-driven development to write tests first and make them pass later? ... I as human, if that was my backlog i wouldnt even know where to start."* And the standard: *"you can follow the INVEST criteria and benchmark against them every time you write a record (story, task). Also Jeffries C3 for writing stories can also help."*

Owner, 2026-09-08, refining the Valuable condition: *"because valuable entails a persona that wants it, which sometimes we do not have, instead of using the user story voice, use job story voice ... one should never force a persona in the story that does not need it or have it. for example a story about patching the system may be causes by a situation, which is publishing of vulnerabilities, and does not involve a person."*

The owner asks for two separable things, and the engine holds one of them:

| the owner asks for | the phase that reads it | enforced before this record |
| --- | --- | --- |
| acceptance criteria, to verify against and write tests from | VERIFY | yes, `policy.definition_of_ready` |
| a requirement, to validate against | VALIDATE | no section holds one |

## Corrected measurement

The first filing of this record claimed **108** records carry nothing to verify against. That figure is wrong and this record supersedes it. It counted the `## Acceptance Criteria` body heading by substring and ignored the structured `acceptance_criteria` field, which `policy._has_acceptance_criteria` documents as an equally valid carrier. 82 active records carry their criteria in that field alone and were all counted as missing. The fault is the one `basicly-lc2bd3v.8` also turned on: a filter on one carrier hides a population.

Re-derived 2026-09-08 over `tracker.all_records`, with the carriers read by the engine's own `plan_record.section_entries` and the field test from `policy._has_acceptance_criteria`:

| carrier | active records |
| --- | --- |
| body section only | 151 |
| structured field only | 82 |
| both | 37 |
| **neither** | **36** |
| total active | 306 |

Two further defects the count exposed:

- **6 records carry the heading and zero parsed criteria**, so a bare heading clears the gate having stated nothing: `basicly-c0k6a4`, `basicly-cs5k8y`, `basicly-jr0l.56`, `basicly-u2hl.60`, `basicly-u2hl.61`, `basicly-vkh0.42.12`. `plan_record` already documents this lenient edge in prose; it is live in the tracker.
- **The 36 are concentrated, not 36 authoring lapses.** `basicly-a4q3` contributes 10 and `basicly-u2hl` 7, so 17 of 36 come from two decomposes that emitted children with no criteria. A gate at dispatch alone would refuse them one at a time; the report is what makes them a worked backlog.

## What is already built, and what is not

Established by reading the code on 2026-09-08, with a positive control run before any zero was believed (`basicly-0bj8q1` reads `ready=True`, `basicly-0u7uns` reads `ready=False, missing=('## Steps to Reproduce', '## Acceptance Criteria')`):

| the first filing's criterion | state |
| --- | --- |
| refuse a dispatch to BUILD with no acceptance criteria, naming the section | **already built** — `policy.definition_of_ready` requires them of every type, and `loop._on_classify` runs it before `_start_build_leaf` |
| record the same finding as advisory outside dispatch | not built — no DoR call on the record-write path |
| a report naming every record failing a checkable condition | not built — `basicly policy dor` takes one id and has no sweep |
| the report runs a positive control | not built |
| negotiable and estimable never gate | holds, because nothing gates them |

So the refusal is not the work. The work is the requirement carrier, the two parsing defects, and the report.

## The Valuable condition, in the owner's voice rule

Bill Wake's original INVEST defines Valuable as *"it needs to be valuable to the customer"*. It requires no persona and no named role. The first filing of this record glossed Valuable as *"a context naming who wants it and why"*, which is stricter than INVEST and is the over-specification the owner's 2026-09-08 instruction removes.

Valuable is therefore satisfied by a stated **trigger**, in either voice:

| voice | shape | triggered by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| job story | `When <situation>, I want to <motivation>, so I can <outcome>.` | a situation |
| user story | `As a <persona>, I want <goal>, so that <benefit>.` | a persona |

A record may carry both. Mike Cohn: *"The two techniques are quite compatible and there's no reason to view them as mutually exclusive."* A record must never be refused for omitting a persona, and a checker must not pattern-match the persona shape alone, because that teaches an author to prepend a fabricated `As a developer` to a story that has no person in it. Cohn names that failure directly: *"When a large set of user stories all begin with 'As a user...' you've got a set of stories for whom the user is not very important."* The patching case the owner gives is the test: the trigger is the publication of a vulnerability and no person appears.

Jeffries' three Cs map onto the sections: Card is the title, Conversation is the trigger, Confirmation is the acceptance criteria.

Sources, verified 2026-09-08: Wake, *INVEST in Good Stories, and SMART Tasks* (xp123.com); Cohn, *Job Stories: A Viable Alternative to User Stories* (mountaingoatsoftware.com); Klement, *Replacing The User Story With The Job Story* — not readable, HTTP 403, so his position against coexistence is recorded from secondary description only. That disagreement does not reach the gate, because a checker accepting either voice satisfies both authors.

## What gates and what advises

The owner's chosen strength: gate at dispatch, advise everywhere else. A record must stay capturable from a terminal in one line, because that is how the backlog is built. It may not enter BUILD without a trigger and a criterion.

| condition | checkable as | gate or advice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Testable | at least one criterion that parses, in either carrier | gate at dispatch |
| Valuable | a trigger section holding either voice's shape | gate at dispatch |
| Small | a token budget | gate at dispatch |
| Independent | dependencies declared, or explicitly none | gate at dispatch |
| a generic persona carrying nothing | the `As a user` string | advice only |
| the situation is a real situation | judgement | advice only |
| Negotiable, Estimable | judgement | advice only, and the report says so |

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a record is dispatched to BUILD, THE ENGINE SHALL refuse it where it carries no trigger, and the refusal SHALL name the trigger section and print both accepted voices so an author picks one rather than defaulting to the persona.
- THE ENGINE SHALL accept a job story trigger with no persona anywhere in the record, and SHALL NOT refuse a record for omitting a persona.

[decision 2026-09-08] The trigger gate applies to EVERY work type, with no exemption.

Owner, asked whether to exempt bug and chore: *"i said apply to all issue types, becaue if we only apply to so called value bearing ones, there is a danger that agents will crate the ones that do not need it just to quicker pass the gate"*

The exemption I had recommended keyed on `issue_type`, and `issue_type` is chosen by the same agent the gate is meant to bind. So the exemption is an escape hatch the gated party controls: an agent facing a trigger it cannot write reclassifies the record as a `chore` and the gate lets it through. The cost of the wider gate is real and measured - 305 of 306 active records carry no trigger in either voice and each needs one written before it can build - but a gate with a self-declared exemption measures nothing at all.

The general rule this is an instance of: never key a gate's exemption on a field the gated party writes. It is the same fault as binding a ratchet on a marker whose absence is ambiguous.

Rejected alternatives, both measured before the choice:
- exempt bug and chore, gating feature/task/epic only: 208 records in scope, 97 exempt. Refused for the reason above.
- gate the section heading and advise the shape: 83 records refused instead of 305. Refused because 223 records already carry a Context heading filled with prose, which is the state that opened this record.

## Trigger

When the dispatch gate refuses a record the board has just offered me a start control for, I want the board to tell me which records can actually be built and what each of the others still owes, so I can write the missing trigger on the record I am about to work instead of discovering the refusal one record at a time.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run on `b94ceff9`, the commit that added the trigger gate:

```
uv run basicly tracker ready | grep -c 'basicly-'
```

Observed: **245** records offered as ready. Then fold the same 245 ids through the gate that now governs a dispatch:

```
uv run python -c "from pathlib import Path; from basicly import tracker, invest; ..."
```

Observed: **1** of the 245 can enter BUILD - `basicly-q1ve1fn`. The other 244 are refused for a missing `## Trigger`. A positive control ran first: the one record known to satisfy the gate is present in the passing set, so the 1 is a measurement and not an empty probe.

Expected: the cockpit reports a number an operator can act on. A start control drawn on a record the gate will refuse is a control that cannot work.

## Cause

`board_record.startable` reads `unit["ready"]`, which is the tracker's dependency walk and says nothing about the Definition of Ready. `basicly-q1ve1fn` made the DoR strictly stronger without teaching the ready signal about it, so the two disagree by a factor of 245. This is the same class of fault as a board fact keyed on the supervisor lock: the label says one thing and the field means another.

## What must not happen

`board_sections.units` sits below `invest` in the layer contract and must stay there, so it cannot compute this verdict. It receives it, exactly as `phase` and `ready` already arrive from `phases` and `ready` and from nowhere else. And only the missing section *names* may cross the wire - a description on a unit row is the 132.5x regression that module exists to prevent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the snapshot producer emits a unit row, THE PRODUCER SHALL record what that record owes the Definition of Ready as a bounded list of section names, and SHALL NOT put any record body on the wire.
- THE UNITS BUILDER SHALL receive the verdict as a parameter and SHALL NOT derive it, so the layer contract holds and an absent verdict renders as absent rather than as satisfied.
- WHERE a record owes any required section, THE BOARD SHALL NOT draw a start control for it.
- THE READY LISTING SHALL keep its existing rank order and SHALL name, on each row it cannot start, the section that record owes.
- THE BOARD SHALL report the count that can actually be dispatched alongside the count the dependency walk calls ready, so the two numbers are never presented as one.
- A TEST SHALL assert a record that satisfies every dependency but owes a trigger is not startable.
- A TEST SHALL assert a unit row carries the owed section names and carries no description or acceptance body.
- A TEST SHALL assert an absent verdict leaves the row unmarked rather than startable, so a producer that could not compute it fails closed.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_snapshot.py`
- `src/basicly/board_sections.py`
- `src/basicly/board_record.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_backlog.py`
- `.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json`
- `tests/test_board_sections.py`
- `tests/test_board_record_page.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: serve the board, read the ready region, and confirm it names one startable record and the owed section on the rest, then check that no start control is drawn on a refused row

## Trigger

When a lane is claimed or anything is parked, I want the wall to still show me what to work on next, so I can pick the next record without leaving the cockpit for the terminal.

## Steps to Reproduce

Render the wall at the size the owner reads it and look at the region, rather than at a test:

```
uv run basicly board --out wall.html --width 1440 --height 900
```

Observed in the screenshot: `NEXT UP - +246 MORE READY` heads a large empty box. Zero rows are drawn. The parked strip and one claimed row are both present below it.

Driven directly against the real snapshot, the mechanism is the `reserved` argument:

| reserved px | rows drawn | the header still claims |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 3 | +243 more ready |
| 200 | 0 | +246 more ready |
| 400 | 0 | +246 more ready |
| 600 | 0 | +246 more ready |

`board_render` passes `acts_reserve + claimed_reserve + parked_reserve + QUEUE_PX`, so any claimed row or parked strip pushes reserved past 200 and the region empties.

Expected: the region draws at least one row whenever the set is non-empty, or it draws nothing and reserves nothing. A box that reserves height and states a count while showing no rows is the worst of the three.

## Cause

`next_up` takes `slots = fits if wide else min(READY_SLOTS, fits)` and then `slots = max(slots // 2, slots - len(set(names[:slots])))`. The floor protects against feature headings eating slots, but `max(0 // 2, ...)` is 0, so it cannot protect against `ready_capacity` returning 0. `ready_capacity(900, 1440, 0)` is 6 and every reserve above ~200px takes it to 0.

This is NOT caused by basicly-lc2bd3v.9, which changed only that region's `note` line - `git diff` over `board_regions.py` for that record touches nothing else. It is the other half of basicly-zj36jf0, which measured the same region overflowing its viewport by 152px.

## Why no test caught it

5465 tests pass on the commit that renders this. Every one of them asserts a count, a note or a row shape against a fixture whose reserve is 0. Nothing renders the wall at a stated size with a claimed lane present and asserts that the region a reader looks at has rows in it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHERE the ready set is non-empty, THE READY REGION SHALL draw at least one row whatever the reserved height, so a reader is never shown a count with no rows.
- WHERE the region can draw no row at all, IT SHALL reserve no height and SHALL say that the wall is too short, rather than drawing an empty box.
- THE HEADER COUNT SHALL agree with the rows drawn: a region showing N rows of M ready SHALL NOT report M as more-than-drawn when it drew none.
- A TEST SHALL render the wall at 1440x900 with a claimed lane and a parked strip present, and assert the ready region contains at least one record id.
- A TEST SHALL drive `next_up` across the reserve range 0 to 600 px and assert the row count never reaches zero while the ready set is non-empty.
- THE REGION SHALL keep the viewport bound it already honours, so closing this SHALL NOT reopen the 152px overflow basicly-zj36jf0 measures.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_render.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions_flight.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `90000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: render the wall at 1440x900 with a lane claimed, screenshot it, and read rows in the NEXT UP region

When the board's own stylesheet has to reimplement a control that a maintained component library already ships, I want those components vendored locally and no network call at page runtime, so I can spend the layout work on what the cockpit shows rather than on how a button looks.

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-07, reading the served board: *"even you mentioned onboarding bootstrap icons and components, i still see a few icons only, and the buttons and components do not look like bootstrap and do not behave like bootstrap."*

And the constraint, in their words: *"you can vendor the bootstrap css, and update the style (css classes) to match our design. i think that bootstrap css can be onboarded using npm as a node package (no CDN, or any internet access for the page to run is allowed)."*

`basicly-e1c4pct` vendored bootstrap **icons** MIT with provenance. Nothing vendored the framework, so every control on the board is hand-rolled CSS: a submit button is a bare `<button>` styled to look like text, and the cards, tables and strips share no component vocabulary.

Taken from the served board at 127.0.0.1:8787 on 2026-09-07.

| what a bootstrap page has | what the board has |
| --- | --- |
| `.btn` with size, variant, focus ring and disabled state | a `<button>` with `background: none` and a hover border |
| `.card` with header, body and consistent radius | four different hand-tuned box treatments across regions |

## Trigger

When five sessions work this repository at once and nothing outside the supervisor lock records which session holds what, I want the cockpit to name the holder of each lane, so I can tell my own work from another session's before I touch a branch.

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-06: *"think about what will be shown on the cockpit if multiple sessions and agents are working on the same repo in parallel, using same branch and worktrees? One of the use cases I encounter in projects is that 4-5 terminals, each with an open session, are working on the same repository."*

Nothing in the board is designed for this. It is the case the cockpit exists for - the owner's own reason for wanting one is *"when multiple parallel sessions and work is being done, it gets buried"* - and it is the one case no record covers.

## What the board can see today, and what it cannot

`basicly-kqh9dj8` shipped this session and answers **one** question: which records have a worktree, and what git says about each. Measured against the owner's case, that is a third of it.

| the question a fifth terminal arrives with | answerable today |
| --- | --- |
| what worktrees exist and what state is each in | **yes** - `board_unsupervised.lanes` |
| which *session* holds which worktree | no - no session identity is recorded outside a supervisor lock |
| is anybody editing the base checkout right now | no |
| what did the other four sessions just do | partly - the events ticker, unattributed |
| am I about to collide with one of them | no - the contention graph exists and nothing consults it (`basicly-zq9i2m.3`) |
| may I start work on record X | no - `ready` says the tracker permits it, not that a peer is not already on it |

The last row is the sharp one. Two terminals can both read `ready`, both pick the top record, and both start. The tracker's claim is written at provisioning, so the window is small but real, and the loser finds out at the merge queue.

## What identity already exists to build on

* `supervise.read_holder` writes a lock with a `session_id` and a heartbeat - but only a supervisor takes it, which is `basicly-k6tpep.5`'s finding: three capabilities are gated on that lock and a `loop run` operator takes none.
* Every worktree has a name, a branch and a git state, which needs no cooperation from the session that made it.
* The ledger records who claimed a record and when, and it is shared across worktrees by the `redirect` file - so the ledger is the one place all five sessions already meet.

So the honest design direction is **the ledger and the filesystem, not a session registry**: anything requiring five terminals to register themselves will be wrong the moment one crashes, and a heartbeat nobody writes is the stale-lock defect this session already found feeding the header for a whole day.

## What must be decided before building

**Is a session a first-class thing the ledger records, or is it inferred?** Recording it means a new event kind, a heartbeat, and a liveness rule - and a crashed terminal then lies until its heartbeat expires. Inferring it from worktrees and ledger writes means the board can never name a session that has not touched anything, but it also cannot be wrong about one.

Prefer inference until a question is found that inference cannot answer. State the question if one is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN more than one session is working a repository, THE COCKPIT SHALL name each unit of work in flight and which worktree holds it, without requiring any session to register itself.
- WHERE the base checkout is dirty, THE COCKPIT SHALL say so, because a landing refuses on it and the operator who caused it may be at a different terminal.
- WHEN a reader considers starting a record, THE COCKPIT SHALL say whether a peer already holds it, and SHALL distinguish "the tracker permits this" from "nobody else is on it".
- WHERE two units in flight declare overlapping scope, THE COCKPIT SHALL name the overlap before the merge queue does.
- THE COCKPIT SHALL NOT claim a session is alive on the strength of a marker nobody is refreshing: a stale lock fed the header a false run line for a full day on 2026-09-06.
- A TEST SHALL drive two concurrent units against one repository and assert both are named with their holders.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_unsupervised.py`
- `src/basicly/board_sessions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json`
- `tests/test_board_sessions.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/checkout.py`
- `tests/test_board_sessions.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `110000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: run two sessions against one checkout, each holding a different record, and read both named with their worktrees on one cockpit.

## Trigger

When the ready set is ordered by a computed score I cannot override, I want a stored rank the scheduler reads before it falls back to the computation, so I can put the record I judge most important at the top and have it stay there.

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-06, on what a backlog surface must do beyond listing:

> *"get inspired by jira, linear, clickup, asana, youtrack... we need a better dependency visualization system than those tools provide. then I could open a backlog and prioritize it, and during prioritization the dependencies would always be considered, so constraints would be set in place. Example: if moving an item from 5th position to the 1st, and that item has an item dependent on item on 4th position, that means that 4th item must be done before 5th and the 5th cannot be placed before it. The system would in this case visualize what items are connected and in which order when one is selected, and will prohibit sorting the backlog in a way that breaks dependencies."*

And the framing: *"adapt these concepts to the agentic-first development, which also humans, if visualized correctly, used."*

## The design question this forces, which must be answered before any code

**This repository has no rank field.** `basicly tracker ready` reports a rank, and it is *computed*, not stored:

```
$ uv run basicly tracker ready --limit 3 --json
{"rank": 1, "record": "basicly-94bk",   "score": 3001, ...}
{"rank": 2, "record": "basicly-a3yi",   "score": 3001, ...}
{"rank": 3, "record": "basicly-g5ce75", "score": 3001, ...}
```

`scheduler.ranking()` derives the order from priority, dependent count and id, and `Ranking` carries the sort policy beside the rows *"because a rank recorded without its policy is uninterpretable later"*. Three records tie at 3001 today, so the visible order between them is the tiebreak, not a judgment anybody made.

So a drag to position 1 has nowhere to land. Two honest routes, and this is the decision to take first:

**(a) The drag writes `priority`.** No new state. The engine already reads priority and every consumer inherits the change. But priority is coarse - five buckets, 480 records at P1 - so a drag inside a bucket changes nothing and the item springs back. Honest, and visibly weak.

**(b) The ledger gains a stored rank the scheduler reads ahead of its computed score.** A drag means something exact. It costs a new field, a new event kind, a migration for 1,253 records, and it puts a human's ordering above the engine's - which is either the point or the danger, depending on the owner's answer.

**Do not build until this is chosen.** A drag that appears to work and is silently ignored by the dispatcher is worse than no drag, and it is the exact failure `basicly-fiow1sr` already shipped once: an argv that looked right and started nothing.

## What the research already settled, and nobody has used

Two closed spikes from 2026-09-04 are the reading for this, and both are unactioned:

* `basicly-hnnmk9.6` - dependency-ordered scheduling in established practice. Its load-bearing finding is that **this repo orders lanes on write-scope overlap, not on consumed results** (`decompose.serializes`, an anti/output dependence model), while declared `depends_on` edges are carried separately. So there are *two* orderings, and a backlog that honours only the declared graph will let a human order two items that collide at the merge.
* `basicly-hnnmk9.9` - an inventory of the nine graphs this repository maintains, including the record dependency graph and the file contention graph, and where they do and do not compose.

The owner's constraint rule is a topological one, and the spike names its literature: Kahn 1962, CPM, and GNU make's *order-only prerequisite* - an edge that imposes ordering without implying data flow, which is precisely the shape of a contention edge.

## What the named tools do, and where each stops

| tool | ordering | dependency handling | where it stops for us |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Jira | stored `Rank` (LexoRank), drag writes it | blocks/is-blocked-by shown as a badge; ordering is not constrained | a human may rank a blocked item first and nothing objects |
| Linear | stored sort key, drag writes it | blocking relations, and a blocked item is marked | same: the warning is advisory |
| ClickUp / Asana | manual order per list | dependencies with optional date shifting | shifts dates, does not refuse an order |
| YouTrack | saved queries and sort | issue links, `depends on` | sort is a query, not a constraint |

**None of them refuses a reorder.** They warn. The owner is asking for refusal, which is the thing that is actually new here - and it is only defensible because our graph is machine-consumed: an order a dispatcher will really execute is worth constraining, where a human backlog order is advisory anyway.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an operator selects a record in the backlog, THE PAGE SHALL draw that record's dependency neighbourhood - what it waits on, what waits on it, and the order those imply - and SHALL distinguish a declared `blocks` edge from a contention edge derived from overlapping scope.
- WHEN an operator moves a record above one it depends on, THE PAGE SHALL refuse the move and SHALL name the chain that forbids it, rather than accepting it with a warning.
- WHERE a move is legal, THE PAGE SHALL apply it through an argv handed to the installed CLI, and the resulting order SHALL be the order `basicly tracker ready` then reports - or the move SHALL be refused as unrepresentable.
- THE PAGE SHALL NOT invent an ordering the engine does not read: a drag whose effect the dispatcher ignores is a lie the operator will act on.
- WHERE two records are unordered by any edge, THE PAGE SHALL say they are unordered rather than implying the list position is a decision.
- A TEST SHALL attempt a dependency-violating move against a fixture and assert it is refused, naming the chain, with a control asserting a legal move is applied.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_backlog.py`
- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_graph.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_backlog.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_backlog.py`
- `tests/test_board_actions.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_backlog.py`
- `src/basicly/board_graph.py`
- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `tests/test_board_backlog.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: `basicly-lc2bd3v.4`
- demonstration: open the backlog, select a record and read its neighbourhood, then attempt to move a dependent above its blocker and read the refusal naming the chain.

## Trigger

When I read a ranked list on the board and disagree with a record's priority, I want to change it from that row, so I can correct the order without leaving the page for a terminal.

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-06, listing the cockpit actions an enterprise board must carry: *"parking, prioritizing, changing scope"*.

Measured 2026-09-06 against `board_actions.ACTIONS`, which is the closed table of everything the board can run: it holds `loop-answer`, `checkpoint-approve`, `record-park`, `record-resume` and `lane-kill`. Parking and resuming already answer *descope* and *scope*. **Nothing changes a priority.**

That leaves the ranked lists the board draws - `NEXT UP`, `THE QUEUE`, the ready set - read-only. An operator who can see that the wrong thing is ranked first must leave the board to move it, which is the exact loss the cockpit exists to stop.

## The verb already exists

`basicly tracker write -- update <id> -p <n>` is the priority write, and it is the same shape the existing park and resume actions use - an argv handed to the installed CLI, never a tracker read. So `consumer-reads-only-the-snapshot` is unaffected.

## No confirm code, and the reason

The rule `record-park` states: a checkpoint carries a code because it is the human gate the anti-autopilot rule protects. A priority spends nothing, starts nothing, and is undone by setting it back. It is the same class as park, so it takes no code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an operator submits a priority for a record, THE BOARD SHALL run `basicly tracker write -- update <id> -p <n>` through the installed CLI and show that command's own exit status and output.
- WHERE the board draws a record in a ranked list, IT SHALL offer the priority change on that record's own row, not only where an ask prefills it.
- THE ACTION SHALL refuse a value the tracker will refuse, before the subprocess runs, and say which values are allowed.
- THE PRINTED COMMAND SHALL be built through the action's own `build`, so the line a reader copies cannot diverge from the argv the button runs.
- A TEST SHALL assert the argv reaches the CLI and changes the record, not that the argv has the right shape - the shape-only test is why `basicly-fiow1sr` shipped an argv that started nothing.

## Scope

## Trigger

When the board prints a command to show me what is waiting and that command reports one of the three records actually waiting, I want the printed command to cover the whole waiting set, so I can trust what the cockpit tells me to run.

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-06, reading the board's alarm band: *"i have no idea what these 3 waiting on the person want from me"*.

The band was drawing `1 HOUR - 3 WAITING ON A PERSON`, one record's name, an engine sentence, and `+2 more waiting`. Everything a person needed to act was either absent, truncated, or wrong.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Land three records so each sits at `verify` with its ship checkpoint unapproved.
2. `uv run basicly board --out /tmp/board.html` and read the band.

Observed: one ask named, two hidden behind a count, the offered command cut off as `do:...`, and the question reading `verify is cleared and nothing is scheduled to advance it`.

## The five defects, in the order they cost a person time

**1. The offered command does not do the job.** Each ask carries `actions[].offer = "basicly loop advance <id>"`. Run against a merged record it prints:

```
[blocked] verify -> verify: ship checkpoint awaiting human approval
```

What actually ships it is `basicly loop run <id> --root <epic-with-a-grant>`, which the board never mentions. **This is the serious one**: an operator surface that prints a command which stops one step short teaches the operator that the board is wrong, and the other four defects are cosmetic beside it.

**2. Only one ask of three is named.** The other two exist only as `+2 more waiting`. A person cannot act on a count.

**3. The offer is truncated.** The band has the exact argv and cuts it at the right edge.

**4. The question is written for the engine.** `verify is cleared and nothing is scheduled to advance it` describes a scheduler state. A person needs the consequence: this merged, advancing it closes the record and tears the worktree down.

**5. There is no advance action.** `board_actions.ACTIONS` holds `loop-answer`, `checkpoint-approve`, `record-park`, `record-resume` and `lane-kill`. `advance` is the most common thing waiting on a human on this board and it is not offered.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHERE an ask carries an `offer`, THE BOARD SHALL print a command that reaches the state the ask is waiting for, verified by running it, and SHALL NOT print one that stops at an unapproved checkpoint.
- WHEN more than one ask is pending, THE BOARD SHALL name every waiting record and its own command, rather than naming one and counting the rest.
- THE OFFERED COMMAND SHALL be rendered without truncation, wrapping instead of clipping where the column is narrow.
- THE ASK SHALL state the consequence of acting in a person's terms alongside the engine's own wording, never instead of it.
- WHERE an ask's kind is `advance`, THE BOARD SHALL offer it as an action on that ask's row, through an argv handed to the installed CLI like every other action.
- A TEST SHALL run each offered argv against a fixture at the state the ask describes and assert it reaches the next state, so an offer that stops short fails rather than renders.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_advance.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_actions.py`
- `tests/test_board_advance.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_advance.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_advance.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `80000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: leave three records waiting at ship, read the board, and run each command it prints - each reaches ship without a second command the board did not name.

## Trigger

When two agents work this repository in parallel and both append an event to the ledger, git reports a content conflict in `events-0001.jsonl` and one of them must hand-resolve a 9.5 MB file, so I want the append to merge cleanly on its own, so I can run lanes in parallel without a human arbitrating the log.

## Steps to Reproduce

Reproduced 2026-09-08 in a throwaway repository carrying this repo's own `.gitattributes` rule, with a positive control run immediately after.

```
printf 'events-*.jsonl -text\n' > .gitattributes
# base commit holds one event; branch agent-a appends one; branch agent-b appends one
git merge agent-b
```

Observed, exit 1:

```
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in events-0001.jsonl
{"id":"e1"}
<<<<<<< HEAD
{"id":"a1"}
=======
{"id":"b1"}
>>>>>>> agent-b
```

The control, the identical history with one word added to the rule:

```
printf 'events-*.jsonl -text merge=union\n' > .gitattributes
git merge agent-b     # exit 0, "Merge made by the 'ort' strategy"
{"id":"e1"}
{"id":"a1"}
{"id":"b1"}
```

So the conflict is the missing attribute and not the append. The control is what makes the first result a finding rather than a guess.

## Why this is the kit's central promise

The tracker kit is the part of basicly that a repository will install standalone, to replace a tracker whose records are edited in place and therefore conflict whenever two people touch the backlog. Append-only is the design that earns that, and it is already built: event ids are content-derived, `events` documents idempotency by event id as the answer to "union-merge duplication", `fsck` treats a repeated id as ordinary because "a union merge duplicates a hunk and the fold keeps one", and `provenance` states that a union merge's arbitrary concatenation folds to the same edges.

Every one of those five call sites is written for a union merge that git is never told to perform. The design is done; the one-word declaration that arms it is missing.

## What must not regress

`-text` must stay, and stay below the `*` rule. Event ids are content-derived, so a byte git rewrote on the way through the index changes an id and every later id with it (basicly-vkh0.21). `merge=union` is added beside it, never in place of it. Union must not reach `snapshot.jsonl` or any `checkpoint-*.jsonl`: those are rewritten rather than appended, and concatenating two of them yields a corrupt checkpoint. Only `events-*.jsonl` is tracked today, and the glob must stay that narrow.

## Acceptance Criteria

- THE REPOSITORY SHALL declare a union merge for the event-log glob and SHALL keep the existing `-text` attribute on it.
- THE UNION DECLARATION SHALL NOT apply to `snapshot.jsonl` or to any `checkpoint-*.jsonl`, because those are rewritten and a concatenation of two is corrupt.
- WHEN two branches each append events and are merged, THE MERGE SHALL succeed with no conflict and the result SHALL hold every event from both.
- THE FOLD OVER a union-merged log SHALL yield the same records whichever branch merged first, so the order git happens to concatenate in is not a fact about the backlog.
- THE KIT DEPLOYMENT CHECK SHALL fail where the union attribute is absent, exactly as it already fails where `-text` is absent, so the requirement cannot be lost by editing one file.
- A TEST SHALL drive the two-branch append merge end to end and assert both events survive, with a control asserting the same history conflicts when the attribute is removed.
- THE KIT SHALL install this attribute into a consumer repository that does not use basicly, since a standalone install is the case this promise is made to.

## Scope

- `.gitattributes`
- `.scripts/kit_deployment.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`
- `tests/test_kit_deployment.py`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `130000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: build two branches that each append an event, merge them, and read every event present in the fold afterwards; then remove the attribute and watch the same merge conflict

## Trigger

When I read the board and an inner component sits flush against the box that contains it, I want every component to take its spacing from one scale, so I can read a region as a group of things instead of as one run-together block.

## Steps to Reproduce

Owner, 2026-09-08, reading the served wall: *"there is not margins or padding, so in some components right now on the board the inner component is glued to the outer component as there is no space between them -> one of many design issues for which we already may have stories."*

Counted over the wall template on 2026-09-08:

| template | padding | margin | gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `board_page.html.j2` | 16 | 21 | 29 |
| `board_record.html.j2` | 10 | 9 | 1 |
| `board_kanban.html.j2` | 6 | 4 | 6 |
| `board_backlog.html.j2` | 4 | 5 | 2 |

The wall's 16 padding declarations carry **12 distinct values**, none of them from a scale:

```
9px 12px 10px · 8px · 7px 0 1px · 5px 9px 7px · 5px 10px · 3px 12px
3px 0 · 2px 9px · 2px 5px · 1px 4px · 1px 0 1px 7px · 1px 0
```

Expected: a spacing value on the board is a step on one scale, so a component nested in another cannot end up with none.

## Cause

Every spacing value is decided at the site that needs it, and a site that nobody looked at got zero. Twelve independent decisions is not a design; it is twelve. Nothing fails when a thirteenth is added, and nothing fails when one is omitted.

## Relation to the bootstrap record

This is the defect that argues for basicly-lywzp71 rather than a competing approach to it. Bootstrap ships a spacing scale and utility classes, so closing this by applying that scale is one job with lywzp71's vendoring, while closing it by hand-tuning twelve values into thirteen is the state that produced the observation. Read lywzp71 before starting here, and prefer closing both together.

## Acceptance Criteria

- THE BOARD SHALL take every padding, margin and gap value from one declared scale, and a value outside that scale SHALL NOT appear in a template.
- WHERE a component is nested inside another, THE INNER COMPONENT SHALL carry a non-zero inset from its container on every side that has a visible border.
- A GATE SHALL fail naming any board template that declares a spacing value the scale does not contain, so a thirteenth ad hoc value cannot land silently.
- THE SCALE SHALL be stated in one place that the templates read, so changing a step is one edit rather than sixteen.
- A SCREENSHOT at 1440x900 SHALL be taken and read before this is closed, because the counted declarations are the symptom and the rendered gap is the requirement.
- CLOSING THIS SHALL NOT reopen basicly-zj36jf0 or basicly-lc2bd3v.10: added inset costs height, and both of those are regions already short of it.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_record.html.j2`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_kanban.html.j2`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_backlog.html.j2`
- `.scripts/check_board_spacing.py`
- `tests/test_check_board_spacing.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `110000`
- depends on: `basicly-lywzp71`
- demonstration: render the wall at 1440x900, screenshot it, and read the inset on a nested component that has none today
