[session handover 2026-09-18] The tracker ledger shards per writer, and the forge claim behind it is measured rather than argued.

STATE: main clean, five records closed (basicly-v5zvsh1 sharding, basicly-62gd7je the landing wiring, basicly-zsq6xkz the retro and the shard-blind readers). uv run basicly verify --mode full PASS. uv run pytest -q -n 4 5816 passed 1 xfailed.

## Trigger

When a team on an existing tracker installs this kit into a repository that already holds a backlog, I want one command that imports their export, so I can move across without retyping every record and without the published README promising something that does not exist.

packages/basicly-tracker/README.md line 22 states 'It also imports a beads JSONL export, so a repository can move its backlog across without retyping it.' That is false. The installer never touches migrate: a grep for migrate, import_, beads and issues.jsonl across kit_installer.py and the package entry point returns nothing, against a positive control that migrate.py holds 12 functions and is real code. migrate.py has no main, no argparse and no CLI verb, so the capability exists and is unreachable for the consumer it was written for.

This is the same defect class as basicly-zsq6xkz, one layer out. That retro gated a design document sentence naming a call the code does not make, and left a README sentence naming a capability the code does not expose.

The engine wrapper src/basicly/tracker_import.py adds rendering and a dry run, not safety - every refusal comes from migrate itself and is already in ImportReport.rejected. So exposing the kit verb loses no guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A standalone consumer with no basicly runs one kit command to import an export and sees what was imported, what diverged and what was refused.
- A dry run reports the same numbers by the same code path and writes nothing, rather than approximating them.
- The README says only what the shipped command does, checked by running it.
- A test imports an export into a fresh ledger through the consumer surface, with a dry run first that leaves the ledger byte-identical as the control.
payload.title: expose the ledger import so a repository leaving beads can actually onboard

payload.description:
## Trigger

When an agent picks up a record in a repository that installed only the tracker kit, I want the record itself to carry acceptance criteria and requirements as typed fields with a gate that refuses unshaped work, so I can verify and validate against the record rather than against my reading of its prose.

Measured 2026-09-18 over this ledger's 1367 created events: 0 carry a requirements field and 28 carry a ## Requirements heading in prose, against a positive control of 467 carrying an acceptance_criteria field and 782 carrying the ## Acceptance Criteria heading. So the zero is the data's and not the probe's. A grep for acceptance or requirement across .basicly/core/kit/tracker/*.py returns nothing: all the shaping lives in src/basicly/invest.py and src/basicly/plan_record.py, which a standalone consumer never receives.

The enforcement point is a definition-of-ready gate rather than a refusal at create. A record is shaped while it is being written, and an import carries records that were never shaped at all, so refusing the write would break the import that basicly-i98ooyo just shipped and would refuse 900 of this ledger's own 1367 records.

Making the ready set itself filter is deliberately NOT in scope and the reason is measured: 900 of 1367 records carry no acceptance field, so a filtering ready set would collapse this repository's own ready count from 274 and stall the engine loop. That becomes worth doing once the backlog is shaped, as its own record.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The kit computes what a record owes - a trigger in either story voice, acceptance criteria, and requirements - reading a typed field first and a prose heading second, so an existing record keeps working.
- create, child and update take --acceptance and --requirements as first-class flags and report what the record still owes.
- A dor verb exits non-zero and names what is missing, so a hook or a skill can gate work on it.
- A record carrying both fields passes the gate, against a control record carrying neither that fails it.

## Requirements

- No engine import: the kit reads its own committed data and takes everything else as an argument.
- Standard library only and no syntax newer than Python 3.9.
- Additive at every existing call site: no current caller of create, update or ready changes behaviour.
payload.title: give the kit the acceptance criteria and requirements an agent verifies against

payload.text:
Third requirement corrected during the build, with the reason. It read 'Additive at every existing call site: no current caller of create, update or ready changes behaviour.' That is not what shipped and stating it unchanged would have been the false claim the last retro added a rule about.

What actually holds: every existing key keeps its meaning and no caller loses a capability, but the write reports gain two keys, owed and remedy. A consumer asserting exact dict equality on a write's JSON sees a change, and this repository's own test_a_swallowed_write_is_reported_not_raised did. Its original assertion is kept as a subset comparison and the new fact is asserted beside it. ready is untouched.

A side effect the pin caught and I had not intended: the first _owed_of went through queries.folded, which is snapshot.load, so a create published the derived snapshot as well as appending. test_the_consumer_writes_only_inside_its_own_directory failed on a stray ledger/snapshot.jsonl. It now folds the events in memory and publishes nothing, which is also the cheaper read.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a human on a team that installed only the tracker kit wants to know what is ready and what is holding the rest, I want one command to write a page they can open, so I can answer it without them reading JSON from a CLI.

SPEC.md section 4.3 requirement 10 already commits to this: 'a generated graph and a static board rebuilt on write'. A grep for html, mermaid or svg across .basicly/core/kit/tracker returns nothing, against a positive control that the same tree holds 21 modules and a working CLI. So the requirement is owed and unmet, and it is the last of the competitive claims with nothing behind it.

Section 15 rejects a web application, and this is not one. No server, no network, no third-party asset: one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and an inline SVG, regenerated on demand, which is exactly what requirement 10 restated the claim to.

The graph must be bounded. This ledger holds 1367 records, and an SVG over all of them is unreadable and enormous, so the rendered subgraph is the dispatchable one - what is ready, what is blocked, and what blocks it - with the count rendered stated against the total on the page. A page that silently drew a subset would be worse than one that drew nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One kit command writes a single HTML file that opens with no network and no other file beside it.
- The page shows the counts, the ranked ready set, what is blocked and what holds it, and every record with its status and what it owes.
- The page carries an inline SVG of the dispatchable dependency subgraph, and states how many records it drew against how many the ledger holds.
- A ledger with no records renders a page that says so rather than failing.

## Requirements

- No engine import, no third-party package, no network, no subprocess, and no syntax newer than Python 3.9.
- The page is one file: no linked stylesheet, no script tag, no external font or image.
- Every figure on the page is read from the ledger, never estimated.
payload.title: let the kit write the static board and graph its spec already owes

payload.name: close_reason
payload.value: shipped: one self-contained page with the counts, the ready set, the blockers, a bounded cluster-whole dependency drawing and every record with what it owes, validated from a wheel with no engine and judged from a browser render rather than its markup

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a consumer shapes a record for an agent to verify against, I want the gate to read one store rather than two, so I can stop the disagreement D-50 was written to end.

D-50 decided that acceptance_criteria and requirements are fields and not headings, that the field becomes the only reader, and that the heading survives only as a read-only fallback for a closed record and is refused for an open one. The shaping module shipped in basicly-b84ql8z accepts a heading on any record. Measured 2026-09-18: a heading-only open record owes nothing, so the gate passes it.

I built that fallback deliberately for backward compatibility and did not check it against the decision before doing so. D-50's own argument applies to the kit unchanged: two representations of one truth is a disagreement that already happened, and the reader that exists reads the weaker store. This repository's own 94 records carrying both stores and disagreeing are what that looks like.

The consequence is the migration D-50 already sized, not a surprise. 782 records carry the heading and 467 carry the field, so tightening the gate makes heading-only open records report what they owe. That is the correct reading of their state, and closed records keep the heading as evidence.
payload.title: make the kit gate read the field on an open record as D-50 already decided

payload.name: acceptance_criteria

A closed record still reads the heading as a fallback, so evidence already written stays readable. The trigger stays a heading, which D-50 keeps.

Every caller passes the record's real status, because defaulting to open would mark 1020 closed records as owing. The engine seam must be able to write both fields before the gate reads only them.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a team installs only the tracker kit and lands branches for a year, I want their shards folded into the trunk without anyone running a command, so I can keep the merge promise from decaying into a directory nobody can git add.

Sharding landed in basicly-v5zvsh1 and the engine got its automatic compaction in basicly-62gd7je. A consumer with no engine has neither: compact is a command someone must remember, and fsck only warns above 1000 shards, so the first alarm comes about a year in. Measured on this repository, 8.2 merges a day is 3000 shards a year, and one git add over 10000 files costs 35.59s on NTFS against 0.66s on ext4 with the ratio doubling every decade.

Measured 2026-09-18 rather than recalled: a post-merge hook fires on a fast-forward pull and on a no-fast-forward merge, both. So a developer pulling the trunk after someone else's branch landed is exactly the moment the shard becomes foldable, and the hook is the right one.

Two problems the tier kit's hook installer did not face. A repository may point core.hooksPath somewhere other than .git/hooks, and writing the wrong place would leave a hook nothing runs. And a hook file may already exist and belong to pre-commit or husky, so it must be merged into rather than clobbered.
payload.requirements: no engine import, standard library only, no subprocess, Python 3.9 floor. The hook body carries no absolute path, no username and no bare python3, because a bare python3 on Windows hits an execution alias. core.hooksPath is read from .git/config as a file, which is the same boundary SPEC section 4.0 already amended for .git/HEAD.
payload.title: compact a standalone consumer's shards without them remembering

payload.name: close_reason
payload.value: shipped: init wires a post-merge hook that folds shards and commits them only when the ledger is the sole dirt, honours core.hooksPath, merges into an existing hook, and uninstall removes only its own block

payload.name: acceptance_criteria

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:

- WHEN the page renders, IT SHALL contain none of the words `producer`, `emitted`, `withheld` or `renderable`.
- WHEN a figure is shown, ITS DENOMINATION SHALL be stated where two denominations exist.
- WHEN the page renders at every width the layout claims, `.scripts/check_render_overflow.py` SHALL report neither overflow nor overlap.
- WHERE a child would satisfy its own criteria while contradicting this design, THIS DESIGN SHALL win and the child SHALL be re-scoped rather than landed.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria

payload.name: acceptance_criteria

- WHEN a page's destination path exists and is a symbolic link, THE WRITER SHALL refuse that page and count it among the refused, rather than following the link.
- THE COMMAND SHALL report the refusal count it already prints, so a refused page is visible to the operator rather than silent.
- WHERE a destination is refused, THE OTHER PAGES SHALL still be written: one hostile entry must not cost the whole render.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- WHEN a repository has an active grant and no supervisor holds a lock, THE HEADER SHALL still name the granted root, its level, its budget and its spend.
- WHERE a supervisor does hold a lock, THE PRESENT behaviour SHALL be unchanged, including the stale marking.
- WHERE the run line is derived without a lock, IT SHALL NOT claim a pass is running: the grant is a fact about the repository and the pass is a fact about a process, and the header must not merge them.
- A TEST SHALL build the header with no lock present and assert the grant figures are drawn, with a control asserting no pass is claimed.
- THE THREE CAPABILITIES ABOVE SHALL share one test naming every board fact that is allowed to depend on the lock, so a fourth cannot be added silently.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria

- WHERE a lane is `queued`, `waits-to-land` or `refused`, THE PRESENT sentence SHALL be unchanged: a pass really will come back to those.
- THE BANNER AND THE REGION SHALL NOT disagree: when the banner says nothing is waiting, no line beneath it may say something is.
- A TEST SHALL drive a board whose only lanes are parked and assert the ready count is reported, with a control asserting a queued lane still reports as waiting.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- The repository shall carry one committed machine-readable snapshot at `.scripts/frozen_surfaces.json` keyed by the five clause names of `integrity._CONSUMER_SURFACES` (cli-surface, config-surface, catalog-source-schemas, generated-file-contract, ledger-format), each entry derived from the code that defines it: the argparse tree of `cli._build_parser()` (commands, subcommands, flags), the accepted section and key names of `config.CONFIG_SCHEMA` for basicly.toml and basicly.local.toml, the `$id` and `required`/`properties` of `.basicly/core/schemas/{fragment,skill,agent}.schema.json`, the generated-manifest `version` and the projected output set, and `events.KNOWN_KINDS`, `events.KNOWN_FIELDS`, `events.EVENT_FAMILY` and `events.LOG_GLOB` from `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`.
- When `uv run python .scripts/check_surface_freeze.py --check` runs on a tree whose derived surfaces equal the committed snapshot, it shall print `surface-freeze: 5 surfaces current` and exit 0.
- When a derived surface differs from the committed snapshot, `--check` shall exit 1 and print one line per drifted surface naming the surface clause and the first differing entry (for example `surface-freeze: cli-surface drifted: +flag verify --frobnicate`), and the same finding shall appear in `basicly verify --mode fast` and `--mode full` as a failing check named `surface-freeze` declared in `basicly.d/basicly-kosxhm.1.toml`.
- When `--fix` runs, it shall rewrite `.scripts/frozen_surfaces.json` from the code and print `surface-freeze: snapshot regenerated`; the verify entry shall declare no `fix_command`, so the fast set never regenerates the freeze on the author's behalf.
- The snapshot shall be byte-identical when generated on Linux, macOS and Windows (sorted keys, LF, posix paths), asserted in `tests/test_check_surface_freeze.py` together with a positive control that a mutated parser produces a drift naming `cli-surface`.
- The `ledger-format` clause of `integrity._CONSUMER_SURFACES` shall also claim `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`, and `tests/test_integrity.py`'s exactly-one-level property shall still hold over every tracked file.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria

- If the range cannot be derived (no base branch, shallow clone with no merge base), the check shall exit 1 naming what it could not read rather than pass vacuously.
- The `pre-push` hook shall refuse such a push by running the same check, because pre-push runs the `full` mode (`.basicly/core/hooks/pre-push.py`); no hook source is edited.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria

payload.name: acceptance_criteria

- Given architecture.md 32.8, when a reader counts `events.KNOWN_KINDS`, then the document states twelve members and the tree holds twelve.
- Given architecture.md 33, when a reader looks for the artifact transport, then the document states the typed `artifact` event is the transport and carries no claim that zero exist.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- WHEN a lane meets a bound, THE GUIDANCE AND THE GATE'S OWN REMEDY SHALL together name a route that its own parser accepts, and the route SHALL be reachable without editing a file another lane declares.
- WHEN a split is proposed, ITS EFFECT ON BOTH GATES SHALL be computable before the cut is made, rather than discovered by making it.
- WHEN the tree grows, THE COUNT OF MODULES WITHIN ONE ORDINARY EDIT OF A BOUND SHALL fall rather than rise, and that count SHALL be reported.
- WHERE a module genuinely has no seam, TAKING THE WAIVER SHALL cost one step and SHALL NOT require a lane to enumerate its subsets to discover that.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- THE WAIVER on `src/basicly/board_actions.py` SHALL be removed in the same change that resolves this record, whichever of the three ways is chosen.
- WHERE the answer is that the measure needs a discriminator, THAT DISCRIMINATOR SHALL be bound to something the producer of the module writes, not to a name or a path - an absence must not be ambiguous.
- WHERE the answer is that the reasons belong elsewhere, EVERY REASON SHALL survive the move: the count of distinct claims before and after is the check, not the character count.
- A TEST SHALL fail if this waiver outlives the record, so it cannot become a standing exemption.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- WHEN an agent has the board and nothing else, IT SHALL be able to answer all nine questions in the table above, and a test SHALL enumerate them so the board cannot drift back into a report.
- WHERE a verb changes the flow of work, THE BOARD SHALL offer it on the row it applies to, not only where an ask happens to prefill it.
- THE BOARD SHALL NOT gain the ability to create a record: the owner keeps that in the terminal.
- `consumer-reads-only-the-snapshot` SHALL still hold: every new capability is an argv handed to the installed CLI.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- WHERE the board draws a record in a ranked list, IT SHALL offer the priority change on that record's own row, not only where an ask prefills it.
- THE ACTION SHALL refuse a value the tracker will refuse, before the subprocess runs, and say which values are allowed.
- THE PRINTED COMMAND SHALL be built through the action's own `build`, so the line a reader copies cannot diverge from the argv the button runs.
- A TEST SHALL assert the argv reaches the CLI and changes the record, not that the argv has the right shape - the shape-only test is why `basicly-fiow1sr` shipped an argv that started nothing.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- WHERE the ready set is non-empty, THE READY REGION SHALL draw at least one row whatever the reserved height, so a reader is never shown a count with no rows.
- WHERE the region can draw no row at all, IT SHALL reserve no height and SHALL say that the wall is too short, rather than drawing an empty box.
- THE HEADER COUNT SHALL agree with the rows drawn: a region showing N rows of M ready SHALL NOT report M as more-than-drawn when it drew none.
- A TEST SHALL render the wall at 1440x900 with a claimed lane and a parked strip present, and assert the ready region contains at least one record id.
- A TEST SHALL drive `next_up` across the reserve range 0 to 600 px and assert the row count never reaches zero while the ready set is non-empty.
- THE REGION SHALL keep the viewport bound it already honours, so closing this SHALL NOT reopen the 152px overflow basicly-zj36jf0 measures.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- THE BOARD SHALL take every padding, margin and gap value from one declared scale, and a value outside that scale SHALL NOT appear in a template.
- WHERE a component is nested inside another, THE INNER COMPONENT SHALL carry a non-zero inset from its container on every side that has a visible border.
- A GATE SHALL fail naming any board template that declares a spacing value the scale does not contain, so a thirteenth ad hoc value cannot land silently.
- THE SCALE SHALL be stated in one place that the templates read, so changing a step is one edit rather than sixteen.
- A SCREENSHOT at 1440x900 SHALL be taken and read before this is closed, because the counted declarations are the symptom and the rendered gap is the requirement.
- CLOSING THIS SHALL NOT reopen basicly-zj36jf0 or basicly-lc2bd3v.10: added inset costs height, and both of those are regions already short of it.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- WHERE an ask carries an `offer`, THE BOARD SHALL print a command that reaches the state the ask is waiting for, verified by running it, and SHALL NOT print one that stops at an unapproved checkpoint.
- WHEN more than one ask is pending, THE BOARD SHALL name every waiting record and its own command, rather than naming one and counting the rest.
- THE OFFERED COMMAND SHALL be rendered without truncation, wrapping instead of clipping where the column is narrow.
- THE ASK SHALL state the consequence of acting in a person's terms alongside the engine's own wording, never instead of it.
- WHERE an ask's kind is `advance`, THE BOARD SHALL offer it as an action on that ask's row, through an argv handed to the installed CLI like every other action.
- A TEST SHALL run each offered argv against a fixture at the state the ask describes and assert it reaches the next state, so an offer that stops short fails rather than renders.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- WHEN an operator selects a record in the backlog, THE PAGE SHALL draw that record's dependency neighbourhood - what it waits on, what waits on it, and the order those imply - and SHALL distinguish a declared `blocks` edge from a contention edge derived from overlapping scope.
- WHEN an operator moves a record above one it depends on, THE PAGE SHALL refuse the move and SHALL name the chain that forbids it, rather than accepting it with a warning.
- WHERE a move is legal, THE PAGE SHALL apply it through an argv handed to the installed CLI, and the resulting order SHALL be the order `basicly tracker ready` then reports - or the move SHALL be refused as unrepresentable.
- THE PAGE SHALL NOT invent an ordering the engine does not read: a drag whose effect the dispatcher ignores is a lie the operator will act on.
- WHERE two records are unordered by any edge, THE PAGE SHALL say they are unordered rather than implying the list position is a decision.
- A TEST SHALL attempt a dependency-violating move against a fixture and assert it is refused, naming the chain, with a control asserting a legal move is applied.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:

payload.description:
## Trigger

When the definition-of-ready gate asks a record for its requirements, I want it to ask only records created after the rule existed, so I can stop refusing 341 records for content nobody could have written.

Measured 2026-09-18 over the folded ledger: all 341 open records owe requirements, 0 carry the field and 0 carry a heading to migrate from. The engine seam could not write that field until basicly-77tjvmk, so the debt was never a lapse, it was impossible. Retro-filling 341 statements would be inventing content, which is the guess you keep.

The discriminator may not be a timestamp. Section 9.5 forbids deriving anything from the clock, and there is no global ordering across records because sequence numbers are per item. So the rule binds on a marker the producer writes at create: a record minted under the rule carries it, an older one does not, and absence is unambiguous because every new record gets it.

The debt stays visible rather than being forgiven. owed still reports requirements for an unmarked record, so the board keeps showing it; only the refusal is withheld.
payload.requirements: the marker is a field the producer writes, never a clock reading and never a global sequence, because neither exists per record. No engine import, standard library only, Python 3.9 floor. No record already in the ledger is rewritten: the rule reads what is there.
payload.title: require requirements only of records minted under the rule

payload.description:
When the rule lands, I want a record minted through the engine to carry the marker, so I can prove the rule is not inert here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- the marker is present

When a kit module reaches the network or spawns a process, I want the boundary gate to refuse it, so I can stop section 4 asserting a property no check reads.

SPEC.md section 4 states the kit is standard library only, no third party, no network, no subprocess. kit-boundary.py checks two rules and neither is that one: does a module import basicly, and does it name an engine path. So half the declared boundary is enforced by prose.

That is the same fail-open shape section 4 itself narrates about the import linter, which analysed one root package while the kit is flat modules outside it and would have reported success forever. A boundary claim nothing reads is indistinguishable from one that passes.

Measured 2026-09-18: no kit module imports subprocess, socket, urllib, http or requests today, against a positive control that six of them import json. So the gate lands green and locks in a property that currently holds, rather than reporting a debt.
payload.requirements: the gate reads the kit's source, never runs it. No new dependency. The refusal message names what to do instead, as the two existing rules do.

payload.description:
When a release refuses because the tutorial names the old version, I want the reason written down, so I can stop someone adding docs/tutorial to the pin globs and quietly falsifying a transcript.

docs/tutorial/first-loop.md opens by claiming every command and every quoted output was executed in a real terminal on a named version. docs-claims enforces that the named version is the newest released one, so a release refuses until the page is re-recorded. That refusal is the gate working.

Adding docs/tutorial to release.PIN_GLOBS looks like the obvious fix and is the wrong one. The pin pattern matches the @vX.Y.Z install line, which is a command, but the page also carries engine: basicly X.Y.Z inside recorded output. Rewriting those would make the opening sentence false while the gate went green. I made that change during v0.14.0 and reverted it.
payload.requirements: no gate is weakened and no waiver is added: the release stays refused until a human re-records the page
payload.title: record why the tutorial is not a release pin target

payload.text:
Re-recorded for v0.14.0 on 2026-09-18. A fresh git repository, basicly installed from a locally built 0.14.0 wheel, then every step of the page walked: install, status, gitignore, policy scaffold, tracker create, policy dor, the install commit, loop status, loop run to the classify checkpoint, the worktree edit and its commit, the landing, the ship approval, git log and the closing loop status.

Every quoted block matched what the page already said apart from ids, commit hashes and sub-second timings. basicly status was identical field for field. The six commits came out in the same shapes and the same order. So the five version strings were the only edit the page needed, and the opening sentence is true.

Two things the recording had to route around, neither a page defect. The shell is not a TTY, so a checkpoint prints a one-time code rather than taking the terminal as the human - which the page already documents as the relay. And loop run --confirm refuses the ship checkpoint whatever code it is given, because the advance reissues the code before reading it; policy checkpoint <id> ship --approve --confirm is the surface that works. The page never shows either, because a reader at a terminal meets neither.

A structural fact that decides how this can ever be done: basicly release tags locally and deliberately does not push, so @vX.Y.Z is unreachable until after the release. The page can only be recorded against a locally built engine, with the git+ line as the documented equivalent.

payload.acceptance_criteria: every fixture that clears the ledger to install a known one clears both globs, asserted by the board corpus tests passing while a stray shard is still present rather than after it is removed
payload.description:
When a fixture replaces the ledger to pin a known corpus, I want it to clear the shards too, so I can stop a stray pending file inflating a frozen count.

Four fixtures cleared events-*.jsonl and not pending-*.jsonl, so a shard that happened to be tracked came along through work_repo and the board counted 7 records against a frozen 6. The pre-push gate caught it after the tag was cut locally.

This is the same sweep miss as basicly-zsq6xkz one layer out. That one found three readers that spelled the glob as a string literal rather than reading the kit constant; this one is the same literal in test fixtures, which the earlier sweep of log_paths callers could not see because a fixture is a writer and not a reader.

The stray shard itself was live data: five events the trunk did not hold, left uncompacted because the tutorial was dirty when the ledger was committed, so commit_tracker_state declined and the shard was committed raw.
payload.requirements: each site is edited by hand against a named count and reconciled after, because a scripted replace across test files is how 23 failures became 80 once before
payload.title: clear both ledger globs wherever a fixture installs a known ledger

payload.acceptance_criteria: ledger_git_rules returns the shard glob as well as the trunk glob, basicly install writes both into .gitattributes, and git check-attr reports merge union on a pending file in a repository installed through the engine, against the trunk file as the positive control
payload.description:
When a repository upgrades through basicly install rather than the standalone kit, I want its .gitattributes to carry the shard rule too, so I can stop two clones on one branch conflicting on a file the design exists to keep conflict-free.

Found by the terminal canary reading source at the v0.14.0 tag, filed there as term-n3rzn, and confirmed here. owned_write.ledger_git_rules returns only the events glob, and cli._scaffold_ledger_attributes appends exactly what it returns. The standalone installer writes both globs and docs/reference/kits.md promises both, so the two install paths diverge and the documentation describes the path a bundled consumer does not use.

This repository carries the rule only because it was hand-edited into .gitattributes during the sharding work, which is why no gate here noticed. A consumer installing v0.14.0 through the engine gets the trunk rule and not the shard rule.

The canary also corrected the framing and it matters. The shard name derives from .git/HEAD, so identity is per BRANCH, not per person. Two clones both sitting on main produce the same tracked path, and the GitHub measurement behind the release covers two different branches rather than that case. The repository's own test_two_writers_on_one_shard_still_need_the_union_attribute already proves union is load-bearing there, and the engine install is the path that lacks it.
payload.requirements: the engine reads both globs off the kit constants rather than spelling either a second time, because a second spelling is what left three readers blind in basicly-zsq6xkz. The wording that reads as one file per person is corrected wherever it appears.
payload.title: the engine install omits the shard merge rule the kit installer writes

payload.acceptance_criteria: the re-pin path writes the previous copy to the same .basicly-bak sibling the force path uses before it writes, and says where it is; a run that re-pins nothing writes no backup and leaves the file untouched
payload.description:
When an upgrade re-pins a consumer's CI workflow, I want the previous copy left beside it, so I can see what changed on a file my own rules put on a confirmation list.

Found by the terminal canary and filed there as term-42xuc arm 2. _write_scaffold at cli.py:1219-1241 inverts the safety: the plain path re-pins and writes in place with no backup, while the --overwrite-scaffolds branch writes a .basicly-bak sibling before replacing. So the flag that sounds destructive preserves the original and the default does not.

It is not theoretical for the canary. That repository carries the workflow with five pinned references and holds CI edits on an explicit confirmation list, so an upgrade rewrites a gated file before a human could be asked, and there is no install --dry-run to preview it.

Arm 1 of term-42xuc - a plain install CREATING a workflow where none existed, at the fallthrough that never consults force - is a larger question about what install may do unasked and is filed separately rather than rushed into this patch.
payload.requirements: one branch in _write_scaffold, no new flag and no change to what the force path does. The message names the backup by the same shape the force path already prints, so a consumer meets one vocabulary.
payload.title: back up a scaffold before the default path rewrites it

payload.acceptance_criteria: a decision is recorded naming whether creation stays default, becomes opt-in, or becomes announce-then-write, with the reason; whichever is chosen is enforced by a test that fails if install creates a workflow the chosen rule forbids
payload.description:
When an upgrade runs in a repository that has no CI workflow, I want to know whether creating one is something install may do without being asked, so I can stop a tool writing into a directory a consumer never opted into.

Found by the terminal canary as term-42xuc arm 1, confirmed here at cli.py:1239-1241: the branch that runs when the path does not exist calls mkdir and write and prints Wrote, and it never consults force. So --overwrite-scaffolds is not what arms creation; a plain install is. I reproduced it by accident in this repository, which had never tracked .github/workflows/basicly-gates.yml and had one after a mistaken install.

Re-pinning a file a consumer already has is a different act from creating one they never had, and the second is the larger one. This is filed apart from basicly-kfj94k8, which only removes the backup inversion, because the answer here is a decision rather than a defect.

The canary listed four shapes without prescribing one: announce before writing, back up on the re-pin path, gate creation behind an explicit opt-in, or add install --dry-run. The second is done. The remaining three are alternatives, not a sequence.
payload.requirements: the decision is written where the other fifty are rather than in a changelog entry. No behaviour changes until it is taken, because the current behaviour is documented in the file's own first line and changing it silently is the same class of surprise being complained about.
payload.title: decide whether a plain install may create a ci workflow unasked

payload.acceptance_criteria: a repository upgraded with basicly install carries a post-merge hook that folds pending shards, asserted on a repository that already had a ledger before the install rather than only on a fresh one; the kits reference stops claiming install leaves nothing to run until it is true
payload.description:
When a repository upgrades with basicly install, I want its post-merge hook folding pending shards, so I can stop the trunk log ceasing to be the readable history on a repository worked from two machines.

Found by the terminal canary after a live v0.14.1 install and filed there as term-ftosv. The kit file is vendored and unwired: .basicly/core/kit/tracker/install_hook.py sets HOOK_NAME to post-merge, and grepping cli.py at e2451c95 for install_hook or post-merge finds only the tier kit's installer and the pre-commit stage activation. The install line says it activated pre-commit, commit-msg and pre-push, and ls of .git/hooks confirms no post-merge against a control of three hooks present.

The contrast control is what makes this a wiring gap rather than a design choice: cli.TIER_HOOK_INSTALLER and cmd_tier_hook run the tier kit's identically shaped install_hook.py as a subprocess and it is a named install step. The engine has the mechanism and uses it for one kit and not the other. Same divergence as basicly-cb61y44, where the standalone installer wrote a rule the engine path did not.

The canary also named the trap: _setup_tracker returns early on an existing ledger, so a fix placed there skips every consumer that already has one - exactly the repositories that have shards to fold.

Not data loss. The fold reads both globs so reads stay correct; the cost is that shards are never consolidated and the trunk stops being the history a person reads.

docs/reference/kits.md states that basicly install brings all three kits with nothing else to run, which is false while this step is missing.
payload.requirements: the engine runs the kit's own installer as a subprocess exactly as it does for the tier kit, holding no kit import, and passes the ledger the same way the standalone package does. The step is not placed inside _setup_tracker, whose early return would skip every existing consumer.
payload.title: wire the tracker shard hook the way the tier hook is already wired

payload.acceptance_criteria: the markdown basicly generates passes markdownlint with default rules, measured the way the canary measures it - projections copied into a directory with a consumer config and no basicly config present - with a ragged table as the positive control proving the rule is active
payload.description:
When a consumer lints their repository with default markdownlint rules, I want the markdown basicly generated into it to pass, so I can stop shipping output that fails a gate we also ship.

Found by the terminal canary after a v0.14.1 install, filed there as term-fawxo, and blocking their commit. Reproduced here, which is the part that matters: copying this repository's own .claude and .agents projections plus AGENTS.md into a directory carrying a consumer-shaped markdownlint config produces 20 MD060 table-column-style errors. The canary sees 62 because their projection set is larger.

This repository passes only because .markdownlint-cli2.yaml disables MD060 for itself, with a recorded reason under basicly-jaz4: the rule fires when one cell of an aligned table is edited without re-padding, and --fix will not re-pad. That reason is about hand-edited markdown. It was never shipped, so a consumer whose config says default true gets the rule and our output fails it.

The standard this misses is our own. The same config file says a violation in a projected file means a template or catalog source regressed, fix it there and rebuild. The generator is emitting markdown that is not lint-clean and the rule was turned off rather than the output fixed.

The canary also reports 24 MD022 and MD032 errors inside the Commit delta auto-generated section that basicly release writes. That half does NOT reproduce here: this repository's own CHANGELOG.md passes the same consumer config with exit 0, so their 24 need their file to diagnose and are not confirmed as ours.

The first probe I ran reported zero and was wrong: markdownlint merges the repository's own config even under --config, so the rule was disabled in my own measurement. A deliberately ragged table as a positive control did not fire either, which is what exposed it. The numbers above are from a directory that carries no basicly config.
payload.requirements: the fix is at the source or the projector rather than by disabling a rule in the consumer's config, because the consumer's lint config is theirs and a rule we silence for ourselves is not a rule we may silence for them. Whatever is chosen, the scoping advice the install prints must name the same paths as the fix.
payload.title: our generated markdown fails a rule we disabled only for ourselves

payload.text:
The CHANGELOG half is settled and is not ours. Grepping the whole tree for 'Commit delta' returns CHANGELOG.md and the ledger only - no source file, no script, no workflow - against a positive control that the string does exist in CHANGELOG.md. Stronger, because absent today is not absent ever: git log --all -S over src, .scripts and any .py returns nothing, against a control of 4 commits when the same search is scoped to CHANGELOG.md. This repository's one such section was written by a human commit, b0bf6daf, and carries the blank line. So basicly release has never emitted that heading and the canary's 12 sections came from something else; a hand fix there stays fixed. Bound: only this repository was searched.

The canary's escaped-pipe finding is a requirement on any projector fix, recorded before the work starts. Their first re-padding attempt refused to write because a cell containing an escaped pipe, in a table documenting the pipe operator, split into a phantom extra column and would have added an empty cell to every row. Split on unescaped pipes only, (?<!\\)\|. A naive split silently widens the table and the damage reads as padding, which is the shape that passes review.

Their verification standard is the one to hold a fix to: refuse to write unless the parsed cell text is identical, then confirm at the diff level that the removed and added lines are byte-identical after squashing spaces, dashes and colons. Two paths sharing no step.

Withdrawn rather than shipped, and the reason is a measurement rather than a preference. The wiring worked - cmd_tracker_hook mirrored the tier one and installed correctly on a repository that already had a ledger, so the canary's early-return trap was avoided. But on the merge that followed, the hook folded the shard and could not commit it: its message carries no record id and tracker-commit-msg, written by the same install, refuses that. So in any basicly repository the hook folds, stages and leaves a dirty tree after every merge, which is the objection that made the clean-tree guard exist in the first place.

The two remaining shapes were not real. Staging without committing is the dirty tree by design. Shipping it as it stands is shipping a hook that cannot commit.

So the engine does not get the hook. It already folds at commit_tracker_state with an id the gate accepts, and docs/reference/kits.md said the opposite - that install brings all three with nothing else to run - which is corrected here. The post-merge hook remains the standalone answer, where there is no commit-msg gate and its commit succeeds.

What is left undone and is the real fix: a repository worked from two machines accumulates a shard from the other machine until the next tracker write or landing folds it. Self-healing in an active repository, not in a quiet one. An engine-side fold on merge, committing the way the engine already does, is filed as the follow-on.

payload.acceptance_criteria: a plain git merge or pull in a repository with basicly folds any shard it brought in and commits it with a record id the commit-msg gate accepts, leaving the tree clean; a tree carrying work in progress is left untouched, asserted against a control showing the shard surviving
payload.description:
When a repository with basicly is worked from two machines on one branch, I want a shard arriving from the other machine folded at the merge, so I can keep the trunk log readable without waiting for the next landing.

The kit's post-merge hook cannot do this for a basicly repository: its commit carries no record id and tracker-commit-msg, written by the same install, refuses it, so it folds and leaves a dirty tree. That is why basicly-jmp6561 was withdrawn rather than shipped.

The engine already has what the hook lacks. commit_tracker_state folds and commits with an id the gate accepts, and merge_worktree calls it at the landing. What is missing is the same fold reached from a plain git merge or pull rather than only from a loop landing.

The gap is bounded and self-healing in an active repository: the next tracker write or landing folds whatever arrived. It is a quiet repository that accumulates, which is the canary's case between landings.
payload.requirements: no bypass of any gate: the commit carries a real record id rather than skipping the hook that asks for one. The engine reaches the fold through the seam it already uses rather than a second mechanism, and a repository without basicly keeps the kit's post-merge hook as its answer.
payload.title: fold a shard at the merge from the engine side

payload.acceptance_criteria: the catalog sources behind the projections carry consistent tables, the projections pass markdownlint under a consumer config with no basicly config present, catalog-lint refuses a table whose delimiter row does not match its cells, and the canary's remaining count goes to zero in one step rather than partly
payload.description:
When a catalog source carries a table whose delimiter row is unpadded while its cells are padded, I want the authoring gate to refuse it, so I can stop shipping markdown that fails a consumer's default lint.

Found by the terminal canary as term-fawxo, blocking their upgrade commit on 62 errors after they cleared their own 31. Reproduced here: this repository's projections produce 20 MD060 errors under a consumer config with no basicly config present, against a ragged table as the positive control.

All 20 are style compact and the cause is one shape. A table writes a padded header and padded cells while leaving the delimiter row bare - pipe dash dash dash pipe - so markdownlint infers compact from the delimiter and then objects to every padded cell. The table is internally inconsistent, which is what the rule exists to catch.

basicly-jaz4 disabled MD060 here for a reason that does not govern this: it named an ALIGNED table, where editing one cell forces a hand re-pad of every other pipe and fix will not do it. None of these are aligned. The remedy is to pad the delimiter row, two characters per column, once.
payload.requirements: the fix is in the catalog sources rather than the projector, so the projector never rewrites authored prose. Any later normaliser splits on unescaped pipes only, because an escaped pipe in a table documenting the pipe operator splits into a phantom column and the damage reads as padding. basicly-jaz4 is annotated rather than left reading as blanket cover.
payload.title: pad the delimiter rows and gate the rule that caught them

payload.acceptance_criteria: a repository whose config already names the managed core gets no advice line for that file, and a repository that does not still gets it - the second half asserted, or the fix is a suppression rather than a check
payload.description:
When install finishes in a repository that already excludes the managed core from its linters, I want it to say nothing, so I can stop training a consumer to skim the region where a tracked CI edit is also reported.

Found by the terminal canary, filed there as term-ip2wz and pressed after it shipped twice unchanged. scaffolds.install_notes tests only whether a config file exists, never what it contains, so it advises extend-exclude on a .ruff.toml that has carried exactly that for releases. The canary verified the exclusion is genuinely in force rather than merely present: ruff format --check over the managed core exits 0 on 54 files.

The same block tells a consumer to hand-edit .pre-commit-config.yaml in a run that separately reports it has just rewritten that file.

Severity is low and nothing fails. The reason it is worth fixing is where it sits: the advice is the tail of the install output, and the tail is also where a re-pin of a tracked CI workflow is announced. Unactionable boilerplate beside a real edit teaches a reader to skip both.

Recorded against myself: this was already a requirement on basicly-fmgwtwi, which is still open, and I shipped two releases without meeting it while telling the canary it was on the record. It was on the record and it was not done.
payload.requirements: the check reads the file rather than testing its presence. A false skip is possible if the path is named for some other reason, and that is accepted and stated rather than guarded, because the cost of a missed note is one line a consumer can still read in the documentation.
payload.title: read the file before advising a change it already carries

payload.acceptance_criteria: external-facts says the control is built from a failure that has been seen rather than an assumed one, and says to check the denominator moved; the always-on surfaces stay under their caps and the projection gates pass
payload.description:
When an agent runs a positive control and it returns zero, I want the rule to say what the control must be built from, so I can stop reading a control's own zero as confirmation.

Asked for by the terminal canary as term-2vkce, and the request is well founded: the rule is in managed core they may never edit, they followed both halves of it, and still got a false reading. The wording said run a positive control and that if the control is empty too the zero belongs to the probe. It never said what the control must be built from.

Their case is the evidence. They planted a table they called ragged; it was valid compact style, so it was never a violation, reported zero, and read exactly like a dead probe. Rebuilt from the defect actually observed - padded cells over an unpadded delimiter row - it reported two errors. What rescued the diagnosis was the denominator: 151 files became 152 when the control was added, which proved the file was read and sent them to the table rather than the tooling.

Three of my own false zeros the same day were the environment answering instead of the code. Theirs is the subtler one and the one the rule did not cover.

Carrying it in their overlay was the fallback, and the objection to that is right: two copies of one rule drift, and ours is the copy every other consumer reads.
payload.requirements: the amendment sits in the existing bullet rather than adding one, because the always-on budget is a standing cost on every consumer. The token cost declared on the fragment is updated to what the projection measures rather than left to drift.
payload.title: amend the positive control rule with what a control must be built from

When a patch release changes nothing the tutorial quotes, I want the page to need one edit rather than five, so I can stop paying a ten minute walkthrough for a version string.

Three runs, zero drift found, five strings edited each time.

The five sites are not one kind of thing and the gate cannot tell them apart. Line 7 is the claim, that every command and output was executed on a named version. Lines 36 and 50 are instructions, the uvx line a reader types. Lines 66 and 68 are transcript, what the tool printed.

The page already elides a timestamp on line 68 with its own convention, so eliding the version beside it is consistent rather than new.

[session handover 2026-09-19] Two releases cut and pushed; a fourth install-advice defect is fixed on main and deliberately unreleased.

STATE. main d0146315, clean, nothing unpushed. Tags v0.15.0 and v0.15.1 both pushed. Version on disk 0.15.1. uv run pytest -q -n 4 = 5909 passed 1 xfailed. uv run basicly verify --mode full = PASS.

SHIPPED IN v0.15.1, both found by the canary within hours of the v0.15.0 tag. The managed-core exclusion advice was fixed into silence in v0.15.0: the check asked whether a config MENTIONS .basicly/core, never whether it EXCLUDES it, and this repo's own .ruff.toml names the path three times in per-file-ignores (basicly-ajqk150). install --dry-run reported the release's own headline feature as broken, because a dry run never syncs the catalog and so ran the vendored kit against the new engine's flags (basicly-v92kmjv); fixing that exposed a second fault under it, the kit computing its own script path even when a host supplies --command.

ON MAIN, UNRELEASED, OWNER'S CALL 2026-09-18. basicly-ap693b0: install advised adding exclude to the .pre-commit-config.yaml it writes itself, whose hooks lint .basicly/core on purpose - no-comments carries pass_filenames true and a files regex matching .py. Followed literally the advice disabled the gates the install had just written. Now silent until the config carries a hook basicly did not write. Held rather than cut because the canary was still on v0.15.0 and a third tag in one day is a version to skip. SHIPS IN THE NEXT CUT - do not let it sit.

OPEN, AND ONLY THE CANARY CAN CLOSE IT. Arm 1, the real fold: terminal-88 carries .basicly/ledger/pending-main.jsonl at 30k, tracked, committed, never folded, hash d3afd42b recorded so the fold can be proven rather than assumed. It is armed but not exercisable - that side pushed, so it has nothing to pull; the fold fires the first time the other machine pushes and this one pulls. Every fold I have measured was on a shard I minted seconds earlier on a throwaway repo. This is the only real-ledger test there is.

ALSO OPEN. basicly-z79v2cf, a clock flake: test_supervise_board.py asserted 0 <= -1.439611 once inside verify --mode full, passed on re-run and 3 of 3 alone; it compares two clocks rather than one monotonic source. CI runs split across two SHAs on both releases: the tag's own commit ran the release job and a later tracker-only commit ran the other three, so 'green on the release commit' is not literally what exists.

METHOD NOTE WORTH KEEPING. Four defects this session were the same shape - a check that answers a question adjacent to the one asked. Mentions-vs-excludes, the dry run previewing an unsynced kit, a grep for a heading rather than for which file it names, a fixture whose directive was deleted while a comment still carried the path. Every one was caught by a row that MUST behave differently, never by the row that confirmed the hope.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value:
- R1. A seat that crashes re-reads what it had not consumed, rather than losing it.
- R2. Nothing an announcement carries is invisible to a reviewer or to the board.
- R3. No daemon, no second store and no network are introduced.
- R4. An announcement that nobody reads is a selection defect that someone can see, not a silent drop.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value:
- R1. Work is never pushed to a seat, because a seat that is not running cannot receive it.
- R2. Two seats never take the same task.
- R3. A seat takes its next task fast enough to stay inside the cache window, or it is released.
- R4. The order tasks are taken in is the order the existing ranked ready set already publishes, so this adds no second scheduler.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value:
- R1. An operator can see inside a running lane without opening a file on the host.
- R2. What the board shows is what the lane actually emitted, never a summary of it.
- R3. Showing a transcript adds no model call and no subprocess to the board, because the board folds files only.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value:
- R1. The answer names the populations that fill a lane's window, with a share for each, not a hypothesis.
- R2. The measurement is repeatable by someone who did not take it.
- R3. The result is allowed to say the gap is irreducible, and that answer closes the spike rather than failing it.

payload.name: requirements

payload.name: requirements
payload.value:

- R2. A match that could not apply an axis says which axis it could not apply, because a silently partial match is worse than none.
- R3. Adding a fifth axis later does not change the three axes that already exist.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value:
- R1. A reader can tell, from the ledger alone, which parts of architecture section 31A exist and which do not.
- R2. Each child states the intended use it is validated against, separately from the criteria it is verified against.
- R3. The set of children covers every `[TARGET]` passage in section 31A and every decision D-45 through D-50, and claims no part the architecture does not specify.
- R4. No child depends on a part of the design the architecture has not decided.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value:

- R2. An open record that was written before the change still yields its criteria after it, with no criterion lost.
- R3. A closed record stays readable as evidence, and nothing rewrites a line of the log to achieve that.
- R4. The second store cannot grow back after the switch.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- Given a folded field whose value exceeds a declared producer bound then the write is refused at the seam with the field named, rather than stored.
- Given a folded field within the bound then the write is unchanged and the fold derives the same state.
- Given a refusal then it says which field and what the bound is, so the caller can drop what is derivable instead of guessing.
- Given an existing oversized value already in the log then the fold derives the same state as before and nothing rewrites it.
- Demonstrated by: uv run pytest tests/test_kit_tracker_events.py -q plus a seam-level test that a 5 MB field value is refused, against a positive control that a small one is accepted

payload.name: acceptance_criteria

- Given the kind blind default is still reachable then a test states which caller reaches it and why that is safe, or the default is removed.
- Given the provenance test docstring then it names the mechanism that actually protects those keys.
- Given both corrections then the differential still finds no divergence on a ledger it found none on before.
- Demonstrated by: uv run pytest tests/test_kit_tracker_provenance.py tests/test_kit_tracker_migrate.py -q plus a differential run over the committed ledger

payload.name: requirements
payload.value:
- R1. One broken record cannot consume a pass.
- R2. The failure rate the health view reports reflects work that was attempted, not a retry storm.
- R3. An operator can tell a record stopped for repeated launch failure from one stopped for any other reason.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value:
- R1. A dispatch never begins billing differently because a host changed a default.
- R2. If a dispatch would bill against an API key rather than the subscription, that is visible before the pass runs, not after the invoice.
- R3. The pin survives a host upgrade without a person remembering to check.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- Given a new requirement document then it carries a machine-checkable section set and a record id that resolves in the tracker.
- Given a requirement document whose sections do not conform then a verify check fails and names the missing section.
- Given an author asks for a new requirement then a scaffold command writes the conforming skeleton rather than the author copying an existing file.
- Given every acceptance criterion a requirement carries is closed then a check reports the document as absorbable rather than deleting it.
- Given the folder holds no requirement document then no gate changes behaviour.
- Demonstrated by: uv run basicly verify --mode fast with a deliberately malformed requirement present, showing the check fail and then pass once corrected

payload.name: requirements
payload.value:
- R1. The failure mode the seat design names is priced, not assumed.
- R2. The measurement uses the host's own reported usage, derived by two paths that share no step.
- R3. The result can say that holding past the window is cheap, and that answer changes the release rule.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value:
- R1. The engine never assumes a cache window a host has not published.
- R2. A host that publishes no window is handled, and the handling is visible rather than silent.
- R3. A window that the vendor changes is corrected in one declaration, not in every call site.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value:
- R1. A second task in a held session costs materially less than the same task in a fresh one, and the saving is measured rather than assumed.
- R2. A session that cannot start its next task inside the host's cache window is ended, because an idle held session is worse than a fresh one.
- R3. A held session is releasable at any moment without losing work, because everything that must survive it is already written.
- R4. A crash of a held session loses no more than a fresh dispatch would.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value:
- R1. A run's recorded cost is the host's own figure, whichever path produced it.
- R2. The runs the engine over-reports are not the runs whose cost matters most, which today they are.
- R3. A future change that removes the de-duplication fails a test rather than shipping silently.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value:
- R1. A record that cannot state its intended use never reaches a lane.
- R2. An author is told which field is missing, not merely that the record is not ready.
- R3. The backlog of records owing a field is visible and falls over time rather than accumulating silently.

## Trigger

When a pass re-enqueues a pending decision item with new numbers, I want the item to keep its decision id and carry the current detail, so I can answer a budget escalation from accurate numbers.

## Context

`decisions.enqueue` is idempotent per `(issue, kind, question)`. When the item is already pending it returns the existing item at src/basicly/decisions.py:100-102 and never rewrites the detail. `PASS_SPEND_QUESTION` in src/basicly/supervise.py is deliberately constant so a repeatedly refusing pass finds the item it already queued, and the numbers live in the detail for exactly that reason. The consequence is that the detail is frozen at first-queue time and every later refusal leaves it untouched.

Measured on basicly-atrqcd 2026-09-01, base 24a0d6f3. `basicly loop decisions basicly-atrqcd` prints for `basicly-atrqcd#3018546b66`:

- `93153836 tokens forecast; 60000000 remaining under the grant; assumed at the unsizeable-lane bound (measured): basicly-jt0dgi, basicly-3iaw0x, basicly-mfavrh, basicly-rv7q88`

Every number and every classification in that line is now wrong. `supervise.admit_pass_spend` over the same four lanes returns `87214845 tokens forecast; 4345392 remaining under the grant; sized:` all four, with `assumed: ()`. Remaining is off by a factor of 13.8, and the line asserts the lanes are unsizeable when their scopes read.

The detail is the only thing a human sees when answering. `PassSpendAdmission.coverage` exists so an operator can see that a number is an assumption before it is the only thing standing between them and the bill; a frozen copy of that sentence defeats it.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/decisions.py`
- `tests/test_decisions.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: L2
- demonstration: `basicly loop decisions basicly-atrqcd` prints the current forecast and remaining budget for basicly-atrqcd#3018546b66

## Earlier acceptance text (the acceptance field is authoritative)

- WHEN a pending decision item is re-enqueued with a different detail, THE ITEM SHALL keep its decision id and carry the current detail.
- WHEN a pending item is re-enqueued with an unchanged detail, NO further comment or notification SHALL be produced.
- WHEN `basicly loop decisions <id>` prints a pending item, THE DETAIL SHALL be the one from the most recent enqueue.
- WHEN a stale detail is superseded, THE ORIGINAL SHALL remain readable in the append-only log rather than being overwritten in place.

When a stale detail is replaced, the original stays readable in the append-only log rather than being overwritten in place.

## Trigger

When a skill states a refusal that the code does not enforce, I want a gate to compare the claim against the flag tables, so I can stop a false claim from reaching a dispatched agent.

## The defect

The `work-tracker` skill carried **three** false statements at once (basicly-7wlhlp), each describing a refusal the code does not make. Every gate in the repository was green throughout. Skill prose is projected, linted for format, and checked for drift against its own source — and never checked against the behaviour it describes.

This is the population a green suite protects least: the consumer is a dispatched agent, so a false claim is not confusion, it is a lane that follows a wrong instruction and files no bug about it. One of the three told the reader that every labelling instruction is false, which would make an agent refuse `loop supervise --label`, the multi-lane path.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read `.basicly/core/skills/work-tracker/skill.yaml` before commit fbf844ba.
2. Note the Refuses section claims `update --add-label` raises, `create` without `--json` is refused, and the ready set is the open records.
3. Check each against `src/basicly/owned_write.py`, `src/basicly/tracker_write.py` and `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/differential.py`.
4. Run `uv run basicly verify --mode fast`, `uv run basicly skills-check --all-default-roots` and `uv run basicly catalog lint`.

Observed: all three claims are false, and every gate reports PASS.
Expected: a claim a skill makes about a refusal is checked against the table that implements it.

## The control that would have caught all three

Proposed by the lane that fixed them. `.scripts/docs_claims.py` already carries the mechanism: an `Assertion` that reads a catalog source and fails when it disagrees with an engine symbol. `_skill_work_types` is the working example, and `tests/test_docs_claims.py` has its anchor-vanished test.

Add an assertion that parses the skill's refusal section and fails when it names an `update` flag that `tracker_argv.UPDATE_LABEL_FLAGS` or `tracker_argv.UPDATE_FIELD_FLAGS` actually translates. That binds the prose to the tables whose change made it false, costs nothing per run, and is a deterministic gate rather than a judged one — which the standing constraints prefer.

## The scope question this raises, and does not answer

34 skills ship. This audited one. Whether the other 33 carry the same class of residue is **unmeasured**, and a per-skill hand audit does not scale. The generalisable form is: a skill that states a refusal names the symbol that implements it, and the gate checks the pair. That is a catalog-schema change, and it is larger than this record. Decide the narrow gate first and let its firing history argue for the general one.

## Scope

- `.scripts/docs_claims.py`
- `tests/test_docs_claims.py`

When the pre-fix text of a false claim is restored, the gate fails; when the corrected text is in place, the gate passes. When a skill has no refusal section, the gate passes without error.

## Trigger

When the harness drives its full loop in a consumer repository, I want no third-party product to sit in the runtime path, so I can upgrade our own state on our own schedule.

## Context

**Corrected 2026-07-30 after the owner sharpened the criterion.** The first version of this epic
read the directive as "zero runtime dependencies" and set out to remove `jinja2`, `jsonschema`,
`pyyaml`, `rich`, `uv`, the pre-commit framework and node. That was wrong, and the correction
matters because it removes a large breaking change from the roadmap.

The axis is not external-versus-internal, nor binary-versus-package. It is:

> **Can we absorb this component's breaking change on our own schedule, or does it dictate terms
> to us?**

A **library or framework** is fine. It is versioned, we pin it, and when it ships a breaking
change we upgrade when ready and fix our own code. The blast radius is our source.

A **product** is not. `beads` is the case in point, and the evidence is already recorded in
`docs/design/work-tracker.md` section 2.10: crossing one of its schema migrations requires
*"exactly one designated clone"* to run `bd migrate` and `bd dolt push` while every other clone
installs the new binary and runs `bd bootstrap`. That is a coordinated, human-sequenced,
multi-machine operation sitting in our critical path. Worse, the upgrade is sometimes not
available at all: br's current main targets schema 17 and its reviewed migration accepts only
13-to-17 and 14-to-17, so a 0.2.19 database has no supported path forward from schema 16. A
dependency we cannot upgrade, and cannot decline to upgrade, is not a dependency we manage.

The compounding factor is that beads owns **our state** - every phase derivation, gate,
checkpoint, dependency edge, decision and run record. A library that owns no state can be swapped
in an afternoon; a product that owns the state cannot be swapped at all without a migration.

## The rule

**No third-party product may own basicly's state.** Libraries and frameworks are permitted and
pinned. An optional extension - existing skills, language or technology guidelines - is permitted
and must stay optional.

## Classification of every current dependency

| Component | Class | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `jinja2`, `jsonschema`, `pyyaml`, `ruamel.yaml`, `rich` | library | **Keep.** Pinned, semver, owns no state. The catalog stays YAML - the stdlib-has-no-YAML-parser problem is no longer forcing a move to TOML. |
| `uv` | tool | **Keep.** Versioned, replaceable, owns no state. |
| pre-commit framework | framework | **Keep.** Dispatches our hooks; owns no state. |
| node (markdownlint hook) | tool | **Keep**, but it is the weakest entry - it is the only one whose absence has actually broken a commit path on this machine, and it earns a re-examination on its own merits rather than under this rule. |
| Python 3.14+ | language runtime | **Keep.** Not a product. Whether the floor should drop is an adoption question, not this one. |
| **`br` / beads** | **product that owns our state** | **Remove.** This is the whole of the directive. Tracked by `basicly-vkh0`. |
| **`bv`** | **product** | **Remove.** Measured at 0 of 141 surfaces used (`basicly-vkh0.2`), so this is a deletion rather than a replacement. |

## Why this epic still exists rather than folding into vkh0

`vkh0` removes the one product we have. This epic is the **policy** that stops the next one
arriving, which is the part that outlives the migration: the rule above written down where an
agent proposing a dependency will read it, the classification kept current, and a gate that
refuses a new runtime dependency it cannot classify.

## Success Criteria

- The dependency rule is stated in the architecture reference, every current dependency is classified against it, `br` and `bv` are gone from the runtime path, and a check refuses a newly added runtime dependency that is not classifiable as a library or framework

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: When the harness loop runs end to end in a consumer repository, no third-party product is invoked or required. When a component is a library or a framework, it stays pinned and declared, and it owns no state. When a new runtime dependency is added without a recorded classification, a gate fails.

## Trigger

When a managed hook script is projected for Copilot or for Claude, I want both families to share one interpreter policy, so I can keep Copilot hooks working when the project environment is broken.

## Context

Found by the lane-C survey 2026-08-14.

```text
hooks.py:158            uv run python <script>                 copilot
claude_settings.py:191  uv run --no-project ... python <script>  claude
```

The rationale at `claude_settings.py:191-192` says every managed hook script is stdlib only, so none of them needs the project environment. That reasoning applies to both families equally.

## Consequence

A consumer with a broken project virtual environment loses their Copilot hooks and keeps their Claude hooks. The two families gate unevenly for a reason nobody chose.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/hooks.py`
- `src/basicly/claude_settings.py`
- their tests

## Trigger

When a lane declares a scope glob that covers a configured append-only path, I want the preflight report to recognize that coverage the same way the landing does, so I can stop a false `contend:` line.

## Context

Found by the lane-B survey 2026-08-14.

```text
contention.py:61   path not in scopes.get(lane, ())     literal string membership
merge.py:942       merge._scope_covers                  decompose.globs_overlap
```

So a lane that declares `docs/**` or `*.md` covers a configured append-only `CHANGELOG.md` at the landing, and the preflight counts it as a lane that contends without declaring.

## Why it matters despite being advisory

Nothing refuses on this surface. The cost is a false `contend:` line. This repository records that an advisory `contend:` line is a finding an operator acts on: one such line named the exact collision under a green verdict and four hand-resolved rebases followed. A false one spends the same attention.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read the two scope tests side by side:

       rg -n 'path not in scopes.get' src/basicly/contention.py
       rg -n -A8 'def _scope_covers' src/basicly/merge.py

   `contention.append_only_report` asks `path not in scopes.get(lane, ())` - literal string
   membership against the lane's declared entries. `merge._scope_covers` asks
   `decompose.globs_overlap(path, glob)`. A lane declaring `docs/**` or `*.md` satisfies the
   second and fails the first.
2. Note the report is inert on this repo as configured, so the case has to supply a path:

       rg -n '^append_only_paths' basicly.toml

   Observed 2026-08-19: `append_only_paths = []`, and `append_only_report` returns its
   "no append-only path declared" line for an empty list before it reaches the membership
   test. So the reproduction belongs in `tests/test_contention.py` against a fixture repo
   that configures `append_only_paths = ["CHANGELOG.md"]`, not against this checkout.
3. In that fixture, give two lanes a `## Scope`: one declaring the glob `*.md` on its own
   backticked line, one declaring nothing that covers `CHANGELOG.md`. Call
   `contention.append_only_report` with both lanes.
4. Read the returned lines.

Observed: both lanes appear in the `... lane(s) will each append to `CHANGELOG.md` and none
declares it` line, so the report names a lane that did declare it and the operator reads a
`contend:` line that is false.
Expected: the lane whose declared glob covers the path is excluded from the count, on the
same glob test the landing uses. The function's own docstring already states that intent -
"A lane that *declares* the path in its own `## Scope` is left out of the count" - so this is
the docstring's rule failing on a glob, not a behaviour change.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/contention.py`
- `tests/test_contention.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_contention.py -q` with a new case that declares `*.md` against `CHANGELOG.md`.
