## Trigger

When one session drives a single unit and another runs a multi-lane supervised pass, but both read the same 32,423-character `harness-loop` skill, I want two smaller skills split by job, so I can read only the half a session needs.

## CORRECTED 2026-08-13

One claim below is wrong. It says the harness-loop skill does not mention `--runner manual`.
**It does, at `harness-loop/skill.yaml:432`**, in an unrelated context (the band verdict). The
real gap is narrower and still real: `grep -i repair` over that skill returns **zero**, so
nothing in it warns that a failed landing briefs and dispatches a metered repair.

Sequencing, added from the same audit: do this split **before** `basicly-u2hl.42`, which is a
trigger-gated content rewrite of the same two skills. Splitting afterwards pays that rewrite
twice. The edge is now recorded.

---

## Context

`.basicly/core/skills/harness-loop/skill.yaml` is 32,423 characters - 2.3x the next largest
skill (`tool-br` at 14,084) and by far the most used (41 invocations, most recent
2026-08-13).

It covers two separable jobs: driving one unit with `loop run`/`loop advance`, and running a
multi-lane pass with `loop preflight`/`loop supervise` including the band table, grant
sizing, and lane watching. A session doing one never needs the other.

It is also incomplete in a way that cost real time on 2026-08-13: nothing in it warns that
`loop advance` dispatches a metered repair agent when the previous landing gate failed. That
gap produced an unbudgeted `claude -p` dispatch against a spent grant, and the fix is
`--runner manual`, which the skill does not mention.

## Proposed check

Two skills, each under the size of the current one, with no duplicated section; the
multi-lane half names the repair dispatch and `--runner manual`. `basicly skills-check
--all-default-roots` passes and the usage counter shows both reachable.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: The single-lane content (`loop run`/`loop advance`) and the multi-lane content (`loop preflight`/`loop supervise`, band table, grant sizing, lane watching) shall live in two skills, each smaller than the current combined one, with no duplicated section. The multi-lane skill shall name that a failed landing dispatches a metered repair agent and that `--runner manual` avoids an unbudgeted dispatch.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- [ ] Two skill directories exist where one existed: one for single-lane driving, one for multi-lane supervision.
- [ ] Neither skill repeats a section found in the other.
- [ ] The multi-lane skill states that `loop advance` dispatches a metered repair agent on a failed landing gate, and names `--runner manual`.
- [ ] `basicly skills-check --all-default-roots` passes and the usage counter shows both skills reachable.

## Trigger

When `worktree-isolation` and `tier-injection` are consumer-facing skills with no distinguishing technology, and both always project into this repo's own listing and spend budget unused here, I want a way to ship a skill to consumers without projecting it locally, so I can free that budget for skills this repo actually uses.

## Context

Skill projection is gated only by `technologies:` detection: `tool-starship`, `tool-tmux`,
`tool-wezterm`, `tool-zsh` and `wsl` are in `.basicly/core/skills/` and are not projected
into `.claude/skills/` here, because their technology is not detected.

There is no way to express "ship this skill to consumer repos but do not project it in
basicly" for a skill with no distinguishing technology. Two skills need exactly that:

- `worktree-isolation` - the engine provisions worktrees itself at classify approval, so the
  skill is redundant here, but a consumer repo not running the loop still needs it.
- `tier-injection` - its own description is about installing a kit "in another repository",
  so it is consumer-facing by definition.

Both currently project here and are never used.

This is a budget question, not tidiness. Both are `invocation: model`, so both carry a
description and both occupy the host's model-invoked listing. Measured 2026-08-13: that
listing is 1,696 tokens against a 2,000-token budget (`catalog_lint.py:313-322`, 1% of the
adapter-default window) - 304 tokens of headroom. Two unreachable-here skills are spending
part of it, and the host evicts descriptions least-invoked-first when it overflows, so the
skills paying the cost are the first to be silenced.

## Proposed check

An opt-out declared in the catalog source or `basicly.toml`, verified by a test that builds
the projection and asserts the named skill is absent from `.claude/skills/` while still
present in the distributed catalog.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: The catalog source format or `basicly.toml` shall support a per-skill opt-out from local projection while the skill still ships in the distributed catalog. A test shall build the projection and assert the named skill is absent from `.claude/skills/` while present in the distributed catalog. `worktree-isolation` and `tier-injection` shall use the opt-out once it exists.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- [ ] The catalog source format or `basicly.toml` accepts a per-skill opt-out from local projection.
- [ ] A test builds the projection and asserts `worktree-isolation` and `tier-injection` are absent from `.claude/skills/`.
- [ ] The same test asserts both skills remain present in the distributed catalog output.
- [ ] `catalog_lint.py`'s model-invoked listing token count (measured 1,696/2,000) drops once the two skills stop projecting here.

## Trigger

When a consumer already lints markdown with their own hook, and basicly's projected markdownlint hook then runs a second time or silently no-ops beside it, I want the upgrade to say so or detect it, so I can avoid a duplicate or dark gate nobody notices.

## Context

Consequence of declaring markdownlint as a node-gated hook in v0.12.2 (basicly-vdlio8i), reported by burndown-chart from a real upgrade. Their .pre-commit-config.yaml now carries their own markdownlint-cli hook reading .markdownlint.json and ours running markdownlint-cli2, over the same files with two rule sets. Both pass, so nothing is broken - but ours no-ops in their tree because markdownlint-cli2 is absent, so the gate that passes is not the gate enforcing anything. Preserving their foreign hook is correct and they are not asking us to change that. What is missing is the notice: v0.12.1 to v0.12.2 is where the second gate silently appears, and the upgrade notes say nothing. Either say it in the notes, or have install name an existing markdown linter the way it now names a linter or secret scanner reaching into the managed core.

Detection, if built, shall cover a linter invoked from inside a consumer's own hook script, not only a `.pre-commit-config.yaml` entry. ## Trigger

When the harness branch's creation moves to INTAKE and dispatch moves to the host runtime, I want `harness-loop` and `worktree-isolation` updated to match, so I can stop a reader trusting a skill that has quietly stopped describing the code.

## Context

Audited 2026-08-09 against the seven decisions taken that day. Both skills are **correct as
written today** and both go stale the moment D32 and D27 are implemented. Filed so the coupling
is not rediscovered by a reader who trusts a skill that has quietly stopped describing the code.

- `worktree-isolation` documents provisioning on `harness/<name>`, which is what `loop.py:327`
  does: the branch and the worktree are created on entry to BUILD. D32 moves branch creation to
  INTAKE, because INTAKE, CLASSIFY and DECOMPOSE all emit artifacts before any worktree exists.
- `harness-loop` is the runbook for driving the loop and carries 14 dispatch references. D27
  makes the host runtime the thing that spawns a role, with the engine supervising lanes rather
  than processes, and D28 replaces the blanket no-agent-spawns-agents rule with a
  roster-bounded one gated by host hooks. D32 also adds `.factory/<issue>/` as where a state's
  artifact is written and read.

## Why this is not doable now

Rewriting either skill today would make it describe a factory that does not exist. That is the
same failure as authoring a skill with no invoker, applied to documentation - and this repo has
paid for a stale document being believed over working code twice in one session.

## Background

## Trigger

When a checkpoint's answered wait time fuses arrival latency and reading time into one fused number, I want a marker for when the operator first views the checkpoint, so I can separate arrival from comprehension in the wait report.

## Context

OQ-15, accepted for settling 2026-08-09.

policy.py:2293 writes a `[harness-wait]` marker when the ENGINE asks and closes it when the answer
arrives. Measured over 129 human-answered checkpoints: median 95s, p25 12s, p90 2090s, max 29012s,
with 17 events over 30 minutes carrying 85% of the 40.5h total - two of them answered in the same
second, and one waited 29012s while the next decision from the same human took 81s.

So the interval is rendezvous, not reading, and arrival latency and comprehension are fused in one
number. That is why factory-loop section 7.4 records the rendered-artifact question as unestablished
rather than refuted.

## Scope

One field: a marker written when the operator first VIEWS a checkpoint, so wait decomposes into
arrival and comprehension. CONFIRM_TTL_SECONDS is 900, so a view event also tells us how often a
challenge has already expired by the time anyone reads it.

## Why it is worth one field

It decides a whole class of proposals - any rendered or restructured checkpoint artifact - that
cannot otherwise be evaluated. The single datum on the other side is wait-decompose, the only
checkpoint with a real artifact to read, at 2490s and n=1.

## Demonstration

A checkpoint answered after a delay records three timestamps, and the wait report separates arrival
from comprehension on real data rather than on a fixture.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: A checkpoint shall record a first-view timestamp, distinct from when it was created and when it was answered. The wait report shall print an arrival portion and a reading portion, using -1 rather than 0 when a view was never measured. The view stamp shall be written when the challenge is printed to the operator, and kept machine-local rather than committed to the shared ledger.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- [ ] A checkpoint answered after a delay records three timestamps: created, first viewed, and answered.
- [ ] `basicly loop status` prints a wait line split into time before anyone looked and time reading, only when a view was measured.
- [ ] An unmeasured view is recorded as -1, never 0, and excluded from the reading-time average.
- [ ] The view stamp is written under the machine-local, gitignored usage directory, not the tracker ledger.
- [ ] The change lands within the module-size ratchet for `policy.py` and `tests/test_policy.py` without a renewed waiver.

## Trigger

When an in-dispatch termination gate relies on a Stop hook that returns decision block, I want to measure how many consecutive blocks one headless dispatch honours, so I can bound the gate by the limit our dispatch actually gets rather than by the documentation.

## Context

OQ-16, accepted for settling 2026-08-09.

Established: a `Stop` hook returning `decision: block` fires and continues the turn under our own
`claude -p` dispatch. Two firings observed on 2.1.226, stop_hook_active moving false to true.

Not established: whether many iterations are reachable, or only the documented override after 8
consecutive blocks.

## Why it must be measured before anything is designed on it

It bounds any in-dispatch termination gate to 8 turns per dispatch. A gate designed for unbounded
iteration that silently stops at 8 is a control that looks like it binds and does not - the failure
shape this repo already names.

## Method

A hook that blocks unconditionally and counts its own firings to a file. Run one dispatch. Read the
count. Do not infer the limit from the documentation; the point is what our dispatch actually gets.

One cheap dispatch. Not to be run before the account usage window resets on 2026-08-12 unless the
budget says otherwise.

- [ ] A probe hook that blocks every Stop and counts its firings runs under one headless dispatch.
- [ ] The record carries the measured consecutive-block count, the agent version and the date.
- [ ] The record states whether the count matches the documented override after 8 blocks.

## Trigger

When the wait-ledger code in `policy.py` cannot move to its own module without its shared timestamp and comment helpers cycling the import graph, I want those helpers placed in a lower tier first, so I can extract the wait ledger and land the parked split.

## Context

basicly-u2hl.50 is DONE and PARKED on branch `harness/basicly-u2hl.50` (commit d59ddfa), behind a
module-size waiver that must die with this bead rather than be renewed.

## Why it is parked

The split adds ~1350 tokens to policy.py and ~1300 to tests/test_policy.py. Both were already many
times the 4000-token cap, so the ratchet's rule is "may only shrink". Trimming the change's own prose
recovered 178 tokens - the rest is code.

## The extraction, measured

The wait block in policy.py is 4739 tokens over 447 lines: WAIT_MARKER, WAIT_KINDS, WaitEvent,
wait_id_for_checkpoint, record_wait, record_first_view, _take_view, wait_events, WaitSummary,
_wall_clock_seconds, split_waits, session_wait_summary. Moving it takes policy.py from ~34000 to
~29300, under its frozen 32482.

## What blocks it, and it is a design call not a move

The block shares `_parse_ts`, `_add_comment` and `_now` with the rest of policy.py. A naive move
makes wait_ledger import policy while policy still imports the wait API, which cycles. Decide where
those three live first - most likely a lower tier alongside the other shared primitives, since
`.importlinter` declares an exhaustive layer stack and a new module must name its tier.

Note the test suite must split with it, or tests/test_policy.py stays over.

## Constraint

Do not renew the waiver. It names this bead as its expiry and says so in both files. A waiver that
survives its own extraction is how these two modules reached 34k and 37k.

## Demonstration

`uv run python .scripts/check_module_size.py` reports no waiver for policy.py or tests/test_policy.py
and both are under their frozen baselines; `uv run lint-imports` keeps both contracts; the branch
merges to main with the full suite green.

The wait-ledger block shall move out of `policy.py` and its test module. The module-size waiver for both files shall not be renewed.

## Trigger

When `basicly verify` only accepts `--mode` and cannot run one declared check by name, I want a `--only` option that runs exactly one declared check with its declared argv, so I can stop hand-rolling a check's argv and reporting a false finding.

## Retro proposal, not applied

Session 2026-09-12. Awaiting the owner decision; a retro finding is never self-applied.

## The incident, twice in one session
Asked whether the bandit gate covers `packages/`, I ran `bandit -q -c pyproject.toml -r src .scripts packages` and reported a failure. The declared check is `bandit -q -c pyproject.toml -r .scripts .basicly/core/hooks .basicly/core/kit`. My invented path list produced a finding the real gate does not have, and I retracted it.

The same shape had already happened with the kits: `uv run --project packages/basicly-tier` reported all three kits broken, because that path reads the source tree where `force-include` has not run. Also retracted.

## Root cause, and why it is not a discipline failure
There is no way to run one declared check. `basicly verify` takes `--mode`, not a check name, so the only route to "run just this gate" is to retype its argv from `basicly.toml` - or, as happened, to approximate it.

Measured on `.basicly/usage/tool-usage.json`: `bandit` 19 direct invocations, `vulture` 67, `pyright` 267, `lint-imports` 140. `verify` appears once. The tools are run directly essentially always, and every direct run is an argv nobody checked against the declared one.

The `core-rules` fragment already says the authority is the code that reads it, not the docs. The authority here is `basicly.toml`, and the harness offers no way to obey it.

## Proposal
`basicly verify --only <name>` runs exactly one `[[verify.checks]]` entry with its declared argv, and refuses an unknown name by listing the ones that exist.

## Why this rather than a hook
A guard on hand-rolled invocations would fire on 493 recorded calls, most of them legitimate narrowing. The cheaper fix is to make the correct path exist, so the improvisation has a named alternative.

## Scope
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: `basicly verify --only` shall run exactly the argv declared for the named `[[verify.checks]]` entry in `basicly.toml`. An unknown check name shall be refused with a list of the names that exist. The command shall exit with the check's own exit code.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- [ ] `basicly verify --only bandit` runs exactly the argv declared for the `bandit` entry in `basicly.toml`.
- [ ] `basicly verify --only` with an unknown name refuses and lists the known check names.
- [ ] The command's exit code matches the underlying check's exit code.
- [ ] A test in `tests/test_verify.py` asserts both the correct-name and unknown-name paths.

## Trigger

When the plan's section 5.2 row 11 asks for evidence on the `chars/4` token estimator, and two measurements disagree in an informative way, I want that band recorded where a test can check it, so I can back the plan's evidence claim without re-arguing the measurement.

`chars/4`, so `ca42` is parked (`deferred`) and its branch `harness/basicly-ca42` is not
landing.

What the plan's section 5.2 row 11 originally asked for was evidence, and two measurements
now exist and disagree in an informative way.

`basicly-u2hl.32` measured `chars/4` against tiktoken `o200k_base` per population:

```text
prose (skill bodies)              +1.6%
beads issue json                 -10.7%
run-record json                  -16.4%
run-record markdown headings     -28.9%
run-record tsv                   -39.5%
```

so `chars/4` is 2.02% **over** on code - refuting the bead's own prediction that code, being
structured text, would sit in the 10-40% under-counting band.

So the estimator is accurate on the populations the factory actually denominates in code and
prose, and badly wrong on serialized records. That is a narrower and better-supported claim
than either bead made alone, and it is the claim the docstring should carry.

the prohibition from `basicly-u2hl.32` on the one use the unit cannot support is retained
and named. A test asserts the recorded band matches a re-measurement on the fixtures.

## Trigger

When a board serve test fails about once with `served is not None` false, but repeat runs reproduce nothing, I want the test to print the board's failure state and the holder age at the point of failure, so I can find the real cause instead of guessing from one run.

## Observation
`tests/test_board_serve.py::test_a_stale_lock_hands_the_fold_back_to_the_viewer` failed inside the pre-push suite on 2026-09-12, refusing a docs-only push. The full suite had passed minutes earlier on the same tree.

```
assert None is not None
tests/test_board_serve.py:218: AssertionError
```

Line 218 is `assert served is not None`. Lines 215 and 216 passed, so `board.refresh()` had returned True and `board.refreshes` was 1.

## Not reproduced
Three runs of the test alone: pass. Three runs of the whole file under `-n 8`: 27 passed each time. Six attempts, zero reproductions.

## Hypothesis ruled out, recorded so nobody spends the same hour
The obvious read is a race between the two independent `live_holder` calls: `refresh` proceeds only when the holder is not live, and `payload` returns `_served` only when the holder is not live, otherwise reading a snapshot file that may not exist. That would explain a None.

It cannot happen. `live_holder` returns None once `age_s >= STALE_AFTER_S`, the test ages the lock to `STALE_AFTER_S + 1`, and an age only grows. The holder cannot become live between the two calls.

So `payload` returned `_served` and `_served` was None, while `refresh` had returned True on the branch that assigns it. Those two statements cannot both be true of one object, which is why this needs an instrument rather than another read.

## Suggested first step
Have the test print `board.failures`, `board._served is None` and the holder age at the point of failure, then leave it in the suite until it fires again. A cause guessed without a second observation is a guess.

## Why it matters
The pre-push suite is the gate before every push. A test that fails about once refuses work that is fine and trains people to re-run rather than read. This is the second timing-dependent test in this file: `basicly-gssz1qa` fixed a different one on 2026-09-12, which compared two pages against the clock.

## Scope
- `tests/test_board_serve.py`
- `src/basicly/board_serve.py`

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: The test shall print `board.failures`, whether `board._served` is None, and the holder age at the point of failure, and stay in the suite until it fires again. The already-ruled-out `live_holder` race hypothesis shall not be re-investigated without new evidence. Once the instrumented failure is captured, the real cause shall be fixed with a regression test.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- [ ] `test_a_stale_lock_hands_the_fold_back_to_the_viewer` prints `board.failures`, `board._served is None`, and the holder age when the assertion fails.
- [ ] The instrumentation stays in the test until the failure is captured at least once more.
- [ ] Once captured, the record names the real cause, distinct from the ruled-out `live_holder` race.
- [ ] A regression test pins the fix so the flake does not return.

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Trigger

When an agent declares a model tier and the host is Claude or Copilot, I want the spawned subagent to run on the model that tier resolves to on that host, so I can rely on a declared tier on both hosts the owner scoped in.

## Context

Filed 2026-07-31 after basicly-kjc5.58 landed. **Re-scoped the same day by the owner, who was right and
the first framing was wrong**: this is NOT claude-only. GitHub Copilot custom agents carry a per-agent
`model` field too, so at least claude AND copilot must be supported. Re-verified against live
authoritative docs rather than recall.

basicly-kjc5.59 is the resolution seam but its scope is `runner.py`/`run_record.py`/`config.py` - the
HEADLESS runner dispatch path, where a model is set by `_apply_model` via a `--model` flag or a
`{model}` placeholder. A natively spawned subagent never goes through that path: the host reads a
per-agent file and takes the model from frontmatter. basicly-kjc5.58 removed that line for every
family, so a declared tier is currently decorative for every natively spawned agent.

Concrete regression from kjc5.58, deliberate and known: the shipped `test-runner` declared
`model: haiku`, now declares `tier: low`, and `.claude/agents/test-runner.md` carries no model line, so
an agent whose own prose says "cheap and fast on purpose" inherits the session model on every spawn.
Verified: `rg '^model' .claude/agents/` matches nothing.

kjc5.58 was still right - the defect was a NON-PORTABLE value in a family-agnostic source. The fix is
to emit the resolved per-surface spelling, which is what basicly-kjc5.61's map must provide.

## Verified facts (live docs, 2026-07-31)

- **Claude Code** reads `.claude/agents/<slug>.md`; `model` takes a hyphenated id (`claude-haiku-4-5`)
  or a short alias (`haiku`), or `inherit`.
- **GitHub Copilot** custom agents live at `.github/agents/<name>.agent.md` (org/enterprise: root
  `agents/`). Frontmatter: `description` (required), `name`, `target` (`vscode`|`github-copilot`),
  `tools`, `model`, `disable-model-invocation`, `user-invocable`, `mcp-servers`, `metadata`; body
  capped at 30000 chars, which `agents.MAX_BODY_CHARS` already matches.
- **Copilot's `model` value is a DISPLAY NAME**, not an id - `Claude Opus 4.5`, `Claude Sonnet 4` -
  and it accepts **a single string OR a prioritized array** tried in order
  (`model: ['Claude Opus 4.5', 'GPT-5.2']`). Our schema cannot express an ordered fallback list today.
- **VS Code reads BOTH** `.github/agents` and `.claude/agents` ("VS Code also detects `.md` files in the
  `.claude/agents` folder, following the Claude sub-agents format"). So basicly-ajq's rationale holds
  for VS Code but NOT for the Copilot cloud agent or Copilot CLI, which do not read `.claude/agents`.
- Copilot `tools` names differ from Claude's and are inconsistent across sources
  (`["read","search","edit"]` in the VS Code doc vs `codebase`/`terminal`/`edit`/`github` elsewhere), so
  a copilot projection needs a pinned tool-name mapping, not a copy.

## Prerequisite

The copilot half has no target file today: basicly still projects to `.claude/agents` only. Reopening
that is filed separately and must land first for the copilot half. The claude half is unblocked once
kjc5.61 lands.

## Open design decision for the owner

Per surface, either resolve the tier to that surface's own spelling and emit it, or emit nothing and
record that the tier was not honoured (the stance kjc5.59 already takes where a family has no slot).
Recommendation: resolve and emit wherever the surface has a model slot, because that is the only case
in which the tier vocabulary changes real behaviour instead of documenting an intention.

Scope: `src/basicly/agents.py`, `.claude/agents/`, `tests/test_agents.py`.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: On Claude, a spawned subagent runs on the model its declared tier resolves to, with no model line in any projected agent file. On Copilot, the tier reaches the per-subagent config that basicly-u2hl.41 builds. A tier the map cannot resolve for a host is refused, and the refusal names the agent, the host and the tier.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When the tracker install offers to import a backlog from beads or beans, I want the storage layout, record format, id shape and detection markers of bd, br and beans established from their own sources, so I can build detection and import on facts rather than recall.

## Context

Read 2026-09-25 by a researcher from primary sources.

- bd (steveyegge/beads, now gastownhall/beads, main 3c30a28d, release v1.3.0): the store is Dolt under .beads/embeddeddolt or .beads/dolt, not committed. .beads/issues.jsonl is an optional export, off by default (export.auto false); bd export writes JSONL to stdout or -o FILE. Markers: .beads/metadata.json, .beads/config.yaml, .beads/dolt or embeddeddolt. Statuses open, in_progress, blocked, deferred, closed, pinned, hooked. Parent links are parent-child dependency edges. Comment id is a string.
- br (Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust, main 565b43c8, release v0.7.0; installed br is 0.3.2): SQLite .beads/beads.db is local; .beads/issues.jsonl is the committed interchange file. No br export: br sync --flush-only writes it. Markers: .beads/ with metadata.json naming jsonl_export, config.yaml (issue_prefix), beads.db. Extra statuses draft, tombstone. Comment id is an integer. br writes absolute paths in source_repo_path, so an import must scrub it.
- bd and br share the core fields and the dependency edge shape {issue_id, depends_on_id, type, created_at, created_by, metadata, thread_id} that our importer already reads (migrate.py).
- beans (hmans/beans, main 99260bf1, release v0.4.2): .beans.yml at the root plus one committed Markdown file per bean under .beans/ and .beans/archive/, file name id--slug.md. YAML frontmatter keys title, status, type, priority, tags, created_at, updated_at, order, parent, blocking, blocked_by; the body is the Markdown after the frontmatter; the id comes from the file name. Statuses in-progress, todo, draft, completed, scrapped; types milestone, epic, bug, feature, task; priorities critical, high, normal, low, deferred. No export command; beans list --json --full gives JSON with the same keys.
- Not established: a real bd export line with edges and comments; the br 0.7.0 flag list; how bd deletes; the beans GraphQL schema.
payload.requirements: Every claim names its source and the version read.
payload.title: research spike: where bd, br and beans keep a backlog and how to detect and read it

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a consumer repo installs basicly, I want it to receive one reviewed `.claude/settings.json` baseline, and basicly to dogfood the same file, so every repo gets the same permission and config posture instead of a hand-copied variant that drifts.

## Context

`basicly permissions-build` and `hooks-build` already co-own four parts of `.claude/settings.json` (`src/basicly/claude_settings.py`): the managed `permissions.deny` list from `.basicly/core/permissions/permissions.yaml`, the managed agent hooks, `worktree.bgIsolation`, and `subagentPromptCacheTtl`. Everything else is hand-authored per repo. A review of the settings files across the housed repos of one workspace on 2026-09-25 found:

- basicly and one consumer (terminal) carry a hand-copied blanket `permissions.allow` of `Bash`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `WebSearch`, `WebFetch`. In default or acceptEdits mode that runs every shell command unprompted, so the prefix-anchored deny list is the only check (see basicly-ejowvgn, basicly-tcmy.40). In auto mode the classifier still reviewed a Bash call in a repo with that allow, so the entry adds no value there.
- The consumers drifted: terminal adds `ask: ["Bash(git push *)"]` and denies `git rebase*`. basicly does not.
- basicly and terminal set `includeCoAuthoredBy: false`, which is deprecated in favour of `attribution`.
- In one consumer (burndown-chart) a blanket `*.json` rule in `.gitignore` ignores `.claude/settings.json`, so its projected hooks and deny list are not versioned. `permissions-check` and `hooks-check` pass locally and say nothing.
- `.claude/settings.local.json` in basicly and terminal has accumulated one-off allows with absolute scratchpad and worktree paths, plus broad entries (`Bash(git *)`, `Bash(uv run *)`, `Bash(python3 -)`).
- Auto mode trust (`autoMode.environment`) lives in user settings. The one shipped by hand names only basicly as trusted, has no `$defaults` entry in `environment`, and makes every other repo of the same owner look external.

## Proposed baseline (projected, co-owned keys only)

- `permissions.deny`: unchanged source (`permissions.yaml`), plus the entries from basicly-tcmy.40.
- `permissions.ask`: a new managed list, first entry `Bash(git push*)`, sourced from the same catalog file as deny.
- `permissions.allow`: basicly projects no blanket tool allow. It either projects nothing, or a small scoped list of read-only commands. The existing blanket entries are removed from basicly's own file.
- `attribution` replaces `includeCoAuthoredBy`, keeping the object form so older clients still load the file.
- Existing co-owned keys stay: hooks, `worktree.bgIsolation`, `subagentPromptCacheTtl`.
- `permissions-check` refuses when `git check-ignore .claude/settings.json` matches, and names the ignore rule and the negation line that fixes it.
- Auto mode: optional, opt-in `--user` step (like `install_hook.py --user`). It prints or merges an `autoMode` block that keeps `$defaults` in every section and trusts the repo's forge owner, not one repo. Verify first which settings sources Claude Code reads `autoMode` from (interface-facts); do not project it into project settings if Claude Code ignores it there.

## Out of scope

`settings.local.json` stays user-owned. A lint that only warns on absolute paths or broad allows there is a possible follow-up.
payload.requirements:
- The ask list and the deny list stay in one catalog file. The projection reads that file and never copies it.
- Keys a consumer authored by hand outside the managed set stay untouched; the merge is additive, like `merge_permission_deny`.
- Commit no machine path, user name or host name into the projected file.
payload.title: Ship one reviewed Claude settings.json baseline to consumers and dogfood it

## Trigger

When a person runs Claude Code in auto mode in a repository that basicly installed, I want the shipped permission rules to work in that mode, so I can work without prompts for routine read and check commands.

## Context

Request from terminal's owner, 2026-09-25, checked against code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes and /auto-mode-config the same day. Today .claude/settings.json ships a blanket Bash, Edit and Write allow plus 25 deny rules, and only the deny list is projected. In auto mode, broad rules that grant arbitrary code execution are dropped: blanket Bash(*), wildcarded interpreters, package-manager run commands, Agent and Monitor rules. Narrow rules stay and resolve before the classifier. An ask rule always prompts. Project settings cannot carry autoMode, so the trust context lives only in ~/.claude/settings.json or managed settings. /auto-mode-setup writes autoMode.environment without $defaults by design, and on this machine that list names basicly as the only trusted repo; after 3 blocks in a row or 20 in total, auto mode pauses. Proposals: (a) project the whole permissions block with narrow allows and no blanket Bash; (b) a user-level check of autoMode.environment; (c) not a basicly defect.
payload.requirements: Every shipped rule has an effect in the mode it is meant for.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When install runs over an existing `.claude/settings.json` with uncommitted or untracked content, a `.basicly-bak` copy equal to the old bytes exists afterwards, and install prints its path.
- When the file is malformed JSON, install exits non-zero, names the file and the parse position, and writes nothing.
- When the file carries a user-authored key, a user hook and `includeCoAuthoredBy: false`, afterwards the key and hook are unchanged, `attribution` holds the equivalent value, and `includeCoAuthoredBy` is gone.
- When `settings.local.json` carries an absolute path or a blanket allow, install lists the finding and the file's bytes are unchanged.
- When `--dry-run` runs, it prints the key-level summary and no file changes.
payload.description:
## Trigger

When `basicly install` runs in a repo that already has `.claude/settings.json` (or `settings.local.json`), I want to merge the baseline into it by a written rule and keep a restorable copy of the old file, so I can install into an existing repo without losing or silently changing its settings.

## Context

Today `permissions-build` and `hooks-build` merge additively into `.claude/settings.json` (`merge_permission_deny`, `merge_agent_hooks` in `src/basicly/claude_settings.py`) and keep no copy. The `.basicly-bak` backups cover scaffold files and untracked projected files only (`cli.py` `SCAFFOLD_BACKUP_SUFFIX`, `projection.back_up_unrecognised`). A malformed settings file is not refused by name: probed 2026-09-25 in a scratch repo, `sync_permission_deny` raises `JSONDecodeError` on a trailing comma, and `cmd_permissions_build` has no handler for it.

## Merge rule, per key

- Managed lists (`permissions.deny`, `permissions.ask`): union, existing entries kept, order kept.
- Managed hooks: replaced by script identity, as today; a user hook on the same event stays.
- `permissions.allow`: kept. Install reports an entry that makes a managed rule moot (a blanket `Bash`, `Edit` or `Write`; an allow that equals a managed `ask` entry) and does not delete it.
- Deprecated keys (`includeCoAuthoredBy`): migrated to `attribution` with the same meaning, and the old key removed.
- Any key basicly does not own: left byte-for-byte as it was.
- `settings.local.json`: never written. Install lists findings only: absolute paths, user or host names, broad allows (`Bash(git *)`, `Bash(uv run *)`, `Bash(python3 -)`), and allows that override a managed `ask`.

## Backup

Before the first write that changes an existing `.claude/settings.json`, install writes `.claude/settings.json.basicly-bak`, unless the file is tracked and has no uncommitted change (git holds that copy). Install prints the backup path and a key-level summary of what changed. `--dry-run` prints the same summary and writes nothing.
payload.requirements:
- One merge function owns the rule. `permissions-build`, `hooks-build` and install call it; none copies it.
- A regression test covers each per-key rule and the malformed-file refusal.
payload.title: Merge the baseline into an existing Claude settings file by rule and keep a restorable copy

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a coding agent installs basicly into a repo, I want it to analyse the repo's existing agent settings before it merges anything, so I can get a merge fitted to what the repo already relies on, and not a mechanical union the agent cannot explain.

## Context

basicly has an agent install prompt for the tracker package only (`packages/basicly-tracker/README.md#install-with-a-coding-agent`, linked from README.md). Nothing guides an agent through installing basicly itself. The mechanical rule in basicly-f002zye cannot judge intent: whether a blanket allow is deliberate, whether a hand-added `ask` or deny (for example terminal's `git rebase*` deny) should stay, or whether `settings.local.json` entries are stale.

## Shape

- An agent install prompt (README section plus a skill) that runs, in order:
  1. `basicly install --dry-run --json`: a machine-readable plan per file and key, so the agent does not parse prose. This needs the `--json` form.
  2. Read `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, the `.gitignore` rules for both, and the user-level `autoMode` block (read only).
  3. Classify every existing entry: kept as is, superseded by a managed entry, conflicts with a managed entry, risky (blanket allow, interpreter allow, absolute path), or stale (points at a path that no longer exists).
  4. Show the user one table of the entries it plans to change and why, with the proposed merged file as a diff. Wait for approval before it removes or narrows any user entry, or edits an ignore file.
  5. Run `basicly install`, then `permissions-check` and `hooks-check`, and report the backup path from basicly-f002zye.
- The agent never edits user-level settings. For auto mode it prints the proposed `autoMode` block (with `$defaults`) for the user to apply. The classifier refuses that edit as self-modification (observed 2026-09-25).
payload.requirements:
- The classification uses the same merge rule as basicly-f002zye. The prompt reads the `--json` plan; it does not restate the rule.
- Validate it as a consumer: a scratch repo seeded with the settings shapes from the parent record (blanket allow, ignored settings file, stale local allows).
payload.title: Guide an agent-driven install to analyse existing Claude settings before merging

payload.description:
## Trigger

When an agent works a multi-item goal for a person, I want the harness to make elapsed time visible and to scale the verification cost to the size of the step, so I can see progress at a pace that matches the urgency and not wait on ceremony.

## Context

Owner feedback 2026-09-30, during the standalone tracker goal: 'I am not sure why it takes so long' and 'the harness should also have a sense of time and urgency'. Measured in that session: the full suite ran 9 times at about 4m45s each (about 43 minutes), mostly once before each commit and again after each gate refusal; six gate refusals (module-size, noqa-debt, the lane ceiling twice, markdownlint, pyright) each cost a re-run. No fragment or skill tells the agent to run the related tests while it iterates and the whole suite once per commit, and none asks it to report elapsed time against a goal.

payload.text: Owner 2026-09-30, restated: the harness must have a sense of time and urgency. A person pays for two things, time and inference (tokens). ## Trigger

When Codex is first used in this repository, I want its consent controls established before implementation, so I can evaluate worktree safety without exposing the checkout to unapproved changes.

- `.codex/config.toml`

- Routine workspace work stays automatic; dangerous operations require consent or refusal.
- Worktrees use the sibling repo.worktrees/name layout, support parallel lanes and preserve uncommitted or unlanded work.

payload.text:
Audit evidence, 2026-10-06. Installed repository-local Codex config and command rules; no application source changed. Codex CLI 0.160.1, Claude Code 2.1.291, Copilot CLI 1.0.91, Git 2.55.0. TOML parsed, six execpolicy probes passed, and codex sandbox executed true using basicly-consent. Restart is required for project rules to reach the active session. Project settings remain uncommitted and therefore do not yet inherit into newly created worktrees.

Verdict: retain checkout.worktrees/name placement. checkout.py:95-101 implements it for standard repositories. Parallel work requires one working checkout per lane, independent dependency environments, and coordinated shared-state operations. Native app-created worktrees need adoption/provisioning or an adapter; starting a client in an existing basicly-managed checkout is the simplest common workflow. No GUI client was exercised.

Confirmed defects: worktree.py:127-133 returns a FAILED hook message instead of refusing creation, and create persists the session anyway (scratch probe confirmed). worktree.py:136-189 creates the checkout before dependency provisioning, with no recovery/session saved on failure (scratch probe confirmed). A valid Git branch suffix nested/name reaches Git successfully but save_session fails because the metadata subdirectory is absent, leaving an unregistered checkout (scratch probe confirmed). worktree.py:165-170 automatically reads and copies .env.local without a consent flag; no real repository dotenv file was opened for this audit. save_session uses a non-atomic write, cap_refusal reads a count separately from creation, and create/cleanup have no lifecycle mutex or active-user lease. merge.py:347 locks tracker commits; merge_worktree and _merge_and_prove do not hold a repository lock around the landing. Serial iteration within one queue is not coordination between independent clients. base_lock.py:hold_file can steal on age alone, without proving the holder dead. Cleanup preserves unlanded branch content and refuses dirty/unknown status, but uses git worktree remove --force after a status read that omits ignored files, leaving a deletion race and ignored-data policy gap. main_checkout assumes common-dir.parent is the base checkout, so separate Git directories/bare layouts require either support or explicit refusal.

Agent parity: runner.py:142-149 and :393-401 force Codex workspace-write/never, overriding interactive approval defaults; current permission-profile docs establish that --sandbox also overrides default_permissions, losing profile-specific dotenv restrictions. Shared tracker redirect writes from a sibling lane reach outside its working root and require a narrowly scoped permission strategy. Permission projection targets only Claude (permissions.py:14-15); permissions-check passing does not cover the newly installed Codex floor. Command prefixes cannot reproduce Claude infix globs, filesystem deny-read glob expansion has a depth bound (configured 16), and CLI overrides remain stronger than repository defaults. Shared confirmation instructions continue to apply to unmatched variants.

Current sources: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-basic ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/rules ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/permissions ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-approvals-security ; https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses ; https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/sessions/manage-sessions ; https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/use-copilot-cli/allowing-tools . Architecture section 18 falsely says Codex cannot set project sandbox/approval defaults; current official documentation refutes it. Worktree-isolation skill claim that Codex has no equivalent native worktree facility is stale relative to installed codex --worktree.

Verification: pytest tests/test_worktree.py tests/test_permissions.py tests/test_permissions_allow.py: 122 passed. pytest tests/test_merge.py tests/test_runner.py: 272 passed. permissions-check passed for its managed Claude list. Full suite,

## Trigger

When the engine completes reviewed tracker work, I want actual matching check results recorded before closure or teardown, so I can complete integrated work without bypassing shared C3 confirmation or losing recoverable work.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/process_confirmation.py`

## Delivery

Use the shared process_evidence contract owned by basicly-hxagpn8. Read current reviewed criterion/check mappings; only actual successful CheckResult argv or recorded executed validator command results that exactly match a planned command can populate confirmation. A broad boolean verification pass does not prove every criterion. Preserve matched actual output and named missing checks; refuse closure before worktree cleanup when evidence is missing. Cover both _on_ship and _run_subtask closures. The separate process owner handles policy.kill_lane cancellation. No invented outcomes, no model guesses, no gate bypass. Direct isolated implementation authorized; final integrated suite owned by controller.

- `.importlinter` declares the new confirmation adapter at its actual dependency layer.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When coding agents work in parallel, I want worktrees that are commissioned, used and decommissioned by one agent-agnostic process, so I can parallelize, merge and see all work safely and fast.

## Owner rules (2026-10-07)

1. Working with worktrees is agnostic of the coding agent.
2. Worktrees live in a sibling folder of the repository, at the same level as the repository folder.
3. Worktrees are never inside the repository (for example under .claude), because they interfere with the CI gates.
4. Worktrees enable a high level of parallel work.
5. A worktree is commissioned, worked in, and decommissioned (deleted and cleaned up) when its work is complete.
6. A worktree lives only until its work is merged back into the branch that created it (usually main, possibly another feature branch).
7. Worktree work is secure, stable, transparent and fast.

The harness needs solid parallelization, merging, transparency, orchestration, coordination, idempotency and agent agnosticity.

## Evidence (measured 2026-10-07)

- git worktree list: 11 live harness worktrees; git merge-base --is-ancestor shows 9 of 11 branches already merged into main and never decommissioned (rule 5, rule 6).
- basicly worktree create refused: concurrency cap reached (11/10 live), so parallel work stopped (rule 4).
- Claude Code auto-mode denied basicly worktree cleanup of two merged, clean worktrees as irreversible local destruction, so decommissioning needs a manual permission (rule 5, rule 7).
- The sibling folder is named basicly.worktrees; the owner wrote <repo>.worktree. Confirm the name (rule 2).
- Memory note: the Agent tool isolation:worktree checks out inside the repository and poisons whole-tree gates (rule 3); basicly worktree bg-isolation exists for it.
payload.requirements:
- Audit src/basicly/worktree.py, the worktree-isolation skill and the loop landing against each of the seven rules, and record a pass or fail with evidence per rule.
- Keep refusal of unmerged or dirty worktrees; never delete unmerged work.
- No dependency changes.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When any clone folds pending shards after a pull, I want the fold to move the shards into the trunk unchanged, so I can pull on every machine without a local commit that rewrites history.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a consumer repository (terminal, basicly v0.20.2 via uvx), git pull on a second machine. The generated post-merge block basicly-tracker compact runs basicly tracker fold.
2. The fold commits chore(tracker): fold pending writer shards into the trunk log, and main is ahead of origin by 1 on every pull.
3. Besides moving pending-main.jsonl into events-0001.jsonl, the commit rewrites 8 existing trunk events: the local machine username in payload fields such as created_by and in prose becomes the machine-username redaction marker, and each event gets a new id (record term-f0z: origin id ev-c78faed0f8, local fold ev-4903f67ebd). The fold diff is +536/-536 lines.

Cause (read in code): basicly tracker fold commits through merge.commit_tracker_state, which calls tracker.scrub_ledger (src/basicly/merge.py:360). scrub_ledger rewrites every ledger file with the redaction of the host that runs it and re-mints the ids of changed events. The same scrub refuses with does-not-re-mint when an event sits in two shards (seen 2026-10-08 in basicly, basicly-jho04rg).

Reported 2026-10-08 by the owner from the terminal repository; reproduced twice there.

payload.description:
Measured on basicly 0.21.5 (basicly-tracker 0.2.1) on 2026-10-09, in a beads (br) migration from a user install on WSL. The import damaged the notes of 6 records and redacted a literal C:\ example in a description.

Cause: beads.py rule windows-drive-path is [A-Za-z]:\\ plus a path tail. Notes that hold the two characters backslash-n after a colon, such as "provision_lefthook.py:\n1.", match it. A real line break does not match.

Reproduction (scratch ledger, basicly-tracker from tag v0.21.5):
1. Write a beads JSONL record with notes "see provision_lefthook.py:\\n1. PINNED_VERSION" (JSON-escaped, so the text holds a backslash and n).
2. basicly-tracker import <ledger> <export>; then show the record.
Observed: notes = "see provision_lefthook.p<redacted:windows-drive-path> PINNED_VERSION". The y, the backslash-n and "1." are gone.
3. A description "Use a literal C:\ path as an example." imports as "Use a literal <redacted:windows-drive-path> path as an example."
4. basicly-tracker update <ledger> <id> --field "description=see provision_lefthook.py:\n1. PINNED_VERSION and <redacted:windows-drive-path>" keeps the text unchanged, including <redacted:windows-drive-path>

Expected: one redaction rule for both write paths. The import keeps text that is not a real path, or flags a real path and keeps the text around it.
payload.title: Import redaction reads a literal backslash-n after a colon as a Windows drive path

payload.description:
Measured on basicly 0.21.5 (basicly-tracker 0.2.1) on 2026-10-09, in a beads (br) migration from a user install on WSL. A caller that forgets the record id reinstalls the kit. Agents also see the tracker skill twice.

Reproduction (scratch HOME, scratch git repo, basicly-tracker 0.2.1 installed with uv tool install from tag v0.21.5 into a scratch tool dir on PATH):
1. basicly-tracker update (no arguments) runs the installer: it edits .gitattributes and .gitignore, creates .basicly/ledger, pins the ledger and wires commit-msg. It exit 0.
2. basicly-tracker update <ledger> <record> --field ... updates a record. The same verb has two meanings, chosen by the argument count.
3. The first installer run wrote the user skill to ~/.claude/skills/basicly-tracker/SKILL.md and ~/.agents/skills/basicly-tracker/SKILL.md, and also wrote .claude/skills/tracker/SKILL.md and .agents/skills/tracker/SKILL.md in the repository. Both descriptions end with the same trigger sentence: "Use when a task plans work, chooses what to do next, files, refines or closes a record, or writes a commit that must name a record id."
4. Control: without a user install on PATH, update (no arguments) refuses and installs nothing; update <ledger> with no record prints the record usage and exits 2.

Expected: separate verbs for the installer and the record update. The installer skips the repository skill, or offers an option to skip it, when the user skill is present.
payload.title: Basicly-tracker update both installs the kit and updates a record

payload.description:
Measured on basicly 0.21.5 (basicly-tracker 0.2.1) on 2026-10-09, in a beads (br) migration.

Cause: process_evidence.criteria strips only - and * bullets (_BULLET), so a "1. text" criterion keeps its number.

Reproduction (scratch ledger, basicly-tracker from tag v0.21.5):
1. create --acceptance "1. When a task is saved, show shall return its title.\n2. When a task is closed, list shall omit it." with a trigger and requirements; add one comment.
2. review --evidence with the criteria written without the numbers.
Observed: exit 1, "Confirmation Plan refused: no acceptance criterion reads When a task is saved, show shall return its title.; each check holds exactly the keys criterion, command, expected; command is an argv list".
3. review --evidence with "1. When a task ..." and "2. When a task ...". Observed: exit 0, accepted.

The refusal does not name the numbering as the cause. Its key-shape sentence (added in basicly-ywt4snr) also misleads here, because the keys are correct.

Expected: strip numbered list markers the same way as bullets, or name the numbering in the refusal. Print the key-shape sentence only when a key fault caused the refusal.
payload.title: Numbered acceptance criteria do not match the review criteria

payload.description:
Reported by the handily session on 2026-10-09, on the basicly 0.21.5 kit. Cost: 4 extra calls and a wrong diagnosis. Related: basicly-fl27qhx (numbered criteria).

Reproduction (scratch ledger, this repository kit at 0.21.5):
1. create with --acceptance as one paragraph of 5 sentences, a trigger and requirements; add one comment.
2. review --evidence with all 6 INVEST keys, conversation [the real comment seq] and 4 checks whose criterion paraphrases the sentences.
Observed: exit 1; stdout "Confirmation Plan refused: no acceptance criterion reads Saving a task shows its title.; each check holds exactly the keys criterion, command, expected; command is an argv list". It does not say that the record holds one criterion (the whole paragraph), and it does not list the parsed criteria.
3. claim. Observed: exit 1, "owes ## INVEST Review: independent, ... ## Conversation, ## Confirmation Plan". The INVEST and Conversation parts were supplied; a refused review records nothing, so claim lists every section without saying that no review is recorded.
4. update --help says only "--acceptance TEXT  the acceptance criteria a check is derived from". The parser reads one criterion per line (plain, - or * bullet), so a paragraph is one criterion.

Correction to the report: review does print its refusal on stdout on the failing exit.

Expected: (a) claim says that no current review is recorded, in place of listing supplied parts as owed; (b) a criterion mismatch lists the criteria the record holds; (c) the --acceptance help of create and update says one criterion per line.
payload.title: Review and claim refusals hide how acceptance criteria are parsed

payload.text: Second case, reported by the handily session 2026-10-09 (seen on handily-fwkt.8.14) and reproduced on the 0.21.5 kit: review a record (exit 0), then update --description, then claim. Observed: claim exit 1, "cannot start: it owes ## INVEST Review: independent, ... ## Conversation, ## Confirmation Plan; an agent reviews it and fills the missing detail first". The cause is that the new revision voided the recorded review, and the message does not say so. Expected: name the void review and the field change that voided it, then say to run review again. Same family as the refused-review case: claim cannot tell "never reviewed", "review refused" and "review voided" apart.

## Trigger

When a person files or re-parents a record, I want the tracker to know the record types and which type may parent which, so I can read an epic path that means the same thing everywhere and the graph view can rely on it.

## Evidence (2026-10-13)

- No rule exists: edges.py refuses only cycles of one edge type; issue_type is a free string (fields.py:52), and only the beads importer names five WORK_TYPES (beads.py:30).
- The tracker page offers five types: task, feature, bug, chore, epic (kit/board/web/index.html:167).
- The engine treats bug, chore and task as leaves that build without a plan (src/basicly/loop.py:59).
- The ledger holds 10 values over 1,670 records: task 654, bug 630, feature 171, chore 140, epic 51, docs 17, question 2, research-spike 2, missing 2, feat 1.
- Parent to child pairs in use: epic>task 406, epic>bug 292, epic>feature 91, feature>task 79, epic>chore 48, feature>feature 9, epic>epic 9, feature>bug 8, task>task 3, feature>chore 3, epic>docs 2, epic>question 1.

## Context

Owner 2026-10-13: "you also need to establish the issue type hierarchy or task hierarchy and who can be whoms child or parent from task, feature, chore, epic which i see in the UI. are there other types too?" Feeds basicly-tpr4xre (epic path and dependency graph).

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a commit names a record id and the branch's own shard (.basicly/ledger/pending-<branch>.jsonl) holds that record's events unstaged, I want the commit refused with the shard to stage, so I can never commit an id whose events stay behind.

## Evidence

Reported by the terminal session on 2026-10-13: on branch agents the kit CLI wrote term-xrypvb into pending-agents.jsonl; only pending-main.jsonl was staged, so the commit named an id whose events were untracked. tracker-commit-msg accepted it because the working tree held the shard. Back on main every cli.py show refused: 'snapshot.jsonl: this would publish 175 records over a file holding 176', until the shard was committed and cherry-picked.

## Proposal

tracker-commit-msg (or tracker-claim) checks that the shard holding each named record is staged.
payload.title: Refuse a commit that names a record whose ledger shard is not staged

payload.text: Owner decisions 2026-10-13 (reply: go, with the type renamed): (1) an epic may parent a feature, task, bug, chore or research record; a feature may parent a task, bug or chore; task, bug, chore and research have no children. (2) Six types: task, bug, feature, chore, epic, research. research replaces research-spike (owner asked spike or research; research chosen as the plain word); docs and question fold into chore; feat becomes feature; any other value is refused by name at input. (3) The 9 epic>epic and 9 feature>feature links stay; new ones are refused. (4) A designer proposes the dependency views on top of this hierarchy.

The tracker page offers the six types.

## Trigger

When an agent deletes files through a shell variable, I want the guidance to give the guarded form, so I can avoid a refusal and an empty variable never expands to /.

## Evidence

tracker-commit-msg (or tracker-claim) checks that the shard holding each named record is staged.

## Sequence

1. Finish Lefthook migration basicly-cdd1iob, remove the Python pre-commit tool, verify consumer upgrade and establish measured baseline.
2. Research tools and inspect existing harness capabilities before selecting architecture. Cover Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, Java, .NET, databases and related technologies.
3. Agree measurable latency budgets and representative workloads at 50k, 200k and 1M lines. Distinguish routine incremental hooks from complete verification; measure cold and warm behavior and correctness after edits, renames, deletions and dependency changes.
4. Decompose implementation into consumer-visible increments with regression gates, costs and runnable demonstrations. Consider affected-project selection and caching after baseline and discussion.
5. Improve agent feedback and requirement-bound verification and validation, including screenshots and visual comparisons where relevant. Simplify the basicly loop where evidence shows friction. Add, change or remove instructions, skills, specialist roles and tooling when justified.
6. Demonstrate upgrade compatibility from the latest released basicly to the upcoming release, including breaking changes, preserving consumer checks and foreign configuration. Older releases may upgrade to latest first.

User-authorized future program. Detailed design, tool choices, numerical budgets and file scopes remain to be researched after the migration baseline. Do not dispatch implementation from this outline.

## Trigger

When multi-technology repositories grow from 50k to 200k and 1M lines, I want to keep routine hooks responsive and verification and validation evidence useful, so I can maintain development speed and check changes against their initial requirements.

## Sequence

1. Finish Lefthook migration basicly-cdd1iob, remove the Python pre-commit tool, verify consumer upgrade and establish measured baseline.
2. Research tools and inspect existing harness capabilities before selecting architecture. Cover Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, Java, .NET, databases and related technologies.
3. Agree measurable latency budgets and representative workloads at 50k, 200k and 1M lines. Distinguish routine incremental hooks from complete verification; measure cold and warm behavior and correctness after edits, renames, deletions and dependency changes.
4. Decompose implementation into consumer-visible increments with regression gates, costs and runnable demonstrations. Consider affected-project selection and caching after baseline and discussion.
5. Improve agent feedback and requirement-bound verification and validation, including screenshots and visual comparisons where relevant. Simplify the basicly loop where evidence shows friction. Add, change or remove instructions, skills, specialist roles and tooling when justified.
6. Demonstrate upgrade compatibility from the latest released basicly to the upcoming release, including breaking changes, preserving consumer checks and foreign configuration. Older releases may upgrade to latest first.

## Planning State

User-authorized future program. Detailed design, tool choices, numerical budgets and file scopes remain to be researched after the migration baseline. Do not dispatch implementation from this outline.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value:
- Preserve all existing gate behavior; do not skip or weaken checks.
- Keep the YAML catalog authoritative and project native configuration from it.
- Remove the pre-commit tool dependency and managed wiring in the same migration.
- Keep standalone kit consumers functional without the basicly engine.
- Defer timing instrumentation, affected selection, caching and Nx changes.
- Keep Lefthook binaries out of Git. Prepare pinned, checksum-verified artifacts explicitly and bundle them in wheel and source distributions outside the projected catalog. Install only the platform executable and MIT license without downloading Lefthook.
- Migrate latest-release engine commands from Git source URLs to version-pinned release wheels, preserving consumer configuration.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- Given a consumer with basicly-managed pre-commit and Claude or Copilot hooks, when upgrading, then all managed hooks use Lefthook and foreign configuration is preserved or a conflict is refused before changes.
- Given a supported platform without a global Lefthook executable, when installing, then a pinned repository-local binary runs Git and agent hooks.
- Given the migration commit, when committing, then the Lefthook pre-commit and commit-msg stages enforce existing gates.
- Given an agent lifecycle payload, when dispatching through Lefthook, then matchers, JSON output and refusal exit codes preserve the agent contract.
- Given partially staged files or a ledger writer, when running hooks, then staged validation and ledger safety remain enforced.
- Given prepared verified artifacts, when building a wheel and source distribution, then both carry the pinned artifacts, the source distribution rebuilds offline with available build dependencies, and unprepared builds refuse without downloading.
- Given the latest released consumer, when upgrading using the new wheel, then managed pre-commit configuration retires, foreign Git and agent hooks survive, generated engine pins become wheel URLs, and no vendor archives enter its catalog.

payload.acceptance_criteria: When a manual handoff requests a tier that cannot be pinned, the harness shall expose the missing provenance before handing off implementation. payload.description:
## Trigger
A manual build handoff can record a requested model tier without a pinned model. Implementation proceeds, but basicly commit later refuses the envelope because Harness-Model provenance is unknown. Observed during basicly-cdd1iob.

## Steps to Reproduce
Provision a manual handoff with the family default tier and no model pin, then request basicly commit --dry-run in the bound worktree. runner.run returns the unhonoured resolution for HANDOFF; record_dispatch persists it; commit.dispatch_model rejects it only when preparing the commit.

## Scope
- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/commit.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_runner.py`
- `tests/test_commit.py`

## Demonstration
Reproduce the manual handoff and show an actionable provenance refusal before implementation, plus a supported evidence-backed recovery for an existing handoff.
payload.requirements: Preserve model-provenance enforcement and ordinary Git hooks. Do not infer the actual executing model from a configured default alone. Preserve existing work and append-only dispatch history.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When a record moves under a parent that the type rule allows, the tracker records the move and the record shows the new parent.
- When a record moves under a parent that the type rule refuses, the tracker refuses the move by name and gives the allowed parent types.
- When a record moves to the top level, its type may be one that sits under no record.
payload.description:
## Trigger

When a consumer finds a record under a parent that the record type rule does not allow, I want to move it under another parent or to the top level, so I can bring the ledger in line with the rule without re-creating the record.

## Evidence

handily, 2026-10-14, record handily-fwkt.18: the epics handily-fwkt.2, handily-fwkt.8 and handily-fwkt.9 sit under the epic handily-fwkt, which the rule refuses (record_types.py CHILD_TYPES: an epic sits under no record). tracker undep refuses their edge: a parent-child edge is not retractable, because removing it re-parents the record while its id still spells its parent, so re-parenting needs its own verb. basicly 0.23.1 has no such verb. Today a retype of such a record is refused, and the record stays out of rule.

## Scope

The tracker kit: a re-parent verb, the id rule for a moved record, the type rule check on the new parent, and its tests.
payload.requirements: - A consumer can move a record to a new parent or to the top level, with the type rule checked, and without re-creating the record.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When verification changes from fail to pass and back to fail, I want the latest failed observation retained, so the loop refuses unsafe advancement before verification reuse is introduced.

## Steps to Reproduce

In an isolated owned ledger, report verify/basicly-verify fail, then pass, then fail through owned_write.append without a repeat flag. gate_source.read_gates currently keeps the pass and the third append reports no new event. The current-tree reproduction is retained on the optimization epic.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/recurrence.py`
- `.basicly/generated-manifest.json`
- `tests/test_gate_report_swallow.py`
- `tests/test_re_record.py`
- `tests/test_gate_recurrence.py`

## Boundaries

Keep per-attempt validation behavior and ordinary consecutive-identical verify/rubric idempotence. Resolve recurrence independently by record, gate and provider in the shared tracker kit used by both engine and standalone consumers. Preserve append-only identities and redaction; no caller repeat flags, timestamp hacks, gate bypasses, persistent cache or affected selection. Do not change ignored note semantics in this unit.

def call(label, args, cwd=repo, duplicate=False):

    with log.open('a') as f:

import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys
from zipfile import ZipFile

assert importlib.util.find_spec('basicly') is None
run = Path('/tmp/basicly-c25o52c-nesting-plan')
root = run / 'recurrence-standalone'
assert not root.exists()
kit = root / 'kit'
kit.mkdir(parents=True)
wheel = run / 'recurrence-dist/basicly-0.24.1-py3-none-any.whl'
with ZipFile(wheel) as z:
    matches = [name for name in z.namelist() if name.endswith('/kit/tracker/recurrence.py')]
    assert len(matches) == 1
    prefix = matches[0].removesuffix('recurrence.py')
    for name in z.namelist():
        if name.startswith(prefix) and name.endswith('.py'):
            (kit / Path(name).name).write_bytes(z.read(name))
def load(name, module_name):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(module_name, kit / (name+'.py'))
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules[module_name] = module
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module

events = load('events', 'basicly_tracker_kit_events')
gates = load('gates', 'basicly_tracker_kit_gates')
recurrence = load('recurrence', 'standalone_recurrence')
ledger = root / 'ledger'
events.append(ledger,[events.Draft('probe-1',events.KIND_STATUS,{'status':'open'})])
observed = []
appended = []
for passed in [False, True, False, False, True, True, False]:
    draft = gates.gate_draft('probe-1','verify',provider='engine',passed=passed)
    resolved = recurrence.at_the_generation_this_write_needs(events,ledger,[draft])
    appended.append(bool(events.append(ledger,resolved)))
    collected = events.read_events(ledger)[0]
    observed.append(gates.fold_gates(collected).view('probe-1').result('verify',providers={'engine'}).passed)
assert observed == [False, True, False, False, True, True, False]
assert appended == [True, True, True, False, True, False, True]
result = {'result':'PASS','engine_available':False,'surface':'packaged tracker recurrence and append APIs','observations':observed,'appended':appended}
(run/'recurrence-standalone-result.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+'\n')
print(json.dumps(result,indent=2))

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Trigger

When a landing repeats full verification on an unchanged source input set, I want proven deterministic results carried into the gate, so I can shorten landing time without accepting stale evidence.

## Context

Existing record basicly-tjhjmk measured two full executions. Current child.4 landing ran all three Pyright platform checks twice; full suites passed7020 tests each, with first landing verify178.787s. The existing landing timer excludes the second verification. Existing raw inputs selectors only control staged selection and do not prove complete reusable inputs. Child.4 repaired recurring gate verdicts before this work.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `src/basicly/verify_receipt.py`
- `src/basicly/pyright_inputs.py`
- `src/basicly/verify_artifact.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_verify_receipt.py`
- `tests/test_pyright_inputs.py`
- `tests/test_verify_artifact.py`
- `tests/test_merge_timing.py`
- `tests/test_loop_lane.py`
- `tests/test_config.py`
- `basicly.toml`
- `docs/how-to/wire-up-the-verify-gate.md`
- `changelog.d/basicly-2tfuwv.changed.md`

## Design

Carry the actual successful VerifyReport from merge to gate recording. Reuse requires an explicit reviewed recipe and matching check argv, mode, complete input inventory and content, configuration, platform, interpreter, tool/runtime and execution environment. Capture before and after execution; changed or unreadable inputs invalidate reuse. Only passed executed observations qualify. Missing, failed, skipped, stale, unsupported or absent receipts execute the checks normally.

First enable the three existing full Pyright platform checks with a version-bounded recipe for installed1.1.411. Cover source additions, removals, renames, module shadowing, config/search paths, type stubs, dependencies, runtime and environment. Bind equivalent workspace paths explicitly; unsupported external paths, configuration or runtime shapes fall back to fresh execution. Preserve dotenv denials. Do not infer reusable inputs from the old staged selectors or dependency-output filenames alone.

All other checks, including pytest and Git/ledger-sensitive checks, remain fresh until their complete contracts exist. This narrows the duplicate full pass; it does not complete the parent mixed-tech optimization goal. No persistent cross-run cache, affected selection, new dependencies or mandatory build system in this unit. Ordinary verify and Git hooks retain fresh execution; same-landing reuse stays inside the engine.

Record executed versus reused results and refusal reasons with source provenance. Measure post-merge verification and combined verification separately from existing merge timing. Cover leaf, queued-child, already-landed and manual paths: missing proof always runs normally.

## Measurement

Use retained real child.3/child.4 before evidence and actual candidate landings; prove compiler invocation counts independently of timing. Target elimination of the three redundant platform compiler processes (previously about30s combined) with at most1s warm fingerprint overhead on this repository. Report measured before/after values and conditions, including fallback/cold cases; do not claim improvement from skipped tests or estimates. The 50k/200k/1M mixed-stack scaling experiment remains on basicly-c25o52c.

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_verify_receipt.py tests/test_pyright_inputs.py tests/test_verify_artifact.py tests/test_merge_timing.py tests/test_loop_lane.py tests/test_config.py -q`

Build the release wheel and run the real loop as a consumer in isolated repositories. An unchanged supported landing reuses only proven compiler results; a changed/unsupported input reruns them and a real compiler failure blocks advancement. Upgrade from released0.24.1 without altering consumer checks.

payload.value:
WHEN an unchanged supported landing reaches gate recording, THE LOOP SHALL use the actual successful matching compiler receipts and execute the remaining checks, without a second unconditional full pass.
WHEN source inventory/content, configuration, runtime, environment, command or mode differs, or evidence is missing/unsupported/failed/skipped, THE LOOP SHALL execute fresh verification and preserve any failure.
WHEN a supported landing is reported, THE EVIDENCE SHALL distinguish executed and reused checks, identify source provenance and record first-stage plus post-merge verification durations.
WHEN the packaged consumer installs fresh or upgrades from released0.24.1, THE NORMAL LOOP SHALL preserve existing check outcomes, foreign hooks and configuration, with measured real before/after timings and compiler invocation counts.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: Reduce unnecessary repeated verification while retaining the same required checks and exact failed outcomes. Reuse only verified deterministic inputs; default to fresh execution for unknown or changed contexts. Preserve ordinary Git and verify workflows, latest-release upgrade, dotenv denials and consumer ownership. Report actual execution, reuse and timing evidence. This unit narrows repeated compiler work; all mixed-stack providers, durable reuse and repository-size scaling remain required on the full parent goal.

payload.text: Design chosen from current evidence: carry actual reports, add explicit per-check recipes, opt in only supported Pyright1.1.411 platform checks first, preserve full fallback for all unknown/mutable contexts. This narrows the second pass by three compiler processes instead of assuming pytest is pure; original card expressly allows removal OR narrowing. Retained child.4 timings put those three compiler calls at29.949s combined in the first pass. Default legacy consumers remain fresh; no persistent cache or affected selection added. Explicit outcome is measured fewer compiler executions with all required checks still evaluated. Input-contract counterexample rules out a filename-only dependency cache. New snapshots must cover inventory additions and both source and runtime context; unsupported recipe conditions are visible fallback, never success by assumption.

body.parent_goal: ACTIVE; mixed-tech providers, durable evidence reuse and scaling still required.

retained_before.caveat: Existing first-stage timing excludes post-merge verification; do not label its sum total workflow time.

body.strategy: Same-landing verified report transfer with explicit complete-input recipes; unsupported inputs execute fresh. Pyright1.1.411 initial recipe; other checks remain fresh.
