payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Trigger

When a landing repeats full verification on an unchanged source input set, I want proven deterministic results carried into the gate, so I can shorten landing time without accepting stale evidence.

## Context

Existing record basicly-tjhjmk measured two full executions. Current child.4 landing ran all three Pyright platform checks twice; full suites passed7020 tests each, with first landing verify178.787s. The existing landing timer excludes the second verification. Existing raw inputs selectors only control staged selection and do not prove complete reusable inputs. Child.4 repaired recurring gate verdicts before this work.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `src/basicly/verify_receipt.py`
- `src/basicly/pyright_inputs.py`
- `src/basicly/verify_artifact.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_verify_receipt.py`
- `tests/test_pyright_inputs.py`
- `tests/test_verify_artifact.py`
- `tests/test_merge_timing.py`
- `tests/test_merge.py`
- `tests/test_loop_lane.py`
- `tests/test_config.py`
- `basicly.toml`
- `.importlinter`
- `docs/how-to/wire-up-the-verify-gate.md`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `changelog.d/basicly-2tfuwv.changed.md`

## Design

Carry the actual successful VerifyReport from merge to gate recording. Reuse requires an explicit reviewed recipe and matching check argv, mode, complete input inventory and content, configuration, platform, interpreter, tool/runtime and execution environment. Capture before and after execution; changed or unreadable inputs invalidate reuse. Only passed executed observations qualify. Missing, failed, skipped, stale, unsupported or absent receipts execute the checks normally.

First enable the three existing full Pyright platform checks with a version-bounded recipe for installed1.1.411. Cover source additions, removals, renames, module shadowing, config/search paths, type stubs, dependencies, runtime and environment. Bind equivalent workspace paths explicitly; unsupported external paths, configuration or runtime shapes fall back to fresh execution. Preserve dotenv denials. Do not infer reusable inputs from the old staged selectors or dependency-output filenames alone.

All other checks, including pytest and Git/ledger-sensitive checks, remain fresh until their complete contracts exist. This narrows the duplicate full pass; it does not complete the parent mixed-tech optimization goal. No persistent cross-run cache, affected selection, new dependencies or mandatory build system in this unit. Ordinary verify and Git hooks retain fresh execution; same-landing reuse stays inside the engine.

Record executed versus reused results and refusal reasons with source provenance. Measure post-merge verification and combined verification separately from existing merge timing. Cover leaf, queued-child, already-landed and manual paths: missing proof always runs normally.

## Measurement

Use retained real child.3/child.4 before evidence and actual candidate landings; prove compiler invocation counts independently of timing. Target elimination of the three redundant platform compiler processes (previously about30s combined) with at most1s warm fingerprint overhead on this repository. Report measured before/after values and conditions, including fallback/cold cases; do not claim improvement from skipped tests or estimates. The 50k/200k/1M mixed-stack scaling experiment remains on basicly-c25o52c.

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_verify_receipt.py tests/test_pyright_inputs.py tests/test_verify_artifact.py tests/test_merge_timing.py tests/test_loop_lane.py tests/test_config.py -q`

Build the release wheel and run the real loop as a consumer in isolated repositories. An unchanged supported landing reuses only proven compiler results; a changed/unsupported input reruns them and a real compiler failure blocks advancement. Upgrade from released0.24.1 without altering consumer checks.

No product weakening or fixture failure claimed as pass.

import hashlib

import os

import sys

artifacts = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
root = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve() if len(sys.argv) > 1 else artifacts
root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
runtime = root / "package-env"
old = Path('/tmp/basicly-cdd1iob-release-0241-1x34l627/actual-tag-dist/basicly-0.24.1-py3-none-any.whl')
new = artifacts / 'reviewed-launcher-dist/basicly-0.24.1-py3-none-any.whl'
assert hashlib.sha256(old.read_bytes()).hexdigest() == '3f4de59aa5aab24c581e9818749d25ede01a53dd2282b8737b58476e489aeaad'
env = os.environ.copy()
env.pop('PYTHONPATH', None)
env.update(UV_OFFLINE='1', UV_NO_SYNC='1', UV_CACHE_DIR='/tmp/basicly-cdd1iob-terminal-9i5r6bmu/uv-cache', UV_FIND_LINKS='/tmp/basicly-cdd1iob-recovered-wheelhouse', UV_LINK_MODE='copy', AI_AGENT='codex')
transcript = root / 'package-consumer.log'

def call(label, argv, cwd=root):
    result = subprocess.run([str(arg) for arg in argv], cwd=cwd, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=180)
    with transcript.open('a') as stream:
        stream.write(label + '\n' + result.stdout + result.stderr + '\nexit=' + str(result.returncode) + '\n')
    assert result.returncode == 0, (label, result.stdout[-2000:], result.stderr[-3000:])
    print(label, 'PASS', flush=True)
    return result.stdout

assert not runtime.exists()
call('create isolated package runtime', ['uv', 'venv', '--python', sys.executable, runtime])
python = runtime / 'bin/python'
engine = runtime / 'bin/basicly'
env['PATH'] = str(runtime / 'bin') + os.pathsep + env['PATH']
env['VIRTUAL_ENV'] = str(runtime)
call('install actual released engine offline', ['uv', 'pip', 'install', '--offline', '--python', python, old, 'pyright==1.1.411'])
call('warm real compiler launcher', [runtime / 'bin/pyright', '--version'])

config = '\n'.join(
    f'[[verify.checks]]\nname="types-{target}"\ncommand=["pyright","--pythonplatform","{target}"]\nmodes=["full"]\n'
    for target in ['Linux', 'Darwin', 'Windows']
)
config += '[[verify.checks]]\nname="tests"\ncommand=["python","-c","print(123)"]\nmodes=["full"]\n'

def prepare(name):
    repo = root / name
    repo.mkdir()
    call(name + ' init', ['git', 'init', '--quiet', '--initial-branch=main', repo])
    for key, value in [('user.name','Consumer Probe'), ('user.email','consumer@example.invalid'), ('core.hooksPath','.githooks')]:
        call(name + ' config ' + key, ['git','config',key,value], repo)
    (repo / 'src').mkdir()
    (repo / 'src/demo.py').write_text('value: int = 1\n')
    (repo / 'pyproject.toml').write_text('[project]\nname="receipt-consumer"\nversion="0.1.0"\nrequires-python=">=3.14"\ndependencies=[]\n[tool.pyright]\nvenvPath="."\nvenv=".venv"\ninclude=["src"]\nextraPaths=["src", "."]\n')
    (repo / 'basicly.toml').write_text(config)
    hooks = repo / '.githooks'
    hooks.mkdir()
    hook = hooks / 'pre-commit'
    hook.write_text('#!/bin/sh\nprintf "foreign\\n" >> "$(git rev-parse --git-path foreign-count)"\n')
    hook.chmod(0o755)
    call(name + ' analysis environment', ['uv','sync','--offline'], repo)
    call(name + ' harness install', [engine,'install'], repo)
    assert (repo / '.basicly/bin/lefthook').is_file()
    call(name + ' offline binary version', [repo / '.basicly/bin/lefthook','version'], repo)
    return repo

upgrade = prepare('upgrade-consumer')
before_config = (upgrade / 'basicly.toml').read_bytes()
before_lefthook = (upgrade / 'lefthook.yml').read_bytes()
baseline = '''
from pathlib import Path
import json
from basicly import verify
root=Path.cwd(); original=verify._spawn;calls=[]
def counted(command,*args,**kwargs):
 calls.append(command[0]);return original(command,*args,**kwargs)
verify._spawn=counted
first=verify.run_verify(root,'full');second=verify.run_verify(root,'full')
assert first.passed and second.passed
assert calls.count('pyright')==6 and calls.count('python')==2,calls
print(json.dumps({'compiler_invocations':calls.count('pyright'),'tests':calls.count('python')}))
'''
call('released baseline real six compiler invocations', [python,'-c',baseline], upgrade)
call('upgrade isolated package engine offline', ['uv','pip','install','--offline','--reinstall-package','basicly','--python',python,new])
call('upgrade harness from actual release', [engine,'install'], upgrade)
assert (upgrade / 'basicly.toml').read_bytes()==before_config
assert (upgrade / 'lefthook.yml').read_bytes()==before_lefthook
fresh=prepare('fresh-consumer')
probe='''
from pathlib import Path
import json
from basicly import verify
root=Path.cwd(); original=verify._spawn;calls=[]
def counted(command,*args,**kwargs):

verify._spawn=counted
origin=verify.run_verify(root,'full',capture_receipts=True)
assert origin.passed and len(origin.receipts)==3,origin
landed=verify.run_verify(root,'full',reuse=origin)
assert landed.passed and sum(bool(r.reused_from) for r in landed.results)==3,landed
assert calls.count('pyright')==3 and calls.count('python')==2,calls
(root/'src/added.py').write_text('broken: int = "not an int"\\n')
changed=verify.run_verify(root,'full',reuse=origin)
assert not changed.passed and calls.count('pyright')==6
assert all(not r.reused_from for r in changed.results)
print(json.dumps({'unchanged_compilers':3,'changed_compilers':3,'fresh_tests':calls.count('python'),'changed_failures':list(changed.failures),'source_duration_s':origin.duration_s,'reuse_duration_s':landed.duration_s}))
'''
for repo in (upgrade,fresh):
    call(repo.name + ' ordinary verify stays fresh', [python,'-c',baseline], repo)
    current=(repo/'basicly.toml').read_text()
    assert current.count('modes=["full"]')==4
    (repo/'basicly.toml').write_text(current.replace('modes=["full"]','modes=["full"]\nreuse="pyright"',3))

## Trigger

When a consumer owns a dependency graph, I want its affected-check plan to drive existing checks against the Git index snapshot, so I can avoid unrelated work without accepting an unstaged repair or losing broad verification when the graph cannot answer.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/hooks/affected_checks.py`
- `.basicly/core/hooks/check_runner.py`
- `.basicly/core/hooks/staged-snapshot.py`
- `.basicly/core/hooks/lefthook-runtime.py`
- `src/basicly/affected.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_affected.py`
- `tests/test_git_hooks/test_affected_checks.py`
- `tests/test_git_hooks/test_check_runner.py`
- `tests/test_config.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`
- `tests/test_verify_artifact.py`
- `tests/test_cli.py`
- `tests/test_hooks.py`
- `.importlinter`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `docs/how-to/wire-up-the-verify-gate.md`

## Design

First consumer-visible provider integration from the approved parent architecture. Existing commands remain consumer-owned. A configured provider receives versioned JSON with candidate check names, comparison identity, immutable index tree and NUL-decoded change statuses including both rename paths. A complete response binds the same context and considered checks, selects only known opted-in checks and explains selection. Missing or unsupported evidence runs every candidate check. Unscoped checks always run. Shared protocol and selection code ships in the distributed hooks and is loaded by the engine; no engine or new dependency is required for consumer Git hooks.

Pre-commit uses its existing snapshot. Explicit affected CLI execution uses the same snapshot mechanism before reading configuration and running checks. Ordinary verification and pre-push stay broad. Bound provider execution, show fallback reasons, preserve partial staging and never infer dependency closure from filename globs alone. Provider completeness is trusted consumer configuration, not a cryptographic proof.

No Nx dependency, language inference or durable result cache is added here. Provider-specific runtime validation and all technology discovery and scaling requirements remain on the parent. Nx runtime awaits a network-state change.

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_affected.py tests/test_git_hooks/test_affected_checks.py tests/test_git_hooks/test_check_runner.py tests/test_verify.py tests/test_cli.py -q`

Then exercise the installed wheel outside this checkout with actual ordinary Git hooks and the affected verify CLI, an index-staged failure canceled only in the worktree, rename/delete/shared configuration changes, provider failures, foreign hook execution and upgrade from released0.24.1. Count actual commands and measure elapsed times. Fixture exports are not automatic language discovery.
payload.requirements: Implement the approved consumer-owned graph direction without mandatory build-system adoption. Preserve snapshot correctness, unscoped checks, exact failed outcomes, foreign hooks, offline package installation, consumer configuration and secret denials. Unknown dependency scope executes broad checks. Full mixed-stack discovery, real provider runtime validation, persistent reuse and50k/200k/1M scaling remain mandatory on the parent.

import dataclasses
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import platform
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

source = Path.cwd()
run = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='basicly-cdd1iob-baseline-'))
repo = run / 'checkout'
subprocess.run(['git', 'clone', '--quiet', '--local', '--no-hardlinks', str(source), str(repo)], check=True)
for rel in ['.venv', 'node_modules', 'build/lefthook']:
    original = source / rel
    if original.is_dir():
        (repo / rel).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (repo / rel).symlink_to(original, target_is_directory=True)
cache = run / 'cache'
cache.mkdir()
env = dict(os.environ, PATH=str(repo / '.venv/bin') + os.pathsep + os.environ['PATH'], PYTHONPATH=str(repo / 'src'), UV_OFFLINE='1', UV_NO_SYNC='1', UV_CACHE_DIR=str(cache / 'uv'), XDG_CACHE_HOME=str(cache / 'xdg'), CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=str(repo))
subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-c', 'from pathlib import Path; from basicly.lefthook_binary import sync_binary; sync_binary(Path.cwd())'], cwd=repo, env=env, check=True)
sys.path.insert(0, str(source / 'src'))
from basicly.hooks import load_hook_specs
specs = load_hook_specs(repo / '.basicly/core/hooks')
agent_specs = [s for s in specs if s.manager != 'git']
rows = []

def measure(label, command, payload, expected, repeats=3):
    data = json.dumps(payload).encode()
    samples = []
    for number in range(repeats):
        start = time.perf_counter()
        result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=repo, env=env, input=data, capture_output=True, timeout=90)
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
        name = f'{label}-{number}'
        (run / f'{name}.stdout').write_bytes(result.stdout)
        (run / f'{name}.stderr').write_bytes(result.stderr)
        sample = dict(seconds=elapsed, code=result.returncode, stdout_sha256=hashlib.sha256(result.stdout).hexdigest(), stdout_bytes=len(result.stdout), stderr_bytes=len(result.stderr), expected=expected, passed=result.returncode == expected)
        samples.append(sample)
    row = dict(label=label, command=command, payload=payload, samples=samples, median_seconds=statistics.median(s['seconds'] for s in samples))
    rows.append(row)
    (run / 'results.json').write_text(json.dumps(dict(source_commit=subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'],cwd=repo,text=True).strip(), python=platform.python_version(), platform=platform.platform(), conditions='Prepared venv, reused node_modules, sequential runs; first sample process-cold, OS/filesystem caches uncontrolled; UV offline and no-sync; isolated clone; no dependency-cold claim', inventory=[dataclasses.asdict(s) for s in specs], measurements=rows), indent=2))
    print(label, round(row['median_seconds'], 6), [s['code'] for s in samples], flush=True)
    return row

bash = lambda cmd: dict(tool_name='Bash', tool_input=dict(command=cmd), cwd=str(repo))
edit = dict(tool_name='Edit', tool_input=dict(file_path=str(repo / 'src/basicly/__init__.py')), cwd=str(repo))
protected = dict(tool_name='Edit', tool_input=dict(file_path=str(repo / 'AGENTS.md')), cwd=str(repo))
patch = lambda path: dict(tool_name='apply_patch', tool_input=dict(command=f'*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: {path}\n@@\n-a\n+b\n*** End Patch'), cwd=str(repo))
traps = {'unsplit-loop-guard': 'V="a b c"; for x in $V; do echo $x; done', 'pipe-status-guard': 'uv run pytest -q | tail -3; echo $?', 'bare-var-guard': 'W="uv run x --"; $W a b', 'rg-replace-guard': 'rg -rn pattern src/'}
for spec in agent_specs:
    if spec.id == 'tier-injection':
        payload = dict(tool_name='Agent', tool_input=dict(subagent_type='implementer'), cwd=str(repo))
    elif spec.id == 'protect-generated-codex':
        payload = patch('src/basicly/__init__.py')
    elif spec.id in ['protect-generated','headroom-guard']:
        payload = edit
    elif spec.stage == 'sessionstart':
        payload = dict(source='startup', cwd=str(repo))
    elif spec.manager == 'copilot':
        payload = dict(toolName='shell', toolArgs=dict(command='git status --short'))
    else:
        payload = bash('git status --short')
    measure('direct-' + spec.id, [sys.executable, str(repo / '.basicly/core/hooks' / spec.script)], payload, 0)
    if spec.id in traps:
        measure('direct-' + spec.id + '-blocked', [sys.executable, str(repo / '.basicly/core/hooks' / spec.script)], bash(traps[spec.id]), 2)

runtime = str(repo / '.basicly/core/hooks/lefthook-runtime.py')
for label, manager, stage, payload, expected in [
    ('claude-bash-allowed','claude','pretooluse',bash('git status --short'),0),
    ('claude-edit-allowed','claude','pretooluse',edit,0),
    ('claude-edit-blocked','claude','pretooluse',protected,2),
    ('codex-patch-allowed','codex','pretooluse',patch('src/basicly/__init__.py'),0),
    ('codex-patch-blocked','codex','pretooluse',patch('AGENTS.md'),2),
    ('claude-agent','claude','pretooluse',dict(tool_name='Agent',tool_input=dict(subagent_type='implementer'),cwd=str(repo)),0),
    ('claude-posttooluse','claude','posttooluse',bash('git status --short'),0),
    ('copilot-posttooluse','copilot','posttooluse',dict(toolName='shell',toolArgs=dict(command='git status --short')),0),
    *[(m+'-sessionstart',m,'sessionstart',dict(source='startup',cwd=str(repo)),0) for m in ['claude','codex','copilot']],
    *[(name+'-blocked','claude','pretooluse',bash(cmd),2) for name,cmd in traps.items()],
]:
    measure('event-' + label, [sys.executable, runtime, manager, stage], payload, expected)
print('RESULT_DIRECTORY', run, flush=True)

## Trigger

When a consumer owns a dependency graph, I want its affected-check plan to drive existing checks against the Git index snapshot, so I can avoid unrelated work without accepting an unstaged repair or losing broad verification when the graph cannot answer.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/hooks/affected_checks.py`
- `.basicly/core/hooks/check_runner.py`
- `.basicly/core/hooks/staged-snapshot.py`
- `.basicly/core/hooks/lefthook-runtime.py`
- `src/basicly/affected.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `src/basicly/verify_artifact.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_affected.py`
- `tests/test_git_hooks/test_affected_checks.py`
- `tests/test_git_hooks/test_check_runner.py`
- `tests/test_config.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`
- `tests/test_verify_artifact.py`
- `tests/test_cli.py`
- `tests/test_hooks.py`
- `.importlinter`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `docs/how-to/wire-up-the-verify-gate.md`

- `changelog.d/basicly-c25o52c.5.added.md`

- `.scripts/validate_affected_consumer.py`

- `tests/test_repo_isolation.py`

## Design

First consumer-visible provider integration from the approved parent architecture. Existing commands remain consumer-owned. A configured provider receives versioned JSON with candidate check names, comparison identity, immutable index tree and NUL-decoded change statuses including both rename paths. A complete response binds the same context and considered checks, selects only known opted-in checks and explains selection. Missing or unsupported evidence runs every candidate check. Unscoped checks always run. Shared protocol and selection code ships in the distributed hooks and is loaded by the engine; no engine or new dependency is required for consumer Git hooks.

Pre-commit uses its existing snapshot. Explicit affected CLI execution uses the same snapshot mechanism before reading configuration and running checks. Ordinary verification and pre-push stay broad. Bound provider execution, show fallback reasons, preserve partial staging and never infer dependency closure from filename globs alone. Provider completeness is trusted consumer configuration, not a cryptographic proof.

No Nx dependency, language inference or durable result cache is added here. Provider-specific runtime validation and all technology discovery and scaling requirements remain on the parent. Nx runtime awaits a network-state change.

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_affected.py tests/test_git_hooks/test_affected_checks.py tests/test_git_hooks/test_check_runner.py tests/test_verify.py tests/test_cli.py -q`

Then exercise the installed wheel outside this checkout with actual ordinary Git hooks and the affected verify CLI, an index-staged failure canceled only in the worktree, rename/delete/shared configuration changes, provider failures, foreign hook execution and upgrade from released0.24.1. Count actual commands and measure elapsed times. Fixture exports are not automatic language discovery.

The packaged validation script requires explicit candidate and released baseline wheel inputs from the validation environment; missing inputs must fail rather than silently download. Run `uv run python .scripts/validate_affected_consumer.py` with those prepared inputs.

## Trigger

When unchanged compiler checks repeat across verification invocations, I want to reuse locally recorded passing results with complete input identity, so I can reduce loop latency without accepting stale verification.

## Scope

## Design

Bind engine/recipe version, repository identity, exact check command/mode and the existing full source, configuration, environment and runtime fingerprint. Persist only actual stable successful executions through atomic bounded storage; never publish a failed or skipped execution as a passing cache entry. Corrupt or unsupported data is a miss. Recheck inputs after verification and rerun reused checks if they changed. Preserve origin and source timings in agent-visible evidence; provide an explicit fresh-run control.

Integrate the same mechanism into CLI and loop verification. Unsupported checks and native no-engine hooks retain fresh execution. No new dependency, remote cache, arbitrary-command cache, mandatory build system or cross-stack discovery is introduced. Measure actual fresh and warm separate-process invocation times and compiler counts. Do not claim whole-loop or repository-size scaling from compiler-only evidence.

Run the focused cache/receipt/config/CLI/loop regressions, then the repository full verifier once after final changes. Build the candidate and run `.scripts/validate_check_cache.py` against a prepared v0.25.0 baseline wheel and the candidate wheel. Exercise actual Pyright, mutation-induced failure, unscoped checks and fresh-run control; publish 30 warm samples and cold setup separately. Preserve offline Lefthook and consumer configuration on upgrade.

import json
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
import pytest
from basicly import loop,policy
from tests.test_loop import CONFIG,_state
root=Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='basicly-confirm-rotation-'))
approved=set()
with pytest.MonkeyPatch.context() as m:
 m.setattr(policy,'checkpoint_approved',lambda _r,_i,name:name in approved)
 m.setattr(policy,'approve_checkpoint',lambda _r,_i,name:approved.add(name))
 m.setattr(policy,'record_checkpoint_wait',lambda *_a,**_k:None)
 m.setattr(policy,'record_wait_request',lambda *_a,**_k:None)
 m.setattr(policy,'_settle_checkpoint_queue',lambda *_a,**_k:None)
 m.setattr(policy,'_grant_approval',lambda *_a:(None,'',''))
 def advance(*_a,**_k):
  if 'ship' in approved:return loop.AdvanceResult('fixture-i','ship','done','tore-down')
  return loop._on_verify(SimpleNamespace(repo_root=root,issue_id='fixture-i',grant_root=None,state=_state('verify')))
 m.setattr(loop,'advance',advance)
 first=loop.run_ceremony(root,'fixture-i',config=CONFIG)
 printed=first.challenge[1]
 before=json.loads((root/'.basicly/usage/checkpoint-confirms.json').read_text())['fixture-i:ship']['code']
 retry=loop.run_ceremony(root,'fixture-i',config=CONFIG,confirms={'ship':printed})
 after=json.loads((root/'.basicly/usage/checkpoint-confirms.json').read_text())['fixture-i:ship']['code']
 assert before==printed
 assert retry.refused==('ship','invalid or expired confirm code')
 assert after!=printed
 print(json.dumps({'fixture':'isolated policy/ceremony integration; no real ledger or approval','printed_matches_store_before_retry':before==printed,'retry_refused':retry.refused,'retry_rotated_store':after!=printed,'ship_approved':'ship' in approved}))

payload.description:
## Trigger

When an authorized harness install or landing needs a protected destination, I want the operation to detect that restriction before mutation and name the supported reviewed retry, so I can finish the authorized upgrade without partial state or broader permissions.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a Codex workspace sandbox with an existing consumer .codex directory protected read-only.
2. Upgrade a consumer in a sibling worktree so the incoming commit adds .codex/hooks.json.
3. Land from the base checkout under normal workspace execution. Terminal reported Errno30 for the protected destination; the old engine hid Git stderr and claimed a clean abort while leaving source artifacts untracked.
4. Run the same normal gated operation through task-scoped require_escalated. Terminal completed the merge and hooks. This is a workflow restriction, not evidence that sandbox protections should be removed.

Current-version behavior must be reproduced independently before implementation; reports involving the v0.23.1 engine remain version-qualified.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/write_preflight.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`

## Design

Use the actual planned destination writes for installation and incoming merge paths to preflight before tracked/index/ledger changes. Skip unchanged protected outputs. Refuse with the protected relative target and exact ordinary retry command. The standalone CLI does not claim it can grant itself permissions. Agent workflow requests task-scoped execution review for an already-authorized hook/config update without asking for that same upgrade authorization again. Preserve unrelated human checkpoint decisions. Keep dotenv denials, hook/signing execution and the sandbox boundary. Never broaden a machine profile or hide foreign files to pass a gate.

## Demonstration

Reproduce denied writes and successful reviewed retries through real Codex tool execution in a disposable base checkout and linked sibling worktree. Verify unchanged HEAD, index, tracked contents, ledger and consumer-owned files after denial; verify safe retry and ordinary native commit/push hook execution. Run targeted regressions during implementation, all required checks/full suite after final changes, and packaged latest-release upgrade validation. A nested sandbox that fails before execution does not prove this behavior; report such coverage as blocked and use an actual native session boundary.

## Trigger

When an authorized harness install or landing needs a protected destination, I want the operation to detect that restriction before mutation and name the supported reviewed retry, so I can finish the authorized upgrade without partial state or broader permissions.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a Codex workspace sandbox with an existing consumer .codex directory protected read-only.
2. Upgrade a consumer in a sibling worktree so the incoming commit adds .codex/hooks.json.
3. Land from the base checkout under normal workspace execution. Terminal reported Errno30 for the protected destination; the old engine hid Git stderr and claimed a clean abort while leaving source artifacts untracked.
4. Run the same normal gated operation through task-scoped require_escalated. Terminal completed the merge and hooks. This is a workflow restriction, not evidence that sandbox protections should be removed.

Current-version behavior must be reproduced independently before implementation; reports involving the v0.23.1 engine remain version-qualified.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/write_preflight.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/worktree.py`
- `src/basicly/hooks.py`
- `src/basicly/lefthook_config.py`
- `src/basicly/codex_hooks.py`
- `tests/test_write_preflight.py`
- `tests/test_cli.py`

## Design

Use the actual planned destination writes for installation and incoming merge paths to preflight before tracked/index/ledger changes. Skip unchanged protected outputs. Refuse with the protected relative target and exact ordinary retry command. The standalone CLI does not claim it can grant itself permissions. Agent workflow requests task-scoped execution review for an already-authorized hook/config update without asking for that same upgrade authorization again. Preserve unrelated human checkpoint decisions. Keep dotenv denials, hook/signing execution and the sandbox boundary. Never broaden a machine profile or hide foreign files to pass a gate.

## Demonstration

Reproduce denied writes and successful reviewed retries through real Codex tool execution in a disposable base checkout and linked sibling worktree. Verify unchanged HEAD, index, tracked contents, ledger and consumer-owned files after denial; verify safe retry and ordinary native commit/push hook execution. Run targeted regressions during implementation, all required checks/full suite after final changes, and packaged latest-release upgrade validation. A nested sandbox that fails before execution does not prove this behavior; report such coverage as blocked and use an actual native session boundary.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When repository tooling leaves ignored runtime telemetry under the catalog, I want package builds to exclude those files, so consumers receive only the harness sources and declared immutable artifacts.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Produce ignored .basicly/usage/tool-usage.json files beneath catalog kit or template directories by using the source checkout.
2. Build the v0.25.1 wheel from that working checkout.
3. Compare its entries with a wheel built from a clean archive of the same tag: the working-checkout wheel includes nested runtime telemetry and its RECORD differs.

The v0.25.1 release uses a clean tag build; its published wheel matches the tested clean candidate and contains no nested runtime telemetry.

## Scope

- `hatch_build.py`
- `tests/test_hatch_build.py`
- `src/basicly/catalog.py`

## Design

Establish the package input boundary from current producer code. Exclude observed runtime telemetry without dropping legitimate catalog resources or consumer-owned installed files. Add a failing dirty-source packaging regression with a positive control for a real kit resource. Keep all pinned Lefthook binaries, source archive, checksums and license in the offline wheel.

## Demonstration

Build from a clean tag and a checkout containing the reproduced ignored runtime files. Compare wheel entry lists and relevant source bytes, confirm telemetry is absent and declared resources remain, then run packaged offline install.

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Trigger

When unchanged compiler checks repeat across verification invocations, I want to reuse locally recorded passing results with complete input identity, so I can reduce loop latency without accepting stale verification.

## Scope

- `basicly.d/basicly-c25o52c.6.toml`
- `src/basicly/verify_cache.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `src/basicly/verify_receipt.py`
- `src/basicly/pyright_inputs.py`
- `src/basicly/verify_artifact.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_verify_cache.py`
- `tests/test_verify_receipt.py`
- `tests/test_pyright_inputs.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`
- `tests/test_verify_artifact.py`
- `tests/test_config.py`
- `tests/test_cli.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
- `.scripts/validate_check_cache.py`
- `.importlinter`
- `docs/how-to/wire-up-the-verify-gate.md`
- `docs/how-to/upgrade-and-check-drift.md`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `changelog.d/basicly-c25o52c.6.added.md`

## Design

Extend the existing reviewed Pyright receipt recipe into an explicitly enabled repository-local cache. Before persistence, fingerprint the actual reviewed Pyright launcher/runtime independently from the engine interpreter so ordinary isolated-engine consumers can qualify safely; unsupported launchers still execute fresh. Existing defaults remain fresh. Bind engine/recipe version, repository identity, exact check command/mode and the existing full source, configuration, environment and runtime fingerprint. Persist only actual stable successful executions through atomic bounded storage; never publish a failed or skipped execution as a passing cache entry. Corrupt or unsupported data is a miss. Recheck inputs after verification and rerun reused checks if they changed. Preserve origin and source timings in agent-visible evidence; provide an explicit fresh-run control.

Integrate the same mechanism into CLI and loop verification. Unsupported checks and native no-engine hooks retain fresh execution. No new dependency, remote cache, arbitrary-command cache, mandatory build system or cross-stack discovery is introduced. Measure actual fresh and warm separate-process invocation times and compiler counts. Do not claim whole-loop or repository-size scaling from compiler-only evidence.

## Demonstration

Run the focused cache/receipt/config/CLI/loop regressions, then the repository full verifier once after final changes. Build the candidate and run `.scripts/validate_check_cache.py` against a prepared v0.25.0 baseline wheel and the candidate wheel. Exercise actual Pyright, mutation-induced failure, unscoped checks and fresh-run control; publish 30 warm samples and cold setup separately. Preserve offline Lefthook and consumer configuration on upgrade.

## Design

Extend the existing reviewed Pyright receipt recipe into an explicitly enabled repository-local cache. Before persistence, fingerprint the actual reviewed Pyright launcher/runtime independently from the engine interpreter so ordinary isolated-engine consumers can qualify safely; unsupported launchers still execute fresh. Existing defaults remain fresh. Bind engine/recipe version, repository identity, exact check command/mode and the existing full source, configuration, environment and runtime fingerprint. Persist only actual stable successful executions through atomic bounded storage; never publish a failed or skipped execution as a passing cache entry. Corrupt or unsupported data is a miss. Recheck inputs after verification and rerun reused checks if they changed. Preserve origin and source timings in agent-visible evidence; provide an explicit fresh-run control.

Integrate the same mechanism into CLI and loop verification. Unsupported checks and native no-engine hooks retain fresh execution. No new dependency, remote cache, arbitrary-command cache, mandatory build system or cross-stack discovery is introduced. Measure actual fresh and warm separate-process invocation times and compiler counts. Do not claim whole-loop or repository-size scaling from compiler-only evidence.

Exercise actual Pyright, mutation-induced failure, unscoped checks and fresh-run control; publish 30 warm samples and cold setup separately. Preserve offline Lefthook and consumer configuration on upgrade.

## Trigger

When a native Git hook hides verification progress until its command exits, I want live named check progress through the runner and Lefthook, so I can keep implementing features while the harness verifies in the background.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/hooks/check_runner.py`
- `src/basicly/lefthook_config.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`

## Design

Flush named progress at check start. Enable the pinned Lefthook follow setting for managed Git hooks, retaining existing agent protocol handling and consumer-owned jobs/configuration. Do not add interactive stdin or parallel jobs. Preserve return codes, staged snapshots, foreign hooks and the complete verification floor. The engine CLI also exposes each check name before starting it. Unsupported controls must remain explicit rather than imply a live stream.

## Demonstration

Run deterministic process-barrier regressions through the actual engine CLI and pinned Lefthook/native Git hook with a pipe reader thread, proving the marker arrives while its child is still waiting. Release the child by a file barrier, not a sleep. Preserve a real failure and agent stdout/exit-code behavior. Run the full verifier once after final source changes, build a wheel, install it into a fresh consumer and repeat the native hook proof.

- When fail-fast is enabled and a selected check fails, both verification runners shall refuse the operation without executing later selected checks and shall name them as not run.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When an early verification check has already failed, I want the harness to stop subsequent work under an explicit fail-fast setting, so feature development does not wait for expensive tests whose passing result cannot make this run pass.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `src/basicly/verify_artifact.py`
- `.basicly/core/hooks/check_runner.py`
- `tests/test_config.py`
- `tests/test_verify_fail_fast.py`
- `tests/test_verify_artifact.py`
- `tests/test_git_hooks/test_check_runner.py`
- `basicly.d/*.toml`
- `docs/how-to/wire-up-the-verify-gate.md`
- `changelog.d/*.md`

## Design

Add a validated boolean verify.fail_fast setting, default false, and explicitly enable it for basicly in a task fragment. Preserve configured order, existing affected and staged snapshot boundaries, and every required check on the passing path. Both the engine and no-engine portable runner must stop after an actual failed check, name remaining selected checks as not run, preserve failure, and never mint successful cache receipts for incomplete work. Retry and landing diagnostics must retain incomplete coverage and cannot claim success from the failed check alone. Do not introduce parallelism, affected selection, new dependencies or test-result caching.

## Demonstration

Run the installed candidate wheel and native Lefthook pre-push against a consumer with a cheap failing check followed by an observable expensive check. Show the later marker absent with fail-fast true, present with default or false, and present after a passing first check. Measure elapsed time with the same bounded expensive fixture for each mode; report this as fixture evidence, not a general repository speed claim. Exercise a recovered first check and a still-failing retry to prove remaining work never vanishes from the verdict.
payload.requirements: Reduce wasted time after a blocking failure while keeping complete passing-path coverage, truthful not-run evidence, safe retries, standalone consumer operation and existing default behavior.
payload.title: Stop verification work after a blocking failure when explicitly enabled

Reproduced with a real disposable Git repository and candidate wheel: cheap-failure exits 7, later-work still creates its marker, overall exit 1 in both engine and portable runners. Positive control searched all 1701 records and found basicly-8vy4; action search found no matching fail-fast card. Existing rerun_failures and merge._verify_for_landing require explicit incomplete-coverage regression coverage; default remains continue-all.

## Trigger

When an early verification check has already failed, I want to stop subsequent work under an explicit fail-fast setting, so I can resume feature development without waiting for expensive tests whose passing result cannot make this run pass.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `src/basicly/verify_artifact.py`
- `.basicly/core/hooks/check_runner.py`
- `tests/test_config.py`
- `tests/test_verify_fail_fast.py`
- `tests/test_verify_artifact.py`
- `tests/test_git_hooks/test_check_runner.py`
- `basicly.d/*.toml`
- `docs/how-to/wire-up-the-verify-gate.md`
- `changelog.d/*.md`

## Design

Add a validated boolean verify.fail_fast setting, default false, and explicitly enable it for basicly in a task fragment. Preserve configured order, existing affected and staged snapshot boundaries, and every required check on the passing path. Both the engine and no-engine portable runner must stop after an actual failed check, name remaining selected checks as not run, preserve failure, and never mint successful cache receipts for incomplete work. Retry and landing diagnostics must retain incomplete coverage and cannot claim success from the failed check alone. Do not introduce parallelism, affected selection, new dependencies or test-result caching.

## Demonstration

Run the installed candidate wheel and native Lefthook pre-push against a consumer with a cheap failing check followed by an observable expensive check. Show the later marker absent with fail-fast true, present with default or false, and present after a passing first check. Measure elapsed time with the same bounded expensive fixture for each mode; report this as fixture evidence, not a general repository speed claim. Exercise a recovered first check and a still-failing retry to prove remaining work never vanishes from the verdict.

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Trigger

When repository tooling leaves ignored runtime telemetry under the catalog, I want to exclude those files from package builds, so I can install only the harness sources and declared immutable artifacts.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Produce ignored .basicly/usage/tool-usage.json files beneath catalog kit or template directories by using the source checkout.
2. Build the v0.25.1 wheel from that working checkout.
3. Compare its entries with a wheel built from a clean archive of the same tag: the working-checkout wheel includes nested runtime telemetry and its RECORD differs.

The v0.25.1 release uses a clean tag build; its published wheel matches the tested clean candidate and contains no nested runtime telemetry.

## Scope

- `hatch_build.py`
- `tests/test_hatch_build.py`
- `src/basicly/catalog.py`
- `tests/test_catalog.py`
- `pyproject.toml`
- `changelog.d/basicly-c25o52c.8.fixed.md`

## Design

Establish the package input boundary from current producer code. Exclude observed runtime telemetry without dropping legitimate catalog resources or consumer-owned installed files. Add a failing dirty-source packaging regression with a positive control for a real kit resource. Keep all pinned Lefthook binaries, source archive, checksums and license in the offline wheel.

## Demonstration

Build from a clean tag and a checkout containing the reproduced ignored runtime files. Compare wheel entry lists and relevant source bytes, confirm telemetry is absent and declared resources remain, then run packaged offline install.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a verified task produces normal tool artifacts, I want to finish shipping without manual cache moves, so I can return to feature work while unrelated files and failed cleanup remain recoverable.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run normal full verification and prepare pinned build artifacts in a harness task worktree.
2. Approve ship and resume the loop. Cleanup refuses project bytecode, pytest, Ruff, import-linter cache and verified build outputs.
3. Observe that the current ship implementation has already closed the record before cleanup raises. A repeat loop run reports already shipped and leaves the worktree behind.
4. A driver currently has to preserve about twenty generated paths manually, invoke worktree cleanup separately, and commit remaining tracker state. The progress task basicly-8vy4 reproduced this exact failure; later tasks used manual preservation before ship to avoid it.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/worktree.py`
- `src/basicly/worktree_contents.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_worktree.py`
- `tests/test_worktree_contents.py`
- `tests/test_worktree_safety.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
- `tests/test_integration_loop.py`
- `changelog.d/*.md`

## Design

Keep artifact ownership strict and evidence based. Derive known generated-artifact recognition from the actual producers and pinned build manifest, preserving unknown content, symlinks, tracked changes and all existing checkout identity/lock/unmerged guards. Prefer reversible preservation when ownership does not justify discarding an artifact; never treat every ignored path as disposable. Centralize behavior so ordinary worktree cleanup and loop ship share it. A failed cleanup must leave an open, retryable record; actual criterion confirmation still precedes teardown. Keep completion refusals recoverable and repeated attempts idempotent. Do not touch other sessions or historical worktrees, require force, change permissions, add dependencies or bypass hooks.

## Demonstration

Install the candidate into a disposable consumer, run verification that creates the supported actual tool artifacts, land normally, and ship using ordinary loop commands with no manual cache relocation. Exercise foreign and malformed cache files, symlinks and a cleanup failure: they must preserve data and the open record. Remove only the fixture-owned blocker and retry; assert one clean closure and no live worktree. Keep actual argv, outputs, archive/preservation locations where applicable and elapsed command time in the proof.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When harness work consumes hours and excessive inference, I want the complete audit and recommendations preserved in the tracker, so I can approve focused changes that reduce time and token waste.

## Findings and reasons

Repeated verification, compulsory tracker ceremony, broad context priming, conflicting repair and validation roles, consumer prompts referencing authoring-only scripts, whole-batch completion barriers, findings delivered only at redispatch, cleanup after closure and late confirmation are established mechanisms. Tracker UI polling adds repeated requests. Historical full verification took 185.826 seconds including pytest 138.127 seconds. A fresh ranking profile took 0.861 seconds wall and 0.806 seconds process CPU; this does not establish sustained saturation or hours-scale effects across consumer repositories.

## Durable evidence

The audit-report artifact contains every recommendation and reason, evidence citations, all 26 skill dispositions, 307 file dispositions and the conceptual dependency map. The audit-evidence artifact contains the tracked inventory, resolved dependencies and independent kit/web reviews. Static dependency references do not prove runtime reachability. Existing performance program basicly-c25o52c remains distinct.

## Approval boundary

User authorized this audit, tracker persistence and next-release planning on 2026-10-17. Filing a story is not implementation approval. All recommendations require individual review and approval. Do not claim, dispatch, implement, cut a release or change policy from this outline. Existing records, requirements, ownership and pre-existing ledger work must remain intact.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When routine harness work spends excessive time on process, context and repeated checks, I want the next release to remove the largest avoidable costs first, so later implementation runs with less time and inference waste.

## Recommended release

Proposed v0.26.0: focused delivery with less ceremony and repeated verification. This is a planning recommendation, not a version bump, approved implementation or release authorization. It uses stories from the complete audit basicly-h79lott and retains the broader performance program basicly-c25o52c.

## Priority and sequence

1. Record representative workflow baselines and review concrete time/token budgets before optimization.
2. Reduce task-expanding instructions, compulsory broad priming and small-task tracker ceremony.
3. Repair authoring-only instructions in consumer paths and the two known landing/cleanup lifecycle defects.
4. Remove measured equivalent verification and validation/review work while preserving input identity and safety.
5. Prove the exact candidate with the same workloads and a clean consumer upgrade.

## Explicit exclusions

Defer batch-streaming orchestration, running-lane notifications, new skill profile machinery, general resource scheduling, broad scan/index optimization, tracker UI redesign and optional comment/style/dead-code policy retirements. Do not combine these into the first release merely because they appear in the audit. Existing Pyright caching, affected-check providers, fail-fast and Codex workspace profiles already exist; enabling them again is not delivery.

## Approval and release policy

Every selected recommendation requires individual user approval and implementation refinement. A sequence is not a dispatch grant. If a selected item cannot be bounded without a large framework or unrelated refactor, return its concrete tradeoff for review rather than expanding the release. Release acceptance uses observed results, not predicted speedups. No arbitrary numeric improvement is claimed before the baseline is reviewed.
payload.requirements:
- Proposed version v0.26.0 only; do not bump, tag, publish or implement from this plan without approval.
- Focus first on the approved time/token savings; preserve existing story ownership and complete audit traceability.
- Keep larger orchestration and optional house-policy retirements outside the initial release.
payload.title: Propose the next release around time and token savings

- When optimized paths encounter changed inputs, foreign configuration, partial staging, missing confirmation or cleanup failure, they shall preserve correctness and recoverability.
- When release acceptance is decided, the exact candidate artifact shall meet the reviewed budgets or report why acceptance remains blocked.

## Trigger

When the focused time/token changes have landed in a release candidate, I want to compare that exact candidate with the baseline through real consumer journeys, so I can accept a demonstrated saving instead of an isolated microbenchmark.

## Required proof

Reuse the same small bug fix, docs change, clean consumer install/upgrade and two-lane journey defined by basicly-h79lott.3. Record end-to-end elapsed time, phase/check durations, duplicate check execution, permission/repair/cleanup interventions and actual token/context usage where the host exposes it. Mark unavailable CPU or billing data as unavailable. Warm and cold conditions must be named, and the exact commit, package hash, check inputs and runtime versions recorded. Reuse valid evidence for the same artifact rather than rerunning by habit. Exercise foreign hooks/configuration, staged-versus-working content, changed inputs and failed cleanup/confirmation controls. Do not claim repository-size scaling or cross-host savings from this limited matrix.

## Approval boundary

This is planning and release acceptance only. Implementation, new dependencies, CI edits, release publication and paid probes require their applicable approvals. Agree numerical time/token budgets after the baseline, before optimization is accepted.
payload.requirements:
- Preserve the complete evidence and actual commands in the tracker.
- Reuse valid exact-input evidence and never manufacture unavailable token, CPU or billing measurements.
- No bypasses, unapproved dependencies, CI edits or publication.

body.head: 8b0a851bdeb10e486fdde3e72b40b8ec0b67f611
body.implementation: All recommendations pending individual user approval. AUD identifiers are proposed audit items, not tracker IDs.

observations.limits: Historical timings are wall time in this checkout. One profiled ranking invocation includes profiler overhead. No consumer-repository end-to-end or sustained CPU benchmark was run. No promised speedup.

recommendations.change: Remove automatic adjacent improvements and mandatory catalog-control work from ordinary repairs; allow a reproducible first defect to be fixed.
recommendations.reason: Local ownership and core completion rules broaden work; root-cause is injected for every bug but says stop after a first occurrence.
recommendations.title: Constrain work to the approved outcome

recommendations.change: Provide a small-task contract with intent, criteria, ownership and observed outcomes; avoid mandatory six-part rationales and synthetic same-card conversations.
recommendations.reason: Readiness/claim/close enforce ceremony in code; prompt compression alone cannot remove it.
recommendations.title: Make tracker evidence proportional

recommendations.change: Measure representative small fix, docs change, consumer install/upgrade and concurrent lanes using existing timing data first; set time/token budgets and collect CPU only where attribution is missing.
recommendations.reason: Existing measurements cover individual checks and dispatches; hours-to-minutes and CPU saturation are not established.
recommendations.title: Establish an end-to-end performance baseline

recommendations.change: Move the required completion confirmation check ahead of the first merge, retaining subsequent evidence checks.
recommendations.reason: Current normal path can merge and only then refuse confirmation.
recommendations.title: Confirm before merging

recommendations.change: Preserve owned work safely and make outstanding cleanup resumable before completion reads as done.
recommendations.reason: Current ship closes before cleanup, and closed derives done on resume.
recommendations.title: Make cleanup retryable

recommendations.change: Select release-note/headroom commands from capabilities the consumer actually has; keep authoring-only behavior in the authoring profile or package a generic implementation.
recommendations.reason: Universal dispatch references private .scripts/check_release_notes.py; shipped headroom hook also depends on private .scripts/headroom.py.
recommendations.title: Repair consumer versus authoring boundaries

recommendations.change: Share verification identity and valid evidence across CLI, hooks, rebased lane, merged tree and push where their actual inputs match; extend reuse check by check.
recommendations.reason: Full tests repeat; existing receipts/cache cover selected Pyright commands and are already enabled. Preserve staged-content and changed-input refusals.
recommendations.title: Avoid repeated equivalent verification

recommendations.change: Feed completed outcomes into the serial dependency-aware landing queue without waiting for the entire dispatch batch.
recommendations.reason: dispatch_lanes waits for all futures before CLI routes any result.
recommendations.title: Land completed lanes while others run

recommendations.change: Extend existing durable found-info routing with recipient scope, sequence and acknowledgement; start with the current coordination mechanism.
recommendations.reason: Findings currently arrive in later dispatch bundles, not running workers; a replacement messaging framework is unnecessary to address that gap.
recommendations.title: Deliver targeted findings to running lanes

recommendations.change: Check planned worktree/Git/protected output operations once and surface exact actionable mismatches; reuse existing write preflight and preserve scoped grants and dotenv denials.
recommendations.reason: Current Codex profiles exist; supervisor preflight does not prove these writes are authorized. PATH engine resolution can also disagree with installed kit version.
recommendations.title: Preflight effective permissions and runtime

recommendations.change: Replace mandatory whole architecture priming with a short current contract and relevant sections; shorten repeated orientation and redundant task instructions.
recommendations.reason: Architecture is 5646 lines; every non-trivial task is told to read it. Skill listings and injected bodies need separate budgets.
recommendations.title: Load context by task

recommendations.change: Choose review work by actual risk and useful repair evidence, report actual gate status, distinguish per-issue ship from release, and supply portable role instructions to Codex.
recommendations.reason: Reviews run serially after FAIL/undecodable verdict too; they intentionally aid repairs. Install versus read-only and push/ship wording conflict, and Codex lacks the resolved role body.
recommendations.title: Make validation and role contracts consistent

recommendations.change: Keep delivery essentials; make authoring, discovery, release, retention and vendor-audit tools optional. Correct zero-use pruning before removing any skill.
recommendations.reason: Skill-tool counters miss inline delivery and some host paths; absence of a recorded invocation is not proof a skill is useless.
recommendations.title: Offer lean skill profiles with reliable usage evidence

recommendations.change: Use measured CPU/I/O demand to admit concurrent check processes separately from agent process slots; use prepared lockfile-consistent dependencies.
recommendations.reason: Agent limits already exist; nominal pytest worker totals do not establish saturation. Worktree provisioning still copies node_modules and may npm install.
recommendations.title: Budget verification resources separately

recommendations.change: Prune excluded directories before traversal, share tracked-file/AST inputs within a check run, and measure headroom only for the requested file.
recommendations.reason: Comments CLI filters after rglob; multiple gates scan the same tree; pre-edit headroom measures all modules.
recommendations.title: Reduce script traversal work

recommendations.change: Pass one immutable folded/indexed view through write guards and revisions while retaining the ledger lock and invalidation rules.
recommendations.reason: A write reads the ledger through multiple guards and append; readiness repeatedly traverses events. Fresh ranking profile is sub-second, so do not present it as the principal hours-scale cause.
recommendations.title: Reuse a ledger view within each transaction

recommendations.change: Use change-triggered shared data and single-flight requests; preserve drafts/focus and back off when hidden.
recommendations.reason: A refresh issues nine API calls plus two for an open card; two-second version polling and unconditional fifteen-second reload overlap.
recommendations.title: Refresh tracker UI without repeated full loads

recommendations.change: Keep concise current contracts, move historical decisions/measurements and target designs out of compulsory priming, and reconcile contradictions and stale examples.
recommendations.reason: D25 conflicts with the absolute comment ban; decision index stops at D44 while body reaches D51; status and kit docs contain superseded claims despite structural doc gates.
recommendations.title: Separate current docs from historical designs

recommendations.change: Retain the standalone comments kit for users who choose it; stop imposing an absolute comment/docstring ban on every consumer by default.
recommendations.reason: It is house policy with unmeasured delivery benefit, conflicts with D25, and can create unrelated edits and documentation displacement. Keep safe-strip proofs if the kit remains enabled.
recommendations.title: Make the comment ban an explicit policy choice

recommendations.change: Remove the separate parentheses-style checker and its redundant guidance if approved; retain parser, lint, type and compatibility checks.
recommendations.reason: It spends a whole-tree tokenization pass enforcing house syntax style rather than a demonstrated defect class. Kit Python compatibility remains a separate requirement.
recommendations.title: Retire the except-form style gate

recommendations.change: Review wired-or-deleted overlap with vulture and filename-only test coverage; retain only controls tied to a demonstrated behavioral failure.
recommendations.reason: Unqualified names/string references and test filenames are weak evidence of real wiring or test coverage, while adding scans and maintenance. Retirement requires explicit policy approval.
recommendations.title: Replace duplicate heuristic wiring checks

recommendations.change: Keep Conventional Commits and the record link; remove arbitrary description character restrictions and universal word-count constraints where they add no consumer value.
recommendations.reason: Mechanical phrasing refusals consume repair turns without establishing correctness.
recommendations.title: Simplify incidental commit and prose rules

recommendations.change: Prepare one candidate artifact/environment and bind reusable proof to its exact inputs; remove redundant setup and checks while retaining fresh-install/upgrade/offline/foreign-hook evidence.
recommendations.reason: The release skill repeats checks and scratch setup; workflow builds artifacts in multiple jobs. The release path should reuse valid evidence instead of requiring repeated manual reconstruction.
recommendations.title: Reuse release preparation and consumer proof

Canonical sources reviewed for generated duplicates; 225 tracked Markdown paths, 26 skill bodies, 43 root Python scripts plus bootstrap/renderer, 28 hook Python files, all 59 kit Python modules and standalone package entry/helper scripts. Static graph inventory includes tests; not every test body was semantically reviewed. Non-script HTML/CSS/templates structurally scanned, not a visual audit. No dotenv reads, network, implementation, tracker writes or full test suite.

findings.claim: One write reads and folds complete ledger multiple times inside global lock; existing parse/fold memoization avoids some computation but does not avoid full byte reads.
findings.recommendation: Reuse one validated immutable transaction view across checks and append, preserving lock ownership and event guarantees. Measure representative small and large ledgers first.

findings.claim: Scheduler computes readiness for every view; revision checks scan full event collection for record and each dependency. Static board repeats aggregate queries and per-record readiness.
findings.recommendation: Build per-record event/dependency indexes per loaded generation and share them among read views; avoid recomputing irrelevant closed-card readiness. Keep revision invalidation semantics.

findings.claim: Every API request stats loaded kit files; background watcher separately polls all kit files once per second. No measured magnitude.
findings.recommendation: Share reload-generation state or make code-reload development-only while preserving refusal to write through changed incompatible kit.

kit-library-review.json.scope: Read-only canonical kit library review. differential.py reviewed from line171 onward; primary reviewed lines1-170. All other listed files read in full. No fresh runtime benchmarks or tests.

resolved-python-dependencies.json.head: 8b0a851bdeb10e486fdde3e72b40b8ec0b67f611
resolved-python-dependencies.json.note: Resolved static imports and literal sibling loader calls. Runtime reachability, dispatch behavior and projection/distribution edges are separately traced in audit.json. Not all dynamic calls are resolvable statically.

findings.issue: Tracker web refresh fans out into repeated full-ledger reads even without ledger changes.
findings.limits: No runtime measurement. Two-second version probe exists already; replacement by elaborate message bus is not necessary.
findings.recommendation: Use change-triggered shared snapshots and single-flight refresh, preserve detail drafts/focus; include in existing basicly-cmv2jgq.2 only after approval.

findings.issue: Engine board periodic HTTP Refresh differs from tracker kit JS polling; keep distinct in graph.
findings.recommendation: Measure board-open workload separately; do not claim all periodic ledger cost happens in kit or all consumers run engine board.

web-entry-review.json.negative_control: All tracked HTML/CSS/Jinja scanned with script regex; it detects canonical kit/skill assets and their projected duplicate copies; no script blocks in root site or board Jinja templates. These non-script bodies were structurally scanned, not all semantically reread.
web-entry-review.json.no_execution: No generated page rendering, tests, network, implementation or tracker writes.

acceptance.description:
## Trigger

When the focused time/token changes have landed in a release candidate, I want to compare that exact candidate with the baseline through real consumer journeys, so I can accept a demonstrated saving instead of an isolated microbenchmark.

## Required proof

Reuse the same small bug fix, docs change, clean consumer install/upgrade and two-lane journey defined by basicly-h79lott.3. Record end-to-end elapsed time, phase/check durations, duplicate check execution, permission/repair/cleanup interventions and actual token/context usage where the host exposes it. Mark unavailable CPU or billing data as unavailable. Warm and cold conditions must be named, and the exact commit, package hash, check inputs and runtime versions recorded. Reuse valid evidence for the same artifact rather than rerunning by habit. Exercise foreign hooks/configuration, staged-versus-working content, changed inputs and failed cleanup/confirmation controls. Do not claim repository-size scaling or cross-host savings from this limited matrix.

## Approval boundary

This is planning and release acceptance only. Implementation, new dependencies, CI edits, release publication and paid probes require their applicable approvals. Agree numerical time/token budgets after the baseline, before optimization is accepted.

- Preserve the complete evidence and actual commands in the tracker.
- Reuse valid exact-input evidence and never manufacture unavailable token, CPU or billing measurements.
- No bypasses, unapproved dependencies, CI edits or publication.

basicly-ewepxov.description:
## Trigger

When a verified task produces normal tool artifacts, I want to finish shipping without manual cache moves, so I can return to feature work while unrelated files and failed cleanup remain recoverable.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run normal full verification and prepare pinned build artifacts in a harness task worktree.
2. Approve ship and resume the loop. Cleanup refuses project bytecode, pytest, Ruff, import-linter cache and verified build outputs.
3. Observe that the current ship implementation has already closed the record before cleanup raises. A repeat loop run reports already shipped and leaves the worktree behind.
4. A driver currently has to preserve about twenty generated paths manually, invoke worktree cleanup separately, and commit remaining tracker state. The progress task basicly-8vy4 reproduced this exact failure; later tasks used manual preservation before ship to avoid it.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/worktree.py`
- `src/basicly/worktree_contents.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_worktree.py`
- `tests/test_worktree_contents.py`
- `tests/test_worktree_safety.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
- `tests/test_integration_loop.py`
- `changelog.d/*.md`

## Design

Keep artifact ownership strict and evidence based. Derive known generated-artifact recognition from the actual producers and pinned build manifest, preserving unknown content, symlinks, tracked changes and all existing checkout identity/lock/unmerged guards. Prefer reversible preservation when ownership does not justify discarding an artifact; never treat every ignored path as disposable. Centralize behavior so ordinary worktree cleanup and loop ship share it. A failed cleanup must leave an open, retryable record; actual criterion confirmation still precedes teardown. Keep completion refusals recoverable and repeated attempts idempotent. Do not touch other sessions or historical worktrees, require force, change permissions, add dependencies or bypass hooks.

## Demonstration

Install the candidate into a disposable consumer, run verification that creates the supported actual tool artifacts, land normally, and ship using ordinary loop commands with no manual cache relocation. Exercise foreign and malformed cache files, symlinks and a cleanup failure: they must preserve data and the open record. Remove only the fixture-owned blocker and retry; assert one clean closure and no live worktree. Keep actual argv, outputs, archive/preservation locations where applicable and elapsed command time in the proof.

basicly-ewepxov.description:
## Trigger

When a verified task produces normal tool artifacts, I want to finish shipping without manual cache moves, so I can return to feature work while unrelated files and failed cleanup remain recoverable.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run normal full verification and prepare pinned build artifacts in a harness task worktree.
2. Approve ship and resume the loop. Cleanup refuses project bytecode, pytest, Ruff, import-linter cache and verified build outputs.
3. Observe that the current ship implementation has already closed the record before cleanup raises. A repeat loop run reports already shipped and leaves the worktree behind.
4. A driver currently has to preserve about twenty generated paths manually, invoke worktree cleanup separately, and commit remaining tracker state. The progress task basicly-8vy4 reproduced this exact failure; later tasks used manual preservation before ship to avoid it.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/worktree.py`
- `src/basicly/worktree_contents.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_worktree.py`
- `tests/test_worktree_contents.py`
- `tests/test_worktree_safety.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
- `tests/test_integration_loop.py`
- `changelog.d/*.md`

## Design

Keep artifact ownership strict and evidence based. Derive known generated-artifact recognition from the actual producers and pinned build manifest, preserving unknown content, symlinks, tracked changes and all existing checkout identity/lock/unmerged guards. Prefer reversible preservation when ownership does not justify discarding an artifact; never treat every ignored path as disposable. Centralize behavior so ordinary worktree cleanup and loop ship share it. A failed cleanup must leave an open, retryable record; actual criterion confirmation still precedes teardown. Keep completion refusals recoverable and repeated attempts idempotent. Do not touch other sessions or historical worktrees, require force, change permissions, add dependencies or bypass hooks.

## Demonstration

Install the candidate into a disposable consumer, run verification that creates the supported actual tool artifacts, land normally, and ship using ordinary loop commands with no manual cache relocation. Exercise foreign and malformed cache files, symlinks and a cleanup failure: they must preserve data and the open record. Remove only the fixture-owned blocker and retry; assert one clean closure and no live worktree. Keep actual argv, outputs, archive/preservation locations where applicable and elapsed command time in the proof.

## Trigger

When the harness costs time and tokens across a complete change, I want a repeatable baseline for the agreed consumer workflows, so I can target measured waste and compare the efficiency release fairly.

## Scope

- `.scripts/measure_workflows.py`
- `.scripts/validate_affected_consumer.py`
- `docs/reference/workflow-performance.md`
- `changelog.d/basicly-h79lott.3.added.md`

## Design

Reuse the native packaged-consumer command recorder and fixture preparation already implemented in validate_affected_consumer.py. Exercise fresh installation and idempotent upgrade, a small Python change, a documentation change, and two independently provisioned lanes with ordinary hooks and loop commands. Preserve command argv, monotonic elapsed times, actual check execution, checkpoint/repair interventions and terminal outcomes. Label prepared dependency/OS caches, deterministic manual edits and unavailable model-token/CPU attribution explicitly. A baseline blockage is recorded as a blockage, never as a successful full workflow. Preserve existing landing/check histories separately from the controlled fixture. Persist the complete result and workload/package identities in the tracker. No paid model calls or dependency changes are required.

## Demonstration

Run the documented script against a locally built pinned wheel. Read the complete JSON result and native transcript. Agree release acceptance targets with the user only after reporting the baseline.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When an approved native ship retry receives the immediately preceding confirmation code, I want that code to remain valid until consumption or expiry, so I can finish normal work without repeated permission failures.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install the pinned pre-change wheel and drive an ordinary manual task through its confirmed change and successful merge.
2. Capture the ship challenge printed by loop run, then immediately run the offered command with its code.
3. Observe ship REFUSED with invalid or expired confirm code, although no human or time delay changed the challenge. All four lanes in the measurement reproduced this.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
- `tests/test_policy_confirm_store.py`
- `tests/test_integration_loop.py`
- `changelog.d/*.md`

## Evidence

loop._on_verify calls approve_checkpoint_guarded with no code before run_ceremony consumes the supplied code. The no-code path issues and replaces the current ship code. Native command evidence and the installed package identity are preserved in native-confirmation-reproduction-v1. This defect directly blocks the agreed baseline and release consumer journeys; its bounded correction is covered by the user pre-approval of everything connected to this goal.
payload.requirements: Preserve checkpoint consent, expiry, replay protection, merge-before-ship and normal Git hooks. No code or test gate bypass.
payload.title: Preserve ship confirmation codes across the native loop retry

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Trigger

When a verified task produces normal tool artifacts, I want to finish shipping without manual cache moves, so I can return to feature work while unrelated files and failed cleanup remain recoverable.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run normal full verification and prepare pinned build artifacts in a harness task worktree.
2. Approve ship and resume the loop. Cleanup refuses project bytecode, pytest, Ruff, import-linter cache and verified build outputs.
3. Observe that the current ship implementation has already closed the record before cleanup raises. A repeat loop run reports already shipped and leaves the worktree behind.
4. A driver currently has to preserve about twenty generated paths manually, invoke worktree cleanup separately, and commit remaining tracker state. The progress task basicly-8vy4 reproduced this exact failure; later tasks used manual preservation before ship to avoid it.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/worktree.py`
- `src/basicly/worktree_contents.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/tracker.py`
- `src/basicly/owned_write.py`
- `tests/test_owned_write_completion.py`
- `tests/test_worktree.py`
- `tests/test_worktree_contents.py`
- `tests/test_worktree_safety.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
- `tests/test_integration_loop.py`
- `changelog.d/*.md`

## Design

Keep artifact ownership strict and evidence based. Derive known generated-artifact recognition from the actual producers and pinned build manifest, preserving unknown content, symlinks, tracked changes and all existing checkout identity/lock/unmerged guards. Prefer reversible preservation when ownership does not justify discarding an artifact; never treat every ignored path as disposable. Centralize behavior so ordinary worktree cleanup and loop ship share it. A failed cleanup must leave an open, retryable record; actual criterion confirmation still precedes teardown. Keep completion refusals recoverable and repeated attempts idempotent. Do not touch other sessions or historical worktrees, require force, change permissions, add dependencies or bypass hooks.

## Demonstration

Install the candidate into a disposable consumer, run verification that creates the supported actual tool artifacts, land normally, and ship using ordinary loop commands with no manual cache relocation. Exercise foreign and malformed cache files, symlinks and a cleanup failure: they must preserve data and the open record. Remove only the fixture-owned blocker and retry; assert one clean closure and no live worktree. Keep actual argv, outputs, archive/preservation locations where applicable and elapsed command time in the proof.

payload.text: Approved goal implementation refinement: source-linked valid bytecode and strictly recognized producer caches can be preserved reversibly with a complete relative-path/hash inventory; never classify arbitrary usage files or all ignored files as owned. Retain checkout identity/lock/tracked/symlink guards. Reuse authoritative owned-write completion admission in a no-write preflight, then perform cleanup, then append the authoritative close. A refusal before teardown preserves the worktree; a late close refusal leaves the record open and retries missing cleanup idempotently. The native observer counter was moved outside consumer trees rather than weakening unknown-file refusal. Scope now includes the common tracker admission seam and its real-ledger tests.
